\"Husen ska stå rakt ner i blåbärsriset!: “The houses should stand right in the blueberry bushes!” declared the architects behind the student housing on Bosön. The nature around the buildings was to be left untouched, and the timber houses were treated with brown tar to blend into the forest.
148 idrottsprofiler i Hall of Fame: 148 sporting greats in the Hall of Fame
1528 befallde Gustav Vasa att Härlanda k: In 1528 King Gustav Vasa ordered Härlanda Church to be torn down. It stood so close to the town that it wasn't needed, and in wartime an enemy could have used it. Its stones went into the church at Nya Lödöse instead.
1651 gav kronan hemmanet Skår till Göteb: In 1651 the Crown granted the Skår homestead to Nils Påfve, commandant of Gothenburg, who was later ennobled as Påfvenfelt, and the farm became known as Påvelund. Påvelundsstugan, a timbered double cottage from the 1770s, was lived in until 1906.
1663 öppnade rådmannen Gustaf Mattsson e: In 1663 the alderman Gustaf Mattsson opened a 'Godh Krogh' – a good tavern – in an inn he had paid for himself. The coaching inn kept 20 horses for travellers, but the posting logs are full of complaints that the horses were worn out.
1782 stod det på en fönsterruta i krogen: In 1782 someone wrote on a windowpane at the inn: 'Gustav III, the foremost citizen.' Carl Anders von Plommenfeldt, a dismissed court official, added: 'He has been, but is now the foremost rogue' – and was later sentenced to death in his absence for lèse-majesté.
1785 köptes Slagsta av friherre Johan Li: In 1785 Slagsta was bought by Baron Johan Liljencrantz. He also owned Fittja farm, Norsborg Manor and Sturehov Palace. The City of Stockholm bought the estate in 1908, and since 1978 it has belonged to Botkyrka Municipality.
1884 bildades Krokslätts municipalsamhäl: In 1884 Krokslätt became a municipal community, a small self-governing township outside the city. By 1913 just over 5,000 people lived there. In 1922 the area became part of Gothenburg, and today it's home to Chalmers Science Park.
1889 byggde Stockholm en sopstation vid: In 1889 Stockholm built a refuse station at Lövsta, and the rubbish arrived on a dedicated railway from Spånga. The refuse trains were nicknamed Silverpilen, the Silver Arrow, and ran until 1970. The passenger train to Stockholm Central took about 33 minutes.
1892 blev gården ett hem för sjuka barn,: In 1892 the house became a home for sick children, Margaretahemmet, opened in the presence of Queen Sofia and Prince Carl. Its 30 beds soon weren't enough, and in 1902 it moved to Åkeshov manor.
1902–1905 byggdes Stockholms stads arbet: Between 1902 and 1905 the City of Stockholm built its workhouse here, with room for 1,432 inmates. The barracks-like complex closed in the late 1960s after fierce criticism of neglect and abuse, and was demolished in 1971. Today the site is Drakenbergsparken.
1917 brann det i smedjan, och byggnaden: In 1917 fire broke out in the smithy and the building was given a new roof. Another fire followed in the 1930s, and the building fell into disrepair. In the early 1970s the City of Gothenburg restored it and the walls were limewashed white.
1924 anlades Torslanda Havsbadskoloni på: In 1924 the Torslanda Havsbadskoloni was laid out on Skeppstadsholmen, with 123 seaside allotment plots of around 1,000 square metres each. It was the first seaside colony in Scandinavia, and the idea came from the local politician Herman Lindholm.
1924 byggde Blomsterfonden sitt hus vid: In 1924 the Blomsterfonden foundation built its house at Rödabergsgatan 1. The foundation had been set up on the initiative of Alma Hedin, sister of the explorer Sven Hedin, and the flats were to be let to people in need at lower rents than usual.
1926 stod ett nytt stationshus klart, ri: A new station building by Folke Zetterwall was completed in 1926. It stood on tall concrete pillars above one of the tracks and had a little café with outdoor seating on a terrace over the trains. It remained in use until the 1980s.
1927–1928 byggde Banan-Kompaniet ett hus: In 1927–1928 the Banana Company built a complex with offices, ripening rooms, packing halls and its own loading dock and railway siding. In its day it was the most modern in Europe, and even after a renovation in the 1990s bananas were still being ripened there.
1933 målade Olle Nyman, själv medlem i o: In 1933 Olle Nyman, himself a member of the Skogskarlarna orienteering club, painted a humorous orienteering race on the walls of the cabin. Among the scenes are a local farmer taking potshots at orienteers cutting across his land, and a major wheeling his bicycle along the ridge.
1933–37 byggde Statens bakteriologiska l: Between 1933 and 1937 the National Bacteriological Laboratory built some 30 buildings here, with laboratories, animal stables and an animal hospital. Most were designed by Gunnar Asplund, and the complex is considered one of Sweden's most important works of early modernism. Today vaccines are made here.
1940 ville Solna anlägga en egen Solnavä: In 1940 Solna wanted a Solnavägen of its own, so Stockholm renamed its street. It became Norra Stationsgatan, after Stockholm's North Station, which stood here from 1924. The brick-red station building with its tower was demolished in 2014.
1942–1946 byggde HSB niohundra lägenhete: Between 1942 and 1946 the housing cooperative HSB built nine hundred flats here. HSB's founder Sven Wallander designed the tower blocks at the top of the island, and the landscape architect Ulla Bodorff laid out the green spaces. The area was showcased at an anniversary exhibition in 1944.
1943 flyttade Sjökrigsskolan från Skepps: In 1943 the Naval Academy moved from Skeppsholmen to Näsby Castle, and around 25 buildings went up around the castle. The academy stayed until 1987.
1957–58 revs fyra landshövdingehus och t: In 1957–58 four landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical tenements with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys – and three smaller houses with 68 flats in all were torn down. In their place came six yellow-brick tower blocks with 379 flats and a central building with mosaic façades. The area is now part of Gothenburg's conservation programme, and the market hall stands where the tram building used to be.
1960 bodde 582 personer i Träkvista och: In 1960 Träkvista had 582 residents and Tappström 343. Ten years later each had grown to around 1,100, and by 1975 the two had merged into one built-up area. Today Ekerö has more than 10,000 inhabitants.
1962 började Lillhagen pröva dagsjukvård: In 1962 Lillhagen became the first hospital in Sweden to try out day treatment for a small group of patients. The idea was to open the big institutions up to the wider community. In 1967 the hospital got its first training flat, where patients could prepare for moving into homes of their own.
1967 fick Frölunda torg pris som bästa b: In 1967 Frölunda Torg was named the best building in Gothenburg, praised for expressing American ideals and the large scale of the era. The architects were Hjalmar Klemming, Lars Grönlund and Erik Thelaus.
1967 fick byggnaden pris som bästa byggn: In 1967 the building was named the best in Gothenburg, with the jury praising how it gave expression to “American ideals and the large scale of the times”. The architects were Hjalmar Klemming, Lars Grönlund and Erik Thelaus, and construction cost 80 million kronor.
1972 slutade tågen stanna vid gamla Möln: In 1972 trains stopped calling at old Mölndals nedre. Commuter trains returned in 1992, and since the Öresund trains were introduced in 2000 you can travel from here straight to Copenhagen.
1975 invigde kung Carl XVI Gustaf tunnel: In 1975 King Carl XVI Gustaf opened the metro station and bus terminal by the centre. At the end of October 2005, Guldhyttan closed – the last shop that had been there since the centre opened.
1987 fick studion en andra studio i en f: In 1987 a second studio was added in a former hair salon next to the old cinema. In 2019 the business was bought by six people, including two former students, and by 2026 Soundtrade had seven studios.
1991 lämnade BP Sverige och anläggningen: In 1991 BP pulled out of Sweden and the plant became OK Raffinaderi. In 1994 it was bought by Mohammed Al-Amoudi's Corral Petroleum for 5.9 billion kronor, and in 1996 it was renamed Preemraff Göteborg.
2005 köptes villan och parken för 24,5 m: In 2005 the villa and its park were sold for 24.5 million kronor and turned into offices, with the Tibell villa from 1929 included in the deal. The council felt the price was too high at the time, even though the whole Papyrus area is listed in its cultural heritage programme.
2006–2007 byggdes gatan om till en espla: In 2006–2007 the street was rebuilt as an esplanade with a grassy central strip. 274 Dutch lindens were planted in four rows: one along each side of the street and a double row down the middle.
2009 tävlade sex arkitektkontor om hur a: In 2009 six architecture firms competed to design the arena. Erséus Architects won with their proposal ‘Well’, and the complex ended up covering 12,600 square metres.
2009–2011 byggdes raffinaderiet om till: Between 2009 and 2011 the refinery was converted into a biorefinery. Tall oil from paper mills is processed in Piteå into crude tall diesel, then shipped here for the final stage before it's blended into the diesel you buy at the pump.
2020 röstade kulturnämnden ned ett försl: In 2020 the culture committee rejected a proposal to rename the square Gui Minhais torg, after the imprisoned Swedish publisher – the Chinese consulate is located here. One of the reasons given: a person must have been dead for at least five years.
286 fruktträd och julmarknad: 286 fruit trees and a Christmas market
400 fruktträd och engelsk park: 400 fruit trees and an English park
79 i namnet syftar på adressen Sandhamns: The ‘79’ in the name refers to the address, Sandhamnsgatan 79, and ‘Park’ to Gärdet, the wide-open park that spreads out in front of the building. Most of the floor-to-ceiling windows look out over Gärdet. The building came third in the Stockholm Building of the Year 2019 awards.
79&Park trappar upp från två till tio vå: 79&Park steps up from two to ten storeys around a 1,000-square-metre courtyard. Its roof is made up of many small squares at different heights, and the pleated facade is clad in cedar.
AB Atomenergi hade inte bara fabrik här: AB Atomenergi had not only a factory here but also offices, a laboratory and a uranium store. Operations were gradually moved to Studsvik in the late 1970s, and today only two buildings remain from that era.
AB Diesels Motorer köpte Rudolf Diesels: AB Diesels Motorer bought Rudolf Diesel’s Swedish patent and built its first workshop here in 1898. The engines, mostly marine diesels, were loaded on to railway wagons right inside the factory. The last diesel engine from Sickla was delivered to Slite in 1951.
ABC-staden och miljonprogrammet: The ABC town and the Million Programme
Abrahamsbergsskolan byggdes 1946 samtidi: Abrahamsbergsskolan school was built in 1946 along with the housing around it, and its yellow brick blends right into ‘the yellow town’, as Abrahamsberg is sometimes called. Not far away in Riksby is something far older: two Viking Age runic carvings on a flat rock. They'd probably lain hidden under soil and moss for several hundred years when children out picking berries discovered them in 1904.
Adventskalendern spelades in här: Where the Christmas calendar was filmed
Affärscentret runt torget ritades av Bac: The shopping centre around the square was designed by Backström & Reinius and opened in November 1946. The south end of the square had the Johanneshov 1 post office, designed by Lars-Erik Lallerstedt. The post office has closed, but the big post horn is still on the brick facade.
Affärsmannen Robert Ditzinger var en omt: The businessman Robert Ditzinger was a considerate father. In 1882 he had two identical main houses built on Långsjö farm, one for each of his two sons. The farm later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö, which stretches down to Långsjön lake on the Huddinge side. Not far from here runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows Göta landsväg, the old highway south.
Aftonstjärnan började visa film 1915 och: Aftonstjärnan began showing films in 1915, and it's now the oldest building in Gothenburg still in use as a cinema. When it reopened in 1994, the opening film was Cinema Paradiso. From 1996 to 2004 Kent Andersson staged his annual revues here.
Ahlby säteri från 1620-talet är det älds: Ahlby säteri, a manor from the 1620s, is the oldest house in Lilla Alby. One of its owners was Clas Fredrik Horn, who was convicted of complicity in the murder of King Gustav III. Twenty-eight metres beneath the street is Solna strand station, with Takashi Naraha's artwork Himmelen av kub, Sky of Cubes, which brings the sky right down to the platform.
Ahlby säteri är Q-märkt, 450 kvadratmete: Ahlby manor is a listed stone building of 450 square metres, with interiors in the rococo style.
Ahlby säteri är ett 450 kvadratmeter sto: Ahlby säteri is a 450-square-metre stone manor house decorated in Rococo style. It carries a Q designation in the local plan, meaning it's protected for its cultural and historical value.
Akalla domineras av arton höghus som stå: Akalla is dominated by eighteen tower blocks standing in a row through the district, with the centre on the south side and lower buildings around large courtyards to the north. The City Museum ranks Akalla among the most interesting districts of the Million Programme, Sweden's great 1960s–70s housing drive.
Akalla kyrka är lika lång som bred och h: Akalla Church is as long as it is wide and tall: 15 metres in every direction. The dark red brick cube was designed by Hans Wieland and stands out clearly above the lower parish rooms. A band of windows runs all the way round the church just below the flat roof.
Akalla nämns första gången 1323 som Akar: Akalla is first mentioned in 1323 as Akarli. The name refers to the people who live by the stream – Igelbäcken, which runs through the area. Settlement here is older still, and there are burial mounds to prove it.
Akallas 46 gator och parker och 22 kvart: All 46 of Akalla's streets and parks and its 22 blocks have Finnish place names, while the footpaths are named after famous Finns – hence Sibeliusgången.
Akallas 46 gator och parker och dess 22: Akalla's 46 streets and parks and its 22 blocks have all been given Finnish place names, while the footpaths are named after Finnish personalities. That's why the streets have names like Torneågatan and Sveaborgsgatan.
Akallastråket passerar i närheten, ett p: Akallastråket passes close by – a walking route of around 18 kilometres that follows the blue metro line from Akalla all the way to Stortorget in Gamla stan, the Old Town. The City of Stockholm has given it the motto 'From 18th-century village to Stockholm's Silicon Valley'. For the very young there's Mulle Meckparken, a themed playground named after the children's book character Mulle Meck.
Aktiebolaget Valand grundades i Göteborg: The company Aktiebolaget Valand was founded in Gothenburg in the late 1880s to create a forum for art, and it built the Valand building at Vasagatan 41.
Albert Lilienbergs stadsplan lät gatorna: Albert Lilienberg's town plan let the streets follow the hilly terrain, even though that ideal had actually gone out of fashion by then. The villas here are often a little larger than in the neighbouring areas, many with two full storeys.
Alby centrum fräschades upp på 1990-tale: Alby centrum was spruced up in the 1990s, with a new, bright metro entrance and a new outdoor square, among other things. In the 2000s the inside was repainted, and Alby's only heated garage went from dark grey to a slightly lighter grey.
Alby gård har anor från medeltiden. Efte: Alby farm dates back to the Middle Ages. From 1895 it was owned by the telephone manufacturer Lars Magnus Ericsson, who rebuilt the main house and planned a model farm.
Alby gård har anor från medeltiden. Sin: Alby farm dates back to the Middle Ages. It took its final form after 1895, when it was owned by the telephone manufacturer Lars Magnus Ericsson. He rebuilt the main house and planned a model farm.
Alby är den enda kända boplatsen från br: Alby is the only known settlement in the Mälaren valley from the second period of the Bronze Age. Around 850 potsherds and a blue glass bead have been found here. Nearby is Albykistan, a stone cist from around 1800 BC.
Alby är den hittills enda kända boplatse: Alby is so far the only known settlement in the Mälaren valley from the second period of the Bronze Age. Finds include some 850 pottery shards, a shaft-hole axe and a blue glass bead.
Alby är hemma för Cirkus Cirkör, som har: Alby is home to Cirkus Cirkör, based at the Subtopia cultural centre, and most residents live in one of the 3,000 flats owned by Botkyrkabyggen. But people were here long before that. Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist grave, dates from around 1800 BC – a type of late Stone Age grave that's very rare around Lake Mälaren.
Albykistan: Albykistan, a Stone Age stone cist
Alelyckan, området alldeles intill, har: The name of Alelyckan, right beside us, comes from alder trees – or perhaps ale, a stand of alders – and lycka, an enclosed field. For a long time the name was linked to the waterworks, where water from the Göta älv river has been turned into drinking water since 1894. In 1990 the street called Alelyckan was renamed Alelyckegatan to avoid confusion.
Alelyckans sportcenter: Alelyckans sportcenter, the Alelyckan sports centre
Alelyckans sportcenter, alldeles intill,: Alelyckans sportcenter, right next to us, began with a daily walk. Every day, Vilhelm Björk walked past the empty water basins at Alelyckan – and one day he had an idea. In 1974 he and Alva Björk founded the sports centre, which now has tennis and squash courts, 25 badminton courts and a floorball hall where you can play pickleball too.
All inredning är av furu, ritad av arkit: All the fittings are in pine, designed by the architect himself. A tall pine cross on the chancel wall is the only altar decoration. From the ceiling hangs a round chandelier five metres across, with twelve clusters of six lamps.
Alla gator i Fruängen är uppkallade efte: Every street in Fruängen is named after a famous Swedish woman, such as Elsa Beskow, Ellen Key and Karin Boye. The blocks, meanwhile, got names like Hårnätet (the Hairnet), Handväskan (the Handbag) and Amorbågen (Cupid's Bow).
Alldeles i närheten ligger Långnäs gård,: Close by is Långnäs gård, which grew out of a larger farm from the mid-14th century and is still privately owned. The Sjövik neighbourhood, with villas and linked terraced houses, sits on a strip of shoreline along Kyrkviken bay that was left out of the Långängen-Elfvik nature reserve, and it borders the Skogshem and Wijk conference centres.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Sköndalsskola: Close by is Sköndalsskolan, a school designed by Cyrillus Johansson and opened in 1953. On Mazarinvägen, architects lived in houses of their own design. Eskil Sundahl built Villa Sundahl as his home, and the husband-and-wife team Hanna and Roy Victorson lived in one of their Sköndal villas. The couple also designed the flower kiosk at the northern entrance to Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Slagsta gård,: Just nearby is Slagsta gård, a historic manor and former estate. Down by Lake Mälaren, Slagstabadet is an inviting place for a swim. It was laid out in the early 1970s on the site of one of Slagsta's two old brickworks, and you can still spot terraces and house foundations in the woods. The Hallunda heritage trail also passes a rock carving, discovered in 1971 and protected as an ancient monument.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Vallhamra ish: Just round the corner is Vallhamra ice rink, home of the Partille HK hockey club. The rink was laid out in 1969, and in September 1981 it got a roof and walls and became an indoor arena. It holds around 300 spectators, and as well as ice hockey, the ice is used for figure skating and public skating sessions. Both the hockey club and the figure skating club have their clubrooms here.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Vantörs kyrka: Close by is Vantör Church, the parish church of Vantör. The name has a long history: the medieval parish of Vantör had a church that, after a fire in the 1400s, became known as Brännkyrka, the Burnt Church. Högdalen's centre also used to have a cinema, the Rondo, which opened in January 1961 and showed films until May 1983.
Alldeles i närheten låg Hundra, ett av S: Right nearby stood Hundra, one of Salem's three crofts for soldier-sailors. It was number 100 – 'hundra' in Swedish – hence the name, and the sailor who lived here was supported by the farms of his district in return for serving in the navy and coastal defence. The neighbouring croft, Skyttorp, was named after a marksman, a 'skytt', who once lived there. It was one of the few cottages in the Stockholm area with its own separate kitchen building, a custom from southern Sweden.
Alldeles i närheten låg Härlanda fängels: Very close by was Härlanda prison, originally Härlanda Central Prison, which was in use from 1907 to 1997. It was designed by the royal architect Gustaf Lindgren and has been a listed building since 1993, and since 2011 the area has been called Härlanda park. The neighbourhood also had a cinema, the Saga, which became a grocery shop after it closed.
Alldeles i närheten låg Tuna gård, en gå: Close by was Tuna, a farm dating back to the Middle Ages, next to what is now Hågelbyleden road. A little further on you can travel even further back in time at Hogslaby, a reconstructed Iron Age village at Hågelby farm. Every child in the municipality gets to spend a day there living in the Iron Age, cooking and working in the smithy. Many of the buildings at Hågelby itself were put up on the initiative of the telephone pioneer Lars Magnus Ericsson.
Alldeles i närheten låg torpet Lugnet, b: Close by stood the croft Lugnet, built in 1771 and pulled down in 1962. A little way from here, Saltvägen winds through the part of Hökarängen nicknamed Kryddhyllan, the Spice Rack, and at Saltvägen 14 the troubadour Cornelis Vreeswijk once lived. Along Lingvägen is Farsta fire station, opened in October 1956.
Alldeles i närheten står Helige kung Ste: Close by stands the Church of Holy King Stefan Dečanski, Gothenburg's Serbian Orthodox church. It's dedicated to Stefan Uroš III Dečanski, King of Serbia from 1321 to 1331 and founder of the Visoki Dečani monastery in Kosovo – today a World Heritage Site on UNESCO's endangered list. Kortedala, all around you, was Gothenburg's first suburb, built in the 1950s.
Alldeles i närheten står Villa Brännugne: Right nearby stands Villa Brännugnen, a private home designed by Gert Wingårdh, with a restaurant that's open to the public. It won Huddinge's architecture award in 2019. A little further off, the Ågestabron bridge crosses Lake Magelungen with one foot in Stockholm and the other in Huddinge – roughly half of it lies in each municipality.
Alldeles intill aulan ligger byggnadsmin: Right next to the auditorium stands Gården Stenbrottet, a listed building built in 1771 by the merchant and baker Joakim Sasse. Now known as Gammelgården, it has gone from lunch restaurant to offices and meeting rooms.
Alldeles intill breder Sisjöns industrio: Right beside us is the Sisjön industrial area, just south of the Söderleden road. It was built in the 1960s for workshops and industry, but over the years it has become a retail park, where these days there's more shopping than welding. Not far away, in Askim's northern cemetery, lies what's known as the privateer's grave – said to be the resting place of a privateer captain who sailed for Lars Gathenhielm.
Alldeles intill ligger Hovgårdsvallen, f: Right next to us is Hovgårdsvallen, the football ground in Björlanda where IK Zenith play their home games. It goes by several names – if someone mentions Hovgården or Zenithgården, they mean the very same pitch. Perhaps having three names is an advantage when the away team is trying to find it?
Alldeles intill ligger Kungliga tennisha: Right next door is Kungliga tennishallen, the Royal Tennis Hall, designed by Sture Frölén and opened in 1943. The Stockholm Open has been played here ever since the first tournament in 1969, with one exception: from 1989 to 1994 it moved to the Globe arena. In 2020, the year of the pandemic, it was cancelled altogether.
Alldeles intill ligger Livgardets Kavall: Right next to us is the Life Guards' Cavalry Barracks, known as Kavkas, built between 1893 and 1898 to designs by Erik Josephson. Its stables are still home to the horses of the mounted royal guard and the mounted police. A little further on is Armfeltsgatan, probably named after one of two gentlemen called Armfeldt – though neither had much to do with this area. That's where you'll find Peter Celsing's Olaus Petri Church from 1959.
Alldeles intill ligger Norra begravnings: Right next to us is Norra begravningsplatsen, the Northern Cemetery, one of the largest in Sweden, with paths named Aftonstjärnans väg, Sommarvindsvägen and Solregnsvägen – Evening Star Way, Summer Wind Road and Sun Shower Road. A little further on is Solna kyrkby, the old church village, where Solna Church dates back to the 1100s and the rectory to the 1720s. Along Solna kyrkväg there's also a row of terraced houses designed by Dag Ribbing, counted among Solna's architectural gems.
Alldeles intill ligger Nya Solevi, ett s: Right beside us is Nya Solevi, a solar farm known as Säve Solcellspark while it was being built. It went up remarkably fast: construction began on 11 September 2018, and the park opened on 14 December that same year. It's designed to produce around 5.5 gigawatt hours of electricity a year. Further on is Säve Airport, where these days only police and rescue service helicopters fly.
Alldeles intill ligger Pepparred, ett av: Right next to us is Pepparred, one of Sweden's really old nature reserves, protected since as long ago as 1925. It covers just 3.5 hectares of old wooded pasture with oak, ash and other broadleaf trees, on a slope between the E6 motorway and the houses south of Pepparred farm, which gave the reserve its name.
Alldeles intill ligger Röda Korsets Högs: Right next door is the Swedish Red Cross University, Sweden's oldest non-religious nursing school. It was founded in 1867 by Emmy Rappe, who had trained in London under none other than Florence Nightingale. The school began in Uppsala and spent many years at Sabbatsberg Hospital before ending up here. A short way off is Flemingsberg church, consecrated in 1976.
Alldeles intill ligger Skrubbatriangeln,: Right beside us is Skrubbatriangeln, also called Skrubba Energicentrum, an industrial area that opened in 1987 and is named after its roughly triangular layout. The Skrubba district borders Tyresö and Lake Drevviken, where the Strandkyrkogården cemetery is just a short distance from here.
Alldeles intill ligger Täby Racketcenter: Right next to us is Täby Racketcenter, with twelve badminton courts, four squash courts, table tennis tables and a gym. A short walk away is Viggbyholm station on the Roslagsbanan railway, where the old station building is no longer needed for the trains and has become a café. The E18 and the railway split Viggbyholm into three parts: Sjösidan, Stationssidan and Rönningesjösidan – the lake side, the station side and the Lake Rönningesjön side.
Alldeles intill ligger Viksjö gård, en h: Right next door is Viksjö gård, a manor house and former noble estate that was owned in the 17th century by the Skytte family, among others. It stands on a rise, and modern Viksjö has spread out across its old fields. A little further off, in Jakobsberg, Järfällabadet opened in 2018. It replaced the old swimming baths from 1971, which had a 48-metre water slide.
Alldeles intill ligger Västra Frölunda k: Right next door is Västra Frölunda cemetery, which dates back to the Middle Ages. The old Västra Frölunda church stood here until it was pulled down in the 1860s, and the wall still has iron rings where churchgoers once tethered their horses. A gravestone inscribed Anno 1728 commemorates Olof Claeson, chief inspector at the Klippan customs station.
Alldeles intill ligger småorten Draget,: Right next door is the little village of Draget, on Vällingevägen north-west of Lake Aspen. A bit further on is its neighbour, Fiskarhagen, which spreads out along Sankt Botvids väg between Lake Aspen and Lake Bornsjön. The road is part of the historic Göta landsväg, the old highway to the south – so people have been passing through here for a very long time.
Alldeles intill ligger Örvallen, Sverige: Right beside us is Örvallen, Sweden's national baseball stadium and the only internationally approved baseball ground in the country. It was finished in 2009 for the men's World Championship. The attendance record – 2,091 spectators – was set at the World Championship match between Canada and Sweden, which Canada won by a crushing 19 to 1. The home team is Sundbyberg Heat.
Alldeles intill lägger Kornhalls färja t: Right here is where the Kornhall ferry comes in – a cable ferry crossing the Nordre älv river to Kornhall in Kungälv municipality. The crossing began in 1850 and was run by private contractors until 1945, when the Swedish Road Administration took over. The shortcut to Gothenburg became so popular that the first motorised ferry arrived in 1951. Today the route is served by M/S Gerd.
Alldeles intill låg torpet Månskär, som: Right next to us stood Månskär, a croft built when the new main road from Hornstull to Fittja was finished in 1673. Several crofts sprang up along the new road, Sadelmakartorp among them, which became a schoolhouse after 1860. Today the area is dominated by Kungens kurva, which together with Skärholmen centrum is counted as the largest shopping destination in the Nordic countries.
Alldeles intill rinner Gudöån, som förbi: Right beside us flows the Gudöån stream, linking Lake Drevviken with Lake Långsjön, and the middle of the stream marks the boundary between Haninge and Tyresö. Along the south bank you can see traces of a trade that has all but vanished: laundering. More well-preserved drying barns survive here than anywhere else in the county, reminders of the days when taking in washing was an important income for smallholders. These days, people come here to paddle a kayak instead.
Alldeles intill stod Stuvsta gårds kvarn: Right beside us stood the Stuvsta gård windmill, up on Kvarnberget – Mill Hill – which is how the Kvarnbergsplan area got its name. A little further on, outside Huddinge's municipal hall, is Bror Hjorth's life-size bronze Girl with a Fruit Basket from 1951, her basket brimming with apples. It was paid for with money left over after the council chamber had been decorated with a large fresco by Sven “X:et” Erixson.
Alldeles intill står Breviks kyrka, förs: Right beside us is Brevik Church, a parish church in Lidingö parish. A short walk away is Abeniuska villan, the Abenius Villa, also known as Ljungströmshof, built in 1910 for Allan Abenius to designs by Ferdinand Boberg and Bror Almquist. The Stockholm County Museum rates the house as culturally and historically irreplaceable.
Alldeles intill står Bräcke soldattorp f: Right next door is Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft from the 1830s that has been a local history museum since 1965. From 1889 it was home to the soldier Sven Olof Emanuelsson Björk. The croft has moved, too – it used to stand north of the village of Bräcke. It's no bigger than one room, a kitchen and a hallway: a modest home for a soldier.
Alldeles intill står Kistastenen, runste: Right next door, at Kista gård, stands the Kista Stone, runestone U 75. More runes have turned up here too: two fragments of Viking Age runestones were built into a cellar wall in Kista for many years before being taken out in 1938. They're now in the Swedish History Museum. A little further away you can see Kista fire station from 1980, with its distinctive concrete training tower.
Alldeles intill står Stensjökyrkan, och: Right beside us is Stensjökyrkan, the Stensjö church, and a couple of hundred metres away, by Lake Stensjön, stood Mustad's margarine factory, which ran from 1897 to 1960. The lake gave its name to both the church and Stensjön parish, which also includes Fågelbergskyrkan. Mölndal's upper station on the Borås line wasn't far from here either.
Alldeles intill står Västra Frölunda kyr: Right beside us is Västra Frölunda church, the parish church of the old parish of Västra Frölunda. The parish covered just over 32 square kilometres and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1945. Not far from here is something much newer: the Järnbrott bus depot, built purely for all-electric buses.
Alldeles intill, i Hagaparken vid Uppsal: Right nearby, in Haga Park on Uppsalavägen, is Haga tingshus, the old courthouse, where the Södra Roslag district court sat right up until the 1950s. A little further on rises the Wenner-Gren Center, the first steel-framed high-rise in Sweden and, when it was completed, the tallest steel-framed building in Europe.
Alldeles intill, i hörnet av Litteraturg: Right next to us, on the corner of Litteraturgatan and Skälltorpsvägen, is Friedländerska kyrkogården, the Friedländer cemetery. With just over twenty graves it's the smallest cemetery in Gothenburg – and it's privately owned, too. It belongs to Bäckebols gård, a manor house a little way off, and together with the manor it has been declared a listed site.
Alldeles intill, vid Norra Kungsvägen, s: Right beside us on Norra Kungsvägen is part of a runestone, Uppland runic inscription 172. It's one of only two runic inscriptions found on Lidingö – the other turned up in 1984 near Bo gård. A little further away is Villa Backen, designed by Ivar Tengbom for August and Célie Brunius and completed in 1910.
Alldeles vid Bällsta bro, i hörnet av Bä: Right by Bällsta bro, the bridge on the corner of Bällstavägen and Mariehällsvägen, is Mariehälls gård. It's a manor house that the Stockholm City Museum has marked in blue on its map for its exceptional historical value. Built in 1790, it's named after Maria Elisabeth Wetterberg, wife of the tanner Melchior Eichhorn. The portico looks a lot like the stern of a ship, which is probably where the legend comes from that the famous shipbuilder af Chapman built the house.
Allmänna gränd ligger på Djurgården, mit: Allmänna gränd is on Djurgården, halfway between Gröna Lund and the Vasa Museum. The amusement park, the museums and Skansen are all just a few minutes' walk away.
Allmänna vägen var landsvägen västerut m: Allmänna vägen, 'the Public Road', was once the country road heading west to Klippan. It was Majorna's main street until Karl Johansgatan was built in 1882. A devastating fire swept along the street in 1862, and that same year the villa at Åhmanssonska gården, the Åhmansson estate, was built. In 1919 Gothenburg's first vocational school opened there.
Allum, köpcentret ett stenkast bort, är: Allum, the shopping centre a stone's throw away, really is big: 50,000 square metres, around 100 shops and about 1,700 parking spaces. Part of the building stretches right over the E20 motorway, with a bus station beneath the passage. Partille Church is close by too, right in the middle of the town centre.
Allébron ser ut som en tunn skiva över S: Allébron looks like a thin slab laid across the Sickla canal. Built in 2000, it carries pedestrians, cars and Tvärbanan light rail trams all on the same deck. The bridge, in Hammarby sjöstad, was designed by Rundquist Arkitekter and carries Lugnets allé between Sickla udde and Sickla kaj.
Allébron är en kontinuerlig balkbro av s: Allébron is a continuous steel girder bridge designed by Rundquist Arkitekter. It links Lugnets allé between Sickla udde and Sickla kaj.
Alléparken, där Västerled möter Alviksvä: Alléparken – 'the Avenue Park' – where Västerled meets Alviksvägen, was named in 1932. In 1944 the writer Gösta Langenfelt called the name a monstrosity, since there was neither a park nor an avenue in sight. But it later turned out he was wrong: there really had been an avenue, leading to the croft of Asplund, and some of its trees are still standing today.
Alphyddans hus har fasader i rött tegel: Alphyddan's buildings have red-brick façades with white balcony fronts and bay windows. Some 700 flats were built here in five tower blocks of 13–15 storeys and eight lower slab blocks. The garages for 500 cars soon proved far too small.
Altaret, dopfunten och predikstolen av l: The altar, font and pulpit, all in pale wood, had interchangeable panels in the liturgical colours of the church year. The altarpiece consisted of three square wall hangings, the middle one showing the Last Supper.
Altaret, dopfunten och predikstolen hade: The altar, font and pulpit had interchangeable panels in the liturgical colours of the church year. After the church was deconsecrated, the furnishings worth keeping went to other churches in Angered.
Altaret, dopfunten och predikstolen var: The altar, font and pulpit were made of pale wood, with interchangeable panels in the liturgical colours of the church year. After the church was deconsecrated, the furnishings worth preserving were moved to other churches in Angered parish.
Altarskåpet är en träsniden triptyk av s: The altarpiece is a carved wooden triptych made by the sculptor Hjalmar Ekberg in 1973. It shows Christ surrounded by people in all walks of life. Ekberg also carved the church's statue of the Virgin Mary.
Altartavlan av Arvid Bryth har fyra bibl: Arvid Bryth's altarpiece shows four biblical scenes carved in wood. The triumphal crucifix was carved by one of the parish's own clergy, the curate Jan Merje.
Altartavlan i Flemingsbergs kyrka är sku: The altarpiece in Flemingsberg church was carved in pine by Per Nilsson-Öst. It shows the disciples on the Sea of Tiberias, barely able to haul in their nets for all the fish, while Christ stands on the shore. The church bell weighs 500 kilos and was cast in Sigtuna.
Altartorp finns med i husförhörslängdern: Altartorp has appeared in the parish registers as a croft belonging to the Vårby manor since 1740. The last crofter, Anders E. Nyström, moved in in 1842 with his wife Maria Christina. According to the priest’s notes, both could ‘read reasonably well’. Today the croft is a private home.
Altartorp kan vara ett av traktens äldst: Altartorp may be one of the oldest crofts round here, thought to date all the way back to 1540. According to local tradition, its name – Altaret, 'the altar' – comes from a place of prayer where soldiers held services before marching off to the battlefields of Europe. A stone's throw away runs Smista allé, a street known for the sheer number of car dealers that have set up shop along it.
Altorps station öppnade 1910, när tågen: Altorp station opened in 1910, when trains started running here from Ösby. The line was extended to Lahäll in 1928 and on to Näsbypark in 1937. Another branch was less fortunate: in 1912 the track was extended from Eddavägen to Svalnäs, but the estate there was never developed as planned, and the line closed as early as 1934. In the nearby cemetery stands Altorp chapel, where services are held over All Saints' weekend.
Alvik har fått sitt namn efter torpet Ah: Alvik is named after the croft Ahlwijken, first mentioned in the land register of 1720. It stood just north-west of today's metro station. By the time the croft moved in 1789, its old site had apparently become an inn.
Alvik är en knutpunkt där Tvärbanan och: Alvik is an interchange where the Tvärbanan and Nockebybanan light rail lines meet the metro. From here you can head out to Bromma, with its villa neighbourhoods and the shores of Lake Mälaren.
Alviks Torn fick bära titeln Västerorts: Alviks Torn, the Alvik Tower, was briefly the tallest residential building in Stockholm's western suburbs. It opened in December 2014 – 18 storeys and 56.7 metres high – but by 2015 Kista Torn had already taken the record. There's sporting history in the neighbourhood too: from 1911 to 1935 this was the site of Tranebergs IP, a sports ground nicknamed Tranan, the Crane, leased by Djurgårdens IF before the club moved to Stockholm Olympic Stadium.
Alviks gårds huvudbyggnad revs 1923. Kva: The main house of Alvik farm was demolished in 1923. All that's left is the farm foreman's house, an early 19th-century double cottage that has served as farmhands' quarters and a storehouse. Today it's used for art and crafts.
Alviks rättarbostad: Alviks rättarbostad, the old farm foreman's house in Alvik
Ambassadören som aldrig flyttade in: The ambassador who never moved in
Ambitionen var att bygga det största sju: The plan was to build the largest hospital in northern Europe here, and in 1965 all the allotment cottages were given notice. But in 1970 the project was shelved when the county council chose to invest in Huddinge Hospital instead. What got built was a long-term care hospital on a quarter of the site.
Andalen, en bit härifrån, är liksom fler: Andalen, a short way from here, is one of several old summer-cottage areas around Torslanda that have grown into neighbourhoods of year-round homes. The residents look after a lot themselves: there's a road association, a private bathing spot run by Andals Badförening and a small harbour run by the local boat club, Andalens Båtförening.
Anders Celsius kusin Olof Celsius den yn: Anders Celsius's cousin, Olof Celsius the Younger, was vicar of Kungsholmen parish for eight years, so it's sometimes claimed the street is named after him. But neighbouring Polhemsgatan and Wargentinsgatan are also named after scientists, so it's most likely the astronomer who's meant.
Anders Sandrew hette officiellt Anders A: The film producer Anders Sandrew was officially still called Anders Andersson when he bought the plot in 1911. He had his office and studio up in the attic but lived in the house only briefly. Today Skeppar Karls salong holds its concerts at Baldersgatan 7B.
Andra gator har fått namn ur fornnordisk: Other streets are named after characters from Old Norse heroic tales, mainly the Sigurd saga and the poems of the Edda. So you can walk along Sigurdsvägen, Brynhildsvägen, Gudrunsvägen and Kung Atles väg.
Andvätt och Gärdar lät rista runorna eft: Andvätt and Gärdar had the runes carved in memory of their father Sven, and Kättilvi in memory of her husband. The carving is so deep and even that it’s still clearly visible, even though it hasn’t been painted in for a long time.
Angered arena har fler badvakter än andr: Angered Arena has more lifeguards than other swimming baths. It also has an electronic system that detects anyone lying motionless in the pool and raises the alarm.
Angered byggdes på 1970-talet och är i d: Angered was built in the 1970s and is now one of Gothenburg's most international districts. It's home to the Blå Stället culture house, and all around are wide stretches of countryside with lakes and forest.
Angered har fått namn efter kyrkbyn, som: Angered is named after its church village, recorded in 1415 as Awngaryd. The name may come from the personal name Agund and the word ‘ryd’, a clearing. Another theory is that it means ‘the people who live by the pool of water’.
Angered planerades för över 100 000 invå: Angered was planned for more than 100,000 residents and built from south to north: Hjällbo in 1966, Hammarkullen in 1968 and Gårdsten in 1969. Then the expansion stalled, leaving the estates as isolated islands in the countryside. Angereds Centrum didn't arrive until 1978.
Angered är en stadsdel på drygt 2 000 he: Angered is a district of just over 2,000 hectares, bordered by the Göta älv river to the west and by Ale and Lerum to the north and east. Until 2015 it counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area, but it now forms an urban area of its own, North-eastern Gothenburg. A short way off is Gunnared cemetery, opened in 2003.
Angereds teater startade 1978, och i ens: Angered Theatre opened in 1978, and Sven Wollter was among its company. Its most celebrated production was Brecht’s ‘Life of Galileo’, staged in 1980 as ‘Jorden rör sig!’ (‘The Earth Moves!’), directed by Peter Oskarson with Wollter in the title role.
Anläggningen byggdes 1913–1916 som drift: The complex was built in 1913–1916 as a maintenance works for the Swedish State Railways. Today the Hagalund depot is the largest train maintenance depot in northern Europe, with a wheel lathe, a train wash and a listed old carriage shed, among other things.
Anläggningen vreds efter de gamla tegarn: The complex was angled to follow the old strips of farmland, and the buildings were designed to look like simple farm buildings with black timber façades. The mosaic floor of the square is a map of the area, based on one from 1861.
Anne Hedmark var lärare på skolan och go: Anne Hedmark taught at the school and was a close friend of the Milles family. She later gave up teaching to become hostess, secretary and curator at Millesgården, the sculptor Carl Milles’s home, and lived there until 1986 in the house that bears her name.
Annedal, Landala, Burås, Eriksberg, Galg: Annedal, Landala, Burås, Eriksberg, Galgekrogen, Geteberget and Gibraltar were all once part of Krokslätt.
Annelund var från början ett torp under: Annelund started out as a croft under Lilla Frösunda. The wholesaler Eric Giers leased it as a summer retreat in 1766–1777 and probably rebuilt it as a small manor house. It most likely got the name Annelund from his wife, Anna Maria Brandel.
Antik & Kuriosa lockade: Antiques and curiosities drew the crowds
Anundsvägen, en villagata en kort promen: Anundsvägen, a residential street a short walk from here, is famous above all for one thing: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom paid a visit in the 1950s. That was around the time Blackeberg itself was growing up – as late as the 1940s, the area was mostly forest and rock. The Kaskad cinema on Blackebergsplan has been here since 1957.
Apelsinlunden har fått sitt folkliga nam: Apelsinlunden, the Orange Grove, got its nickname from the orange-red colours of its buildings. The estate was built in 1967, during the Million Programme housing drive, to designs by Lars Bryde, and it's one of Stockholm's largest areas of low-rise tower blocks. A little further on, Götalandsviadukten crosses the tracks at Älvsjö station, where an early concrete arch bridge was built around 1910.
Apotekaren med kortvågssändare: The pharmacist with a shortwave radio
Apoteket Korpen flyttade hit och öppnade: Apoteket Korpen, the Raven pharmacy, moved here and opened in 1927. The pharmacist, John Fredrik Karlsson, printed the shop's leaflets in the basement and was a keen radio ham, with a shortwave transmitter of around 100 watts up in the attic.
Apotekshusets ursprungliga inredning är: The original interior of the Apotekshuset, the pharmacy house, is the oldest surviving one in Sweden. Today you can see it in the Kronan pharmacy at Skansen, together with fittings from Carl Wilhelm Scheele's pharmacy in Köping. Gustav III himself may have been the architect of the building.
Arbetarbostad i krigets bostadsbrist: Workers' housing in a wartime shortage
Arbetarrörelsens arkiv och bibliotek: The Labour Movement Archives and Library
Arbetarrörelsens torg är fullt av minnen: The labour movement's square is full of memories. The Branting Monument was commissioned from Carl Eldh back in 1935 but not unveiled until 1952, and it became his largest and last completed work. Here too is the Olof Palme memorial 'Mitt hjärta i världen' ('My Heart in the World'). LO-borgen, designed by Ferdinand Boberg in 1899, was originally built for a timber merchant and has been the headquarters of LO, the Swedish Trade Union Confederation, since 1926.

This square belongs to the labour movement, and it's full of memories. Carl Eldh was commissioned to make the Branting Monument as early as 1935, but it wasn't unveiled until 1952, becoming his largest and last completed work. You'll also find the Olof Palme memorial here, Mitt hjärta i världen, 'My Heart in the World'. LO-borgen, the headquarters of the trade union confederation, was designed by Ferdinand Boberg in 1899 and originally built for a timber merchant. And Maskrosbollen, the Dandelion fountain made for LO's centenary, has since moved to Nacka.
Arenan invigdes med operan Aida med Birg: The arena opened in 1971 with the opera Aida, starring Birgit Nilsson. The following year 72,000 people saw the musical Jesus Christ Superstar over five days, with Agnetha Fältskog as Mary Magdalene.
Arenan är på cirka 45 300 kvadratmeter f: The arena covers some 45,300 square metres over seven floors. It houses a full-size football pitch, sports halls, gyms, a sports injury clinic, a sports hotel and even a primary school and a sports-focused upper secondary school. It was designed by OkiDoki! Arkitekter.
Arenan är på cirka 45 300 kvadratmeter i: The arena covers around 45,300 square metres over seven storeys and was designed by OkiDoki! Arkitekter. It cost 800 million kronor, and alongside a ski track and a football pitch it houses a sports hotel, an injury clinic, a primary school and a sports-focused upper secondary school.
Arendal hör tillsammans med Härröd och S: Together with Härröd and Syrhåla, Arendal belongs to Lundby parish, and the three are known as Lundby's outer farmsteads. The boundaries are oddly drawn, leaving the area as an enclave entirely cut off from its home parish.
Together with Härröd and Syrhåla, Arendal belongs to Lundby parish. Thanks to a curious quirk in the boundaries, the area forms an enclave, completely cut off from the rest of its parish.
Arendal är stort men nästan folktomt: på: Arendal is big but almost empty: in 2012 just 90 people lived on its 890 hectares. The Arendal shipyard was here from 1963 to 1989. Today it's a large logistics and industrial area, home to Volvo Buses' headquarters and development department, among others, as well as factories for several of Volvo's suppliers.
Arendal, Härröd och Syrhåla hör till Lun: Arendal, Härröd and Syrhåla belong to Lundby parish and are known collectively as Lundby's outer farmsteads. Thanks to some odd boundary drawing, they form an enclave entirely cut off from their home parish.
Arendals Idrotts-Klubb, förkortat AIK, s: In the 1890s, Arendals Idrotts-Klubb (AIK for short) founded a golf club and laid out a course, both among the first in Sweden. Viktor H. Setterberg created an 18-hole course measuring 1,692 metres at Skalebackarna. During the First World War the course was ploughed up for farming.
Arkenterminalen ska ha sju järnvägsspår,: The Arken terminal is to have seven rail tracks, 3,360 metres of track in all, on a 65,000-square-metre site. Fully built, it is planned to handle 70,000 semi-trailers a year, with ten trains a day.
Arkipelag på ruinmotorvägen: An archipelago on the ruined motorway
Arkitekten Arvid Stille ritade 1918 en l: In 1918 the architect Arvid Stille designed a small artificial lake, Fullerstasjön, to collect floodwater, but it was never dug. The ground was soggy enough anyway: the centre was built on an old lake bed and had to be shored up with piles after it began to subside badly.
Arkitekten Arvid Stilles stadsplan från: The architect Arvid Stille's town plan of 1918 covered 208 plots, but it too was never fully carried out. The small artificial lake Fullerstasjön, meant to collect water during floods, was never dug, for example.
Arkitekten Bo Grefberg föreslog att en g: The architect Bo Grefberg proposed that a dilapidated old barn be pulled down and replaced by a church of the same size. The red-painted wooden church was consecrated in autumn 1984 but only got the name Sätraängskyrkan at its tenth anniversary. The bell tower is older, from 1976, and was paid for with voluntary donations.
Arkitekten Erik Stark läste in kärnfysik: The architect Erik Stark studied nuclear physics so he could design the reactor hall. The walls were made of iron-ore concrete 50–60 centimetres thick, topped by a pool. According to Stark, this solution put Sweden ahead of the US in safety design.
Arkitekten Harald Thafvelin inspirerades: The architect Harald Thafvelin drew inspiration from Greek culture. The sturdy pillars in the nave resemble Greek columns with capitals, though simplified and cast in concrete. The ceiling is divided into pyramid-shaped panels, and outside every twelfth course of brick is laid in a pattern to create a shadow effect.
Arkitekten Hjalmar Klemming såg Kärrtorp: The architect Hjalmar Klemming saw Kärrtorp as a warm-up for Svenska Bostäder's next big project, Vällingby. The buildings were to form a wall against the outside world and free up large green spaces for play. Klemming himself moved into the twelfth floor of one of the tower blocks.
Arkitekten Jacob Gate ritade 1909 både V: In 1909 the architect Jacob Gate designed both Villa Höganloft, in Old Norse style – it has since been a café, a restaurant and a Home Guard building – and the Trisshusen, an early take on terraced housing. A stone's throw away are the Canada Houses, thought to be among the very first terraced houses in Sweden. The area also has Bo kvarn, a windmill from 1816 and one of the oldest in the Stockholm area still standing where it was built.
Arkitekten Lars Bryde ritade 34 kubiska: Architect Lars Bryde designed 34 cube-shaped, three-storey houses with flat roofs. The facades came in three shades: reddish brown in Klacklappen, orange in Pliggen and yellow in Skohornet. The area was made car-free, and the houses are now marked by the City Museum as being of cultural-historical value.
Arkitekten Lolle Lundquist hade ett affä: The architect Lolle Lundquist had a shopping centre in Minneapolis in mind. When the mall was completed in 1968, it was the first glass-roofed shopping centre in northern Europe.
Arkitekten Ralph Erskine, som själv bodd: The architect Ralph Erskine, who lived on Lovön himself, dreamed of a lakeside town on Lake Mälaren at Tappström, and Ekerö centrum is what came of it. The area was finished in 1991, and Erskine was prouder of this project than any other: it works as a complete community, he said in an interview, and that was something he probably hadn't managed anywhere else. Keep an eye out for the centre's landmark, a dot more than twenty metres tall.
Arkitekten som aldrig flyttade in: The architect who never moved in
Arkitekttävlingen om kommunalhuset gav 4: The architectural competition for the municipal offices drew 43 entries. Sture Frölén won with his proposal "Perhaps", praised for its restrained façades. The war delayed construction, and the building was completed in 1948.
Arkitekturen i bostadsområdet Gretas bac: A short walk from here, on Gamla Stockholmsvägen, is the Gretas backe housing area, whose architecture won Huddinge's building award in 2017 – an award that had only just been launched. It's part of Glömsta, a former noble estate that is now a residential area to the south, east and north of Lake Gömmaren.
Arkivet grundades i juli 1902 på initiat: The archive was founded in July 1902 at the initiative of Oscar Borge, who was also a distinguished marine biologist. The library was actually ten years older than the archive, but it wasn’t until 2001 that both were officially included in the name.
Artillerigården har använts för artiller: Artillerigården, the Artillery Yard, has served the army's gunners since the 1640s, and today it's home to Armémuseum, the Army Museum. Hidden beneath the yard are two air-raid shelters from the Second World War, which are sometimes opened for tours. Round the corner at Artillerigatan 14 was Gastrologik, a Michelin-starred restaurant with no menu – the chefs simply decided what you'd eat. Since 2024 the restaurant ergo has taken over the premises.
Arton höghus på rad: Eighteen tower blocks in a row
Askarna mitt i bussterminalen: Ash trees in the bus terminal
Askim ligger vid Askimsfjorden, en del a: Askim lies on Askimsfjorden, an arm of the Kattegat, in hilly country where the villas cluster close to the coast. The name is often pronounced 'Ash-im'. In 1975 the built-up area of Askim merged with Gothenburg's, and today the district counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. Askims torg, the local square, is a short walk away.
Askim uttalas ['aʃim]. Namnet skrevs Ask: Askim is pronounced ['aʃim]. In 1489 the name was written Askym. The ending -hem means a dwelling or farm, while the first part contains the ash tree.
Askim uttalas ”Ashim”, med ett sje-ljud,: Askim is pronounced ‘Ashim’, with a ‘sh’ sound – which tends to catch visitors out. The parish of Askim goes back to the Middle Ages and lies in the southern part of Gothenburg municipality. A short way from here is the coastal area of Skintebo, which was farmland until the early 1970s.
Askims gamla stenkyrka från 1200-talet b: Askim's old 13th-century stone church burned down in the middle of a service on 12 November 1876. The church bells were saved, and a memorial stone now marks where it stood.
Askims kyrka ligger inom promenadavstånd: Askim church is within walking distance. A little further on is Sisjön, a lake in the Sandsjöbacka nature reserve that's good for swimming and fishing, with both perch and pike. Curiously, the municipal border between Gothenburg and Mölndal runs straight through the middle of the lake, and there's a hiking trail all the way round.
Askims kyrka står bara ett par hundra me: Askim Church is just a couple of hundred metres away. It's the parish church for a parish stretching along the coast south of Gothenburg, which became part of Gothenburg municipality in 1974. At the marina in Hovås there's also a sea rescue station. Its first boat, in 1983, was the former pilot boat Alice Olsson.
Askims kyrka, uttalas ”Ashim”, ligger al: Right next door is Askim Church – pronounced 'Ashim'. Its parish is large, almost 37 square kilometres, and in 1974 it became part of Gothenburg municipality. Within the parish lie parts of Billdal, Gundal and Högås, the town of Hovås and, of course, the parish church itself.
Askims norra kyrkogård, bara några minut: Askim's northern cemetery, just a few minutes away, hides an intriguing secret. What's known as the privateer's grave is said to be the resting place of a privateer captain who sailed under Lars Gathenhielm. The cemetery dates back to the Middle Ages, and its older part is enclosed by a stone wall with two lychgates.
Askims socken har vuxit rejält. Den 31 d: Askim parish has grown enormously. On 31 December 1888 it had 1,352 inhabitants; by 2000 the figure had risen to 21,434. The parish belonged to Askim hundred, an old administrative district, and became part of Gothenburg municipality in 1974. The parish church, Askim Church, is a short walk from here – and by the way, the name is pronounced 'Ash-im'.
Askimsbadet öppnade provisoriskt 1927 oc: Askimsbadet opened on a trial basis in 1927 and was run by the city from 1928. It once had changing huts, a first-aid hut and a café, and for many years Doktor Allard's 'bathing children' came here on holiday. In 1965 a 25-metre pool was built for swimming lessons.
Askimsbadet öppnades provisoriskt av Sär: Askimsbadet beach was opened on a trial basis by the Säröbanan railway in 1927, and the city took it over the following year. In its heyday it had changing huts, a first-aid hut, room for 300 tents and 540 little cabins. In winter, the pool built in 1965 doubled as a cold plunge for the sauna.
Aspen lades ner redan efter nio år, i ma: The Aspen cinema closed after just nine years, in May 1961. In the 1970s and 80s the Spårvägen table tennis club took over the premises as a training hall, and J-O Waldner was among the players who trained here regularly.
Asperö är en liten ö i Göteborgs södra s: Asperö is a small island in Gothenburg's southern archipelago with just over four hundred year-round residents. Neighbouring Rivö is uninhabited, but the Asperö islanders' free-roaming sheep and horses graze there among the foundations of huts from the old herring booms and two abandoned graveyards. On Brännö next door lies the songwriter Lasse Dahlquist, in a churchyard whose memorial grove is the smallest in Gothenburg.
Asplund, Stadshuset och stjärnhusen: Asplund, City Hall and the star houses
Aspnässkolan var Järfälla sockens första: Aspnässkolan was the first school in Järfälla parish. It opened in 1846 in a manor house at the Aspnäs crossroads that had once been a roadside tavern. The old school building was pulled down in 1959, but it lives on in a surprising way – today it's a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor recreation centre. Right next door is Aspnäskyrkan, a Pentecostal church.
Aspnässkolan, ett par minuter bort, var: A couple of minutes away is Aspnässkolan, the very first school of Järfälla's own parish. It opened in 1846 in a manor house the parish had bought, a building that had once been a roadside tavern. The oldest schoolhouse was pulled down in 1959, but it lives on in a surprising way – today it's a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre. The hospital itself belongs to Region Stockholm, and among other things has a health centre and a pharmacy.
Aspudden började byggas på 1910-talet, o: Aspudden was built from the 1910s onwards, and many of the new homes had no bathroom. That made Aspudden's bathhouse on Schlytersvägen hugely popular, and it stayed open from 1919 all the way until 2009. Even older is Villa Emmalund from 1885, where a farm slaughterhouse – mostly for horses – operated until 1912, when slaughtering at the public abattoirs became compulsory.
Aspuddsparken är en av Stockholms störst: Aspuddsparken is one of Stockholm's biggest staffed playgrounds with animals – perfect if you fancy saying hello to a goat or two. Next door is Aspuddens IP, a sports ground opened in 1913. Locals call it Linnéa, after a villa where the boys who founded the club IF Linnéa used to play football. On Manhemsgatan is the fountain sculpture Fontändamm, created in 1912 by the architect Albin Brag, who also designed several of the area's Art Nouveau buildings.
Astrid Lindgrens berg: Astrid Lindgrens berg, Astrid Lindgren's Hill
Aula Medica har en amfiteater för cirka: Aula Medica has an amphitheatre seating around 1,000 people and partly spans Solnavägen. Its facade of triangular glass panels in different colours hides a frame of glulam timber and steel that you can see from inside.
Av Mörby gård finns bara några höga aska: All that's left of Mörby farm is a few tall ash trees, standing right in the middle of the bus terminal in front of the hospital. The farm burnt down on 23 September 1976, just three weeks before its fate was to be decided after a long battle over demolishing it for Norrtäljevägen.
Av Stuvsta gård finns bara arrendatorsbo: All that's left of Stuvsta farm is the tenant's house. The only windmill still standing in Huddinge today is Balingsta mill by Lake Orlången.
Av de äldre inredningarna finns lite kva: Little remains of the older interiors. But the library has a 17th-century grisaille-painted ceiling taken from a house in Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Av det försvunna runstensfragmentet finn: All that survives of the lost runestone fragment is a scrap of text: ‘... raise the stone in memory of Svarthövde ...’. So we don’t know who Svarthövde was or who raised the stone.
Av fragmenten från källarväggen går bara: Only a couple of words can be made out on the fragments from the cellar wall. Translated, they read roughly: "björn … after brother …"
Av geotekniska skäl gick det inte att dr: For geotechnical reasons the tram line couldn't be extended all the way to Rymdtorget, which left a gap of about 400 metres. For the first few years this was bridged by a moving walkway, which was later taken out. A public lift is still there.
Av geotekniska skäl kunde spårvagnen int: For geotechnical reasons the tram line couldn't be brought all the way to the square, so the stop ended up about 400 metres to the west. For the first few years the gap was bridged by a moving walkway. That's gone now, but a public lift up to Stjärnbildsgatan is still in service.
Av idrottsparken finns bara Tennispavilj: All that's left of the sports ground is the Tennis Pavilion. It had two indoor tennis courts with wooden floors and was moved in 1911 to Fiskartorpsvägen 20, where it still stands today.
Av inskriften går det fortfarande att lä: You can still make out from the inscription that someone, perhaps named Sirhun, had the stone raised. At the end it says that Öpir carved the runes.
Av reservatets 52 hektar utgör Strålsjön: Of the reserve's 52 hectares, Lake Strålsjön makes up only about half a hectare. The aim of the reserve is "to preserve a less common type of habitat".
Av runstenen vid Edsbacka finns bara fot: Only the base of the Edsbacka runestone remains. The inscription names Holmsten and Forkunn, who raised the stone for their father, and ends with the prayer "God help his soul".
Axel Kandell löste den branta tomten gen: Axel Kandell solved the problem of the steep plot by putting the entrances inside the building. From three corridors running right through it, you go up or down to the 32 flats. Each flat has its own 18-square-metre terrace, and the five highest also have a studio.
Axel Wenner-Gren tjänade en förmögenhet: Axel Wenner-Gren made a fortune from vacuum cleaners and fridges. The Nobel laureate Hugo Theorell suggested a centre for visiting researchers, and in 1955 Wenner-Gren donated 8 million kronor. The government chipped in with a free plot.
BK Häcken spelade allsvenskt här på disp: BK Häcken played top-division Allsvenskan matches here under a special exemption, as the ground didn't meet the association's standards. It was demolished in 2014, and Häcken moved temporarily to Gamla Ullevi. By summer 2015 the new Bravida Arena stood on the same spot.
BP började bygga raffinaderiet 1965, i e: BP started building the refinery in 1965, at a time when the company was more or less mass-producing refineries around the world. Princess Alexandra of Kent opened it on 12 September 1967. Since then it has been called both OK Raffinaderi and Preem Raffinaderi.

BP began building the refinery in 1965, at a time when the company was putting up refineries around the world almost on a production line. It was opened on 12 September 1967 by Princess Alexandra of Kent.
BP började bygga raffinaderiet 1965, och: BP began building the refinery in 1965, and on 12 September 1967 it was opened by Princess Alexandra of Kent. It has since been known as OK Raffinaderi and, from 1996, Preemraff Göteborg.
Backa Röd heter hyreshusområdet runt knu: Backa Röd is the rental housing area just round the corner, with 1,500 flats. And no, despite röd meaning red, the name probably has nothing to do with colour. Here it most likely means cleared land – ground that was once cleared for farming. The district has the Backavallens IP sports ground and also Gothenburg's very first neighbourhood sports ground.
Backa kyrka byggdes 1864–1865 efter ritn: Backa Church was built in 1864–1865 to designs by Johan Fredrik Åbom, replacing a medieval church. It was remodelled around 1930, when the tower took on its present shape.
Backa kyrka ritades av Johan Fredrik Åbo: Backa Church was designed by Johan Fredrik Åbom in the Romanesque Revival style and came into use in 1864, though it wasn't consecrated until 1868. The original pointed tower was in poor condition and was replaced in 1927 by today's pyramid-shaped spire.
Backa socken i Bohuslän hörde en gång ti: Backa parish, in the province of Bohuslän, once belonged to the Västra Hising district and was a rural municipality in its own right. In 1948 it became part of the City of Gothenburg, and its old parish church, Backa Church, is a short way from here. The parish covered almost fifteen square kilometres, and by 1988 more than 20,000 people lived here.
Backa socken tillhörde Norge före 1658 o: Backa parish belonged to Norway before 1658 and was hit by several wars. So the Danes built a star-shaped fort by the river, ringed by an earth rampart and a moat. It was called Pulitz skans, and later Fredrikshamns skans.
Backa teater startade 1978 som Skolteate: Backa Teater started in 1978 as Skolteaterensemblen, the School Theatre Ensemble, and spent years playing on various small stages, mostly at Backa Kulturhus – hence the name. In 1989 it moved into an old bolt factory at Backaplan, and since 2007 it has performed at Lindholmen.
Backa, även kallat Hisings Backa, ligger: Backa, also known as Hisings Backa, lies on the east side of Hisingen and stretches from Brunnsbo in the south to Skälltorp in the north. The old Backa parish became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1948. Backa Church, the parish church, is a little way from here, and a bit further on is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, a square named after the famous author.
Backen där kyrkan står: The hill where the church stands
Backkameror före sin tid: Reversing cameras ahead of their time
Bada på Husbybadet: Go for a swim at Husbybadet
Badbollen är polerat stål: A beach ball of polished steel
Badet började i slutet av 1950-talet som: The baths started out in the late 1950s as Hägersten's open-air sun-and-shower bath, with nothing but showers and a toilet block. The pools came later; the largest is 25 metres long and 1–1.4 metres deep. Personnevägen is named after Nils Personne.
Badet har länge haft fri entré under som: The pool has long been free to use in the summer months. A renovation began in 2025 and is due to finish in 2027, after which there will be an entrance fee.
Badet som följer gamla åkrar: A pool that follows the old fields
Badet som håller extra koll: A pool that keeps an extra-close eye
Badet som nästan revs: The pool that was nearly demolished
Badhus och kägelbana: A bathhouse and a skittle alley
Badkläderna med? En kort promenad bort l: Brought your swimming things? A short walk away is Stora Mölnesjön in eastern Rannebergen, with a bathing spot and jetty on its western side. A little further on is Lilla Mölnesjön, part of the Vättlefjäll Natura 2000 area, and in the other direction the Lärjeån valley nature reserve begins.
Badort för förmögna göteborgare: A seaside resort for wealthy Gothenburgers
Badort för stadens rika: A seaside resort for the city’s wealthy
Badort med tidig golfbana: A resort with an early golf course
Badort med villa av saltpråmar: A seaside resort and a villa of salt barges
Badorten med sommarvillor: A seaside resort of summer villas
Bagare by var förr namnet på Turebergs g: Tureberg farm was once called Bagare by, 'the Baker's Village', and that's where the area gets its name. For many years this was the site of Sollentunamässan, once Sweden's third-largest exhibition centre, until it was demolished in 2017 to make room for housing. Today the area is dominated by Rättscentrum, a justice centre with a police station, district court and remand prison. Running through it all is Malmvägen, known locally as Tian, 'the Ten', after its ten tower blocks – a Million Programme housing project that drew international attention when it opened in 1972.
Bagaregårdsskolan stod klar i april 1918: Bagaregårdsskolan, the school designed by Johan Jarlén, was finished in April 1918, with a base of rough grey stone and an elegant little clock tower on the roof. Round the corner was the Saga cinema, which opened in 1942 and closed in 1964. The following year Bengt Johansson bought the building and opened a grocery, Saga hemköp – the first shop in what became the Sagabutikerna chain. From the box office to the checkout, you might say.
Bageriet Anderson Bakery byggde 1997 ett: In 1997 Anderson Bakery built an unusual office block on Regulatorvägen with an almost life-size windmill on the roof. Today the bakery is run by Lantmännen Unibake, where 30 staff bake over 100,000 baguettes a day.
Baggeby blev plötsligt slutstation i jun: In June 2023, Baggeby suddenly found itself at the end of the line. The old Lidingö Bridge had been demolished, and construction faults meant the new Lilla Lidingöbron couldn't yet carry trains. So the Lidingöbanan trams turned round here instead of carrying on to Ropsten. Up in the villa suburb of Mosstorp, a short walk away, Hersby water tower stands at the end of Vattentornsvägen.
Baggeby är en av Södra Lidingöbanans urs: Baggeby is one of the original stations on the Södra Lidingöbanan line, opened in January 1914. The little station building dates from the start and is rated as being of "great cultural and historical value". Until the late 1970s a Pressbyrån newsagent's kiosk stood next to it.
Bakom Lisebergs staket en bit härifrån l: Behind the fence of Liseberg, the amusement park, not far from here, is Balders Hage, the spot where the Örgryte IS sports club was founded in 1887 and where a skating rink opened on New Year's Day 1888. Today the Balder roller coaster thunders past nearby – one of the biggest wooden roller coasters in the Nordic countries. And if you fancy a fright, there's Gasten, a haunted hotel where live actors lie in wait to scare visitors.
Bakom altaret sitter en glasmålning av L: Behind the altar is a stained-glass window by Lars Abrahamsson, showing branches, lush foliage and a red apple. He also designed the altar, whose top is made of limestone from Borghamn in Östergötland. The silver font bowl has a dove on the inside.
Bakom den trekantiga parken döljer sig e: Behind the triangular park lies one of Stockholm's most talked-about unsolved crimes. On 4 May 1932, Lilly Lindeström was found murdered in her flat at Sankt Eriksplan 11 – the case that became known as the Vampire Murder. There are happier memories just round the corner: the Capitol cinema from 1926 closed in 1985 but reopened in 2018 as Bio & Bistro Capitol.
Bakom granitmuren intill parken ligger V: Behind the granite wall next to the park lies Västra kyrkogården, the Western Cemetery, on a slope in what is now the middle of Kungälv. When it was finished in 1864 it was just outside the town, and it was called Nya kyrkogården, the New Cemetery, to set it apart from the old one. Most of the headstones in the northern part date from the early 1900s, while the newer ones are in the south. In other words, the town has grown right past its own graves.
Bakom husen renar Käppalaverket avloppsv: Behind the houses, the Käppala plant, Käppalaverket, has been treating wastewater since 1969, and it's considered one of the most efficient treatment works in the world. Not far away is Käppalaställningen, a Second World War anti-aircraft battery that reopened in 1994 as a memorial to Stockholm's air defence – the only one of its kind in Sweden. A bit further on is M/S Soya III, a tanker built in 1936 to carry soybean oil and now a conference ship.
Bakom hållplatsen ligger Östra Mölna rad: Behind the stop lies the Östra Mölna terraced housing estate, also known as Vita staden, the White Town. The architect Nils Tesch designed its 52 terraced houses and eight villas back in 1954, but they weren't built until 1962 to 1972. The municipality rates the area as irreplaceable for its cultural history. Not far off stands Villa Sjöstigen, designed by Ferdinand Boberg in 1911 as an experiment in affordable summer housing.
Bakom murarna i Härlanda satt fångar frå: Behind the walls at Härlanda, prisoners were locked up from 1907 to 1997. The old central prison is now a listed building and goes by the name Härlanda park. The Saga cinema on Sofiagatan closed in 1964, and the following year it became a grocery shop – Saga Hemköp, the first in the Sagabutikerna chain. Tucked in among the buildings, you'll also find the ruins of an old church.
Bakom namnet Almedal finns ett litet bar: Behind the name Almedal is a little child. The area is named after Alma Buchholtz, who lived only from 1840 to 1841 – the daughter of a former owner of the Almedal country estate. The name lived on in the linen mill that Hans Hemming Wesslau founded by the Mölndalsån river in 1848, Almedahls fabriker. Almedalsvägen has been here since 1933.
Balltorp kan låta som en modern förort,: Balltorp might sound like a modern suburb – and it's true that it grew mainly in the 1980s. But people were living here as long as 10,000 years ago! The district is in the southern part of Västra Mölndal, which corresponds to the Fässberg district, and a little further on are both Västra and Östra Balltorp – West and East Balltorp.
Bandhagen var från början ett torp under: Bandhagen started out as a croft belonging to Örby Castle, mentioned as early as 1677. The cottage burnt down in 1942 and the last barn was demolished in 1961. It stood about 300 metres north-east of today's centre.
Bandhagens centrum invigdes 1954 tillsam: Bandhagen's centre opened in 1954 along with the metro station, and it's still owned by the housing cooperative HSB Bandhagen, with just over 500 flats and around twenty shops. Towering above it is the Murbruket block, an eleven-storey slab block from 1955. The City Museum rates both the building and the whole district as culturally and historically valuable.
Bandhagens gymnasium vid Trollesundsväge: Bandhagens gymnasium, the upper secondary school on Trollesundsvägen, was built between 1957 and 1959, with the assembly hall added ten years later. It housed a range of upper secondary courses until 2002, and in the early 2000s the building was converted into flats. So today people live in the old classrooms – and the City Museum has marked the property green as especially valuable.
Bangården har över 60 spår men saknar he: The rail yard has more than 60 tracks but no train protection system such as ATC at all. Instead, every train movement here is run as shunting, at no more than 30 km/h.
The cyclotron's magnet alone weighed 600 tonnes. No single part could weigh more than 30 tonnes, and they were shipped to Frihamnen. The concrete was mixed with iron ore and weighed twice as much as normal concrete, so the wheelbarrows could only be filled halfway.
Bara ett par hundra meter bort, nära Glö: Just a couple of hundred metres away, near Glömstavägen, is Glömstahällen, a rock carved with runes in the Glömsta valley. Glömsta only became a district in its own right in 2018 – before that it was part of Flemingsberg. Its houses are clustered around Lake Gömmaren, and what was once an area of old holiday cottages is gradually filling up with new homes.
Bara ett par minuter bort ligger en sten: Just a couple of minutes away is a stone house nobody has quite dared to live in: Dvärgahuset, the Dwarf House. It's a stone cist grave from the Late Neolithic, and people once believed it was home to dwarves. It was described in writing as early as the 17th century – and local people surely knew of it long before that. The archaeologist Oscar Montelius examined it in 1899.
Bara ett par minuters promenad härifrån: Just a couple of minutes' walk from here are the ruins of Ytterby's old church. It was built in the 12th century, when this was Norwegian land, and legend says Saint Olaf himself built it. It served as the parish church until 1870. The station on the Bohus line is much younger – it opened in 1907.

Just a couple of minutes' walk from here stands Kälvesta kvarn, a 17th-century windmill also known as Lilla Stampan and Lunda kvarn. The City Museum has blue-listed it – the highest heritage rating there is – for its exceptional cultural and historical value. Not bad for a mill that started out on Observatoriegatan in the city centre.
