Bara ett stenkast bort ligger Nilento St: Just a stone's throw away is Nilento Studio, a recording studio founded in 1993 by the musicians Lars Nilsson and Jenny Nilsson. It began life as a mobile studio and is now popular for everything from jazz and big band to choirs, opera and symphony orchestras. Since 2013 they've also run their own record label.
Bara ett stenkast bort står Kummelbysten: Just a stone's throw away stands the Kummelby stone, a runestone carved in the late 11th century – almost a thousand years before the suburb appeared. It's beside Kummelby church, built where Kummelby farm once stood. The first church was so small, with room for only 50 people, that it was nicknamed Kummelby lillkyrka, the Little Church. The new church was consecrated just before Christmas 2000.
Bara ett stenkast bort står Villa Lundin: Just a stone's throw away stands Villa Lundin, built around 1911 and now one of the few well-preserved villas from that era. People often called it 'the Castle', and the Lundin family who lived there are said to have owned one of Fagersjö's two cars in the 1930s. Real luxury in those days!
Bara i Sverige fick omkring 3 000 fartyg: In Sweden alone, around 3,000 vessels were fitted with an Avance engine. Most of the exports went to Russia, where the engines powered motor ploughs. In 1907 the company changed its name from Automobilfabrik to Motorfabrik.
Bara nedre halvan av runstenen finns kva: Only the lower half of the runestone survives. In 1923 a caretaker said he had helped build the quay at Islinge harbour in 1902, and that the top of the stone had been used as fill. Attempts to dig it up in the 1940s came to nothing.
Bara några minuter bort reser sig Tyresö: Just a few minutes away rises Tyresö View, 82 metres and 23 storeys tall – in 2016 the fourth-tallest residential building in the whole of Stockholm County. About as close is Tyresö Centrum, a glass-roofed shopping centre with 74 shops, plus the council offices and a library whose exhibition hall always has something new on show.
Bara några minuters promenad bort väntar: Just a few minutes' walk away is Kärna bokskog, a beech wood that became a nature reserve in 2008. It's a treat for lichen lovers, with several red-listed species, and the plant life includes a rare grass, wood fescue. The reserve covers about 18 hectares and is managed by the West Coast Foundation, and parts of it have been adapted so that everyone can get around.
Bara några steg härifrån porlar Sankt Bo: Just a few steps from here, Saint Botvid's Spring bubbles up – a cold-water spring at the south-eastern tip of Lake Bornsjön. About fifty metres away is the Söderby Stone, a runestone beside the old Södertäljevägen road. And a little further on is the Söderby burial ground, one of the best preserved in the Mälaren Valley, with around 150 visible graves from the early Iron Age, along with the 18th-century farm of Nedre Söderby.
Bara två arenor i världen: One of only two stadiums in the world
Bara två dagar efter invigningen 1968 sk: Just two days after the centre opened in 1968, the newspaper Dagens Nyheter ran the headline “Tear down Skärholmen”, calling it one of the most inhumane centres ever built. The article sparked a media campaign against the whole Million Programme, Sweden's great 1965–1975 housing drive.
Bara under 1910 byggdes 15 femvåningshus: In 1910 alone, 15 five-storey blocks went up in Gröndal, all with flushing toilets – a novelty at the time. A one-room flat with kitchen cost 250–300 kronor a year in rent.
Barkarby villastad: Barkarby villastad, the old garden suburb
Barkarby is a place in the middle of a makeover. The commuter station took its present form on 10 October 2016, with four tracks and a ticket hall on the Barkarby bridge. Meanwhile a new metro station is being built underground, and a new entrance at the north end of the station will become the main entrance once everything is finished.

Barnarbetare i batterifabriken: Child labour in the battery factory

Bastun byggdes från september 2014 i en: Work on the sauna began in September 2014 in a public workshop led by Raumlabor Berlin. It stands on a concrete mooring dolphin between Kvillepiren and Norra Frihamnspiren piers and holds 20 people. The year after it opened, it was nominated for the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden’s top architecture award.
Bastusjön är bara 0,04 kvadratkilometer: Bastusjön covers just 0.04 square kilometres but is a full 5.9 metres deep. It lies 16 metres above sea level.
Beatles på tennisbanan: The Beatles on the tennis court
Bebyggelsen i Skintebodalen fick Per och: The housing in Skintebodalen won the Per and Alma Olsson Foundation's prize for the best new building in Gothenburg in 1975. In recent years its attractive location has sent property prices soaring.
Beckbrukets chefsbostad: The manager's house at Beckbruket, the old tar works
Befästningen Södra skans byggdes 1643–45: The Södra skans fortification was built in 1643–45 on the hill where Söderstadion stadium now stands. The last wall to be built, from 1859, actually survives – it's now incorporated into one of the new buildings by Söderstadion.
Begravningskapellet från 1969 ritades av: The funeral chapel from 1969 was designed by Sven Ivar Lind in dark-fired brick, with four corner windows that cast a beautiful raking light. By the entrance a seven-branched candlestick is etched into the plaster, and a wall bears plaques in memory of the victims of the Holocaust.
Begravningskapellet på Silverdals grifte: At Silverdal Cemetery, the funeral chapel and the crematorium are built together. The whole Gärdestad family is buried here. The cemetery itself was laid out in 1914 as a garrison cemetery for the Stockholm garrison. And the Silverdal area very nearly got a different name: when planning began in 1989, the project was first called Margreteborg.
Begravningsplatsen anlades i början av 1: The cemetery was laid out in the early 1960s together with a crematorium and two chapels, Rosens kapell and Liljans kapell – the Chapel of the Rose and the Chapel of the Lily. It was designed by Gunnar Martinsson and Klas Fåhræus after an architectural competition and covers 17 hectares.
Begravningsplatsen invigdes den 9 juni 1: The cemetery was consecrated on 9 June 1827 by the archbishop and hymn writer Johan Olof Wallin, whose speech contained the oft-quoted words: ‘Know ye upon what ground ye stand? Ye stand upon your own graves!’ Twelve years later he was buried on that very spot.
Begravningsplatsen ligger i ett grönområ: The cemetery lies in a green space among pine trees and bilberry bushes, designed by landscape architect Gunnar Martinsson. The burial sections are named after plants, such as Cypressen, Eken and Flädern – the cypress, the oak and the elder.
Bellevue var från början namnet på en vi: Bellevue was originally the name of an 1860s villa on a wooded hill north of the Säveån river. The name is French – belle vue, beautiful view. The villa burnt down completely in 1970.
Bellman och Strindberg på krogen: Bellman and Strindberg at the inn
Bensinmack under torget: A petrol station under the square
Bensinmack, fotolab och kapell: Petrol station, photo lab and chapel
Berget där isen låg: The hill where the ice lay
Berget fick ge vika för macken: A rock gave way to a petrol station
Berget kyrkan står på hette på 1600-tale: In the 1600s the hill the church stands on was called Tysktölskullan or Tistelskullan. The plot itself is known as Sprängkullen, after the quarrying that went on here in the early 1800s.
Bergets äldsta kända namn är Kråkberget,: The hill's oldest known name is Kråkberget, Crow Hill, recorded in 1668. The name Vita bergen, the White Hills, probably comes from the pale bedrock of what was once a bare hill. On the highest point, 46 metres above sea level, stands Sofia Church, and on the other summit a music pavilion from 1907 shaped like an echo temple.
Berghällen med U 80 sluttar mot en svack: The rock face bearing runestone U 80 slopes down to a hollow that was probably once a strait – perhaps the one that gave Sundby farm its name. In the mid-1000s the carving sat barely a metre above sea level, clearly visible to passing ships. All that remains of the waterway today are the Spångaån and Bällstaån streams.
Bergrummet tömdes på utrustning 1987, me: The rock chamber was stripped of its equipment in 1987, but the interior is largely intact – a time capsule from the 1950s to the 1970s. The owner still keeps the heating and dehumidifiers running, and a plan to turn it into a car park was shelved.
Bergrummet är det sista bevarade av de s: The rock cavern is the last surviving of the large bomb-proof factories from the Second World War. The equipment has been gone since 1987, but the interior is largely intact, a time capsule from the 1950s to the 1970s. A proposal to turn it into a car park was dropped.
The Bergshamraleden road cuts the district in two. Instead of the homes planned above the road, in the mid-1980s Skandia built a building that spans it – sometimes called Bergshamra bro, the Bergshamra Bridge. Today the insurer If has its head office there.
Bergshamras tunnelbanestation har en ova: Bergshamra metro station has an unusual design: Bergshamravägen runs over an underground bridge directly on top of the passage between the southern entrance and the platform. The station opened in 1978. The area also has some old houses down by the Stocksundet strait, such as the villa Fjällstugan from 1835 and Stocksundstorp farm, whose buildings probably went up around 1753.
Bergsjön ligger högt, och från vissa pla: Bergsjön sits high up, and from some spots you can see the island of Vinga at the harbour entrance. Gärdsåstoppen hill, to the south-west, is 130 metres high and can even be seen from the city centre.
Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap: Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap, the heritage railway society
Bergslagsbanan fick köpa marken i Huvuds: The Bergslagen railway was allowed to buy the land at Huvudsta from the landowner Max Wibom on condition that a station building was put up here. When Swedish Railways took over in 1945 the line was electrified and the steam engine shed became redundant, but it was kept for emergency preparedness.
Berndt Hellebergs konstverk föreställer: Berndt Helleberg's artwork shows a bird keeping watch over its eggs. The yellow bird flies above Bromma torg, while the eggs – one black, one yellow and one blue – lie scattered around the square. See if you can spot them!
Berzelius var med från start: Berzelius was there from the start
Berättarministeriet i huset: The Ministry of Stories in the house
Beslutet att bygga Angereds Centrum togs: The city's executive committee voted unanimously to build Angereds Centrum on 9 April 1975. Barely a year later, on 2 February 1976, councillor Åke Norling broke the first ground.
Beslutet att bygga på åkermarken togs 19: The decision to build on the farmland was taken in 1986. The neighbourhood then grew from the north-west – Eklanda Hage and Eklanda Skog – towards the south and south-east, Eklanda Vall and Eklanda Äng. The local football club, Solängens BK, has 800 members.
Beslutet om ett kulturhus togs 2013, och: The decision to build a culture house was taken in 2013, and the city held events to find out what the people of Bergsjön wanted. Sweco Architects won the design competition, construction began in 2020 and the building opened on 17 August 2022.
Beställ på morgonen, hämta på kvällen: Order in the morning, collect in the evening
Beställningen var tydlig: kungen skulle: The brief was clear: the king was to stand on foot, not sit on horseback, and he was not to wear a hat, so that his ‘noble brow’ could be seen. His clothes were modelled on the uniform he wore when he was killed at Fredriksten Fortress in 1718.
Besök Akalla by med 4H-gård och kafé: Visit Akalla village, with its 4H farm and café
Besök Sankta Birgitta kyrka: Visit St Bridget's Church, Sankta Birgitta kyrka
Besök Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet (1 min) oc: Visit the Maritime Museum and Aquarium (1 min) and look out for the statue of the sailor's wife in Sjömanstornet, the Sailors' Tower, gazing out over the river.
Besök Sveriges VVS-museum: Visit Sveriges VVS-museum, the Swedish Plumbing Museum
Besök konsthallen Accelerator i det gaml: Visit the Accelerator art gallery in the old underground lab
Besök museilägenheten Kämpingebacken 13: Visit the museum flat at Kämpingebacken 13 (2 min), its interior preserved just as it was in 1969, when Tensta was built. Tensta Konsthall, the art centre, is a couple of minutes away.
Betongkyrka med segel: A concrete church with a sail

Biblioteket öppnade 1964 under namnet Vå: The library opened in 1964 as Vårväderstorgets bibliotek. In 2020 the Swedish Arts Council named it a Romani reading embassy, with a special focus on the Romani minorities and their language. On an ordinary day it gets 700–800 visitors.
Biblioteksbyggnaden från 2004 ritades av: The library building from 2004 was designed by Christer Malmström and won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden’s top architecture award, that same year – sharing it with the Museum of World Culture in Gothenburg.
Bifrost ligger på det som var inägor til: Bifrost was built on the former fields of Toltorp village, where the last harvest was brought in in 1963. Just a few years later, in 1967, work began on the blocks of flats. The Tegen housing cooperative, formed in 1970–1971, has 477 flats.
Bilarna på Stuvstaleden försvinner in i: Traffic on Stuvstaleden vanishes into the Kungsklippan rock through the Stuvsta tunnel, 193 metres long and opened in 1994. Before that, the road ran right through the middle of Stuvsta, and the noise was a real problem. The oddest thing about the tunnel is its northern entrance: it's built into a block of flats, put up at the same time, that straddles the opening.
Bilfabriken kom på 1960-talet: The car plant arrived in the 1960s
Bilfabriken som gjorde motorer: The car factory that made engines
Bilförbud på Mälaröarna: Cars banned on the Mälaren islands
Billdal bjuder på både kyrka, park och h: In Billdal, church, park and sea are all within walking distance. Billdal church is just a couple of hundred metres away, and right beyond it begins Billdals park, a nature area with Billdals gård, the manor house. A little further on, the Killingsholmen peninsula juts out into the sea, with a municipal small-boat harbour and its own boatyard, Killingsholmens Varv.
Billig mat och kägelbana: Cheap food and a skittle alley
Billman-Regulator hade tidigare tillverk: Billman-Regulator had previously made its products at some 15 different addresses and could now bring everything together under one roof. The factory was designed by Karl G.H. Karlsson, one of the most sought-after industrial architects of the day, and opened in June 1964 in the presence of Prince Bertil. The office building is now considered of cultural and historical value.
Bilmuseet som levde i sju månader: The car museum that lasted seven months
Bilpremiär i tennishallen: A car premiere in the tennis hall
Bio Capitol vid Skanstorget har visat fi: Bio Capitol on Skanstorget has been screening films since 1941, and since 1999 it has been home to Cinemateket, the film archive's cinema. A stone's throw away was Sprängkullen, an activity centre started in 1974 that became a key meeting place for the progressive music movement and later the punk scene, with plenty of well-known bands taking the stage. And Husargatan is named after the Crown Prince's Hussars, who were once stationed in barracks at the end of the street.
Bio Kaskad, alldeles intill, öppnade 195: Bio Kaskad, the cinema right next door, opened in 1957, closed in the late 1990s and came back to life in 2018. Beneath the square, part of the metro platform runs inside the rock, lined with green, blue and yellow tiles. The cooperative housing block nearby was built in 1952 with 84 small flats for single people and young couples without children, complete with a central kitchen, restaurant and shop in the building.

Bio Kaskad, right next door, opened in 1957, closed in the late 1990s and came back to life in 2018. Under the square, part of the metro platform is set into the rock and lined with green, blue and yellow tiles. The collective housing block nearby was built in 1952 with 84 small flats for single people and young couples without children. And Josephinahemmet is named after Queen Josefina, the wife of Oscar I.
Biocafé Tellus vid Vattenledningsvägen ä: Biocafé Tellus on Vattenledningsvägen is one of the few old neighbourhood cinemas left in Stockholm, with a café that hosts all kinds of cultural events. A little further away is the Aspen cinema. When it opened in 1952 it was the first privately run cinema to open in Stockholm since 1943, with 300 seats but no balcony.
Biografen Aspen lades ner redan 1961. På: The Aspen cinema closed as early as 1961. In the 1970s and 80s the auditorium became a training hall for the Spårvägen table tennis club, and J-O Waldner was among those who trained here. Since 2019 Aspen has been a cinema again, with two screens, a stage and a bistro.
Biografen Bristol på Sturegatan invigdes: The Bristol cinema on Sturegatan opened on New Year's Eve 1939, when it was owned by Algot Myrgren. Today it's both a cinema and an arts venue. A little further on is Folkets hus, the community hall, built back in 1903, with rooms for meetings, conferences and parties; the main hall holds up to 100 people. And on the nearby Esplanaden you'll find a bust of the town's founder, Anders Petter Löfström.
Biografen Gnistan hade 435 platser och l: The Gnistan cinema had 435 seats and stood on the corner of Brämaregatan and Tunnbindaregatan. At its opening in 1938, the actor Ludde Gentzel read a prologue written by Fritz Schéel – a compulsory part of any cinema opening at the time.
Biografen Prisma öppnade den 21 november: The Prisma cinema opened on 21 November 1960 with Let's Make Love, starring Marilyn Monroe. Its name had been chosen in a vote by readers of the local paper Västerort.
Biografen Reflexen byggdes av SF och rit: The Reflexen cinema was built by the film company SF and designed by Sverker Feuk. The auditorium had 437 seats, 48 of them so-called courting couches for two, and a 10.5 by 4-metre CinemaScope screen. A red neon sign glowed above the entrance.
Biografen Rex ägdes av Hugo Hansson och: The Rex cinema was owned by Hugo Hansson and stood at what was then Backavägen 75, now Granåsgatan 2. The last screening took place in June 1958.
Biografen Rival invigdes 1937 med en pro: The Rival cinema opened in 1937 with a prologue by the revue star Karl Gerhard, and back then it had 1,218 seats. On 4 July 2008 the film Mamma Mia! had its premiere here. The hotel opened in 2003 as Sweden's first lifestyle hotel.
Biografen Rondo gick i brunt: brun samme: The Rondo cinema was decked out in brown: brown velvet in the foyer, brown walls, a brown curtain and brown wall-to-wall carpet. Only the 436 armchairs were upholstered in green.
Biografen Roxy öppnade den 15 november 1: The Roxy cinema opened on 15 November 1956, the same month as the library on the square. Its last show was on 28 March 1965.
Biografen Savoy hade 363 platser och stä: The Savoy cinema had 363 seats and closed in the mid-1960s. After that the pop group Hep Stars rehearsed in the space, and their manager Åke Gerhard ran the first studio here.
Biografen Vingen på Gamla Björlandavägen: The Vingen cinema at Gamla Björlandavägen 145 had a short but eventful life. It was built and run by Leif Harald Winqvist and opened on 19 December 1957. Rolf Magnusson took it over in 1960, but on 2 January 1962 the lights went out for good. Right next to the stop is Toleredskyrkan, a church in Lundby parish.
Biografen drivs av Kulturhuset Möllan i: The cinema is run by the Möllan cultural centre in the Folkets hus building by the town hall square. Café Möllan is in the same building, so you can stop for fika – a coffee and a bite – before the show.
Biografen som blev kyrka: The cinema that became a church
Biografen öppnade 2001 och drevs först a: The cinema opened in 2001 and was first run by the American chain AMC. SF struck back by refusing to let AMC show Swedish films and took over the Vågen cinema in Skärholmen. After just two years AMC gave up and sold its screens to SF.
Biografens ridå formgavs av konstnären T: The cinema's curtain was designed by the artist Tor Hörlin and showed the view from his studio at Kornhamnstorg. In 2005 the film 165 Hässelby had its world premiere here.
Biograferna har avlöst varandra här. Bio: Cinemas have come and gone around here. Biografteatern on Sveagatan was already showing films in 1904–1908. Mignon on Linnégatan had 182 seats and was open from 1941 to 1982. At Sveaplan there was Klappan, and after it Svea, until 2008. The street is named after the Olivedal estate.
Biokriget i Kungens kurva: The cinema war in Kungens kurva
Biomedicums långa fasader består av omkr: Biomedicum's long façades are made up of some 1,500 shimmering green, angled glass panels that hang like a curtain outside the wall itself. The windows can't be opened. In the central hall, the Atrium, daylight pours in through around forty round skylights.
Bion som blev teater: The cinema that became a theatre
Bion som vaknade igen: The cinema that came back to life
Biskopsgårdens kyrka ritades i brutalist: Biskopsgården Church was designed in the Brutalist style by Johannes Olivegren. A triangular, white-painted concrete roof reaches up towards a free-form concrete tower. The bell frame is shaped like a mainsail with three free-hanging bells, and a weathercock sits at the very top.
Biskopsgårdens kyrka vid Vårväderstorget: Biskopsgården Church on Vårväderstorget was completed in 1961 to designs by the architect Johannes Olivegren.
Bjurslättskyrkan är en så kallad vandrin: Bjurslätt Church is a 'travelling church', built to be moved. It went up in 1966 as Länsmansgården's church and was moved here when Länsmansgården got a permanent church in 1972. It was consecrated on its new site in 1973.
Björkhagen hörde under två korta år, 199: For just two years, 1997 and 1998, Björkhagen was part of the Hammarby district, which was abolished when the number of city districts was cut from 24 to 18. A stone's throw away rises Duggregnet 5, Stockholm's tallest residential building when it went up in 1957. And from the metro station starts Sörmlandsleden, a hiking trail that's part of the European long-distance path E6.
Björkhagens skola invigdes 1949, ritad a: Björkhagen School opened in 1949, designed by the architect Åke Lindqvist, and on its eastern side the school grounds run right up to Nackareservatet, the Nacka nature reserve. The nearby Taklampan block also backs straight onto the reserve, and it was one of ten projects nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2018. So here, deep forest is practically on your doorstep.
Björknäs nämns i skrift redan 1436 och h: Björknäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436 and takes its name from the farm Stora Björknäs gård. It sits at the eastern end of the Skuru bridges, where the Skurusundet strait marks a provincial border: west of the water is Södermanland, east of it Uppland. The bridges have been built in three stages – in 1915, 1957 and 2023. When the newest opened it took over the name Skurubron, and the older ones became Gamla Skurubron, the Old Skuru Bridge.
Björkö, eller Bohus-Björkö som postorten: Björkö – or Bohus-Björkö, as its postal address has it – has just over 1,500 permanent residents. Out on Björkö Huvud, near Bovik, the Gothenburg Outdoor Association owns a stretch of land used as a naturist area, with swimming and camping. Also near Bovik is Pjonken, famous for the masses of hepaticas – little blue anemones – that flower there every spring.

Björkö – or Bohus-Björkö, as its postal address has it – has a few more secrets than you might expect. Out on Björkö Huvud, near Bovik, the Gothenburg outdoor association owns a stretch of land that's used as a naturist area, with swimming and camping. The island has about 1,500 year-round residents and covers just under five and a half square kilometres.
Björlanda kyrka, en bit härifrån, står p: Björlanda Church, a short way from here, stands on north-western Hisingen and has belonged to Torslanda-Björlanda parish since 2010. The old parish of Björlanda counted as part of Bohuslän and merged into the City of Gothenburg in 1967. It's a big parish, almost 44 square kilometres, and in 2000 it was home to just over 5,000 people.

Björlanda Church, a little way from here, stands on north-western Hisingen and has been part of Torslanda-Björlanda parish since 2010. The old parish of Björlanda belonged to the province of Bohuslän and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000, just over 10,000 people lived in the parish. It covers a large area, almost 44 square kilometres, and in 2000 it had just over 5,000 inhabitants.
Björlanda, kyrkbyn i Björlanda socken, h: Björlanda, the church village of Björlanda parish, has had trouble deciding what it is. Until 2015 it was a locality in its own right, then it became part of Torslanda, in 2018 it was a locality of its own again, and since 2023 it's been counted as part of Gothenburg. Its houses cluster around the church and were mostly built in the 1990s.
Björn och Fulluge högg stenen: Björn and Fulluge carved the stone
Bland de ett 60-tal träd som planeras på: Among the 60 or so trees planned for the square are sequoias and tulip trees, as well as robinia, or black locust. The two parts of the square cover 9,000 square metres between them.
Bland de första Wallenbergarna här var A: Among the first Wallenbergs here were André Oscar Wallenberg and his wife Anna von Sydow; his bronze bust stands behind the mausoleum. Back in the 1600s and 1700s the site was already used as a burial ground for the Malmvik manor.
Bland de sista barnrikehusen: Among the last homes for large families
Bland dem som deltog i inrättandet av KI: Among those who helped found the Karolinska Institute was the chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius. His research laid the foundations of the university's scientific profile, and he was counted as a professor at the new institute as early as 1811.
Bland dem som gått på Farsta gymnasium f: Former pupils of Farsta upper secondary school include the writer Alex Schulman, the world wrestling champion Martin Lidberg and the stand-up comedian Janne Westerlund.
Bland dem som gått på Hulebäcksgymnasiet: Former pupils of Hulebäcksgymnasiet include the metal band Avatar, radio personality Navid Modiri and Hanna Ferm, runner-up in Idol 2017.
Bland dem som är födda i Lindome finns s: Lindome’s famous sons and daughters include cartoonist Rune Andréasson, actor Jessica Liedberg, director Björn Runge and actor and singer Tage Severin.
Bland eleverna på Farsta gymnasium finns: Former pupils of Farsta gymnasium include the writer Alex Schulman, wrestling world champion Martin Lidberg, stand-up comedian Janne Westerlund and editorial writer Karin Pettersson.
Bland gästerna fanns Karl XII, Carl von: Guests included Karl XII, Carl Linnaeus and Carl Michael Bellman, who wrote about life at the inn. In 1741 Linnaeus noted that they reached Fittja, "where we waited a long time for horses". Gustav III arrived by boat from Drottningholm.
Bland gästerna på Fittja värdshus finns: Guests at Fittja inn have included Charles XII, Carl Linnaeus and Bellman, who wrote about life here. In 1741 Linnaeus noted: “…we came to Fittja, where we waited long for horses.” The coaching logbooks are full of complaints about worn-out horses.
Bland gårdens ekonomibyggnader finns sta: Among the farm's outbuildings are the stable and the storehouse from the late 1800s. The storehouse is now home to a summer café.
Blockhusudden är Djurgårdens östligaste: Blockhusudden is the easternmost tip of Djurgården. This is where Stora Sjötullen, the great maritime customs house, once stood – it's mentioned as early as 1623. Every boat coming in from the archipelago had to stop here and pay a toll before it could reach the city. Along Blockhusringen there are several fine villas, among them Johannisberg, whose summer salon has been listed since 1935. And a little further on, the art treasures of Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, await.
Blockmakaren Gustaf Andersson tillverkad: The blockmaker Gustaf Andersson made pulley blocks for the navy, and his lathe still stands in the main room, which doubled as his workshop. On the ground floor the widow Emilia Gustafsson rented a room with her five children and worked as a cleaner, washerwoman and newspaper deliverer.
Blockmakarens hus har återställts till h: The blockmaker's house has been restored to how it looked in 1917–1923. So there's no electricity or running water, and the privy stands in the little courtyard. People lived here right up until 1975.
Blommensbergsviadukten är 300 meter lång: The Blommensberg viaduct is 300 metres long and stands up to 30 metres above the valley floor. Its 29.5-metre-wide roadway rests on thirteen pairs of round concrete pillars, each 1.5 metres thick.
Blommor och grönsaker till stan: Flowers and vegetables for the city
Blå gången och Take the A-train: Blå gången and Take the A-train
Blå linjen nås via Blå gången, en drygt: You reach the blue line via Blå gången, the Blue Passage – a tunnel of just over 100 metres with moving walkways. It's home to Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd's Take the A-train from 1984. While the City Line rail tunnel was being built in 2011–2017, the walls were covered with information boards, but the artwork has since been restored.
Blå linjen växer fyra kilometer: The Blue Line grows by four kilometres
Blåsut är en utomhusstation som öppnade: Blåsut is an open-air station that opened on 1 October 1950. Alongside the speed stripes, Ann Edholm's 2008 artwork includes an abstract composition that might just make you think of a face.
Bo Möller gav Lidingö Arena en tydlig ho: Bo Möller gave Lidingö Arena a strong horizontal look, with long ribbons of windows and sun shades in red-painted metal. The red is echoed in the reddish-brown brick and the sheet-metal details. Since 1996 the building has also housed a 31-room hotel.
Bo gård hette från början Vikby, byn i v: Bo farm was originally called Vikby, the village in the bay – the bay being Kyrkviken. Burial grounds nearby show it was already an important farm in prehistoric times. In the Middle Ages it owned most of the farms and crofts on Lidingö.
Bo gård saknar huvudbyggnad, och någon s: Bo gård has no main house, and as far as anyone knows one was never planned. Instead, two yellow L-shaped buildings and two red pavilions enclose a courtyard. The wings were built in 1777.
Bo kvarn, gårdens husbehovskvarn, byggde: Bo kvarn, the farm's own mill, was built in 1816 just east of the farmhouse. It's one of the oldest windmills around Stockholm still standing where it was first built.
Boberg gav Villa Sjöstigen formen av en: Boberg designed Villa Sjöstigen as a larger version of a Norwegian mountain cabin, with tarred shingles on the walls. It’s the only known example of his low-cost villa.
Bocken stor som en tiokrona: A goat the size of a ten-krona coin
Bodal finns på en karta från 1661 som Bo: Bodal appears on a map from 1661 as Boodaal. In the late 18th century the tenant farmer Israel Hansson lived here in a long, single-storey log house, and in 1796 he became churchwarden at Lidingö Church.
Bodals gård byggdes om 1934–1935 till bo: In 1934–1935 the main house of the old Bodal farm was converted into a home for Supreme Court justice Birger Wedberg. It was later renovated and became part of the school, which was completed in 2009 with a new building designed by Gillberg Arkitekter.
Bodals gård byggdes om 1934–35 för justi: Bodal manor was remodelled in 1934–35 for Supreme Court justice Birger Wedberg in the 1920s Classicism known as Swedish Grace – the same style as Carl Malmsten's furniture. The rusticated corners, on the other hand, were the height of fashion in the 17th and 18th centuries.
Bodals kyrka började som ett kapell 1972: Bodal Church began as a chapel in 1972 and became a church in 1983. In the 2010s damp damage was discovered; the church closed in 2017 and was demolished in October 2018.
Boden vid nyodlingen: The hut by the new clearing
Bollen i rågåkern: The ball in the rye field
Bollen, Skidan och Värjan: The Ball, the Ski and the Foil
Bollhav och småländsk husmanskost: Ball pits and Småland home cooking
Bollhavet testades här: Where the ball pit was tested
Bollhus och saltmagasin: A real-tennis court and a salt warehouse
Bollmora centrum invigdes 1965 som ett l: Bollmora centrum opened in 1965 as a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In the early 1990s it was converted into a mall, but just before the reopening in 1992 a major fire swept through several buildings and delayed the opening.
Bollmora gård låg ungefär i korsningen N: Bollmora farm stood roughly where Njupkärrsvägen meets Industrivägen. A Shell petrol station later occupied the site until it was demolished in 2012, and since 2014 there has been a Willys supermarket here.
Bollmora var faktiskt en egen tätort åre: From 1965 to 1974, Bollmora was actually a town in its own right, but these days most people call the area Tyresö centrum. There's a glass-roofed shopping centre with 74 shops and a library with its own exhibition hall. Towering over it all is Tyresö View, 82 metres and 23 storeys high – in 2016, the fourth-tallest residential building in the whole of Stockholm County.
Bollmora var åren 1965–1974 en egen täto: From 1965 to 1974, Bollmora was a town in its own right, but these days most people call the area Tyresö centrum. This is where you'll find the glass-roofed shopping centre with 74 shops, the municipal offices and a library with its own exhibition hall. A little further off is Tyresövallen – formerly Bollmoravallen – the home ground of both Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns, with room for about 2,700 spectators.
Bollmora, som Tyresö centrum egentligen: Bollmora, the real name of Tyresö centrum, was a locality in its own right from 1965 to 1974, and it had 16,566 inhabitants in 2010. A few minutes away is Bollmoradalen Church, the parish church of Tyresö parish, which covers the whole municipality. Bollmora grew fast in the 1960s thanks to Lex Bollmora, a law that allowed Stockholm's housing companies to build here.

Bollmora – the real name of Tyresö centrum – was a town in its own right from 1965 to 1974 and had 16,566 residents in 2010. And a little further on, Tyresö View rises 82 metres – one of the tallest residential buildings in the county.

Boo breder ut sig på västra delen av ön: Boo spreads across the western part of the island of Värmdö, east of the Skurusundet strait. It was a town in its own right until 2015, but since then it has merged with the Stockholm urban area – so in practice, the big city has made it across the water. Not far from here is the glittering Kocktorpssjön, a small lake in the district.

Bostadshuset 79&Park, alldeles intill, ä: The residential building right next door, 79&Park, was designed by the Danish firm Bjarke Ingels Group and was nominated for Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2019. A little way off, in a 1920s warehouse in Frihamnen, the free port, the financier Robert Weil and museum director David Neuman founded what became the Magasin III art museum in 1987. Since May 2024, however, the museum no longer runs public activities in Stockholm.
Bostadshuset på Bäckebols gård byggdes 1: The farmhouse at Bäckebol was built in 1764 and gained another storey in the 1830s. South of the farm lies the Friedländer Cemetery, which has been a private burial ground since the 1770s.
The farmhouse at Bäckebol was built in 1764 and gained an extra storey in the 1830s. Just south of the farm lies the Friedländer Cemetery, a private burial ground since the 1770s.
Bostadsområdet Alphyddan byggdes 1960 ti: The Alphyddan housing area was built between 1960 and 1965 to designs by the architects Backström and Reinius, with the Svindersberg nature area as its green neighbour to the east. A little further on is Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, where Atlas Diesel made diesel engines until 1951. Today it's a cultural centre with a library and cinema. Next door, Sickla Köpkvarter has around 160 shops and restaurants.
Bostadsområdet Annedal vid Bällstaån har: The Annedal housing area by the Bällstaån stream is named after a plot of land owned in the 1880s by Anna Augusta Wickman-Olsson. Around 2,000 flats went up here between 2008 and 2013, and at its north-western end the area is rounded off by the Mattisborgen block and its tower. Across Ulvsundavägen lies Solvalla, the trotting track.
Bostadsområdet Krusboda, i området här o: The Krusboda housing estate, all around us, went up in the first half of the 1970s, between 1970 and 1975, and has a school of its own, Krusboda skola. A longer walk away is Barnsjön, a small forest lake just under nine metres deep, with a public swimming spot. It's part of the Tyresån catchment, so the water here eventually finds its way into the Tyresån river.
Bostadsområdet Myrängen-Högmora ligger i: The Myrängen-Högmora neighbourhood nestles into Kynäsberget hill, between the western end of Magelungen and lake Trehörningen. Högmora is mostly holiday cottages with a few year-round homes, and it became a district in its own right in 2018. Myrängen has terraced houses and a school for the youngest children. Beyond them, forest and hills take over – an area of national importance for outdoor recreation.
Bostadsområdet Västra Smedshagen invigde: The Västra Smedshagen housing area opened in 1987. It was designed by the architect Johan Nyrén, with four-storey buildings grouped around enclosed courtyards.
Bostadsområdet byggdes 1982–1988 på en p: The housing estate was built in 1982–1988 on a plateau around Rissne torg. With no through road it’s quiet, and some sixty sculptures by well-known Swedish artists are dotted between the buildings.
Bostadsområdet byggdes mellan 1969 och 1: The housing estate went up between 1969 and 1974, spreading south of the Alebäcken stream, which had previously marked Rävekärr's boundary. The first tenants moved in in 1973, and the school and nursery were finished in December 1974.
Bostäder ovanpå gallerian: Homes on top of the mall
Botkyrka folkhögskola har särskilt locka: Botkyrka folk high school – an adult education college – has proved especially popular with women who have been some way outside the job market. Its textile course and women's course have been a springboard into further study and working life.
Botkyrkahallen tar omkring 1 500 åskådar: Botkyrkahallen holds about 1,500 spectators, and the adjoining halls are used for table tennis, strength sports and gymnastics, among other things. Since it opened it has also been the sports hall for Brunnaskolan, whose own hall burnt down in 1996.
Botkyrkahallen, några minuter härifrån,: A few minutes from here is Botkyrkahallen, opened by King Carl XVI Gustaf in summer 2000 and home to Balrog IK's men's team. Not far off is S:t Botvids gymnasium, a sixth-form school best known for its contemporary circus programme run together with Cirkus Cirkör. Former pupils include the artist Dogge Doggelito and the politician Ibrahim Baylan.
Botten som aldrig hittades: The bottom no one ever found
Brandbilar byggda av brandmännen: Fire engines built by the firefighters
Branden och brandrean: The fire and the fire sale
Branden och den nya kyrkan: The fire and the new church
Branden som förändrade taket: The fire that changed the roof
Brandmän som flyger ut till sjöss: Firefighters who fly out to sea
Brandstation där gården brann: A fire station where the manor burned
Brann två gånger, prisades tredje: Burned twice, celebrated the third time
Branting blev 1920 Sveriges första socia: In 1920 Branting became Sweden's first Social Democratic prime minister. The following year, 1921, he shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Christian Lange for his work in the League of Nations.
Bredvid ligger U 81, som aldrig blev kla: Next to it is U 81, which was never finished. The serpent band is uneven and the lines so shallow they're hard to see. The only legible word is the man's name Ärnmund, and the carver was hardly as experienced as the master behind U 80.
Bredäng är ordentligt kuperat: Bredängss: Bredäng is seriously hilly: Bredängsskolan, the school, sits 62 metres above sea level, and Bredängshemmet, the care home, a full 67 metres. Bredängsparken, next to the centre, is one of the biggest parks in the district, and drinking alcohol has been banned there because things used to get rowdy. Bredäng Church doesn't have a building of its own – it's in a parish hall at one end of the shopping centre.
Bredängs centrum invigdes 1965 och har e: Bredäng's centre opened in 1965 and holds an important place in Stockholm's planning history. It was the first fully realised example of an all-in-one centre, with shops, a school, a library and a church grouped around the metro station.
Bremnäs är en liten by med ett lite förv: Bremnäs is a little village with a slightly confusing life in the statistics. Statistics Sweden counted it as a small locality for fifteen years – until it had grown together with its neighbour Stora Lycke, and the two suddenly became a single urban area with the double name Lycke och Bremnäs. The area belongs to Lycke parish, on the coast south-east of Marstrand, and the parish church, Lycke Church, stands not far from here.
Breviks gård, som gav området sitt namn,: Brevik farm, which gave the area its name, dated back to the 1300s. Its last main house was pulled down in 1987, and Brevik's shopping centre now stands in its place. Next to it is Blocket, built in the 1910s and one of Lidingö's oldest blocks of flats. In 1905 the farm's owner offered to pay for a small elementary school, today number 7 Banvägen. A little way off is the Abenius villa, designed by Ferdinand Boberg.

Breviks gård, the manor that gave the area its name, went back to the 14th century. Its last main building was pulled down in 1987, and Brevik centre stands there now. Next to it is Blocket, built in 1914–1915 and one of Lidingö's oldest apartment buildings. In 1905 the estate's owner offered to fund a small primary school – today Banvägen 7. Not far away is Abeniuska villan, the Abenius Villa, designed by Ferdinand Boberg.
Bristol var från början bara biograf. 19: Bristol started out as just a cinema. In 1977 it was rebuilt so it could double as a theatre, and in 2018 it became a cultural venue. The auditorium seats 144 and is run by two volunteer associations offering film, dance, music and theatre.
Bristol ägdes från början av Algot Myrgr: Bristol was originally owned by Algot Myrgren and was purely a cinema. In 1977 it was converted for theatre, and since 2018 it has been run by two non-profit associations, offering film, dance, music and theatre. The auditorium has 144 seats.
Broar var en specialitet för Bergsunds M: Bridges were a speciality of Bergsunds Mekaniska Verkstad, which supplied some 800 railway and road bridges. One of the last was the new Liljeholmsbron in 1928. In 1860 the works had more than 500 workers, and by 1902 it employed 1,075 people.
Bromma flygplats invigdes den 13 maj 193: Bromma Airport was opened by King Gustaf V on 13 May 1936 and was the first airport in Europe with asphalt runways. Its old hangars were the largest in Northern Europe in their day, and today they house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre – where the first hypermarket moved in as early as 1972.
Bromma flygplats invigdes i maj 1936 av: Bromma Airport was opened by King Gustaf V in May 1936 and was the first airport in Europe with asphalt runways. Its old hangars were the largest in northern Europe in their day, and today they house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre. The first hypermarket moved in as early as 1972.
Brommadepån, som stod klar 1944, byggdes: Brommadepån, the tram depot completed in 1944, stands where there was emergency housing from 1917, and trams from the Ängbybanan, Nockebybanan and Tvärbanan lines have all been parked here. Not far away, in the summer of 1927, no fewer than 29 brand-new villas along Ekorrvägen were put on show at the Bygge och Bo housing exhibition in Äppelviken. The garden suburb of Ulvsunda next door was originally called Kungsholms villastad.
Brommahöjden har bara tre lägenheter per: Brommahöjden has just three flats per floor to keep its silhouette slim. The white band framing the gable balconies carries on over the roof, so from a distance the building can look like an upside-down U. Some of the balcony glass is pastel-tinted to give the façade a playful touch.
Bromsten hade en egen station på järnväg: Bromsten had its own station on the Stockholm–Västerås railway, with a small centre that boasted a post office, an ironmonger’s and a milliner’s. The station closed in February 1968, just before the commuter trains to Kungsängen started running.
Bromstens gårds huvudbyggnad revs sommar: The main building of Bromsten farm was demolished in summer 1964 to make room for more traffic on Duvbovägen. The plan was to move the house to Åsögatan in Södermalm, but it turned out to be in far too poor a condition.
Bron i inskriften förde resenärerna på G: The bridge mentioned in the inscription carried travellers on Göta landsväg, the great road south, over a stream in the marshy Glömsta valley – an important link between Stockholm and southern Sweden. The carving was once painted, probably in black, red and white, and stood out clearly to everyone who passed.
Bron på vägen till Drottningholm: The bridge on the way to Drottningholm
Bron som brast under kungen: The bridge that gave way under the King
Bron som en Wallenberg betalade: The bridge a Wallenberg paid for
Bron som kallas Guldbron: The bridge they call the Golden Bridge
Bron som väntade på plank: The bridge that waited for planks
Bron är svetsad av upp till 25 millimete: The bridge is welded from stainless-steel plates up to 25 millimetres thick, which were then glass-blasted. It was made in Trollhättan and transported to Stockholm in three sections, and silver sand has been mixed into the asphalt on the deck.
Brons många liv: A bridge rebuilt again and again
Brostugan byggdes som bostad åt brovakte: Brostugan was built as a home for the bridge-keeper when Gustav III had the first bridge to Drottningholm built in 1787. His job was to open the bridge and collect tolls from those crossing, and the bridge-keeper lived here right up to 1931.
Brostugan på Kärsön har anor från 1700-t: Brostugan, the Bridge Cottage, on Kärsön dates from the 18th century and stands beside Nockebybron, a swing bridge across Lake Mälaren. The bridge has recently been given a new lease of life: the Swedish Transport Administration has moved the footpath and cycle path to the other side and added a reversible lane that switches direction with the flow of traffic. The work is part of building the Stockholm Bypass, Förbifart Stockholm.
Brotorp became part of Sundbyberg in 1949. The first residents moved in in 2007, and terraced houses, semi-detached houses and blocks of flats are still going up.
Brotorp är Sundbybergs ytmässigt minsta: Brotorp is Sundbyberg's smallest district by area, just three per cent of the municipality. For a long time the land was used by the military, and not far from here was Järva skjutfält, an army training ground on Järvafältet. Today Brotorp is Sundbyberg's share of Järvastaden, a large new urban development it shares with Solna.
Brottet blev naturminne 1972 och var nat: The quarry was declared a natural monument in 1972 and was a 1.2-hectare nature reserve from 2011 to 2016. Since 2016 it has been part of the larger Änggårdsbergen nature reserve.
Browallshof är den enda av områdets malm: Browallshof is the only one of the area’s old suburban manor houses still standing. The Clas på Hörnet inn had been closed since the 1860s, but in 1984 it reopened in the old main building.
Brunnaskolans egen idrottshall brann ned: Brunnaskolan's own sports hall burned down in 1996. Since Botkyrkahallen opened, the school has held its PE lessons there. The neighbouring rooms are also used for table tennis, strength sports and gymnastics.
Brunnsbokyrkan från 1972 ritades av Rolf: Designed by Rolf Bergh, Brunnsbo Church from 1972 is meant to recall a tent – a nod to the tabernacle the Israelites carried through the wilderness. Seen from above it forms an eight-pointed star, held up by two crossed glulam beams.
Brunnsparken är stadens hjärta för kolle: Brunnsparken is the beating heart of the city's public transport – almost every tram line passes through here. Right next to it is Gustaf Adolfs torg, with a statue of the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers, and that's why Gothenburg has canals: the Dutch knew how to build on clay.
Brunnstorpsnäs är en liten ort vid Nordr: Brunnstorpsnäs is a little village on the banks of the Nordre älv river on Hisingen, with just 87 residents in 2023. Small but important – this is where the Kornhall ferry crosses the river to Kornhall in Kungälv municipality. The village is in the former parish of Säve, around two kilometres north-west of Säve itself.
Bruno Wendels trähus ritades av arkitekt: Bruno Wendel’s wooden house was designed by the architect Adrian C. Peterson. It needed renovating as early as the beginning of the 1900s, and a major rebuild in the 1930s added 30 rooms that are still used as boarding accommodation.
Bryggan som lyftes på plats: The jetty that was lifted into place
Bryggaren som köpte godset: The brewer who bought the estate
Bryggaren som köpte grannen: The brewer who bought the neighbour
Bryggeriet lades ner 1945, men varumärke: The brewery closed in 1945, but the Club Soda brand lived on with Apotekarnes, Pripps and Carlsberg before disappearing in 2006. The spring was restored in 2009, and today you can pump up salty water with a hand pump.
Bräcke by ligger i Torsby socken, fyra k: The village of Bräcke lies in Torsby parish, four kilometres from the Kattegat coast and seven kilometres north of where the Nordre älv river meets the sea. At the Råckeröd pass, about 700 metres east of the village, stands Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft from the 1830s. It's now a local heritage museum – and it was actually moved there from a spot north of the village.
Bräcke cemetery has a grim history. Cholera hit Sweden hard in the 19th century, and the disease entered the country through Gothenburg. This cemetery was opened during the epidemic of 1834 and stayed in use until 1886, when Lundby church was completed with its own churchyard. It's now a protected ancient monument, and since 2017 it has been a memorial garden for scattering ashes.
Bräckelinjens banvall har legat nästan o: The old embankment of the Bräcke line has been left almost untouched since the tracks were removed. Gothenburg’s current comprehensive plan includes proposals to rebuild the line.
Bråvallavägens station, en bit härifrån,: Bråvallavägen station, not far from here, opened in 1909. It's a small station, with about 150 people getting on there on an ordinary winter weekday. In 2013 two trains collided there while carriages were being coupled. In the other direction is Altorp station, in use since 1910, a passing point on the single-track stretch towards Näsbypark.
Bröderna Börje och Folke Claeson fick id: The brothers Börje and Folke Claeson came up with the idea after visiting trade fairs on the Continent. They rented the Royal Tennis Hall, and the first fair opened in 1942. The exhibition halls in Älvsjö were built on a field that was once Lake Brännkyrkasjön.

The brothers Börje and Folke Claeson got the idea after visiting trade fairs in Europe. The first fair opened in 1942 in the Royal Tennis Hall and was named S:t Eriks-Mässan after Stockholm's patron saint, St Erik.
Bröderna Gert och Göran Bjerendahl var i: For several decades the brothers Gert and Göran Bjerendahl were among Sweden's top archers. Göran competed at four Olympic Games, finishing sixth at best. Gert went to two Olympics and came eighth with the Swedish team in 1988.
Bröllopsmiddag under eken: A wedding feast under the oak
Bullegummans hus ägdes en tid av Götebor: For a time, the Bun Lady's house was owned by the City of Gothenburg and used as a reception centre for refugees. The street got its present name in 1965.
Bullegummans hus är i ursprungligt skick: The Bun Lady's house survives in its original state, and the hatch in the wall where she sold her buns was still there in 2011. For a time the house was owned by the City of Gothenburg and served as a reception centre for refugees.
Bulleluckan finns kvar: The bun hatch is still there
Bullhuset blev flyktingsluss: The bun house became a refugee centre
Buss längs Söder och ut till Mälarhöjden: A bus ride across Södermalm and out to Mälarhöjden, where Jakobs stege (Jacob's Ladder) leads down to Lake Mälaren and the Bellmanskällan spring bubbles. On the way back, hop off on Södermalm for the highest natural viewpoint in the inner city.
Buss och båt till stugan: By bus and boat to the cabin
Buss till Ropsten, Lidingöbanan till AGA: Bus to Ropsten, the Lidingö line to AGA's yellow optics tower, and then a long boat trip along the shores of Lidingö, Nacka and Djurgården back to Nybroplan.
Bussarna mot Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsu: Buses to Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsund and Tjörn leave from the travel centre, and right next door is Kongahälla Center, with around a hundred shops and restaurants, opened in 2019. The E6 motorway roars past alongside. A little further away is Oasen, a swimming pool and ice rink built after the old public baths burned down. It has a 25-metre pool and a rehab pool with warmer water.
Bussen går via Sickla och Nacka kvarn, d: The bus runs via Sickla and Nacka kvarn, where the Nacka ström stream drops 18 metres in 500 metres.
Bussen går över Kungsholmen förbi Kungsh: The bus crosses Kungsholmen, passing Kungsholmstorg, where Otto Strandman's fountain sculpture Vesslan (the Weasel) has stood since 1912.
Busslinjen som började 1922: The bus route that began in 1922
Busstation under bron: A bus station under the bridge
Bussterminal ovanpå spåren: A bus terminal above the tracks
Bussterminalen ritades av den norske ark: The bus terminal was designed by the Norwegian architect Niels Torp and opened in 1996. The walls and roof are all glass and steel, forming a bright waiting hall 150 metres long. The same year it won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award.
Bussterminalen vid tunnelbanan togs i br: The bus terminal by the metro opened in 1968, mainly for buses to Ekerö. It replaced the old terminus for the Mälaröbussarna buses at Kronobergsparken near Fridhemsplan in the city centre.
Butiksbiträdet som gifte in sig: The shop assistant who married in
Bygden här på sydöstra Färingsö har gaml: The countryside here in south-eastern Färingsö has a long history. Mörby village can be traced back to the mid-1400s, and neighbouring Ekeby is mentioned as early as 1342, when Eskil Petersson and his wife Cecilia exchanged land with Vårfruberga convent. At Troxhammar stands a Viking Age granite runestone a full 2.2 metres tall.
Byggd av stenen på platsen: Built from the stone on site
Byggd på stadens sankaste plats: Built on the city's lowest ground
Byggdes muren av krigsfångar?: Was the wall built by prisoners of war?
Bygget av Huvudstaleden stannade av bris: Work on the Huvudsta road stalled for lack of money and after calls for a 1,000-metre tunnel under Huvudsta. A roughly 200-metre stub of motorway was left behind and is now known as the 'ruin motorway'. Student barracks used to stand there.
Bygget av Partille Arena startade den 5: Construction of Partille Arena began on 5 December 2013 and took three years. Once finished, it replaced the old Partillebohallen sports hall, which was finally demolished in April 2017.
Bygget kom igång senast 1773 och det mes: Building was under way by 1773 at the latest, and most of it was finished by 1777. Then Carlberg set off on a journey abroad lasting almost five years, which held up the final stages. The manor wasn't ready to move into until 1780.
Bygget slukade 55 000 kubikmeter betong: The construction swallowed 55,000 cubic metres of concrete and 2,225,000 bricks. The three factory units were 1,100 metres long in total, and the four-million-square-metre site was then the largest industrial site in Sweden.
Bygget slukade 55 000 kubikmeter betong,: Construction swallowed 55,000 cubic metres of concrete, 3,380 tonnes of reinforcing steel and 2,225,000 bricks. The three factory units were 1,100 metres long altogether, and the site was then the largest industrial plot in Sweden.

Construction swallowed 55,000 cubic metres of concrete, 3,380 tonnes of reinforcing steel and 2,225,000 bricks. The three factory units were 1,100 metres long in total, and the 4-million-square-metre site was then the largest industrial plot in Sweden.
Bygget startade 1960 och centrumet invig: Construction began in 1960, and the centre opened in 1965 as one of the most modern in the region. The architect Sture Frölén designed both the layout and every single building, commercial and public alike.
Byggföretaget SIAB levererade sina hus i: The construction firm SIAB delivered its houses in large prefabricated sections assembled on site, while Skånska Cementgjuteriet built its houses on the spot. Skånska's areas turned out more varied and better suited to the terrain. As the houses were built with state loans, the footprint could not exceed 140 square metres.
Byggherrarna längs Odengatan 3–13 kom öv: The developers along Odengatan 3–13 agreed on a uniform streetscape, a reaction against the motley villas of Lärkstaden. They all used dark-red Helsingborg brick but varied the details. In 1912 Svenska Dagbladet wrote of a uniformity "previously unknown in Stockholm's architectural history".
Byggmästaren Andreas Gustaf Sällström ro: The master builder Andreas Gustaf Sällström bought the estate at auction in 1889 for 55,000 kronor. At the same time he was building the new Royal Opera, and when King Gustav III's old opera house was demolished he moved valuable interior details here.
Byggmästaren som byggde villan på Florag: The builder who put up the villa at Floragatan 4 in 1881 obeyed the rule requiring villas along the street. But tucked well out of sight on the plot, he also built a three-storey block of flats, a stable and a coach house.
Byggnaden ritades av Erik Ahnborg, och g: The building was designed by Erik Ahnborg, and its glass facades in various shades of blue became a familiar Sollentuna landmark. Hall II opened in 1987, adding another 6,000 square metres of exhibition space.
Byggt mitt i en järnåldersby: Built in the middle of an Iron Age village
Byggt på gammal sjöbotten: Built on an old lake bed
Byn Krokslätt nämns redan på 1300-talet,: The village of Krokslätt is mentioned as early as the 14th century, but nobody knows for sure what the name means. It may come from the many taverns (krogar) here – in the 18th century it was spelled Krogslätt. It could also refer to the bends (krokar) of the Mölndalsån river, or to a medieval personal name, Krok.
Byn bjuder på ett litet vikingatida gall: The village has its own little gallery of Viking Age stones. One runestone, U 44, signed by the carver Snare, vanished some time between around 1795 and 1850 and only resurfaced in 1981, in pieces that were then fitted back together – it's more than two metres tall. Another, U 43, has stood at the entrance to a farm since 1937, and on a boulder set into the ground, a man called Saxe had runes carved in memory of his mother.
Byn har rötter i sena järnåldern, vid en: The village dates back to the late Iron Age, on a sea inlet that post-glacial land rise slowly turned into Edsviken bay. The inlet may have given it the name ‘Myr-byn’, the bog village. In 1952 the county council bought 8.7 hectares of the farm’s land, and Danderyd Hospital grew up there.
Byn som gav kyrkan dess namn nämns 1474: The village that gave the church its name is mentioned in 1474 as Herlandæ by. In 1925 the ruin was excavated and restored at the city's expense, and the memorial stone calls it Gothenburg's oldest Christian monument.
Byn som låg här före torget: The village that came before the square
Bynamnet Sörred finns belagt redan 1388: The village name Sörred is recorded as early as 1388, as Surfua rudi. The first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning something like a careless fellow or sloven, and the second from the Old Swedish ryd, cleared land.
Bynamnet finns belagt redan 1567, då som: The village name is recorded as early as 1567, as Skinteboda or simply Skintan. It has several possible meanings, including good soil, furrow, pit, ditch or sunken lane. The word skinta in the sense of good soil crops up in several places around Askim.
Bysten av Carl Michael Bellman avtäcktes: The bust of the poet and songwriter Carl Michael Bellman was unveiled in 1829. The year before, the court confectioner Carlmark had opened a café here, and it was named Bellmansro – 'Bellman's Rest' – after the bust. The restaurant burned down in 1955, but the spot has kept the name. Next door is the Oakhill mansion, which Ferdinand Boberg designed for Prince Wilhelm in 1910. It has been the Italian Embassy since 1926.

The bust of Carl Michael Bellman was unveiled in 1829. The year before, the court confectioner Carlmark had opened a café here. The bust made it popular, and the place later took the name Bellmansro, 'Bellman's Rest'. The restaurant burned down in 1955, but the spot still goes by that name. Next door is the Oakhill palace, designed by Ferdinand Boberg for Prince Wilhelm in 1910, and home to the Italian Embassy since 1926.
Byt vid Slussen. Vid Mariatorget passera: Change at Slussen. At Mariatorget you pass the fountain Tor's Fishing, from 1903.
Bäckahagens skola byggdes i etapper mell: Bäckahagen school was built in stages between 1953 and 1968 to designs by the architect David Dahl, and it came with its own caretaker's flat and even its own dental clinic. Bandhagen as a whole is a fine example of folkhem architecture – the style of Sweden's post-war welfare state – with low blocks arranged around leafy courtyards and the odd taller tower block to break things up and add variety.
Bäckebol Center är ett av Hisingens stor: Bäckebol Center is one of Hisingen's big retail parks, with around twenty shops spread over no less than 95,000 square metres. Shops come and go – one left in 2010, only to return three years later. A short way off flows the Lärjeån river, which rises north of Gråbo and joins the Göta älv river at Lärjeholm.
Bäckebols gård, en bit härifrån, är en h: Bäckebol Manor, a short way from here, is a manor house and former noble estate beside a stream. Work on the stone house was begun in 1764 by Johan Oliveholm, a weighmaster and ironworks owner, and the manor was restored in 1943–1944. It has been a listed building since the 1960s, and Gothenburg's smallest cemetery belongs to the estate too.

Not far from here is Bäckebols gård, a manor house and former estate beside a stream. The weighmaster and ironworks owner Johan Oliveholm began building it in stone in 1764, and the house was restored in 1943–1944. It has been a listed building since 9 January 1969 – and the estate even includes Gothenburg's smallest churchyard.
Bäckebols herrgård började byggas i sten: Work on the stone manor house at Bäckebol began in 1764, commissioned by Johan Oliveholm, a weighmaster and ironworks owner. A limestone staircase leads up to the front door, half-moon lunette windows sit high in the gables, and a plaque in the hall records how the house came to be built.
Bäckebols kyrksal invigdes på trettonded: Bäckebol's church hall opened on Twelfth Day 1971, and its last services were held on 30 May 2021. The end wall was decorated with a metal sculpture showing scenes from the life of Jesus. The congregation moved to Brunnsbo Church and Backa Church.
Bällsta är en trädgårdsstad av små trähu: Bällsta is a garden suburb of small wooden houses from the 1940s. Around 200 of these cottages were built by their owners themselves, using materials and instructions supplied by the City of Stockholm's small-house office. A little further on is Solvalla, Sweden's national trotting stadium, with room for 35,000 spectators and home to Elitloppet, one of the biggest harness races in the world. On a hill nearby stands the radar tower that locals call Golfbollen, the Golf Ball.
Bällstavägen följer en gammal väg från B: Bällstavägen follows an old road from Bällsta bridge to a ferry landing at Tyska botten. It was laid out around 1675 and cut right across the burial ground, probably destroying some of the graves.
Bällstaån är 10,5 kilometer lång men fal: Bällstaån is 10.5 kilometres long but drops only about ten metres, so it has no fast-flowing stretches. Almost all of it has been straightened, and only a short section near Hjulsta and Tensta still follows its original course.
Bänk vid vattnet med utsikt mot Långholm: A waterside bench looking out to Långholmen
Bärby Korsväg är bara cirka 650 meter lå: Bärby Korsväg is only about 650 metres long, running between Kongahällavägen and Svensbyvägen in the little village of Bärby. But the village has a grander past than the road suggests: from 1824 to 1887 Bärby was the court seat for the Västra and Östra Hising districts, where cases from much of Hisingen were tried.
Både Sparreholms bilmuseum och Skokloste: Both the Sparreholm car museum and the Skokloster motor museum have claimed that their Cadillac was the one in the accident. The royal court had three identical cars, and according to one motoring historian there’s no way of telling which it was. The press photos show no number plates, just a royal crown on the boot.
Båten Rescue Mignon Wallenius, en gåva f: The rescue boat Rescue Mignon Wallenius, donated by the Wallenius shipping companies in 2005, was stationed at Malevik in summer for call-outs off Särö. Today the station's boats include Rescue Josephine, an 11.8-metre enclosed vessel built in 2021.
Båten lägger till vid Allmänna gränd och: The boat calls at Allmänna gränd and passes Saltsjöqvarn, Finnboda and Kvarnholmen on its way out towards the harbour entrance.
Båten lägger till vid Dalénum, Nacka str: The boat calls at Dalénum, Nacka strand with Milles' water arch, Kvarnholmen and Finnboda before reaching Nybroplan.
Båtsmanstorpet byggdes i början av 1700-: The sailor’s croft was built in the early 1700s for a seaman in the navy. Between 1892 and 1907 it was the schoolhouse for local children. A photo from the early 1900s shows two schoolmistresses and 20 children.
Båtsmännen hette alltid Myrman: The boatmen were always called Myrman
Båtsmännen här fick soldatnamnet Tupp, s: The navy boatmen here were given the soldier's name Tupp (Cockerel), which passed on to each new boatman. Other names in the same company included Lax, Örn, Mild and Släthår. A boatman was entitled to a cottage, a small barn and a byre for two cows.
Båtturen tillbaka går via Skeppsholmen,: The boat trip back goes via Skeppsholmen, the navy's old island.
Bö herrgård omnämns redan 1485, och 1746: Bö manor is first mentioned in 1485, and in 1746 none other than Carl Linnaeus came to visit and wrote about the house and its garden. He's said to have planted a pear tree there. Closer by is Örgryte New Church, built in the Gothic Revival style with a tower almost 60 metres tall. It got electric lighting in 1908 – the same year as its neighbour, Bö School.
Börja bland växthus och dammar i Botanis: Start among the glasshouses and ponds of the Botanical Garden and finish out among the islands. The tram carries you from the city's green lungs to the marina and the archipelago.
Började i Malmstens egen skola: It began in Malmsten's own school
Började i en tennishall: It started in a tennis hall
Canadahusen byggdes 1907–1908 efter enge: The Canada houses were built in 1907–1908 on an English model, originally meant for the craftsmen who were building the garden suburb. They are just 5.75 metres wide. Two similar blocks, Chile and Peru, were planned but never built.
Canonhuset, några minuter härifrån, bygg: Canonhuset, a few minutes from here, was built for the electronics company Canon and houses offices, a warehouse and a workshop. It's one of the few examples of Swedish high-tech architecture and has the City Museum's highest heritage rating. A little further on is Sätra pistol range, which – despite its name – is in Bredäng, and is the only range of its kind in the whole of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
Capitol öppnade 31 juli 1926. Över entré: Capitol opened on 31 July 1926. Over the entrance was a canopy on columns with capitals shaped like lotus flowers. The oval auditorium was pink, the curtain blue and brown, and there were 639 seats.
Carl Gustaf Wrangel hade sex stora bygge: Carl Gustaf Wrangel had six major building projects on the go at the same time, among them Skokloster. When he died in 1676 work here ground to a halt, and it was only completed by the next owner, Baron Erik Lovisin.
Carl Johan Bernadotte var vice vd för An: Carl Johan Bernadotte was deputy CEO of Anglo-Nordic Traktor, which built workshops here in 1953. He also helped persuade the American firm Sundstrand to move production here. At its peak the factory employed about 500 people and was Huddinge's largest employer, but it closed in 1974.
Carl Malmsten tillbringade barndomens so: Furniture designer Carl Malmsten spent his childhood summers here, as his grandfather Cadier had bought Övre Karlsro. He began renting the house from his aunt in 1920 and bought it five years later. He built studios, made much of the fitted interior himself and, in 1930, stripped off the fretwork gingerbread trim in favour of a more classical look.
Carl Michael Bellman besökte gärna Fågel: The poet and songwriter Carl Michael Bellman liked to visit Fågelsången farm by the lake Trekanten. His younger sister Fredrika Eleonora lived there with her husband, the palace treasurer Georg Stiernhoff.
Carl Milles Flöjtspelande ängel, ett av: Flöjtspelande ängel, the Flute-Playing Angel, is one of Carl Milles's late works, originally meant for the Saint Martin Fountain, and you'll find it in several places, including by Lidingöbron, the Lidingö Bridge. At the landing of the old Lidingö Bridge stands a small building by Ivar Tengbom, opened in 1925 and used as a waiting shelter until 1967. It's such a windy spot that people nicknamed it Vindarnas tempel, the Temple of the Winds.
Carl Milles studerade elefanter i djurpa: Carl Milles studied elephants at the Jardin des Plantes zoo in Paris in 1898. They were clearly one of his favourite animals, giving him the chance to work with volume and mass.
Carl-Erik Lindell var den siste på Fulle: Carl-Erik Lindell was the last person to farm at Fullersta. He gave it up and from 1902 sold 'Lovely plots for villas and homes of your own'. The brochure stressed that the trip from Stockholm Central took just half an hour.
Carlanderska sjukhuset intill uppfördes: Carlanderska sjukhuset, the hospital next door, was built in 1927 to designs by Arvid Bjerke and was originally called Carlanderska sjukhemmet, the Carlander nursing home. A little way off, in Renströmsparken park, stands Solringen, the Sun Ring, a 4.4-metre ring by Claes Hake. It has a twin: a version in patinated bronze went up that same year, 1993, in Hjørring in Denmark.
Centralpalatset är ett typexempel på sve: Centralpalatset is a textbook example of Swedish National Romanticism, with a dark brick facade, bay windows and a steep mansard roof. On the west side rises a corner tower bearing the year 1913. The municipality has given the building its blue rating, the highest heritage grade.
Centrum och bostäderna byggdes i etapper: The centre and the homes were built in stages between 1983 and 1991. The culture centre houses a library, a gallery and Erskinesalen, a hall for theatre, concerts, talks and films.
Centrum pryds av 22 konstverk av bland a: The centre is decorated with 22 works of art by artists including Peter Dahl, Petter Hellsing and Asmund Arle. Huddinge centrum is twinned with Jokkmokk in Swedish Lapland, and every year it hosts the Jokkmokk Days – complete with an ice sculpture competition.
Centrumet byggdes mitt i järnåldersbyn T: The shopping centre was built right in the middle of the Iron Age village of Tibble gård, one of the densest archaeological sites in Sweden. Many burial grounds were excavated, and by 2000 only a few remained.
Centrumet hette egentligen Forum Nacka,: The centre was officially called Forum Nacka, but most people called it Nacka Forum – and on 13 September 2010 it changed its name to match. Today its four floors hold 123 shops and 18 restaurants and cafés.
Centrumet invigdes 1965 som Bollmora cen: The centre opened in 1965 as Bollmora Centrum, a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In the early 1990s it was rebuilt as a shopping mall and renamed Tyresö Centrum in 1992. A major fire in several of the buildings delayed the reopening.
Centrumet invigdes 1965 under namnet Bol: The centre opened in 1965 as Bollmora centrum, then a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. It was rebuilt as a shopping mall and reopened as Tyresö Centrum in 1992.
Centrumet ritades av den danskfödde arki: The centre was designed by the Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann, who was given a free hand. The result was low façades of glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond in the middle. Kampmann also designed the nearby slab blocks.
Chalmers började som Chalmersska slöjdsk: Chalmers started life as the Chalmersska slöjdskolan, a craft school. Under William Chalmers' will it was to be an industrial school for poor children who had learned to read and write. It wasn't called a university of technology until 1937.
Chalmers tekniska högskola grundades 182: Chalmers University of Technology was founded in 1829 with money left by William Chalmers, who had worked for the Swedish East India Company. All around you is the Johanneberg campus, where thousands of engineers are trained every year.
Chapmans torg fick sitt namn 1939 efter: Chapmans torg was named in 1939 after the legendary sea captain Charles Chapman, who worked here in Majorna in the 18th century. Many of the people who lived in Majorna once earned their living in the shipyards and the harbour.
Charabang på nya vägen: A charabanc on the new road
Charlottenburg var från början Frösunda: Charlottenburg started out as Frösunda croft, which appears on a map from the 1670s. Adolf Fredrik Wijnbladh rebuilt it as a house with nine rooms in a row and named the place after his wife, Charlotte Arbin.
Charlottenburg var från början ett torp: Charlottenburg started out as a croft belonging to Stora Frösunda. In 1801 Adolf Fredrik Wijnbladh rebuilt it as a house with nine rooms in an enfilade and named it after his wife, Charlotte Arbin. By the entrance is a stone labyrinth – a 'jungfrudans', or maiden's dance – from 1990.
Choklad, konst och plask! Marabouparken: Chocolate, art and splashing about! Marabouparken is open to everyone. By the 1970s its sculpture collection had grown to sixteen works, and the paddling pool is a big draw for families. The art gallery opened in 2010 and is built underground, next to the old cocoa laboratory. Nearby, Sundbyberg Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb and has burnt bones from a Viking Age grave on display.

Chocolate, art and splashing about! Marabouparken is open to everyone, with a sculpture collection that had grown to sixteen works by the 1970s and a paddling pool that draws families with children. The art gallery opened in 2010 and is built underground, next to the old cocoa laboratory building. The park was laid out from 1937 by Sven Hermelin and Inger Wedborn on the site of Sundbyberg's old manor farm from 1785.
Chokladfabriken Marabou kom till Sundbyb: The Marabou chocolate factory came to Sundbyberg in 1916 and shaped the town for decades. Marabou is now in Upplands Väsby, but Marabouparken remains and is known for its art gallery. The metro station, from 1985, lies 26 metres down in the rock, with a connection to the commuter trains.
Cisternen rymde 400 kubikmeter vatten fr: The tank held 400 cubic metres of water drawn from the ridge at Ulriksdal. But the wells were pumped so hard that brackish water from Brunnsviken seeped in. As early as 1926 Sundbyberg switched to water from Lake Mälaren, and the tower was left with no purpose.
City ritades av Curt Strehlenert på HSB:: The City cinema was designed by Curt Strehlenert at the HSB architects’ office. The auditorium was styled as an open-air theatre, with dark blue walls and ceiling and lighting that looked like a starry sky. It had 500 red armchair seats, and the name shone out over the square in big red neon letters.
City var en av flera förortsbiografer fr: City was one of several suburban cinemas of its day. Forum in Årsta centrum opened in 1951, Fontänen in Vällingby in 1956, and in 1961 both Fanfaren in Farsta and Reflexen in Kärrtorp opened their doors.
Clarebergs gård hette först Berg. När ko: Clarebergs gård was originally called Berg. When Magnus Lagerström, a councillor of commerce and director of the Swedish East India Company, took it over in 1735, he renamed it after his wife, Clara.
Coldinuorden fick fästningen Nya Chartag: In 1786 the Coldinu Order, a convivial society, was given the 'fortress' Nya Chartago by the wine steward of the Pelikan tavern. It was a round tower with a saluting battery, where members sailed out to play at sieges and battles. In 1797 the fortress was ceded, and the commandant was granted free passage out with his men and ten cannon.
Containerslottet med vindbrygga: The container castle with a drawbridge
Dag Ribbings tio radhus i rött tegel ble: Dag Ribbing's ten red-brick terraced houses were ready to move into in 1950 and quickly became popular with staff at the nearby Karolinska Hospital. As a result, most of the households in the housing association were doctors' families.
Dagens Jacobsdal byggdes 1798 i timmer o: Today's Jacobsdal was built of timber in 1798 and still has its 18th- and 19th-century joinery and tiled stoves. The house is let as a home through the Royal Court's own housing queue. Since the 1960s Bergshamravägen has separated it from the neighbouring house, Karlshäll.
Dagens Lundby nya kyrka invigdes 1996. F: Today's Lundby New Church was consecrated in 1996. Its model was a simple medieval Italian country church, a basilica. It's built of red brick in various shades on a granite base, with floors of limestone and oak. The winning competition entry was called "A Journey Through Time and Space".
Dagens bro byggdes av Bergsunds mekanisk: Today's bridge was built by the Bergsund engineering works and finished in time for the Stockholm Exhibition of 1897. It was made wide enough for the Strandvägen trams, and its cast-iron railing is decorated with stylised plants.
Dagens kyrka ritades av Arvid Bjerke och: Today's church was designed by Arvid Bjerke and consecrated on Palm Sunday 1923. It's built of rough-hewn augen gneiss quarried right here, and a weathercock tops the copper cap of the tower.
Dalen ner mot havet: The valley down to the sea
Dalens sjukhus från 1977 är ett välbevar: Dalen Hospital, completed in 1977, is a well-preserved example of the late modernist architecture of its day and an important piece of urban planning history.
