A little way off, on the Nytorp field, stood the croft of Nytorp, which belonged to the Hammarby estate. It disappeared in the early 1960s to make way for the Nytorpsbadet pool. The Dalen residential area is made up of 14 courtyard blocks, and the City Museum has classed the whole of it as culturally valuable.
Dalkullorna som skötte gravarna: The Dalarna girls who tended the graves
Daléns första fyr med solventil: Dalén's first lighthouse with a sun valve
Damm som skyddar Mälaren: A pond that protects Lake Mälaren
Dammen som blev en gångbro: The weir that became a footbridge
Dammen var en myr: The pond was once a bog
Danderyds gymnasium: Danderyds gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Danderyds kyrka ligger ett par minuter b: Danderyd church is a couple of minutes away, right next to the busy E18 towards Norrtälje. By the gate stands the runestone U 127, one of the Jarlabanke stones. South of the churchyard is Berga gård, a farm that probably goes back to the Viking Age, with an 18th-century manor house. And beside the church is Klockare Malm's Chapel, used for smaller christenings, weddings and funerals.
Danderyds kyrka, en bit härifrån, gömmer: Danderyd Church, a little way from here, hides several Viking Age runestone fragments. One of them, the top of a sandstone runestone, was discovered as recently as 1938 in the Banér family vault during restoration work, and it's now mounted on the inside of the church's west wall. Just west of the church stands another runestone, U 131, between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall.
Daniel Asplund kom till Stockholm som ni: Daniel Asplund arrived in Stockholm at nineteen with nothing to his name and became a wholesale merchant in 1781. At Bergsund he founded a starch works, a bleachery and a dye works. He built homes for his workers and in 1793 started a school for their children.
Danskar och svenskar på Rya Nabbe: Danes and Swedes at Rya Nabbe
Danskarna erövrade Älvsborg 1612 efter a: The Danes captured Älvsborg fortress in 1612 after bombarding it from Sannabacken. Under the peace of 1613 the ransom was set at one million riksdaler in silver, paid in four instalments over six years. The Danes didn't leave the fortress until 1619.
Danvikens begravningsplats invigdes 1834: Danviken Cemetery opened in 1834 as a burial ground for the poor and for cholera victims, and many people from Sicklaön and eastern Södermalm were buried here too. The last burial took place in 1956, but a number of gravestones and crosses survive.
Danvikshem byggdes 1912–1915 av Kreuger: Danvikshem was built in 1912–1915 by Kreuger & Toll in the National Romantic style, with Aron Johansson as architect. The monumental building at the sea approach to Stockholm was designed for more than 400 residents.
De 160 försäljningsplatserna i de gamla: The 160 market pitches in the former horse stables are known as spiltor, or stalls. You'll find everything here from glassware, china and books to toys, fabrics, tools and work equipment.
De 75 atriumhusen från 1960 kallades i f: Locals nicknamed the 75 atrium houses from 1960 'the rabbit hutches'. The street names all have a coin theme – Växelmyntsgatan, Pennygången and Fyrktorget – and when new link houses went up in 2012, their street became Kastmyntsgatan.
De eleganta villorna i Lärkstaden byggde: The elegant villas of Lärkstaden were built around 1912. Prime Minister Karl Staaff lived at Tofslärkan 3 from 1912 to 1915, and the villa next door, Tofslärkan 6, has been the Latvian Embassy since 1995. The plots were tiny: Tofslärkan 3 measured just 292 square metres, including a nine-metre strip for the garden.
De fem rödmålade stugorna längs Kvastmak: The interiors of the five red-painted cottages along Kvastmakartrappan, the Broom-Maker’s Steps, weren’t renovated until the early 2000s – and running water and indoor toilets were deliberately left out. Instead, new outdoor privies and water pumps were put in the yards, and the walls were given freshly printed wallpaper in 1920s patterns. The cottages may only be used as studios.
De femton husen är grupperade kring en g: The fifteen buildings are grouped around a shared courtyard, six facing Kärrtorpsvägen and nine facing the new Sophie Sagers gata. The courtyard doubles as a public park, and the rendered façades come in warm, muted colours.
De flesta gatorna här har namn efter tid: Most of the streets here are named after ways of measuring time – Tideräkningsgatan (Calendar Reckoning Street), Kalendervägen, Halvsekelsgatan (Half-Century Street). The squares follow the theme too: Årstidstorget, Citytorget, Kortedala torg and Kalendertorget.
De flesta gatunamn i Hagsätra kommer frå: Most of the street names in Hagsätra come from places in the province of Närke. Olshammarsgatan, for instance, is named after Olshammar in Askersund municipality.
De flesta villorna längs Segeltorpsvägen: Most of the houses along Segeltorpsvägen went up in the 1940s and 1950s. The owners built them with their own hands, using instructions and materials from the City of Stockholm.
De första arbetarhusen i Tallbacken var: The first workers' houses in Tallbacken were red wooden buildings resembling farm labourers' row houses. They were built of rough planks insulated with wood shavings and heated with firewood. The privies were in a separate building, the laundry was down by the lake, and electricity didn't arrive until 1922.
De första eleverna gick vidare till yrke: The first students went on to become organ builders, sailmakers, goldsmiths, mirror makers, lithographers and sugar refiners. Teaching was meant to be practical rather than strictly academic – and free of charge.
De första färjorna var roddfärjor. År 18: The first ferries were rowing boats. In 1874 Eriksbergs Mekaniska Verkstad delivered a 12-horsepower steam launch, nicknamed Bonnafröjda. The ferry that replaced it in 1927 came from Stockholm, where it had carried trams across to Lidingö.
De första företagen här, Billman-Regulat: The first companies here – Billman-Regulator, LM Ericsson and ASEA – all worked with electricity. So the blocks were given names like Anoden, Katoden, Batteriet and Ackumulatorn (Anode, Cathode, Battery and Accumulator), and the streets are called Jonvägen, Elektronvägen and Regulatorvägen.
De första hallarna var långa industrihal: The first halls were long industrial sheds in corrugated metal, orange with blue details. The cladding has since been replaced with aluminium-coloured panels. The fair's landmark is the 19-storey hotel from 2006.
De första hyresgästerna flyttade in 1969: The first tenants moved in in 1969. From 1984, for about ten years, the estate underwent a major renewal: the courtyards were redesigned and some buildings were given colourful façades.
De första kolonisterna kom i maj 1936, o: The first allotment holders arrived in May 1936, and by the end of the year around 200 plots were already in use. By the early 1950s, every single plot had a cottage on it.
De första mässhallarna liknade långa ind: The first exhibition halls looked like long industrial sheds, with façades of corrugated orange metal and blue details. Over the years the orange cladding has been replaced by aluminium-coloured panels.
De första patienterna flyttades in den 1: The first patients moved in on 14 May 1924, but the official opening didn't take place until 3 September. The first chief physician was Dr Torild Lundén.
De första rödakorssystrarna utbildades f: The first Red Cross nurses were trained mainly to care for the wounded in war. As early as 1897 two Swedish Red Cross nurses were sent to the war in Greece, and in 1912 the first Red Cross ambulance was sent there.
De första skolorna i området byggdes som: The area's first schools were single-storey pavilions. Tomtebergsskolan opened in spring 1963 in eight pavilions, and Slottsbergsskolan on Munspelsgatan was put together from prefabricated pavilions in time for autumn 1965.
De första villorna i Birka byggdes kring: The first villas in Birka were built around 1900 as large two-and-a-half-storey houses for several families, most of them clad in wooden panelling and many with glazed verandas. The carpenter Arvid Samsiö helped build Villa Birka, which gave the area its name.
De gamla trähusen runt berget: The old wooden houses on the hill
De japanska körsbärsträden planterades i: The avenue of Japanese cherry trees was planted during the 1997–98 makeover, when Stockholm was European Capital of Culture, and the large pond was added at the same time. The ice rink has been here since November 1962.
De nya husen ritades av Brunnberg & Fors: The new buildings were designed by Brunnberg & Forshed, with facades of rust-red Corten steel that match the 1940s brick. City architect Karolina Keyzer said they show that architecture doesn’t have to shout or be expensive to make its mark.
De röda neonglasögonen satt först ovanfö: The red neon glasses originally hung above the entrance and were made by Morneon, one of Sweden's biggest illuminated-sign makers. When the lettered sign arrived in the 1960s, the glasses moved to the right-hand side of the facade.
De röda tegelhusen byggdes 1944–1949 som: The red-brick buildings went up in 1944–1949 as barnrikehus – subsidised housing for large families – designed by Ernst Hawerman and Nils G:son Friberg for Stockholmshem. They're among the last of their kind built in Sweden.
De som fick lotterna i den andra etappen: Those who got plots in the second phase often came from allotment areas in Stockholm's southern suburbs that had been cleared, and many brought their old cottages with them. Unlike the functionalist cabins, these were often in a rustic folk style and looked like little crofts.
De tre vingarna: De tre vingarna, the Three Wings
De två funkisvillorna från 1932 planerad: The two functionalist villas from 1932 were designed for families with several children and domestic help. They had flower rooms, a maid's room in the attic and, in the basement, a garage for the master of the house's car. Today both are private homes.
De två hemmanen i Sandbäck hette Prästgå: Sandbäck's two farmsteads were called Prästgården and Kullen. From 1677 the curate of Fässberg, Per Hermenius, lived at Prästgården. In 1777 Kullen belonged to Martin Holterman, and after his death his widow gave the farm's income to the parish school.

Sandbäck's two farmsteads were called Prästgården and Kullen. In 1673 Prästgården came under Johan Gabriel Stenbock, and from 1677 the Fässberg chaplain lived there. When Kullen's owner Martin Holterman died, his widow donated the farm's income to the parish school.
De två små likadana husen norr om fontän: The two small matching buildings north of the fountain were built in 1924–1925 in the Nordic classicism of the 1920s, to designs by Hugo Jahnke. One was a kiosk, the other a taxi stand.
De yttersta skären sköljs ständigt över: The outermost skerries are constantly washed by salt water and support little more than lichens and salt-tolerant grasses. On the larger Amundö islands people even farmed, and in sheltered spots sessile oak, silver birch and black alder grow.
De åtta studenthusen på Bosön står i sol: The eight student houses on Bosön island fan out around a small hill, and each has a sporting name: Bollen, Bågen, Båten, Hjälmen, Kubban, Kulan, Skidan and Värjan – the Ball, the Bow, the Boat, the Helmet, the Kubb, the Shot, the Ski and the Foil. The laundry on the hill is called Kompassen, the Compass.
Delfinkar och 3,6 km staket: Dolphin basins and 3.6 km of railings
Delvis under Södertäljevägen, en bit här: Partly beneath the main road, Södertäljevägen, a little way from here, lies Svarta Löt – one of the best-known medieval assembly sites in the area, where local courts, or “things”, were already being held when Stockholm was founded. It's thought to have been near the croft of Eriksberg, once called Tingsta, on the Kumla estate. Older still is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone burial chamber from the late Stone Age, dated to around 1800 BC. Only seven graves of this kind are known in the whole of Stockholm County.
Den 1 april 1949 fotograferade trafikins: On 1 April 1949 the traffic inspector Einar Lundh photographed the first train to switch onto the new double track between Baggeby and AGA. The picture shows the station name on the ridge of the roof and a Linderoths station clock on top. Both are gone today.
Den 1 december 2018 invigdes folkbibliot: On 1 December 2018 the public library Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature, opened in one of the tower blocks in the middle of the square. It replaced Gamlestaden's old library in the community centre, which closed that autumn.
Den 1 januari 1914 förbjöds försäljning: On 1 January 1914 the sale of fresh meat on the square was banned for reasons of hygiene. Soon fish, butter, cheese, bread and cooked food were banned too, and many traders moved into the market halls. That left the market gardeners and the fruit, vegetable and flower sellers.
Den 1 oktober 1930 började spårvagnslinj: On 1 October 1930 tram line 19 began serving the area. It ran on the same embankment that the metro line of the same number uses today. On 9 September 1951 the trams were replaced by the metro.
Den 12 mars 1992 skenade ett strömlöst s: On 12 March 1992 a tram that had lost power ran away backwards down Guldhedsgatan and Aschebergsgatan at an estimated 100 km/h. At Vasaplatsen it derailed and ploughed across the stop. Thirteen people were killed and 29 injured.
Den 14 april 1993 rasade marken vid Agne: On 14 April 1993, the ground gave way at the Agnesberg industrial estate on the eastern bank of the Göta älv river, not far from here. A ship's pilot spotted the landslide at nine o'clock – by which time a patch of land about 20 by 50 metres had already slid into the river. The slide reached right up to an industrial building, and several smaller slips followed later that day.
Den 15 juli 2008 rånades Casino Cosmopol: On 15 July 2008 Casino Cosmopol was robbed – the first time a casino had ever been held up in Sweden. Its four floors held around thirty gaming tables and some 350 slot machines.
Den 18 juli 1994 firade herrlandslaget i: On 18 July 1994 the Swedish men's football team celebrated their World Cup bronze medals in Rålambshovsparken, known locally as Rålis. More than 70,000 people sang När vi gräver guld i USA along with the band GES.
Den 18 mars 1923 kom närmare 4 000 perso: On 18 March 1923 almost 4,000 people turned up at IFK's old home ground to watch them beat Göteborgs BIS 7–0. Around New Year 2001–2002 the pitch was covered in crushed stone and turned into a car park.
Den 19 oktober 1979 inledde Abba här den: On 19 October 1979 Abba kicked off the European leg of their final world tour here. In 1985 the arena hosted the Eurovision Song Contest, presented by Lill Lindfors and won by Bobbysocks from Norway. Kiss have played here eight times.
Den 22 februari 1944 fällde ett sovjetis: On 22 February 1944 a Soviet bomber dropped three bombs here. Two landed in Eriksdalslunden park and the third destroyed the new Eriksdal Theatre. Nobody was hurt, but a few seconds later and Södersjukhuset hospital could have been hit. It was the only time bombs fell on Stockholm during the war.
Den 23 juli 1901 exploderade lasten på b: On 23 July 1901 the cargo of the barque Louise Adelaide, which had come from Philadelphia with crude oil and paraffin, exploded by the superphosphate factory. Ten people were killed. The wreck was identified during surveys in 2008–2009.
Den 23 mars 1836 såldes Kungsporten för: On 23 March 1836 Kungsporten, the King's Gate, was sold for 345 riksdaler banko to the master coppersmith Carl Erik Lilja, but the purchase passed to the city. Despite several attempts to save it, the gate was demolished in 1836–1838.
Den 26 april 1937, på sin 45-årsdag, fly: On 26 April 1937, his 45th birthday, Harry Hjörne moved with his family into a third-floor flat in the GP building, home of the Göteborgs-Posten newspaper.
Den 26 december 1961 öppnade biografen F: On 26 December 1961 the Fanfaren cinema opened, with 535 seats and a CinemaScope screen. After various ups and downs it closed in May 1992.
Den 26 september 1986 spelade Cliff Burt: On 26 September 1986, Cliff Burton played his last concert with Metallica here at Solnahallen. Shortly afterwards he was killed when the tour bus crashed outside Ljungby in Småland.
Den 27 september 1912 testade Ericssons: On 27 September 1912 Ericsson's friend Gustaf Dalén was testing acetylene cylinders in a quarry at Alby. One that had failed to explode went off as he walked up to it. Dalén barely survived and lost his sight.
Den 29 maj 1958 invigdes arenan med en m: The stadium opened on 29 May 1958 with a match between the Swedish national team and a Gothenburg city side, watched by 49,493 spectators. It ended 2–2, and the very first goal was scored by Gunnar Gren. That evening a 'Miss Ullevi' was crowned as well.
Den 3 april 1973 öppnade OBS i Bäckebol,: On 3 April 1973, OBS opened in Bäckebol: 30,000 square metres, and at the time the biggest hypermarket in the country. Long before that, this was Bäckebol farm. Work on its stone manor house began in 1764 under the weighmaster Johan Oliveholm, and it has been a listed building since 1969. The estate's owners even have a private burial ground of their own, in use since the mid-1700s.
Den 3 mars 1957 beslöt magistraten i Göt: On 3 March 1957 Gothenburg's city authorities decided to split Arendal into two districts, Arendal and Syrhåla. Arendal became a purely industrial area – only 90 people lived there in 2012 – and it's home to the headquarters of Volvo Buses, among others. Syrhåla kept its old name, first recorded in 1550, which means a swampy place or sour ground.
Den 5 september 1970 brann huset efter e: On 5 September 1970 the store burned down after an electrical fault in an advertising sign. The management hadn't been able to decide between 'Möbel-IKEA' and 'IKEA', so both signs had gone up. Some 8,000 people queued for the fire sale – some had slept in tents – and the store reopened in March 1971.
Den 5 september 1970 brann varuhuset eft: On 5 September 1970 the department store burned down after an electrical fault in an advertising sign. Around 8,000 people queued for the fire sale, some of them having slept in tents. The insurance payout of 23 million kronor was the biggest in Sweden up to that time.
Den 6 november 1810 gick Sveriges första: On 6 November 1810, Heden hosted Sweden's first horse race run the English way. There were three races, each over an English mile. George Hebden won two of them and Emanuel Norling the third.
Den 7 maj 1977 blev Göte Kärnsby Ullevis: On 7 May 1977 Göte Kärnsby became Ullevi's ten-millionth visitor.
Den 8 februari 1812 stal Lasse-Maja till: On 8 February 1812 the notorious thief Lasse-Maja and two accomplices stole the church silver from Järfälla church. After the thefts he was caught, convicted and locked up in Carlsten fortress in Marstrand.
Den 8 september 1966 klippte statsrådet: On 8 September 1966, after seven years of construction, government minister Olof Palme cut the ribbon. Frölunda Torg was then the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries, and it had its own tram stop from day one. In the first four days alone, 50,000 people came through the doors.
Den 8 september 1968 invigde prins Berti: On 8 September 1968 Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen and its shopping centre. Back then it was entirely open-air, with streets and walkways, and had its own cinema, Vågen. In 1984 the streets were glazed over.
Den andra gasklockan togs i bruk år 1900: The second gasholder came into use in 1900 and was then considered the largest in the world, with a capacity of 65,000 cubic metres. It was needed: gas production had more than doubled during the 1890s.
Den branta kyrktomten krävde mycket arbe: The steep church site took a lot of work. The terrace walls and church park weren't built until the 1940s, and were finished in 1943.
Den bro du ser i dag blev klar 1980, bre: The bridge you see today was finished in 1980, next to the 1929 bridge. It's a steel girder bridge resting on nine concrete pillars, with a clearance of just 1.6 metres.
Den danskfödde arkitekten Hack Kampmann: The Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann was given a free hand and designed low façades of glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond. City commissioner Walfrid Frank praised the architects for abandoning 'the sky-storming' in favour of a human scale.
Den del av Hagsätra som ligger sydväst o: The part of Hagsätra south-west of Huddingevägen has a name of its own: Ormkärr. A little further away is Hagsätra Centre, which opened in 1960 after just a year of building – the same year the metro reached Hagsätra. The centre's trademark is Barnet med käpphästen, 'The Child with the Hobby Horse', a copper sculpture designed by Marie Stenqvist.
Den del av Ånäsvägen som går mellan Redb: The stretch of Ånäsvägen between Redbergsplatsen and Ejdergatan once had a delightful name: Nyfikeliden, or simply Nyfiken and Nyfika – 'nyfiken' means curious. 'Liden' means a slope, and the name probably comes from a house called Nyfika on a map from 1790. Ånäsvägen itself was named in 1883 after the Ånäs country estate and is just over a kilometre long.
Den ena igensatt, den andra i bruk: One sealed, the other in use
Den faluröda Sätra friidrottshall invigd: The Falu red Sätra athletics hall opened in April 1998. The idea was that it would also host badminton if Stockholm won the 2004 Summer Olympics.
Den första bastun var en prototyp. Somma: The first sauna was a prototype. In the summer of 2024 it was replaced by a permanent building that looks exactly the same from outside. Everything was renewed except the metal facade panels, which were kept.
Den första bilen från Torslandaverken va: The first car off the line at the Torslanda plant was a Volvo Amazon, presented to King Gustaf VI Adolf. At the opening in 1964 the King rode through the factory in the back seat of a Volvo ÖV4. Two days later, more than 20,000 employees and their families were invited.
Den första bron byggdes av Svea ingenjör: The first bridge was built by the Svea Engineer Regiment to supply the Södra Fronten defence line. Work began in 1913, but a shortage of planks for the roadway meant it wasn't finished until the following year. After the First World War it lost its strategic importance.
Den första bron över Lullehovssundet var: The first bridge across the Lullehovssundet strait was a pontoon bridge from around 1830, just west of today's bridge. The old road embankment and a milestone reading "1 MIL" survive. The stone bears the initials of the county governor, Gustaf Fredrik Liljencrantz.
Den första bron över sundet, en flottbro: The first bridge across the strait, a pontoon bridge, was laid around 1830 just west of today's bridge. The old road embankment and a milestone reading "1 MIL" survive. The stone bears the initials of the county governor, Gustaf Fredrik Liljencrantz.
Den första klaffbron över Tappström bygg: The first bascule bridge over Tappström was built in 1828. In the 1880s it was replaced by an opening wooden bridge paid for by the bank director André Oscar Wallenberg. New bridges then followed in 1930 and 1973.
Den första kyrkan byggdes i romansk stil: The first church was built in the Romanesque style in the 1100s. In the late 1200s it was ravaged by fire and rebuilt in the Gothic style, and by around 1500 it had reached its present size. The small church bell dates from 1653.
Den första kyrkan med namnet ritades av: The first church of that name was designed by Adrian C. Peterson and consecrated in 1886. The driving force was the vicar Uddo Lechard Ullman, a champion of Gothic Revival in Swedish church architecture. The altar group, with a large crucifix, came from Munich.
Den första kyrkan, i nygotik: The first church, in Gothic Revival style
Den första kända ägaren av Partille herr: The first known owner of Partille Manor was Oluff Nilsson. In 1583 he bought the estate from the Crown for 18½ daler in silver coin and two oxen.
The first known owner of Partille Manor, Oluff Nilsson, bought the estate from the Crown in 1583 for 18½ silver dalers – and two oxen.
Den första staden som hette Göteborg gru: The first town called Gothenburg was founded in 1603 on Hisingen at Färjenäs, and its people were mostly Dutch merchants. The Danes burnt it down in 1611, and all you can see today is the foundation of the church that stood at the heart of the town.
Den första stationen öppnade den 15 dece: The first station opened on 15 December 1876, when the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen railway was inaugurated. A new station building designed by Erik Lallerstedt followed in 1908. It was torn down in 1975 and replaced by a sheet-metal building above the tracks.
Den första ångbåtsbryggan för sommarhuse: The first steamboat jetty for the Fridhem summer houses was called Bedalunds brygga, after one of the first houses, from around 1877. From Fridhemsbryggan the long staircase known as Jakobs stege (Jacob's Ladder) climbs up to Mälarhöjdsvägen.
Den första ön ur havet: The first island out of the sea
Den förste ägaren, tullkontrollören Pett: The first owner, customs inspector Petter Eriksson-Svedberg, built a manor house here as early as 1775. He had a garden laid out and planted 100 oaks and more than 100 willows. Before that there was only a small cottage on the hillside.
Den försvunna Ingvarsstenen var troligen: The lost Ingvar stone was probably about 3.3 metres tall. It was raised by Andvett in memory of his brother Huge, who died with Ingvar on his expedition east. In 1869 an old man said a large, split stone had lain in the pasture, and believed it had sunk into the ground.
Den försvunna runstenen U 93 bar ungefär: The lost runestone U 93 read roughly: Sigvast and ... and Anund had the stone raised in memory of Torsten.
Den försvunna stenen från Flysta är känd: The lost stone from Flysta is known through its inscription: 'Djärv … this in memory of Est, his son. Torbjörn carved.' In other words, Torbjörn was the rune carver.
Den gamla Brunnsbohallen är en tegelbygg: The old Brunnsbo hall is a brick building with a steep gabled roof shaped like a giant prism. Light pours in from above onto an inner hall, most of which is now a café. The space has been described as almost sacred – rivalling the smaller church on the square.
Den gamla Spånga socken var stor. Fram t: The old parish of Spånga was a big one. Until 1949 it took in Hässelby Palace, the estates of Akalla, Bromsten, Rinkeby and Tensta, and its parish church, Spånga kyrka. In 1948 about 21,000 people lived here, before the parish was dissolved and split between Stockholm, Sollentuna and Sundbyberg.
Den gamla byn hade fyra gårdar som låg i: The old village had four farms that sat in different parishes. Hökegården and Sörgården belonged to Fässberg parish, while Kongegården and Nordgården were in Örgryte parish.
Den gamla elverksbyggnaden intill har ha: The old power station next door has had a colourful past. It was built in 1893 to supply electricity to Djursholmsbanan, the local railway, and later became a film studio used by companies such as Film AB Imago and Svensk TV-produktion. Today it's home to Marina läroverket, a school with a maritime theme. One of its courses is called Archipelago Captain – even though no such title actually exists.
Den gamla gränsen mellan Sverige och Nor: The old border between Sweden and Norway runs straight through the TC final assembly plant. That means the south-western part was in Sweden and the rest in Norway.
The old border between Sweden and Norway runs straight through the TC final-assembly plant. Its south-western corner was in Sweden, and the rest in Norway.
The old border between Sweden and Norway runs straight through the TC final assembly plant. So the south-west corner of the hall was once in Sweden and the rest in Norway.
Den gamla gården Gåshaga gav namn åt hel: The old Gåshaga farm gave its name to the whole district, though the last of its buildings was pulled down in 1971. For a long time, the shoreline at the southern tip of Lidingö, facing the Hustegafjärden and Höggarnsfjärden bays, was set aside for industry and boatyards, with quays for bigger ships. When the companies left, the area filled up with apartment blocks, terraced houses and villas instead.
Den gamla kyrkan låg kvar på begravnings: The old church stood in the churchyard until 1869. The new one, designed by Adolf W. Edelsvärd, was built about 700 metres to the west on Toftaåsen ridge and consecrated on 15 July 1866 by Dean Peter Wieselgren.
Den gamla kyrkans mindre klocka från 179: The old church's smaller bell, from 1792, bore a long inscription recording that Gustav III had been murdered by one of his subjects and that 14-year-old Gustav Adolf had been proclaimed king. The larger bell, from 1694, urged: “Go to church, fall down there.” Both have since been recast.
Den gamla landsvägen från Nedre Lindö ti: The old country road from Nedre Lindö to Malmvik is still here and is now called Wallenbergs allé. It was closed to through traffic when the new route of Ekerövägen opened in 1997. Four milestones stand along the road across Lindö.

The old country road from Nedre Lindö to Malmvik is still there and is now called Wallenbergs allé. It was closed to cars when the new route of Ekerövägen opened in 1997. Four milestones stand along the road across the island.
Den gamla mangårdsbyggnaden, Ryska villa: The old manor house, known as the Russian Villa, was demolished in 1929 to make way for the State Seed Testing Institute. The estate was farmed until 1965. The institute's main building later became offices and, in the 2010s, owner-occupied flats.
Den gamla sjukstugan i Mölndals Kvarnby: The old cottage hospital in Mölndal's mill village had 24 beds. In 1913 the doctor Knut Belfrage showed that it had averaged 29 patients, and the county council realised a new hospital was needed. Fässberg municipality offered a plot in Bosgården.
Den gamla stationen revs i etapper 2014–: The old station was demolished in stages in 2014–2015, when the line was widened to four tracks. The new platform ended up about 250 metres further north, and during construction passengers had to use temporary entrances.
Den gamla tunneln användes för ett indus: The old tunnel carried an industrial railway until 1967, when the Essingeleden motorway was built, and its entrances are now sealed. The 520-metre eastern tunnel from 1909 is still in use – for instance when new C30 metro trains were delivered.
Den grå kuben på toppen av Kista Science: The grey cube on top of Kista Science Tower is an extension of the lift shaft. The tower was meant to have more floors, but construction was halted by the financial crisis of the early 2000s and the shaft was never shortened.
Den gröna Hannebergsparken var från börj: The leafy Hannebergsparken was originally the bed of a lake.
Den gröna Tuvanparken har en dramatisk h: Green Tuvanparken has a dramatic past. In 1892 Tuvans hem, a home for people with nervous disorders, was built here; it was later renamed Solna sjukhem. Three patients died in a fire in 1940 and the home closed. The building was later used for things like billeting soldiers, until it was demolished in 1960 and the site became a park. Nearby stands Alby Church, a listed building that was taken out of use in 2013.
Den gula arrendatorbostaden har tre vera: The yellow tenant farmer's house has three verandas stacked on top of each other and plenty of ornate fretwork. Down by Lake Järlasjön, Björkman's mill from 1872 still stands with its tall white chimney, and the area's oldest building is the mill house from 1787.
Den här delen av Göta landsväg ingår tro: This stretch of Göta landsväg is probably part of the even older Tingsvägen, which was already there when Stockholm was founded in the 1200s. The road's narrow, winding course gives away its long history.
Den här delen av Hökarängen kallas inoff: This part of Hökarängen is nicknamed Kryddhyllan, the Spice Rack – and one look at the street names tells you why. The troubadour Cornelis Vreeswijk once lived at Saltvägen 14, on Salt Road. Right next to it is Skönstaholm, terraced and linked houses built between 1949 and 1952 to designs by Nils Sterner and Erik F. Dahl. Nearby stood the croft Lugnet, from 1771 to 1962.
Den jättelika postterminalen räknades so: This gigantic postal terminal was once one of the largest single buildings in Sweden, and from 1983 it was where the post was sorted. Once the sorting stopped, new tenants moved in, and in 2021 SL, Stockholm's public transport company, opened the biggest bus depot in the Nordic countries in part of the building. Two fragments of a Viking Age runestone were found on the grounds of Tomtebodaskolan, the school here. One was discovered in 1903 but probably went missing before 1911.
Den kupolformade byggnaden är Volvohalle: The dome-shaped building is Volvohallen, an exhibition hall that Volvo Cars built in 1975 to designs by the architects Lund & Valentin. Construction of Volvo's Torslandaverken plant began in Sörred, a village name recorded as early as 1388 as Surfua rudi. Sörred belonged to Björlanda parish until it became part of Gothenburg in 1967.
Den liggande skyskrapan: The skyscraper lying on its side
Den lilla bäcken Flabäck har varit en ri: This little stream, the Flabäck, was once a national border! It separates Kållered from Lindome – and so the province of Västergötland from Halland – and while Halland belonged to Denmark, right up until the Peace of Brömsebro in 1645, the border with Sweden ran right here. The name comes from Flaksjö, and in the 17th century it was spelled, among other ways, Flaksjöbäcken.
Den lilla kyrkan i närheten heter Älvsbo: The little church nearby is called Älvsborgs kyrka but used to be Hagens kapell, Hagen Chapel. A bit further on, traffic thunders underground through the Gnistängstunneln tunnel on the Västerleden ring road. It's 712 metres long and carries around 55,000 vehicles a day. The tunnel was originally a single tube, but the exhaust fumes became such a problem that in 1996 a concrete wall was built to split it in two.
Den lilla orten Fiskarhagen ligger klämd: The little village of Fiskarhagen is squeezed between two lakes, Aspen and Bornsjön, south-west of Norsborg. Its houses line both sides of Sankt Botvids väg, part of the historic Göta landsväg highway – so travellers were passing through long before the buses arrived. Nearby, the Männö udd peninsula juts out into Bornsjön. It's split between Botkyrka and Salem and is part of the Bornsjön nature reserve.
Den lilla villagatan Anundsvägen, alldel: Anundsvägen, the little residential street right beside us, has a royal claim to fame: Queen Elizabeth II paid a visit here in the 1950s. Björklunds hage, a little further on, is far older. It's a burial ground from the early and late Iron Age, the second largest in Bromma, and it served the Viking Age settlement of Ängby. You can see the graves clearly just south of Bällstavägen.
Den ljusgula stenbyggnaden uppfördes av: The pale yellow stone building was put up by the ironworks owner Frans Adam Björling in the 1850s and is an example of the plain late Empire style. Its two timber wings are older, from the 1700s; one is used by the sea scouts.
Den låga delen av Wenner-Gren Center, me: The low-rise part of the Wenner-Gren Center, with the tower at its focal point, resembles a sundial. Its shape follows the little lake Ormträsket that used to be here. The tower narrows as it rises, to make it look even taller.
Den låga raden av hus längs vägen kallas: The low row of houses along the road is called Långa raden, the Long Row, and it was built in the 1780s at the behest of King Gustav III. The courtiers lived in Kavaljershuset, the Cavaliers' House; the palace pharmacy was in Apotekshuset; and from Kanslihuset, the Chancellery, built in 1787, the county governor – the king's favourite, Adolf Fredrik Munck – held court. Since 1991 it's all been part of the Drottningholm World Heritage Site.
Den långa raden av låga hus längs Malmgå: The long row of low buildings along the north side of Malmgårdsvägen is a well-preserved industrial setting from the 18th and 19th centuries. There was a brewery, a slaughterhouse and the Barnängen textile mill. The old Hammarby customs house on the corner of Ljusterövägen, however, was demolished in 1907.
Den nuvarande betongbryggan vid Fridhem: The current concrete jetty at Fridhem arrived in 1985 and was set in place by the floating crane Lodbrok. In summer M/S Prins Carl Philip and S/S Drottningholm call here on their way between Stadshuskajen and Drottningholm Palace.
Den nuvarande kyrkan ritades av Torsten: The present church was designed by Torsten Hansson and consecrated in 1961 by Bishop Bo Giertz. Its gables bulge outwards, while the faces of the concrete tower curve inwards. The pointed spire is crowned with a copper cockerel.
Den nya herrgården byggdes för den ryske: The new manor house was built for the Russian ambassador Peter van Suchtelen, a great patron of art and literature. He died at 85 just as the house was finished in 1836, and probably never moved in. Two magnificent crystal chandeliers are what he left behind.
Den nya huvudbron mellan Södermalm och G: The new main bridge between Södermalm and Gamla stan, the Old Town, is officially called Slussbron, but the media also call it Guldbron, the Golden Bridge. It opened to traffic on 26 October 2020. And the border between the provinces of Uppland and Södermanland actually runs right through the area.
Den nya kyrkan byggdes 1878–1879 på Stor: The new church was built in 1878–1879 on land belonging to Stora Hovås, partly with material from the old one. Unusually, the nave runs north to south, with the chancel at the southern end and the tower to the north.
Den nya kyrkan har en stomme av tegel br: The new church is built of brick fired in Denmark. Twelve consecration crosses are set into the brick walls along the nave, and the chancel has a large altar cross in sunken relief.
Den nya kyrkan, ritad av Nyréns arkitekt: The new church, designed by Nyréns architects, is built of timber and is white both inside and out. The worship space is laid out crosswise, with the altar against the long wall. The organ and bell tower came along from the old church.
Den nya skolbyggnaden invigdes den 18 se: The new school building was opened on 18 September 2009, with Crown Princess Victoria among the guests. Lidingö city gave her a glass dish made by the local artist Jonas Torstensson. Today the school has about 65 students.
Den nya skolbyggnaden ritades av Gillber: The new school building, designed by Gillberg Arkitekter, was joined to the manor house. It was opened on 18 September 2009 in the presence of Crown Princess Victoria, who was given a glass dish by the Lidingö artist Jonas Torstensson.
Den nya stadsdelen skulle egentligen het: The new district was originally to be called Södra Gubbängen, South Gubbängen. But the Gubbängen fields in between were so wide that the name Hökarängen was chosen instead. Before then there were only three crofts here – Starrmyran, Lugnet and Bergholm – all of them since demolished.
Den runda formen valdes för att möblerna: The round shape was chosen so the furniture would show better in a building without corners. The architect was Claes Knutson, then the city architect of Ljungby. Inside were four full floors along the outer walls and three half floors in the middle, with no walls at all.
Den röda trävillan Villa Bellona från 19: Villa Bellona, a red wooden house from 1907, is the last of the seven professors' villas that once stood at Experimentalfältet. The others were pulled down when Södra huset was built, and Bellona was due to go too before the decision was reversed. The architect Ralph Erskine left his mark on the campus with buildings such as Allhuset, the student union building that won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, and the Aula Magna lecture hall, where Nobel lectures have been given.
Den rödmålade uthuslängan byggdes om 182: The red-painted outbuilding was rebuilt in 1825 for Ling, the father of Swedish gymnastics. It was widened, lengthened and given an upper floor, all to make more room for the exercises of his gymnastics system.
Den sista allsvenska matchen 2012 spelad: The last Allsvenskan match of 2012 was played between the two clubs that had opened the stadium in 1937, AIK and Malmö FF. At an open day that November, visitors could start the demolition themselves by taking seats and turf home as souvenirs.
Den sista butiken från starten: The last shop from the start
Den siste torparen på Nytorp var Olof Ni: The last crofter at Nytorp was Olof Nilsson, born in 1746, who worked the land with his wife Margareta, their three children and hired help. In 1800 Nytorp disappeared from the tax records.
Den som dömts till bysättning satt i häk: Anyone sentenced to bysättning, imprisonment for debt, was held with no time limit – and it was the creditor who had to pay for their keep. The jail held 40–50 people. Imprisonment for debt was abolished altogether in 1879.
Den som gjort flest poäng i innebandy i: The top points scorer in floorball at Jakobsberg sports hall is Joakim Lindström, with 345 points between the 1995/96 and 2007/08 seasons – roughly 1.3 points a game.
Den stora affärsbyggnaden där matvaruaff: The large retail building that housed the Billhälls grocery store was known as Billhällshuset. In 2004 it was renamed Sisjö Centrum, and since then it and its neighbours have been marketed together as Sisjö Köpstad.
Den stora anläggningen vid Ranhammarsväg: The large complex on Ranhammarsvägen was designed by the architects Erik and Lars-Erik Lallerstedt, father and son, starting in 1938.
Den stora arenan här är Scandinavium, in: The big arena here is Scandinavium, which opened in 1971. It has hosted ice hockey, concerts and world championships. Right next door is Nya Ullevi stadium.
Den stora byggnaden här är Handelshögsko: The large building here is the School of Business, Economics and Law at the University of Gothenburg. The blocks around it make up Vasastaden, one of the city's best-preserved turn-of-the-century neighbourhoods.
Den stora faluröda ladugården vid Ekeröv: The big Falu-red barn on Ekerövägen was built in 1937 by Alfa Laval and included a granary and a mill. After standing empty for many years, it got a new lease of life when Ekerö Möbler opened here in 1985.
Den stora halvcirkelformade byggnaden ru: The huge semicircular building around Fatbursparken is known as Bofills båge, Bofill's Arch, after the Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill, and it was completed in 1992. Where the park is now, there was once a lake, Fatburssjön, which was filled in during the 1800s when the railway arrived.
Den stora korsformade altartavlan är byg: The large cross-shaped altarpiece is a mosaic of ceramic pieces in many colours, made in 2001 by L. Söder. The altar, in red-glazed wood, is carved with symbols of Christ.
Den stora kvarnen vid farleden byggdes 1: The big mill by the shipping lane was built between 1888 and 1890 by Holmberg & Möllers Qvarn AB – and its spot by the water was no accident. The mill kept grinding until the late 1980s, when its owner, Kungsörnen, shut it down. The core of the building has been preserved and now houses flats and a hotel. Up on Bageriberget there's a viewpoint.
Den stora kyrkklockan göts av Ohlssons k: The large church bell was cast by Ohlsson's bell foundry in Ystad. The small bell comes from a closed-down chapel at Lillhagen.
Den stora sammansättningshallen från 190: The great assembly hall from 1908–09 is shaped like a basilica, with ceilings between five and fifteen metres high and daylight pouring in through long rows of roof lanterns. Two overhead cranes from ASEA, lifting up to 30 and 25 tonnes, ran along the ceiling, and one of them is still there.

The great assembly hall from 1908–1909 is shaped like a basilica, with a nave, side aisles and a ceiling up to fifteen metres high. Overhead cranes from ASEA, lifting 30 and 25 tonnes, ran along the roof, and one of them is still there.
Den södra korsarmen blev färdig 1817 men: The southern transept was finished in 1817 but turned out bigger than the northern one, so the church is a little asymmetrical. Inside, the ceiling is decorated with Johan Ross the Elder's Rococo painting of the Last Judgement, with Christ at the centre of the church.
Den tyska maltkaffefirman Kathreiner gjo: The German malt coffee company Kathreiner made coffee substitute from roasted grain in a five-storey brick factory here. But the duty on coffee beans was low in Sweden, so real coffee was hardly any dearer. By 1920 the company had already sold the premises.
Den uppmärksammade Tensta Gospel Choir g: The acclaimed Tensta Gospel Choir was founded in 1996 as a project to bring different cultures together. The church premises were completed in 1973, and today several choirs are based here, including Sound of Gospel and Tensta Gospel Revelation.
Den ursprungliga Svampen ritades av Holg: The original Svampen – “the Mushroom” – was designed by Holger Blom and unveiled in 1937. When the square was redeveloped it was due to be demolished and replaced by a fountain, but after protests an exact replica was built four metres away. The new Mushroom, 3.29 metres tall, was unveiled in 1989.
Den ursprungliga Ulvsunda kvarn var från: The original Ulvsunda mill dated from the 1600s. It was a post mill, where the whole mill house turned to face the wind. A storm around 1890 wrecked the sails, and another in 1912 brought the entire building down.
Den utvändiga målningen på Jarlabergs va: The exterior painting on Jarlaberg's water tower is by the artist Åke Pallarp. It's made up of abstract patterns and letters that together spell out the word 'NACKA'.
Den vackra byggnaden här är Riddarhuset: The handsome building here is Riddarhuset, the House of Nobility, from the 1600s, where the Swedish nobility used to meet. Right next door is the island of Riddarholmen and Riddarholmskyrkan, the Riddarholmen Church, where Swedish kings have been laid to rest for several hundred years.
Den vita byggnaden intill är Bergslagsba: The white building next door is the old Bergslagsbanan railway station, designed by the brothers Axel and Hjalmar Kumlien and opened in 1881. Since 1923 it has been known to locals as Vita huset, the White House. Today it's part of Regionens hus, the headquarters of Region Västra Götaland. The Nils Ericson bus terminal won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 1996 – and at Hotel G, perched on top of the Central Station, you can enjoy a sauna with a view over the railway tracks.

The white building next door is the old station of the Bergslagsbanan railway, known locally as the White House since 1923. Designed by the brothers Axel and Hjalmar Kumlien, it opened in 1881 and is now part of Regionens hus, the head office of the Västra Götaland Region. The Nils Ericson bus terminal won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 1996. It was designed by the Norwegian architect Niels Torp, with walls and roof entirely of glass and steel.
Den vita kupolen är Avicii Arena, som ti: The white dome is Avicii Arena, formerly known as the Globe. It opened in 1989 and was long the world's largest spherical building, until the Sphere in Las Vegas overtook it in 2023. On the outside, the SkyView glass gondolas will carry you right up to the top.
Den äldre delen, Vitsand, byggdes 1962–1: The older part, Vitsand, was built in 1962–1966 as four slender slab blocks of eight to nine storeys. They used to be grey but now each has its own colour: red, green, yellow and blue, from south to north.
Den äldsta kända bilden av kyrkan hittad: The oldest known picture of the church was tracked down in Denmark by art critic Kjell Hjern. It's a watercolour from 1790 by the Danish actor Adam Gielstrup, painted while he was performing in Gothenburg, and bears the caption Udsigt af Ørgryde Kircke ved Gothenborg paa Vejen til Norge – 'View of Örgryte Church near Gothenburg on the Road to Norway'.
Den årliga mässan Antik & Kuriosa var en: The annual Antik & Kuriosa fair was a big favourite with visitors. Other events held here included garden, crafts and sport-fishing fairs.
Depån från tunnelbanans början: The depot from the metro's early days
Depån togs i bruk 1975. Det har pågått p: The depot opened in 1975. Planning has been under way to build a depot for the Tvärbanan light rail trams on the same site.
Depån togs i bruk i november 1952, samti: The depot came into use in November 1952, just as the metro line between Hötorget and Vällingby opened.
Depån öppnade 1945 som Brännkyrkahallen,: The depot opened in 1945 as Brännkyrkahallen, for buses and trams. Ahead of the launch of the metro's red line, the rail section was rebuilt in 1963–64 and renamed Nybodahallen. The Hägersten viaduct on the Essingeleden motorway runs above its roofs.
Desmond Tutu i Prinsvillan: Desmond Tutu at the Prince’s Villa
Det bevarade runstensfragmentet är målat: The surviving runestone fragment is painted red and was used as teaching material at Tomtebodaskolan, a school for blind children. Since 2006 it has been part of the Tomteboda collection at the Museum for the Visually Impaired. The legible part says only “Sven …”.
Det cirkelformade huset Fysikern byggdes: The circular Fysikern building was put up in 2000, adding more student housing. Following a commission in 2016, Arkitema and Fidjeland Architects designed new buildings in site-laid brick, and the first flats were ready in 2020.
Det delvis vattenfyllda stenbrottet har: The partly flooded quarry has become a popular film location. Scenes for Pippi Longstocking, The Brothers Lionheart, Love Boogie, Sökarna and Vägen till Klockrike have all been shot here.
The partly flooded quarry has become a popular film location. Scenes for productions including Pippi Longstocking, The Brothers Lionheart, Sökarna and Vägen till Klockrike were shot here.
Det du ser av Riksarkivet är bara en lit: What you see of the National Archives is only a small part. The stores fill six floors in a rock cavern as big as a cathedral, almost entirely below the surface of Lake Mälaren, at a constant 17 degrees. Eighty kilometres of shelving was supposed to last for 50 years, but the archive filled up and in 1995 a new one opened in Arninge.
Det enda synliga tecknet på Elefanten ov: The only sign of Elefanten above ground is the radio mast on the hill above. Until 1997, the test signal for air-raid sirens and the ‘important public announcement’ alarm was broadcast from here.
Det entomologiska kvinnorovet: The sculpture The Entomological Rape of Women
Det faluröda Falkenerarbostället från 17: The Falu-red Falconers' Lodge from 1726 was home to the royal falconers for 150 years. It was built for Fredrik I's huntsmen and falconers, and the post then passed down through the von Hamm family. The last von Hamm died here in 1867.
Det fanns ingen bro som klarade spårvagn: No bridge could carry trams, so the cars were taken across on a specially built ferry between Islinge and Ropsten. Passengers stayed in their seats the whole way, then rolled on into the city's tram network.
Det fanns redan ett Gamlestadstorget frå: There was already a Gamlestadstorget, dating from the 1890s – now built over and reduced to a cul-de-sac. So that emergency services wouldn't type the wrong one into their GPS, the city's culture department decided in 2013 that the new square by the travel centre would be called Gamlestads torg.
Det femvåningshus som folk kallade Linné: The five-storey building people called the Linnéplats Palace was built in 1904 but suffered serious subsidence. On 24 March 1983 it was demolished with 275 kilos of dynamite packed into 2,144 holes. Its tiled stoves had already been sold to the USA.
Det finns bygglov för fler delar: en str: There’s planning permission for more phases: a street park, a pool park and an indoor concrete hall sunk into the ground, with a roof you can skate on. What’s missing, though, are the political decisions to finish the job.
Det finns en vägkrog i Aspnässkolans his: Aspnäs School has a roadside tavern in its past. When Järfälla parish opened its very first school in 1846, it bought a manor house at the Aspnäs crossroads that had once been a tavern. That house was demolished in 1959, but the school still has buildings from 1901 and 1945. And the old schoolhouse? It now does duty as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre.
Det finns planer på att flytta Sävenäs s: There are plans to move Sävenäs station to Gustavsplatsen on the Västlänken line, near Gamlestaden. That would put more workplaces and local transport within walking distance.
Det första Cyklopen fick namn efter ett: The first Cyklopen was named after the big round window on its front, like the one-eyed giants of Greek myth. It was built of wood around shipping containers so it could be packed up and moved, as planning permission was only for five years. People also called it the Container Castle, and it even had a drawbridge.
Det första Cyklopen fick sitt namn av et: The first Cyklopen was named after its big round window, like an eye. Built of wood around shipping containers so it could be packed up and moved, it was nicknamed Containerslottet, the Container Castle. The current building opened in 2013 and has won awards, including for its architecture.
Det första belägget för namnet Ekerö, ak: The earliest record of the name Ekerö – written 'akru' – is on a runestone found as recently as 22 April 2013 on Bogesundslandet.
Det första belägget för namnet Ekerö, sk: The earliest record of the name Ekerö, written akru, is on a runestone found on 22 April 2013 on Bogesundslandet.
Det första belägget för namnet Ekerö, ”a: The earliest record of the name Ekerö, “akru”, is on a runestone found on 22 April 2013 on Bogesundslandet.
Det första fartyget som byggdes här var: The first vessel built here was the brig Aurora, launched in 1848. The yard grew into one of the country's largest, and in 1872 it built its first warship, the gunboat Blenda. The last ship left the yard in 1974.
Det första förslaget, ett lasarett med 5: The first proposal, a 50-bed hospital, was estimated to cost 243,100 kronor. Construction dragged on, and by the time the hospital was finished in 1924 it had 74 beds and had cost 1,500,000 kronor. The 1915 architectural competition was won by Arvid Bjerke.
Det första tullhuset kom 1622, troligen: The first customs house was built in 1622, probably on the foundations of Gustav Vasa's blockhouse, which gave the headland its name. In those days the shipping lane was closed off with a double row of booms between Blockhusudden and what is now Nacka strand. Customs operations ended in 1881.
Det gamla 1950-talscentret sjönk, efters: The old 1950s centre was sinking, because it stood on a former lake bed. The ground had to be stabilised with piles before today's centre opened in 1985. The debate was lively, with many people wanting an indoor shopping centre.
Det gamla Snickartorpet, vars nuvarande: The old Snickartorpet croft, whose present cottage dates from the mid-1800s, still stands next to the manor. The last crofter died in 1852. Today the croft has been done up and is used for conferences and intimate dinners.
Det gamla brygghuset på Svindersvik är i: The old brewhouse at Svindersvik is now a café – just the place for a fika. In the park stand gnarled apple trees descended from the 1700s, and the house is open to the public in summer.
Det gamla huset på Hornsgatan 82 kallas: The old house at Hornsgatan 82 is known as Bysis. From 1782 to 1872 it was Stockholm's debtors' prison. Next door was the Rixi cinema, which became a recording studio in 1971. Parts of ABBA's Ring Ring and Carola's debut album Främling were recorded there. Today it's called Ingrid studio, and artists such as Lykke Li and Peter Bjorn and John have recorded here.
Det gamla ladugårdskomplexet är till sto: The old cowshed complex is largely intact and is now part of the Alby industrial area. Cirkus Cirkör has a permanent circus hall in some of the buildings.
Det gamla torpet Islinge gård har gett n: The old croft of Islinge gård gave its name to the whole of Islinge, in north-western Lidingö. On Lilla Värtan, south of Islingeviken bay, stands Torsvik lighthouse, also known as the Islinge lighthouse. It was built in 1950 and switched off in 1980, but it still marks the finish line of the Lidingö Runt sailing race. Islinge is also home to Nyckelviksskolan, an art school with courses in art, crafts, architecture and design.
Det gamla torpet Tussmötet har gett namn: The old croft of Tussmötet has given its name to Tussmötevägen, a city block and Tussmöteparken park. Even the local cinema was called Tusse-Bio when it opened in March 1938 on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen. It later changed its name to Corso and closed for good in December 1969.
Det gula tornet byggde AGA 1943 för att: AGA built the yellow tower in 1943 to test and manufacture equipment such as periscopes for Swedish submarines, and production carried on inside the rock behind it until 1987. Today the area is called Dalénum, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén, who worked here from 1912 until his death in 1937. The ice rink next door became familiar to a wide audience through the TV series HCZ.
Det gula tornet en bit härifrån har ett: The yellow tower just up the road has an exciting past. AGA's optics tower was built in 1943, and in the factory carved into the rock behind it, AGA tested and made, among other things, periscopes for Swedish submarines. Production carried on in various forms until 1987, and the tower was renovated in 2022.
Det gulputsade huset med Restaurang Jern: The yellow-rendered building that houses Restaurang Jernet was designed in 1926 for Lidingö Järn- & Färghandel, a hardware and paint shop. It was meant to be preserved, but the ground was contaminated. The solution was to demolish it, clean up the site and build a lookalike on the same spot.
Det går inte att missa Karlatornet: med: You can't miss Karlatornet. At 246 metres and 73 storeys, it's the tallest building in Sweden and the Nordic countries, and its exterior was completed in 2024. Around the tower, the new Karlastaden district is taking shape with some 2,000 homes. The area has a long industrial past: the shipbuilding and engineering group Götaverken was based here on Lundbyvassen from 1841, and the last part of the shipyard closed in 2015.
Det har funnits planer på att låta gröna: There were once plans to split the green metro line at Johannelund, with a new branch towards Hässelby villastad and Lövsta. It never happened. Instead, a tunnel for the Förbifart Stockholm bypass is being built here, and Johannelund will become an interchange between the bypass and the metro.
Det här var en gång gurkland. Axel Svens: This used to be cucumber country. Axel Svensson's market garden ran from 1907 until the 1970s, and cucumbers were its speciality. Where its greenhouses once stood is now the garden suburb of Hildedal. Svensson's two-storey house from 1919 is still there at Växthusvägen 60 – fittingly, on Greenhouse Road – a reminder of the days when market gardens were a common sight here.
Det här är ett hörn fullt av unika saker: This corner is full of one-offs. Sätra's indoor athletics hall from 1998 is the only one in the municipality designed for youth athletics competitions. The Sätra pistol range is the only one of its kind in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. And Pingstkyrkan Bredäng is the only Pentecostal church in Stockholm's south-western suburbs. A little further on is the Church of Saint Maroun, which used to be called Sätra Church.
Det höga betongtornet i närheten hör til: The tall concrete tower nearby belongs to Kista fire station, built in 1980. It's a training tower for firefighters and a familiar local landmark. At Kista gård, the old farm, stands Kistastenen, the Kista runestone – proof that people lived on Järvafältet long before Kista became a hub for the IT industry.
Det höga huset på berget är Fyrtornet Da: The tall building on the hill is Fyrtornet Dalénum, the Lighthouse Tower, designed by Wingårdh and completed in 2020. At 68 metres above sea level, it's the highest building on Lidingö. Down by the shore is the Larsberg bridge-keeper's cottage from around 1803, built for the bridge that, that same year, linked Larsberg with Kaknäs on the Stockholm side. The whole area was once home to the AGA factories, where Gustaf Dalén worked.
Det höga huset som syns på långt håll he: The tall building you can see from miles away is Tyresö View. It's 82 metres high with 23 storeys, and in 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County. Under the glass roof of the shopping centre are some 70 shops, the municipal offices and a library with its own exhibition hall.
Det jättecentrum som aldrig blev: The giant centre that never was
Det lilla köket skulle laga mat på torrv: The small kitchen was meant to cook from enough dry goods to last six days. The food was to be delivered from a school canteen above ground. There were 120 beds for 200 people, since people would work 12-hour shifts.
Det lugna radhusområdet Kälvesta bär på: The quiet terraced streets of Kälvesta hold a sad chapter in Swedish aviation history. On 15 January 1977, a Skyline aircraft operating Linjeflyg Flight 618 crashed into this residential area. All 22 people on board were killed, and the tragedy is remembered today as the Kälvesta air disaster.
Det lustiga namnet Pungpinan kommer från: The odd name Pungpinan comes from a tavern that stood here from the 17th century until the 19th. The Pungpinan croft, built in 1763 on the Skarpnäck estate, was named after the tavern, and in 1933 it became a meeting place for young people from the newly built cottage area. Later the youth organisation Unga Örnar met here too, and since 2000 the croft has been privately owned.
Det långa huset från 1964 kallas Ormen L: The long building from 1964 is called Ormen Långe, the Long Serpent, because of its shape. The newest housing area, Myrstuguberget, was designed by the architect Ralph Erskine and built in 1985–86.
Det långa, slingrande skivhuset Ormen Lå: A short walk away is Ormen Långe, 'the Long Serpent', a long, winding block of flats. Together with six tower blocks on Botkyrkavägen, it had the honour of being the first modern suburban housing in these parts. Right next to it is Fittjanäset, a headland between Lake Mälaren and Lake Albysjön. Fittja bridge spans the narrow strait over to Fittja – and right up until the late 1950s, this was exactly where the main road traffic heading south out of Stockholm crossed.
Det mesta av Käppalaverket ligger inne i: Most of the Käppala treatment works lies inside a cavern in the bedrock. Sewage flows here through a 60-kilometre tunnel system all the way from Märsta, mostly by gravity alone.
Det mesta av Skintebo ligger i en dalsän: Most of Skintebo sits in a hollow ringed by hills. Follow a narrow valley half a kilometre west and you reach the sea.
Det norra och större brottet har en kort: The larger, northern quarry has a short curved mine tunnel and the beginnings of another. The southern one has a small open pit.
Det nya sjömanshemmet byggdes 1942. I Bi: The new seamen's home was built in 1942. Its Billman Hall holds Torsten Billman's celebrated fresco 'To the Seafarers – Workers of the Sea' from 1944, nearly 20 metres long and spread across two walls.
Det nybyggda gymnasiet Jakobsbergsskolan: The newly built Jakobsbergsskolan upper secondary school opened in 1970. In 2000 it was split into five schools, including SAM-gymnasiet, and in 2016 all the municipal upper secondary schools were merged again as Järfälla gymnasium.
Det officiella namnet Jægerdorffsplatsen: The official name, Jægerdorffsplatsen, is actually historically wrong, since the property was usually spelt Jägersdorf or Jägersdorff. Even so, the everyday version Jaegerdorffsplatsen wins hands down: in 2012 it got 370 hits in the Swedish media archive, against 11 for the official one.
Det sista miljonprogrammet: The last of the Million Programme
Det sista mjölet maldes 1930: The last flour was ground in 1930
Det sjunde inseglet spelades till stor d: Much of The Seventh Seal was shot in and around Filmstaden, the old film studios, in just 35 days. The witch's pyre was prepared with the help of a fire brigade captain and watched by a large crowd – many of them children – from the tower blocks next door. The crew tried to keep the buildings out of shot, but reflections from their windows can be seen in a couple of scenes.
Det skulle ha hetat Södra Gubbängen: It was meant to be called Södra Gubbängen
Det slingrande huset fick namnet Ormen L: The winding building was named Ormen Långe, the Long Serpent, after the ship of the Viking king Olav Tryggvason. The name even became the official property designation, which was originally Solgården.
Det stora kontorshuset alldeles i närhet: The big office building nearby is Bankhus 90, now called Ursvik Entré. It was built between 1989 and 1992 for Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken, following an architecture competition. A short way off stands something much older: the Stora Stampan windmill, probably one of the oldest surviving windmills in Greater Stockholm.
Det största återkommande evenemanget är: The biggest recurring event is the Gothenburg Horse Show, a qualifier in the show jumping World Cup since 1978. Twelve times it has even hosted the World Cup final.
Det sägs att Gustaf Fröding placerade ku: It's said that the poet Gustaf Fröding placed King Sigurd the Crusader in the chancel of this very church in his poem of the same name. It appears in his 1891 debut collection Gitarr och dragharmonika: "Kung Sigurd drömmer, att han är ung, kung Sigurd drömmer om palmer!" – "King Sigurd dreams that he is young, King Sigurd dreams of palm trees!"
Det tornprydda huset vid farleden kallas: The house with the tower by the shipping lane is known as Smugglarvillan, the Smugglers' Villa. Built in 1912, the Bremer Villa tells of fortunes made from herring fishing around the turn of the century and from bootlegging in the 1920s. On the island's highest point, 31 metres above sea level, stands the sea mark Valen, the Whale. Beneath it, a compass rose is carved into the rock along with the year 1684.
Det tyska flygarässet Hermann Göring arb: The German flying ace Hermann Göring worked on and off as a pilot in Sweden in the 1920s. In spring 1925 he spent a few weeks flying the Stockholm–Danzig route from Lindarängen. The Free Port and its seaplane harbour also feature in Stieg Trenter's 1946 crime novel Lysande landning.
Det var 14-årige Otto Ludvig Jonsson som: It was 14-year-old Otto Ludvig Jonsson who found the Vårby Hoard on 16 April 1871, while gathering brushwood in the woods near Lake Mälaren. As a reward he was given 250 kronor.
Det var arkitekten Sven Wedenmark som by: In 1939 the architect Sven Wedenmark rebuilt and extended the building in the functionalist style. The Rex cinema was owned by Hugo Hansson.
Det var bolaget Lidingö villastad, under: From 1906, the company Lidingö villastad, led by Hjalmar Arwin, turned Lidingö from farmland and a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers into a modern suburb. Its very first purchase, and its first office, was Vattängen farm on Stockholmsvägen. In the middle of the villa town you'll also find Centralpalatset, built in 1912–1913, and Vasaborgen, which was planned as early as 1913 but not built until 1923.
Det var drottning Victoria som drev på,: It was Queen Victoria who pushed for the clinic, after hearing from her mother about good results with X-rays and radium in Germany. It deliberately opened in an ordinary eight-room flat to make patients feel more at ease. The equipment: one X-ray machine and 120 mg of radium.
Det var en nykterhetsklubb som byggde hu: The building was put up by a temperance club and opened in 1903 as a Folkets hus, a community hall. In the 1940s it became a sweet factory, from 1954 a warehouse, and by the mid-1980s it was almost ready to be pulled down before it was restored.
Det var grosshandlarna Fredric Althainz: In 1887 the wholesale merchants Fredric Althainz and Carl Bengtsson bought Farsta farm – around 1,000 hectares. Althainz’s firm owned Eldkvarn mill on Kungsholmen, where Stockholm City Hall stands today. They divided the land into almost 600 plots.
Det var i juni 1956 som 30-åriga drottni: In June 1956 the 30-year-old Queen Elizabeth asked to see a Swedish housing area. Accompanied by King Gustaf VI Adolf, she visited the house at Anundsvägen 49, then owned by the Larsson family.
Det var kyrkoherde Bengt Thure Molander: In the early 1970s the vicar Bengt Thure Molander came up with the idea of the heritage trail, to make the island's many ancient monuments better known. The Lovö local history society laid it out, and in 2015 it was reopened with new signs. The route is marked with slanted blue metal plates.
Det var mycket bråk på krogen, och 1853: There was plenty of trouble at the inn, and in 1853 it was banned from serving spirits. In 1872 it closed altogether for lack of customers, and the building became a primary school. It wasn't until Walpurgis Eve 1983, 111 years later, that Christer Lingström opened a restaurant here again.
Det var på Grand som Olof och Lisbeth Pa: It was at the Grand that Olof and Lisbeth Palme watched the film The Mozart Brothers on 28 February 1986, before the Prime Minister was murdered on his way home. The cinema visit became hugely important in the investigation.
Det var tänkt som Centrala Bromma: It was meant to be Central Bromma
Det var översten Albert Amundson som eft: It was Colonel Albert Amundson who gave the house its castle-like look after 1889, adding a towered extension, tall Renaissance gables, bay windows and turrets. Upstairs he fitted out a knights' hall with 17th-century furniture.
Det vita huset med grön kopparkupol på h: The white building with a green copper dome on the corner of Basargatan was designed by city architect Heinrich Kaufmann and built in 1850. The dome was added in 1891, when the savings bank bought the building. Since 2004 it has housed the Chinese Consulate General.
Det välvda trätaket och väggarna målades: The vaulted wooden ceiling and the walls were painted by John Sten in a style recalling 17th- and 18th-century church painting, with naive scenes from the Bible. The church is well preserved from when it was built and is popular for weddings.
Det äldsta belägget för namnet Ekerö, ”a: The earliest record of the name Ekerö, "akru", is on a runestone found on 22 April 2013 at Bogesundslandet.
Det är inte varje dag man ser en soffgru: It's not every day you see a three-piece suite on a rooftop – but you will here. The furniture store founded by Skinngruppen in 1975 has become a local landmark thanks to the giant sofa perched on top. Krokslätt used to be an industrial area, home to the Krokslätt factories, and it's also where the very first self-built family homes in the Gothenburg area went up.
Dieselverkstaden används i dag av Nacka: Today Dieselverkstaden, the old Diesel Workshop, is used by Nacka's culture department, with a library, a cinema and several stages.
Dieselverkstaden hette ursprungligen Sam: Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, was originally known as the Assembly Hall, and Atlas Diesel built diesel engines here right up until 1951. Since 2002 the old factory hall has been full of culture instead, with an arts centre, a library, a climbing centre and a five-screen cinema. And deep beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter is a test mine where rock drills and mining machines are put through their paces.
Direkt väster om gården ligger ett gravr: Just west of the farm is a Bronze Age burial cairn, 35 metres across and 5–6 metres high. It's the second-largest known cairn in the province of Södermanland.
Ditzingers två hus är inte bara lika, de: The two Ditzinger houses aren't just alike – they're mirror images of each other. Their style was inspired by the timber-panelled architecture of well-to-do Stockholmers' summer villas. The brothers didn't keep them long: they sold the property as early as 1890.
Djupt inne i berget under bostadsområdet: Deep in the rock beneath the Eriksberg housing area, the red line's metro trains sleep. Norsborg depot lies 18 to 37 metres down inside Aspberget and the Eriksbergsåsen ridge, connected to the metro at Norsborg. Norsborg station itself, a couple of minutes from here, opened in 1975 and is the westernmost station on the whole network.
Djupt inne i ett bergrum i Edsberg finns: Deep inside a rock cavern in Edsberg lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a command centre built in 1972–77 to withstand a nuclear bomb, with room for 200 people. It was meant to protect the leaders of Stockholm and Sollentuna municipalities in the event of war. After standing empty for 19 years, it was bought in 2017 by the Swedish Armed Forces, who modernised it and put it back into service. Above ground, life is more peaceful, with Edsberg church, a red wooden church.
Djupt under campus forskade man en gång: Deep under the campus, scientists once carried out research in accelerator physics. Since 2019 the old laboratory has been the Accelerator art gallery, opened by the artist Tino Sehgal. The lab is named after Manne Siegbahn, winner of the 1924 Nobel Prize in Physics. Ralph Erskine designed the Law Building as a semicircle wrapped around an old oak – and the same idea of sparing the oaks shaped Aula Magna too.
Djupt under fötterna, 27 till 36 meter n: Deep below your feet, 27 to 36 metres down in the bedrock, is the metro station, opened in 1975. Above it is one of the biggest shopping centres in the Stockholm region, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants. Across Centralvägen is Eric Grate's Park, named after the sculptor, who spent the last fifteen years of his life in Solna. Two of his bronzes stand there: Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God.
Djursholm är villornas rike, och i närhe: Djursholm is a world of grand villas, and nearby is Villa Snellman, one of the early works of the architect Gunnar Asplund. Djursholm's own Strandvägen, along the waters of Lilla and Stora Värtan, is often counted among the most exclusive addresses in Sweden. The Djursholm railway, Djursholmsbanan, used to run past here, and for many years there was a little kiosk selling sweets and newspapers on the narrow platform at the Bragevägen stop.
Djursholms slott ägdes av ätten Banér i: Djursholm Castle belonged to the Banér family for over 300 years, from 1508 to 1813, and parts of it date from the late Middle Ages. Today it's the municipal hall – and you can hire its banqueting rooms for a wedding. On the hill next door is the water tower from 1890. It was built beside a little Dutch-style windmill, which was pulled down shortly afterwards. And Djursholm's co-educational school, founded in 1891, stood just nearby.

Djursholm Castle was owned by the Banér family for more than 300 years, from 1508 to 1813, and parts of it date from the late Middle Ages. Today it's the town hall, and you can even hire its banqueting rooms for weddings. On the hill beside it stands the water tower from 1890, built next to a small Dutch-style windmill that was pulled down shortly afterwards. The tower has been dry since 1960.
Domarringen vid radhusen: The stone circle by the terraced houses
Domkyrkan, ofta öppen dagtid: Gothenburg Cathedral, usually open during the day
Donsö är en levande skärgårdsö med Donsö: Donsö is a lively archipelago island with its own church and more than 1,500 year-round residents. A little to the south is tiny Kårholmen, which has a lovely story. On 7 May 1933, twenty people hired a motorboat, founded a club called Arbetarna till havet – “Workers to the Sea” – and were allowed to take over the island. They were all poor working people, and today the island is almost entirely covered with just over 80 summer cottages.

Dopfunten är gjord av Sven Palmqvist på: The font was made by Sven Palmqvist of Orrefors from loose glass blocks arranged in a square. The ceiling of the nave consists of folded concrete screens that let daylight in between them.

Dricksvattnets slutstation: The end of the line for drinking water

Drottning Kristina var gäst här redan 16: Queen Christina was a guest here as early as 1645, and in 1670 King Karl XI and the Queen Dowager Hedvig Eleonora came to visit. In the 19th century callers included Fredrika Bremer, Carl Jonas Love Almqvist and Anders Zorn.
Drottning Kristina var gäst på Edsberg r: Queen Christina was a guest at Edsberg as early as 1645, and in 1670 King Karl XI and the Queen Dowager Hedvig Eleonora came to visit. In the 19th century the palace welcomed guests such as Fredrika Bremer, Carl Jonas Love Almqvist and Anders Zorn.
Drottning Kristina ägde Rörstrands slott: Queen Kristina owned Rörstrand Palace from 1649 to 1651 and set up an academy for young noblemen here, modelled on one in Paris. They learned riding, fencing, dancing and languages.
Drottningtorget ligger mitt framför Cent: Drottningtorget is the square right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. Much of the Nordic region's largest tram network sets off from here. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and while many other Swedish cities scrapped their trams, Gothenburg chose to keep them.
