Du är nu i Majorna, strax väster om Mast: You're now in Majorna, just west of Masthugget, where ships' masts were once hewn. Up on the hill stands Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church from 1914 and one of the city's best-known landmarks. By the square are the Maritime Museum and Aquarium and Sjömanstornet, the Sailors' Tower, topped by the statue of a sailor's wife gazing out over the river for ships that never came home.
Du är nu i Masthugget, där fartygens mas: You're now in Masthugget, where ships' masts were once hewn. Up on the hill stands Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church from 1914 and one of the city's best-known landmarks. By the square you'll find the Maritime Museum and Aquarium and Sjömanstornet, the Sailors' Tower, topped by the statue of a sailor's wife gazing out over the river for ships that never came home.
Duggregnet 5 vid Björkhagsplan ritades a: Duggregnet 5 at Björkhagsplan was designed by the architect Georg Varhelyi, and anyone who knows Le Corbusier's famous Unité d'Habitation in Marseille will spot the family likeness straight away. When it went up in 1957 it was Stockholm's tallest residential building, and today the City Museum has marked it blue, its highest grade. Down in the metro station are artworks by Lenka Jonesson, unveiled in 1991.
Duon bakom Thaliapriset: The duo behind the Thalia Prize
Duvbo kyrka invigdes första advent, den: Duvbo Church was consecrated on Advent Sunday, 27 November 1904, by Archbishop Johan August Ekman. The guests included Prince Carl and Princess Ingeborg. The idea came from Carl Alm, a local district officer who lived in the garden suburb of Duvbo himself.
Duvnäs nämns i skrift redan 1436, men vi: Duvnäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436, but the villas only came once the Saltsjöbanan railway station opened in 1893. By Ringparken stands Herrgårdsvillan, built in 1910–1911 as a show home to tempt buyers to the new building plots, and in the park is Ringparksstugan, the cottage where neighbours celebrate the year's festivities. A little further on is Duvnäs Lower Manor, built by the industrialist Robert Finlay in the late 1740s.

Duvnäs is mentioned in records as early as 1436, but the villas didn't arrive until the Saltsjöbanan railway opened its station here in 1893. In Ringparken stands Herrgårdsvillan, the Manor Villa, built in 1910–11 as a show home to tempt buyers to the new building plots. The park is also home to Ringparksstugan, a cottage where neighbours get together for their yearly celebrations. A little further on, Kvarngården – the miller's house from the mid-1700s – is a reminder of the old watermill that once stood by Duvnäsviken bay.
Där Alviks gamla industriområde en gång: Alvik's old industrial area by Lake Mälaren is now mostly offices and a handful of restaurants. Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, is an events venue nearby where the TV competition show Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail plunges into the rock through the Alvik tunnel, about 250 metres long, and then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the 400-metre Alvik bridge, completed in 2000.
Där Arendalsvarvet låg finns i dag ett s: Where the Arendal shipyard once stood there's now a large logistics and industrial area, home to Volvo Buses' head office and the Volvo Museum, among others. The property company Platzer bought most of the site from Volvo in 2016.
Där Ekebyhovsbacken ligger fanns på 1950: In the 1950s the site of today's Ekebyhovsbacken ski slope was a gravel pit with a 55-metre summit. It was built up with demolition rubble to 82 metres above sea level – the highest artificial point on the ridge. The longest run is 510 metres.
Där Eriksbergsskolan ligger fanns förr e: Where Eriksbergsskolan school now stands there was once a marsh where people went skating in winter. Parts of the bottom were black, and rumour had it that a wagon full of tar had come off the rails. It later emerged that the state railway SJ had once treated railway sleepers with creosote here.
Där Flatenbanan ligger fanns torpet Ekst: Where the Flaten track is now, there used to be the croft of Ekstubben, belonging to Skarpnäck farm. In 1972 the Stockholm raggare – Sweden's American-car enthusiasts – opened a motor clubhouse here. The clubhouse survives and is now used as an indoor track for radio-controlled model cars, and the outdoor tracks are 330 and 340 metres long.
Där Fågelbergskyrkan står låg förr Rävek: Fågelberg Church stands where Rävekärr vicarage used to be. The last priest moved out in 1978, and the vicarage was demolished on 19 January 1984. On 1 December that same year, Bishop Bertil Gärtner consecrated the new church.
Där Husby står i dag övade militären änd: Where Husby stands today, soldiers were still training right up until 1965, as Järvafältet was a military training ground. The district was built in 1971 and was first called Husby gård. Today it has Husbybadet, a swimming centre with an adventure pool, a 25-metre pool and a diving tower with 1- and 3-metre boards.
Där Linnégatan går rann förr Djupedalsbä: Where Linnégatan runs today, Djupedalsbäcken stream once flowed – its oldest known name, from 1624, was Ryssbäcken. It came down from Slottsskogen and dropped 12 metres towards Järntorget. In 1878 it was decided to fill it in and channel it through a culvert to the Göta älv river.
Där Obs! Stormarknad slog upp portarna 1: Where the Obs! Stormarknad hypermarket opened its doors in 1963, there was once Haga gård, an outlying farm of the Vårby estate that was pulled down in the early 20th century. The store building is still here, but Obs! closed in 1998 and furniture shops moved in. Right next door is Fittjanäset, and across the narrow strait to Fittja ran Fittja bro, the Fittja bridge – the main road south out of Stockholm until the end of the 1950s.
Där Segeltorps gård låg står i dag en na: Where Segeltorp farm once stood, there's now an oak protected as a natural monument. It was protected in 1961, and by 2005 its trunk measured a full 464 centimetres round.
Där Skogskyrkogården ligger fanns tre gr: There were once three gravel pits where Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, now lies. One of them was shaped into an artificial valley with a reflecting pond, and selling the gravel was expected to cover the construction costs. Much of the digging was done as relief work during the First World War and the Depression of the 1930s.
Där Skärholmens centrum ligger i dag fan: Where Skärholmen centrum stands today there was once a farm, Smista gård, dating back to at least the 800s, and people were living nearby as early as the 200s, in the Roman Iron Age. In the 1700s and 1800s Smista was an outlying farm belonging to Vårby gård. Today you'll find, among other things, the Red Cross folk high school, some of whose courses even travel abroad, and Skärisbiografen, a cinema that opened in 2017.
Där Spånga IP ligger i dag fanns Spånga: Where Spånga sports ground is today, the Spånga radio broadcasting station stood from 1930 to 1954.
Där Spånga IP ligger i dag låg mellan 19: Where Spånga IP sports ground is today, the Spånga broadcasting station stood from 1930 to 1954. At the local trade school, engines were built that were used in races at Solvalla.
Där Stockholmsmässan står i dag låg en g: Where Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, stands today, there used to be a lake. Brännkyrkasjön, also called Kyrksjön, lay just south of Brännkyrka Church and was drained bit by bit, from the 1870s right through to the 1950s. Since 1971 the exhibition halls and car parks have occupied the western side of the old lake bed, while the eastern side is still mostly open land.
Där Ulriksdals Golfklubb ligger i dag gi: Where Ulriksdal Golf Club is today, the pace used to be much faster – this was once the site of the Ulriksdal racecourse. The commuter rail station is 7.1 kilometres from Stockholm Central, on the line towards Märsta, and took on its present look in 1990, with the ticket hall on the platform and the entrance through a pedestrian tunnel.
Där bostadsområdet Minneberg ligger låg: The Minneberg housing area stands on the site of the old Stockholm Bonemeal Factory, which turned out glue, bone oil, chicken feed and even a washing powder called Pärlglans. The smelly business moved away in 1968, and Minneberg was built in the 1980s. Next door is Tranebergs gård, a farm that goes back to a ferryman's croft from the 1670s. The croft was named Traneberg after its owner, Bengt Trana.
Där bostadsområdet Rissne ligger i dag h: The Rissne housing estate stands on old military ground. The Svea Artillery Regiment had its barracks here until 1963, and the Ordnance Administration School took over the site until 1977. The blocks of flats only went up between 1982 and 1988. Fittingly, the square was called Dragonplan, Dragoon Square, before it was renamed Rissne torg.
Där egendomarna Hammarby, Enskede och Sk: Where the estates of Hammarby, Enskede and Skarpnäck met, the boundary was marked by a big white-painted stone called Vita sten. It's still there, by the bus stop south of Sockenvägen below Gränsberget hill.
Där idrottsplatsen ligger stod tidigare: Sweden's first broadcasting station once stood where the sports ground is now. It was demolished when construction began. The bandy rink opened in December 1977 with an international between Sweden and the Soviet Union.
Där kyrkan står vände förr spårvagnarna: Where the church stands, trams used to turn in a loop with two stops: Källviken for getting off and Nockeby for getting on. The loop was removed in 1960, and Källviken was renamed Nockeby. King Gustav VI Adolf attended the consecration.
Där luftvärnet en gång siktade mot himle: Where the anti-aircraft guns once took aim at the sky, the two chimneys of the Käppala sewage works now stand right in the middle of the old firing range.
When the sun shines on Hisingen, there's electricity to be harvested. The Nya Solevi solar park, in Säve north-west of Gothenburg, is designed to produce around 5.5 gigawatt hours a year. It went up in record time: the first spade went into the ground in September 2018 and it opened in December the same year. While it was being planned, it was called Säve Solcellspark.
Där torget ligger i dag stod från 1630-t: From the 1630s until 1825, the Baroque palace Makalös – “Matchless” – stood where the square is today.
Där villorna står i dag låg förr åkrar s: The villas you see today stand on what were once fields belonging to Viksjö gård, a farm that goes back to prehistoric times. In 1921 the farm was sold to Viksjö AB, which went on farming the land, but in 1963 a group of builders began developing the area. The result is a mix of villas and terraced houses from the 1960s, 70s and 80s, with patches of nature in between.
Där ån lämnar Aspen har stranden grävts: Where the stream leaves Lake Aspen, the bank has been dug out into a narrow canal about 140 metres long that leads into the park. It then widens into several small ponds before carrying on eastwards.

Dösen byggdes omkring 3500 före Kristus: The dolmen was built on a seashore around 3500 BC, when the sea stood 15 metres higher than it does today.
EFS-föreningen i Furulund fanns i tjugo: The EFS congregation in Furulund – part of a Lutheran revival movement – existed for twenty years before its church was built in 2001. As early as 2007 it was extended, almost doubling the size of the worship space.
EPAs torg i Nationalteaterns låt: The 'EPA square' of a Nationalteatern song
Edsbacka krog grundades 1626 vid landsvä: Edsbacka krog was founded in 1626 on the road between Stockholm and Uppsala. Gustav II Adolf granted the inn a charter, the first of its kind, and a copy hangs in the entrance today.
Edsbacka krog grundades redan 1626 av pr: Edsbacka krog was founded as early as 1626 by the quartermaster Henrik Olofsson, who received a royal charter from Gustav II Adolf to run an inn on the road between Stockholm and Uppsala. It was the first charter of its kind, and a copy hangs in the inn's entrance today.
Edsbacka krog vid Edsviken blev den förs: Edsbacka krog, by the Edsviken bay, became the first restaurant in Sweden to hold two Michelin stars, under the restaurateur Christer Lingström. The stars went when it changed hands in 2010, but since spring 2021 the restaurant has once again been called Edsbacka krog. Back in the 17th century, a fallen runestone lay just north of the restaurant; its base now stands just south of the avenue up to Edsberg Palace.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och fick: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and was given a makeover around 2004, including a new multi-storey car park. Here you'll find a library, a pharmacy, an Ica supermarket and two grill restaurants, Oscar and Ló Mero Kök och Bar. Right next door is Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church belonging to Sollentuna parish. The district is also home to Edsberg Palace, Rudbecksskolan school and the Edsbacka krog restaurant.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och har b: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and has a library, shops and a couple of grill bars. Right beside it stands Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church. And somewhere in the rock not far away lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a command centre built in the 1970s to withstand a nuclear bomb, and now back in use by the Swedish Armed Forces.
Edsbergs slott stod färdigt 1760 vid Eds: Edsberg Palace, on the northern shore of Edsviken bay, was completed in 1760 at the initiative of Thure Gustaf Rudbeck, and the Rudbeck family owned it for almost 200 years. Today part of the Royal College of Music's chamber music programme is based here, and the palace has its own wedding room. Close by is Edsbacka krog, the first restaurant in Sweden to win two Michelin stars.
Edsbergskyrkan ritades av Lars Olof Tors: Edsberg Church was designed by Lars Olof Torstensson and completed in 1972. He designed the 2004 altarpiece together with his son Jonas: a painted steel cross surrounded by glass in different colours.
Edsängens gravfält, ett par hundra meter: A couple of hundred metres away is the Edsängen burial ground, with around 125 Viking Age mounds – one of the largest in Sollentuna. Not far from there is something completely different: Elefanten, the Elephant, a command centre blasted into the rock and built to withstand a nuclear bomb. Closest of all is Rudbecksskolan, one of Sweden's biggest sixth-form schools, with around 2,400 students and a national athletics programme.
Edvard Wavrinsky var bland annat ordföra: Among other roles, Edvard Wavrinsky chaired the Gothenburg shooting society, whose range lay on and just south of today's square. When the name was confirmed in 1954, the city council also highlighted his work for temperance and popular movements.
Efter 1861 blev den gamla sjukhusbyggnad: After 1861 the old hospital building became workers' housing for the Sommelii oil mill. Today it's ordinary owner-occupied flats, and it's listed, so the exterior mustn't be altered.
Efter Karl XV:s död 1872 tog kocken Jean: After King Karl XV died in 1872, the chef Jean-François Régis Cadier, founder of the Grand Hôtel, took over the lease. He laid out kitchen gardens at Tivoliudden to supply his hotel with vegetables, and traces of them remain in Tivoliparken.
Efter Postens omvandling år 2000 krympte: After the Swedish postal service was restructured in 2000, operations shrank, and by 2009 just over 300 people worked here. In April 2015 the last mail trains rolled out of Tomteboda.
Efter andra världskriget växte nya föror: After the Second World War, new suburbs sprang up in western Stockholm. This route takes you to Vällingby, planned as an "ABC town" combining work, housing and a centre, and on to Tensta, built during the Million Programme, Sweden's great 1960s–70s housing drive.
Efter att Rondo stängde 1983 byggdes lok: After the Rondo cinema closed in 1983, the premises were converted in 1984. A pharmacy moved into the part facing the square, and the auditorium was given an extra floor with shops and flats.
Efter att Wallenbergs tagit över lät de: After the Wallenbergs took over, in 1895 they had photographer Caroline Gaudard record the interiors – she was much in demand in Gothenburg's wealthy homes. Several of her photographs turned up in 2021 in the archives of AB Papyrus, showing how the villa looked around 1900.
Efter att anläggningen tagits ur bruk 19: After it was taken out of use in 1998, the facility stood completely intact, with all its original fittings, until 2017. In 2010 the idea of giving it listed-building status was raised.
Efter att kommunen bildades 1971 använde: After the municipality was formed in 1971, it used the Härryda Cross, made up of the initials HK. When it tried to register this as a coat of arms in 1977, the application was rejected because the symbol couldn't be described in heraldic terms. A logo featuring an aeroplane followed instead.
Efter att tornet tagits ur bruk i slutet: After it was taken out of use in the late 1960s, the tower served as a radio mast for the city's communications radio and the National Police Board. Since 2008 it has held 74 fan-shaped student flats, with a shared roof terrace on the eleventh floor.
Efter badet: The sculpture Efter badet, 'After the Swim'
Efter den första flottbron kom en ny bro: After the first pontoon bridge came a new bridge, opened on 5 June 1929 after a difficult build. Today's bridge was built alongside it to the east – a steel girder bridge on nine concrete piers, with a clearance of just 1.6 metres.
Efter dieseltiden tillverkades bergborra: After the diesel era, rock drills and compressors were made here, and in the early 1960s Atlas Copco employed about 2,100 people in Sickla. In 1992 production moved to Örebro.
Efter en domstolsprövning sänktes höjden: After a court ruling, Gasklockan was scaled down to 90 metres and around 300 flats. The city terminated the land agreement in 2019, and the dispute concerns, among other things, who should pay for cleaning up tar and oil left from the gasworks era.
Efter en stor ombyggnad 1922 rymde Resta: After a major rebuild in 1922, the Restauranten had several dining rooms, a banqueting hall, a wedding room, a 200-seat cinema and its own bowling alley. The cinema also hosted theatre, dances and concerts.
Efter ett medborgarförslag 2011 rengjord: Following a suggestion from a resident in 2011, a millstone was cleaned up and moved in summer 2013 to Gymnasievägen below Kvarnberget. It's sandstone, about 1.25 metres across, with grooves that channelled the flour out to the edge. Two more stones are set into the pavement by Kvarnbergsgården.
Efter flera bränder är dagens kyrka den: After a series of fires, today's church is the fourth to stand here. Designed by Carl Wilhelm Carlberg in a Neoclassical style, it has been a cathedral since 1665, when Gothenburg became the seat of a bishop.
Efter folkparkstiden revs alla anläggnin: Once its days as a people's park were over, all the attractions were torn down, and Krokäng has been an ordinary park for strolling ever since, covering about 7.5 hectares. It has an unusually rich stand of hazel and old oaks.
Efter folkskolan kunde Spångaelever gå v: After elementary school, Spånga pupils could move on to the trade school, which trained engine fitters and mechanics. Places were limited, and the engines built there were used in races at Solvalla.
Efter föräldrarnas död ärvde Branting en: When his parents died, Hjalmar Branting inherited a considerable fortune – and ran through it in a few years on parties and generous loans. He was also sentenced several times to prison and fines, for offences including blasphemy and breaching press laws.
Efter häktestiden har Bysis varit epidem: After its years as a jail, Bysis has served as an isolation hospital, a disinfection station, a printing works and a handicrafts venue. From the late 1960s the Stockholm Chess Federation was based here, and in 1970 the Museum of the Painting Trade moved in.
Efter hökarna bodde Karin Christoffersdo: After the grocers, Karin Christoffersdotter lived here until her death, and in her day the place was called Krögareholmen, 'Innkeeper's Island'. Perhaps she ran an inn – or it may simply be a slip of the district judge's clerk's pen.
Efter istiden låg hela Järfälla under et: After the Ice Age, the whole of Järfälla lay beneath a sea about 100 metres deep. Around 5200 BC the first hilltop poked up out of the water – today's Hummelmoraberget.
Efter landstinget blev huset vanligt kon: After the county council moved out, the building became an ordinary office block. Following a sale and renovation in 2017–2018, it’s now a hotel, Hotel Gio, with the restaurant Mama Gio on the ground floor. Both names pay tribute to Gio Ponti.
Efter lång strid beslutades 2015 att väg: After a long battle, it was decided in 2015 that the wall should be protected and become the centrepiece of a new park. But in 2020 it was found to be in such poor condition that it risked collapsing, and it was demolished in December 2021.
Efter mordet på Gustav III stannade bygg: After Gustav III was assassinated, building work in the park stopped – except on this very tower. One theory is that Duke Karl, Grand Master of the Swedish Order of Freemasons, wanted to use it for Masonic rites. The King's brother-in-law had already built a similar brick tower on his Louisenlund estate in 1784.
Efter många år med ungdomsverksamhet sto: After many years as a youth centre, the building stood empty in 2008 and was renovated. Today it’s privately owned, and the plot, once 10,100 square metres, has been divided into four.
Efter några ekonomiskt tuffa år utsågs L: After a few tough years financially, Lingström was named Chef of the Year in 1985. The first Michelin star came in 1992 and the second in 2000. In 2002 the restaurant opened a classic casual offshoot across Sollentunavägen: Edsbacka Bistro.
Efter sitt fälttåg 1790 ville Gustav III: After his campaign of 1790, Gustav III wanted to raise a monument to himself at the top of the hill, roughly where Storkyrkan, Stockholm Cathedral, stands – and the church could happily be torn down. A new theatre was planned by the water. The only part that happened was the King's statue at Skeppsbron.
Efter slutet av 1800-talet har husen i s: Since the late 1800s the buildings have stayed much as they were. The farm is still private land owned by the Wedberg family, so visitors can't go beyond the gate. By the entrance, a modern single-storey timber house has been built that blends into its surroundings.
Eftersom ingen bor i kontorsområdet stan: Since nobody lives in the office district, trains used to stop calling here after about half past ten at night, and at weekends only in the middle of the day. Since August 2011 every train stops here.
