En hållplats öppnades här redan 1878. St: A small halt opened here as early as 1878. The 1963 station building was demolished in stages in 2014–2015 when the line was widened to four tracks, and a new platform was built about 250 metres further north. The new station opened on 10 October 2016.
En informationstavla vid stigen berättar: An information board by the path explains that many species live in this urban oasis. When spring and summer arrive, the fen's creatures are in a hurry: they need to find a partner, mate and raise strong young.
En jungfrudans vid entrén: A stone labyrinth at the entrance
En järnväg kallad Krutbanan: A railway called the Gunpowder Line
En jättegryta i källaren: A giant's kettle in the cellar
En jättemyra att klättra på: A giant ant to climb on
En klaffbro byggdes över Tappström redan: A bascule bridge was built over Tappström as early as 1828. In the 1880s it was replaced by an opening wooden bridge paid for by the bank director André Oscar Wallenberg. New bridges followed in 1930 and 1973, and a brand-new swing bridge was planned to take over in 2023.
En koloni som flyttade: An allotment colony on the move
En konstskola ur en studiecirkel: An art school born from a study circle
En kort bit bort ligger Svensbydösen, äv: A short way from here is Svensbydösen, also known as Queen Hacka's Grave. It's the only known long dolmen – a Stone Age burial chamber – in Gothenburg, and the oldest structure in the municipality. Legend has it that a gold ring forged by a giant lies inside, and treasure hunters have done the tomb serious damage looking for it. When the Norrleden road was being planned in 1978, archaeologists excavated the site and confirmed that it really was a dolmen.
En kort bit bort står Centrumkyrkan, en: A short distance away is Centrumkyrkan, a church that changed hands in an unusual way. The Methodists had used it since 1996, but when their congregation grew too small, they handed the building over to the Church of Sweden in 2023. In November 2025 it was consecrated as the new church for Kållered parish in the Mölndal pastorate.
En kort promenad bort fanns Hallinge, en: A short walk away was Hallinge, a small locality that Statistics Sweden designated in 1990, made up of temporary housing just south-west of the Smedstorp croft. It borrowed its name from Hallinge gård, a farm a kilometre and a half away. Today only the Smedstorp croft is left, so Hallinge turned out to be a brief footnote in the statistics.
En kort promenad bort korsar Linnarhults: A short walk away, Linnarhultsbron, the Linnarhult Bridge, crosses the Lärjeån river. It was built in the early 1970s to replace an old stone arch bridge – but the old bridge was never pulled down and still stands right next to the new one. Two bridges side by side: one from the age of the car, the other from a slower time.
En kort promenad bort ligger Ahlby säter: A short walk away is Ahlby säteri, a stone manor house from the 1620s and the oldest surviving building in Lilla Alby. One of its owners was Clas Fredrik Horn af Åminne, who was convicted of complicity in the murder of King Gustav III. Landsvägen, the Country Road, has kept its rural-sounding name because it was once part of the main road out of Stockholm. It's also where you'll find Swedbank's head office, built in the shape of a double V.
En kort promenad bort ligger Annelunds g: A short walk away is Annelund farm, where Per Henrik Ling, ‘the father of gymnastics’, lived from 1822 to 1839. The main house and the gymnastics wing are both listed. According to an old tall tale, Gustav III gave the farm to his favourite, Elis Schröderheim – but it isn't true. Schröderheim lived on another farm that has since vanished.
En kort promenad bort ligger Kärra kyrka: A short walk away is Kärra Church, which was a chapel until 2001 and has belonged to Tuve-Säve parish since 2010. Across the Göta älv river is Agnesberg, where travellers have found food and a bed for several hundred years – it was a coaching stop long before the railway arrived in 1880.
En kort promenad bort ligger Lundby Kolo: A short walk away are the Lundby allotments, Lundby Koloniträdgårdar, originally known as Lundby kolonien – though in 1972 the association had to give up roughly half its land for a football pitch and a car park. Nearby runs Hjalmar Brantingsgatan, one of the city's longest streets at almost 4,400 metres. And down at Frihamnen, along this same street, is the lowest point in Gothenburg, two metres below mean sea level.
En kort promenad bort ligger Park Studio: A short walk away is Park Studios, where artists such as Ace of Base, Stina Nordenstam and Dan Hylander recorded in the 1990s. From 2004 to 2016 the studio was owned by the band Kent and their producer. Park-Bio, the cinema in Örby's Folkets hus community centre, opened in 1928 and showed films until 1968 – and since 2021 the projector has been rolling again. As for Örby Palace, it's now rented by the Embassy of Vietnam.
En kort promenad bort ligger Skändla rös: A short walk away is Skändla rös, a Bronze Age burial cairn 18 metres across and just over two metres high. It sits on the boundary between Bohuslän and Västergötland – which, until the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658, was the border between Sweden and Norway. Every year there's a haymaking day in the meadows next to it, when the grass is cut by hand, scythes and all.
En kort promenad bort ligger Sköndalssko: A short walk away is Sköndalsskolan school, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and opened in 1953. The Swedish National Heritage Board describes its design as unusual for its time, with many interesting architectural details. In the other direction is the Gubbängen business area, also known as the Norra Sköndal industrial area – one of the very smallest in the city.
En kort promenad bort ligger Vällingby c: A short walk away is Vällingby centre, the model for the 1950s suburban dream known as the 'ABC town'. Here you'll find Trappan, a civic centre from 1956 designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, built in terraces between a lower and an upper square and home to theatre, music and a library. Right next door is the brick church of St Thomas, S:t Tomas kyrka, by Peter Celsing, consecrated in 1960, with a wooden crucifix by the artist Bror Hjorth.
En kort promenad bort ligger Västra Fröl: A short walk away is Västra Frölunda churchyard, which dates back to the Middle Ages. The old Västra Frölunda church stood here until it was pulled down in the 1860s. Look out for the iron rings in the churchyard wall – they were for tying up horses. The oldest gravestones date from 1680 and 1729.
En kort promenad bort ligger herrgården: A short walk away is the manor of Stora Frösunda, built in 1783 and given its palatial look in the 1890s. Today it's owned by SAS Institute, and next to it stands the runestone U 121. Nearby rises Hagahuset, built between 1954 and 1957 to house the entire administration of Stockholm County Council.
En kort promenad bort ligger kulturhuset: A short walk away is Cyklopen, a self-run, non-profit cultural centre with music, art and adult education. The first building was burned down by arsonists in 2008, but it was rebuilt. Just below Högdalen centre is Högdalen skatepark: with about 5,500 square metres of concrete, it's the largest in Stockholm and almost as big as Stapelbäddsparken in Malmö.
En kort promenad bort ligger tjärnen Kla: A short walk away is Klare mosse, a pond that's one of the best spots on Hisingen for frogs and newts. Among them is the rare great crested newt, which thrives among all the little pools and hollows. The pond had become overgrown, but it was given a new lease of life by the Osbäck project, and from here the Osbäcken stream flows down towards Björlanda kile.
En kort promenad bort står De tre vingar: A short walk away stands De tre vingarna, The Three Wings, a monumental steel sculpture by the American artist Alexander Calder. The city bought it in the early 1960s, but Angered was running late, so from 1967 the sculpture stood on Götaplatsen as a stopgap. It didn't move out to Angered until 1979. Nearby is Angered Arena, with an ice rink and a swimming pool that puts special emphasis on teaching children to swim.
En kort promenad bort, längs Solvädersby: A short walk away, along Solvädersbyn, are 124 houses with a properly sporting past. They were first built for the 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer, used again for the 1995 World Athletics Championships, and finally settled here in 1996. That's why the streets there have athletics names instead of weather names. On the same site, in 1954, what was then the longest building in Europe went up; it was demolished in 1995.
En kort promenad härifrån ligger Bräcke: A short walk from here is Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft built in the 1830s and a local heritage museum since 1965. From 1889 it was home to the soldier Sven Olof Emanuelsson Björk. The croft hasn't always stood here – it used to be north of Bräcke village. Inside there's only room for a single room, a kitchen and a hallway.
En kort promenad härifrån ligger Dvärgah: A short walk from here is Dvärgahuset, the Dwarf House, a stone cist grave from the late Neolithic. People once believed it was a home for dwarfs – hence the name. Three huge blocks form a roof over the burial chamber, and one of the end slabs has a round hole ground into it whose purpose nobody knows.
En kort promenad härifrån står Torslanda: A short walk from here is Torslanda church, said to be one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. It's the parish church of Torslanda, which until 1967 lay outside the City of Gothenburg, in the old Västra Hising district of the province of Bohuslän. Since 2010 it has been part of Torslanda-Björlanda parish.
En kort promenad härifrån, bredvid Bromm: A short walk from here, beside Bromma Church, is Stockholm's smallest and oldest school, Bromma kyrkskola, dating from 1864. In the mid-1890s the teacher here was also the parish clerk, the organist and the local vaccinator. Before the school was built, children learned their letters in a small room in Gamla Klockargården, the old parish clerk's house next door – teaching had been the parish clerk's job since the mid-1600s.
En kort sträcka ner mot älven. Vid Stenp: A short hop down towards the river. Many of the more than a million Swedes who emigrated to America boarded their ships at Stenpiren.
En kort tur ner mot Sickla udde, där mar: A short ride down towards Sickla udde, where much of the land was built up with blasted rock when Hammarby sjö was lowered by about five metres in 1925.
En krog fanns vid Aspnäs säkert från 179: There was certainly a tavern at Aspnäs from 1792. In 1836 the parish meeting demanded that its licence be withdrawn, and one wholesale merchant claimed the court records were proof of the misconduct there. The tavern seems to have closed around 1843.

En kyrka som slutat vara kyrka finns en: A short walk from here is a church that's no longer a church. Lövgärdet Church was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016 – formally taken out of religious use. Before that it even switched parishes, belonging to Gunnared parish from 1973 and to Angered in its final years. Lövgärdet itself is a neighbourhood in the Gårdsten district of north-eastern Gothenburg.
En landsortskyrka i stan: A country church in the city
En landsväg i ungefär samma sträckning s: A country road following roughly the same route as today's Stockholmsvägen already appears on Lars Kietzlingh's map of 1720. At Torsvik it met a ferry to and from Ropsten – before the bridges, that was how you got into town.
En lind på minst 800 år: A linden at least 800 years old
En liten stump av Bräckelinjens spår fin: A short stretch of the old Bräcke line actually survives. These days trams use it as a skid-training track.
En lättsam dag för barnfamiljer: spårvag: An easy-going day for families: tram out to Skansen with its Nordic animals, a stroll past the Gröna Lund amusement park and a ferry back to Slussen.
En lång tur genom hela staden. Luta dig: A long ride right across the city. Sit back and listen.
En midsommarkrans i taket: A midsummer wreath on the ceiling
En minnessten på Järvafältet bär inskrip: A memorial stone on Järvafältet is inscribed: 'The armed forces units garrisoned in the Stockholm area trained here 1905–1970'. Even so, the shooting went on longer still: Järva's firing ranges didn't close until 2002.
En minnestavla på fasaden berättar att h: A plaque on the facade says the building was paid for by the 'rare generosity' of an anonymous donor, adding: 'To God he is not unknown.' The parish doctor lived and saw patients upstairs.
One minute to Gröna Lund amusement park.
En ny idrottshall omgiven av studentläge: The plan was for a new sports hall surrounded by student flats – something never before built in Sweden. But because the city couldn't guarantee it would rent the hall, the developer decided not to go ahead.
En oljemålning från 1865 av Johan Christ: An 1865 oil painting by Johan Christoffer Boklund shows Karl XV and his family on an outing to Calles klimp, a rocky outcrop. Karl XV himself made the original for a woodcut of the spot. The National Museum later renamed the painting "Calles klint".
En pappa som köpte utsikten: A father who bought the view
En portal från Gamla stans krog: A doorway from an Old Town tavern
En promenad bort ligger Slätta damm, som: A short walk away is Slätta damm, a pond that formed around 1860 in S.A. Hedlunds park. There's a barbecue spot and a waffle café by the water, and in cold winters people go skating on the ice. The birds you'll see swimming here are mostly ducks and goldeneyes. The park is part of Hisingsparken, the largest park in Gothenburg.
En promenad längs stråket spänner över m: A walk along this route spans many eras, from Storkyrkan, the 13th-century cathedral in Gamla stan, to the arenas and shopping malls of the 21st century. Along the way you'll also pass the Serafimer Hospital, Sweden's very first hospital.
En resa genom hundra år av Stockholmsark: A journey through a hundred years of Stockholm architecture: from Gunnar Asplund's library and the 1923 City Hall to Ricardo Bofill's arch and Backström & Reinius's star-shaped houses in Gröndal. You'll switch between bus and the Tvärbanan light rail and hop off wherever the buildings are best seen.
En riktig kuriosa: på J. Sigfrid Edström: Here's a real oddity: on J. Sigfrid Edströms gata, traffic drives on the left – even though the rest of Sweden drives on the right. It's down to the way the tracks in and out of the Rantorget tram depot are laid out. The street is named after the first director of Gothenburg's tramways. In Gårdahallen next door, the tram society Spårvägssällskapet Ringlinien looks after the city's vintage trams and buses.
En rundkyrka att fly till: A round church to flee to
En runorm i form av en åtta: A rune serpent in a figure of eight
En runorm i åtta: A rune serpent in a figure of eight
En sal döpt efter arkitekten: A hall named after the architect
En seglivad skröna säger att godstågslok: A stubborn tall tale has it that a freight locomotive sank into the mud and was forgotten. Långsjöparken even has a play locomotive sinking into a sandpit. But the story isn't true: the engine was scrapped in Östersund, and not until 1966.
En skola som delats och slagits ihop: A school split up and merged again
En slöjdskola för fattiga barn: A craft school for poor children
En smal allé ut till Malmvik: A narrow avenue out to Malmvik
En stadskarta runt taket: A map of the city around the ceiling
En station helt utan konst: A station with no art at all

En stor del av Stockholms gat- och kants: Much of Stockholm's paving and kerb stone was quarried here. From 1884 to 1919 around 100 men worked here all year round, and the stone was shipped out on barges, since the water was the only way in or out. The quarry closed in 1937, when cheaper stone could be bought from Bohuslän and Blekinge.

Much of Stockholm's paving and kerbstone was quarried at Stenhamra. From 1884 to 1919 around 100 men worked here all year round, and the stone was shipped on barges, since the water was the only link. Quarrying stopped in 1937, when cheaper stone could be bought from Bohuslän and Blekinge.

En vattenvakt bodde i stugan till en bit: A waterworks keeper lived in the cottage until some way into the 1950s, and the last of the family didn't move out until 1963. After that the house fell into disrepair. It was restored to its original condition, with period furniture, and reopened on 9 September 2007.

En vit fläck på kartan: A blank spot on the map
En väderkvarn har stått på Kvarnbacken s: A windmill has stood on Kvarnbacken since the 1780s, and it was in use until the 1920s. It burned down in 1980, and the replicas built afterwards burned in turn in 1997 and 2005. Only the foundations are left, but Walpurgis Night and Midsummer are still celebrated on the hill.
En väderkvarn som har flyttat två gånger: Here's a windmill that has moved house twice! Kälvesta kvarn, also called Lilla Stampan, was built in the 1600s and first stood on a hill by Observatoriegatan in central Stockholm. In 1884 it was moved to Lunda, and in 1892 it arrived at its current spot on Skestavägen in Solhem, a short walk from here.
En väg rakt genom gravfältet: A road straight through the burial ground
En å nästan utan fall: A river with hardly any drop
Endre Nemes väggkonstverk består av ett: Endre Nemes's mural is made from some sixty kinds of marble and measures 9.30 by 8.40 metres. The stonemasons put 7,500 hours into it before it was unveiled in April 1955.
Enebyberg är ett villasamhälle med cirka: Enebyberg is a residential community of about 5,000 people, full of houses from the first half of the 20th century. It belongs to Danderyd municipality but borders both Täby and Sollentuna. A couple of blocks away is Eneby Church on Eneby torg, which the Church of Sweden and the Uniting Church in Sweden share.
Engelsmannen Samuel Owen hade monterat å: The Englishman Samuel Owen had assembled steam engines in England before becoming works manager at Bergsund. Under his direction, the Bergsund foundry built the first steam engine ever made in Sweden, in 1807.
Enkel sten från slutet av 1000-talet: A plain stone from the late 11th century
Enligt Jan Wallander bodde Per Albin Han: According to Jan Wallander, Per Albin Hansson and Sigfrid Hansson lived with their families off the same stairwell in the 1920s. The artist Einar Jolin painted in a top-floor flat, and a cousin became tutor to Egypt's Crown Prince Farouk.
Enligt Trafikverket ska ytterligare ett: According to the Swedish Transport Administration, another tunnel tube is to be built through the cliff at Lindö, as part of the improvements around the Förbifart Stockholm bypass.
Enligt en gammal skröna skulle Gustav II: An old story has it that Gustav III gave Annelund to his favourite, Elis Schröderheim, but it isn’t true. The name most likely comes from the wholesale merchant Eric Giers, who named the farm after his wife, Anna Maria.
Enligt en legend tappade drottning Krist: Legend has it that Queen Christina’s horse lost a silver shoe here as her coronation procession passed by in 1650. The story is highly unlikely, since Silverdal isn’t on the road between Ulriksdal and Stockholm. What’s more, the croft was originally called Skogsdal.
Enligt en muntlig tradition ska smedjan: Local lore has it that the smithy belonged to Älvsborg Castle, but that has never been proven. What is certain is that it's marked as Smedia on a map from 1783.
Enligt en sägen byggdes stenmuren runt S: Legend has it that the stone wall around Stengärdet was built by Russian prisoners of war in the 1700s. No one knows for sure when it went up, and some of the stones even bear the marks of modern rock drills.
Enligt en teori lät Sankt Sigfrid bygga: One theory has it that Saint Sigfrid had Örgryte's first Christian church built here in the 11th century. The legend may hold a grain of truth: during a restoration, the remains of a wooden church dated to the 1000s were found. The stone church from the 1200s probably doubled as a stronghold.
Enligt en tradition planerades mordet på: According to tradition, the assassination of King Gustav III was planned at the manor over a Christmas dinner in 1791. Carl Fredrik Ehrensvärd, whose father owned Hallunda, admitted his involvement and was sentenced to exile for life.
Enligt ett förslag från 2017 skulle tvil: Under a 2017 proposal, the twin towers would have been 243 and 183 metres tall, with a sky bar, restaurant and visitor centre at the top. Of the nearly 1,200 planned homes, more than 95 per cent would have been one- or two-room flats.
Enligt folkräkningen 1910 bodde lagerbit: According to the 1910 census, stockroom assistant Karl Fritiof Leonard Hagman Svensson lived here with his wife Gerda and their two children. The family were probably the first to live at Valdorshem.
Enligt gamla beskrivningar var tullen in: According to old descriptions, the toll gate was no pleasant spot: muddy roads, shabby wooden shacks and trading booths. To make matters worse, the gallows hill and the cholera cemetery were nearby.
Enligt legenden tappade drottning Kristi: Legend has it that Queen Christina's horse lost a silver shoe here as her coronation procession passed in 1650. The story is highly unlikely, though, since Silverdal doesn't lie on the road between Ulriksdal and Stockholm – and the croft was originally called Skogsdal anyway.

Legend has it that Queen Christina's horse lost a silver shoe here during her coronation procession in 1650. It's a very unlikely tale, since Silverdal isn't on the road between Ulriksdal and Stockholm – and the croft was originally called Skogsdal.
Enligt legenden växte helgonet Sankt Bot: Legend has it that Saint Botvid grew up at Hammarby gård, a short way from here by Prästviken bay on Lake Aspen – and Botkyrka is named after him. In the Middle Ages the farm became a rectory, and the present main house from 1804 was the church's rectory right up until 1997. The farm is even mentioned in the runic inscription on the famous Botkyrka monument by the church.

Legend has it that St Botvid grew up at Hammarby farm, a short way from here on Prästviken bay in Lake Aspen – and it's after him that Botkyrka is named. In the Middle Ages the farm became a rectory, and the present main house, from 1804, served as the church's rectory right up until 1997. The farm is even mentioned in the runic inscription on the famous Botkyrka monument; the original is in the Swedish History Museum, while a copy stands by the church.
Enligt planerna skulle utbyggnaden ta 12: The development was supposed to take 12 years but ended up taking 18. Along the way it was built more densely, so instead of the planned 12,000 residents there were 16,300.
Enligt stadsplanen skulle villorna i Lär: Under the town plan, the villas in Lärkan were to be single-family homes, but the rule was often dodged. Staaff's house had rooms to let, with their own WC and shower, on the upper floors. Only 21 of the 51 plots were built with true villas for a single household.
Enligt tidskriften Studio sjöng Joey Tem: According to the magazine Studio, Joey Tempest recorded the vocals for Europe’s ‘The Final Countdown’ at Soundtrade. At the time the studio was working with the record label Alpha Records.
Enligt traditionen fick krogen Pungpinan: Tradition has it that the Pungpinan inn got its name from guests squeezing (pina) their purses (pung) to pay for their brännvin, Swedish aquavit. It was also known as Skarpnecks krog or Krogen i kröken, 'the inn on the bend'. The inn is first mentioned in 1670, and the building was demolished in 1876.
Enligt traditionen var det en man från L: Tradition has it that a man from Livonia called Mickel lived in the hillside cottage Mickelsberg. The cottage stood right up against a rock face. It's gone now, but the name lives on in Mickelsbergsvägen.
Enligt traditionen visade Gustav Vasa pr: Tradition has it that Gustav Vasa proved his courage at the Battle of Vädla in 1517, right where the bridge’s northern abutment stands today.
Eric Grates park fick sitt namn 1993. Fö: Eric Grate's park got its name in 1993. Besides Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God, there's a third bronze by Grate here: Nike de Sant Andria from 1968.
Erik Dahlbergh tecknade Rissne gård på 1: Erik Dahlbergh drew Rissne farm in the 1660s: a four-storey manor house with stepped gables. In 1811 the top two floors were removed because of rot. Since 1983 the farm has been a listed building.
Erik Josephson återanvände gamla delar i: Erik Josephson reused old salvaged parts in his villa. The entrance door on Valhallavägen was carved in the 1700s, and the carriage gate on Baldersgatan comes from the Piehl house on Drottninggatan, with carved helmets and double axes in the Empire style.
Eriksberg var ett av Göteborgs stora var: Eriksberg was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. The huge gantry crane that still towers over the site is a reminder of those days, and it has become a landmark for the whole riverside.
Eriksbo byggdes 1968–1971 med omkring 1: Eriksbo was built in 1968–1971, with around 1,100 flats in three-storey slab blocks, on land taken over from Angered municipality in 1967. There are older detached houses here too. The area is made up of three parts: Hjällbogärdet, Västergärdet and Östergärdet.
Eriksbo ligger i Lärjeåns dalgång, med b: Eriksbo sits in the Lärjeån valley, with steep hills north of Gråbovägen. The Västgöta railway once ran through the valley, and its old trackbed is now a cycle path.
Eriksbo ligger i Lärjeåns dalgång, och h: Eriksbo sits in the valley of the Lärjeån river, its houses climbing a slope towards Gråbovägen, with steep hills rising on the north side. The Västgötabanan railway once ran through the valley, and its old embankment is now a cycle path.
Erikskrönikan berättar att stormannen Jo: Erik's Chronicle tells how the nobleman Jon Jarl was killed by Estonians in the 13th century. His wife fled to Hundhammar, gathered men and drove the Estonians up onto the hill Estaskär. There they lost their lives, and she had their ships hauled ashore and burnt.
Eskil Sundahl fyllde sin villa med moder: Eskil Sundahl filled his villa with modern conveniences such as underfloor heating and triple glazing. "To reduce the bother of shovelling snow", he had the area in front of the garage heated with electric cables – effective but expensive, as he himself pointed out. A lift ran between the entrance and the living floor.
Eskil Sundahl gav sin villa golvvärme, t: Eskil Sundahl gave his villa underfloor heating, triple glazing and a lift between the entrance and the living floor. To avoid shovelling snow, he had the forecourt by the garage heated with electric cables – effective but expensive to run, as he himself pointed out.
Essingeleden svävar förbi här på Blommen: The Essingeleden motorway sweeps past on the Blommensberg viaduct, spanning the Vinterviken valley and almost skimming the roofs of Blommensberg school. The bridge opened on 21 August 1966. Just a stone's throw away is Stora Fågelsången, an 18th-century farm by the little lake Trekanten, whose garden is now allotments – without the usual cabins. A bit further on stands Sankt Sigfrid's church, a red wooden church moved here from Vasastaden in 1904.
Etoile öppnade 2018 i kvarteret Sländan,: Etoile opened in 2018 in the Sländan block, founded by the chefs Jonas Lagerström, Rakel Wennemo and Danny Falkeman. The cooking is described as experimental, with flavours from all over the world.

Ett av de sista tillskotten är en jättel: One of the latest additions is an enormous car showroom in the Spejaren block, finished in 2019. It covers more than 25,000 square metres: two floors of sales and offices and two of parking. Small wonder the area is known as the 'Smista allé car cluster'.
Ett av landets bäst bevarade: One of the best preserved in Sweden
Ett av rummen har en kakelugn från 1700-: One of the rooms has an 18th-century tiled stove. It was brought here from Lärjeholm manor, and before that it stood in the pastor's residence of the German Church.
One of the rooms has an 18th-century tiled stove. It came here from the Lärjeholm estate, and before that it stood in the parsonage of the German Church.

Ett hotell man bor i på riktigt! Hässelb: Here's a hotel people actually live in! When Hässelby familjehotell, the family hotel, opened in 1955, it was the builder Olle Engkvist's largest co-housing block. The staffed services were dropped in 1976, but residents still keep some of them going as volunteers. Its neighbour, Hässelby ungdomshotell, the youth hotel, originally had flats for young people and for pensioners, as well as artists' studios and a day nursery.

Ett litet namnskämt: tunnelbanestationen: Here's a little naming quirk: Abrahamsberg metro station isn't actually in Abrahamsberg at all, but in Riksby. Before the metro came, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals in glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are a nod to the tiled stations of the tram era. Close by is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955.
Ett litet tempel på en kulle: A little temple on a hill
Ett lokstall som heter Sundbyberg fast d: An engine shed called Sundbyberg – even though it's in Solna! The old steam locomotive shed and water tower building were put up in 1904 by the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen Railway, and SJ named them Sundbyberg because they were near that station. The buildings are well preserved and considered of very high cultural and historical value. The nearby Huvudstaleden road was planned as part of an urban motorway, but only part of it was ever built.
Ett minne från biograftiden lever kvar:: One reminder of the cinema days lives on: the cinema's drinking fountain still stands in the studio's entrance.

Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Kvarnto: A couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, a rune-carved rock slab discovered in 1943 by the author Jan Fridegård. Its inscription includes the word 'stepsons', which is rare in runic texts. Nearby is the egg-shaped Näsbydal housing estate, with 900 flats ranging from a single room to seven rooms over two floors. Next door, the Grindtorp area sits beside what used to be Täby's racecourse.
Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Tacksäg: A couple of hundred metres away is Tacksägelsekyrkan, the Church of Thanksgiving, also known as Trångsund Church. It was designed by the architect Sture Frölén and consecrated in 1957, as Trångsund was growing into a town. It served as the parish church until 1987, when Mariakyrkan in Skogås took over. Beside the church there's a memorial grove and a small burial ground.
Ett par hundra meter bort står Tibble ky: A couple of hundred metres away stands Tibble Church, which has been called the Cathedral of Roslagen and is both church and administrative centre for Täby parish. The Tibble district is also home to Täby Centrum, and its library holds a Viking Age runestone fragment from Lissby measuring just 47 by 46 centimetres. It was found in 1930 together with a piece that turned out to belong to a different stone.

A couple of hundred metres away is Tibble Church, sometimes called the cathedral of Roslagen, which serves as both a church and the administrative centre of Täby parish. The Tibble district is also home to Täby centrum, and its library holds two fragments of Viking Age runestones found at Lissby in 1930. One of them measures just 47 by 46 centimetres.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån ligger Hög: A couple of hundred metres from here is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry, where feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined from 1945 until the late 1950s. The rock also held rare minerals such as monazite and columbite. Today the quarries are part of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve, which is also home to the small lake Axlemossen.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån låg Hörnin: A couple of hundred metres from here, by what is now Parkhemsvägen, stood Hörningsnäs gård, a manor and large estate in Huddinge parish. The farm buildings burned down in the 1950s, but the name lives on in the Hörningsnäs housing area. A little further on is Lake Trehörningen, where you may spot bats and protected frogs and toads.

A couple of hundred metres from here, where Parkhemsvägen runs today, stood Hörningsnäs, a manor and sizeable estate in Huddinge parish. In the late 1950s the rural municipality of Huddinge bought the estate and had the house burned down, but the name lives on in the Hörningsnäs housing area. A little further away is Lake Trehörningen, where you might spot bats and protected frogs and toads.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån stod Hagst: A couple of hundred metres from here stood Hagstaeken, a mighty oak in Glömsta. Measured round the trunk, it was the biggest of the ten oaks protected as natural monuments in Huddinge. On the night of 3 December 2025 it was cut down for safety reasons, following a government decision and despite protests. A little further on, the valley of Glömstadalen opens up, an area the municipality values for its cultural heritage.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån står Stens: A couple of hundred metres from here is Stensjökyrkan, one of the two churches in Stensjön parish. A little further on, at the very top of the steep hill on Kvarnbygatan known as Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow, is Mölndal's city museum. Its café serves lunch on weekdays and coffee and cakes at weekends – a well-earned reward after that climb.
Ett par hundra meter sydväst om gamla Ve: A couple of hundred metres south-west of old Veddesta farm is Fruns backe, a burial ground with more than 70 visible graves. The village probably dates back to the early Viking Age. On Kvarnbacken hill are the remains of the farm's windmill.
Ett par kvarter bort ligger Atlantisområ: A couple of blocks away is Atlantis, a 1950s terraced-house village that drew international attention – Olof Palme lived here with his family from 1968 to 1983. Further off, in Beckomberga, stood Beckomberga sjukhus, a psychiatric hospital built in 1930–1932 that stayed open until 1995. Since the mid-2000s its old buildings have been turned into homes.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Filmstaden H: A couple of minutes away is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's biggest cinema, with eighteen screens and 4,166 seats in all. It's part of Kungens kurva, which together with Skärholmen Centre draws 30 million visitors a year. Long before the popcorn arrived, this was the site of Sadelmakartorp, the saddler's croft, which dates back to the late 17th century and became a schoolhouse after 1860.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Högdalens sk: A couple of minutes away is Högdalen skatepark, also known as Highvalley Skateworld – a whole concrete world for skaters, with a freestyle area, a children's area, the Mega Ditch and a bowl. At around 5,500 square metres, it's the biggest in Stockholm. Next door is Cyklopen, a cultural centre run entirely by volunteers, and a little further on is Högdalen's town centre, which was modelled on the centre in Vällingby.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Skärisbiogra: A couple of minutes away is Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is run by Kulturhuset Stadsteatern, Stockholm's culture house and city theatre. Its neighbours are the Red Cross folk high school, offering courses with an international and humanitarian focus, and the old Skärholmen upper secondary school from 1974. Underneath it all lie traces of Smista gård, a farm that goes back to the 800s, in the Viking Age.
Ett par minuter bort snurrar Vridande mo: A couple of minutes away, Vridande moment, ‘Torque’, slowly turns. Also known as Skruven, the Screw, Aston Forsberg's steel sculpture has become the emblem of Skärholmen centrum. It won first prize in an ideas competition in 1968. Skärholmen centrum had 15 million visitors in 2013, and together with nearby Kungens kurva, home to the world's second-largest IKEA store, it forms the biggest out-of-town shopping area in the Nordic countries.
Ett par minuter härifrån börjar Ulriksda: A couple of minutes from here, the Ulriksdal nature reserve begins – about 32 hectares between the Brunnsviken and Edsviken bays, protected since 1988. It also includes the ancient graves of the Mellanjärva burial ground. In the palace park stands Villa Beylon, a pink-rendered brick villa from 1803, next to Ulriksdal Palace Theatre, which has been a state-listed building since 1935.
Ett par minuter härifrån ligger Björkäng: A couple of minutes from here is the Björkängen sports ground, with a football pitch and two ice rinks where Huddinge IK play their home hockey games. One of the rinks used to be called Nickehallen, after the club stalwart Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. Until 2018 the area belonged to the Stuvsta-Snättringe municipal district, which was then split in two, so that Stuvsta and Snättringe each became a district of their own.
Ett par minuter härifrån står runstenarn: A couple of minutes from here are the Häradsvägen runestones, a pair from the Viking Age. One of them has had quite an adventure: in the 1800s it served as a doorstep in Lindal, then went missing for a while before turning up again in 1938, lying on a burial mound at Skälby gård. The other was given a rather fanciful interpretation by Olof Rudbeck the Elder in his work Atlantica.
Ett par minuter härifrån, längs Hallunda: A couple of minutes away, on the Hallunda heritage trail opposite Slagsta motel, is a rock carving that wasn't discovered until 1971. Nearby is Slagsta gård, a historic manor, and down by Lake Mälaren is Slagstabadet, an EU-designated bathing spot with excellent water quality. One of Slagsta's two brickworks once stood there, and in the woods you can still make out terraces and old house foundations.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Lå: A couple of minutes' walk away is Långsjö farm, on the northern shore of Lake Långsjön. It has two identical main houses, and the reason is a touching one: the businessman Robert Ditzinger built them in 1882, one for each of his two sons. The farm goes back to the 17th century and gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Ty: A couple of minutes' walk away is Tyresövallen, formerly known as Bollmoravallen. It's the home ground of Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns, with room for about 2,700 spectators. Tyresö's ice rink is in the same area, and a little further on is the glass-roofed Tyresö centrum, with the municipal offices and library.
Ett par stenkast bort, i Sundby, ligger: Just a short way off, in Sundby, two rune-carved rock slabs lie side by side: U 80, large and richly decorated, and U 81, which was never finished. Sundby is counted as part of Old Spånga. The name has been known since 1312, although the district itself wasn't created until 1953, on land the City of Stockholm had bought from Spånga in 1949.

Ett stenkast bort ligger Hagsätra centru: A stone's throw away is Hagsätra centrum, the local town centre, which opened in 1960 – the same year the metro arrived. Look out for Barnet med käpphästen, the Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist that has become the centre's emblem. A little further on there's an outdoor pool with a funny name: Älvsjöbadet. Despite what it says, it isn't in Älvsjö at all, but right here in Hagsätra. It was built in 1937–1938.
Ett stenkast bort ligger Älta kyrka, int: A stone's throw away is Älta Church, beside Ältavägen. The road was built in 1934 and winds for just over eight kilometres through the open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. The neighbouring area of Stensö carries a memory of the water: the peninsula was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip the Stensö beach invites you in for a swim.
Ett stenkast bort står Vårby gårds kyrka: Close by is Vårby gård church, colourful and full of imagination, and considered one of the first postmodern buildings in Sweden. It was consecrated on 25 May 1975 and sits on a slope looking out over Lake Mälaren, next to a Viking Age burial ground. And just south-west of the church, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard – a cache of silver treasure – was discovered in 1871.
Ett stenkast härifrån breder Rålambshovs: Just nearby is Rålambshovsparken – Rålis to the locals – named after the old Rålambshov estate. The park was laid out in the 1930s, at around the same time as Västerbron, the Western Bridge, and Lilla Västerbron, the Little Western Bridge, runs straight across it. By the square you'll also find Riksarkivet, the National Archives. Its main building was completed in 1968, when the archives moved here from Gamla Riksarkivet, the Old National Archives, on Riddarholmen.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Albykistan,: A stone's throw from here is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist – a type of late Stone Age grave that is very rare around Lake Mälaren. Only seven are known in the whole of Stockholm County, and this one has been dated to around 1800 BC. From the Stone Age to the big top: Alby is also home to Subtopia, the base of the contemporary circus company Cirkus Cirkör.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Bullegumman: Close by is Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, named after Mrs Liljegren, who in the 1930s sold home-baked buns through a hatch in the wall of her house to children on their way to Påvelundsskolan. The house was later used for a while as a reception centre for refugees. It still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there in 2011.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Kristineber: A stone's throw away is Kristineberg Castle, a manor that looks like a castle. It was once a malmgård – a country house on the edge of the city – and still has much of its 18th-century character. The main house has been a private home since the 1930s, while the wings are used by Kristinebergsskolan school. Over by Fredhällsparken park was the Tranan cinema, which showed films from 1933 to 1961.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger en teater s: A stone's throw from here is a theatre that used to be a barn. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is home to six amateur theatre societies, all under one shared umbrella organisation. These days it's mostly revues and comedies created by young people, and the building even has an English-language theatre group.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Ågestaverke: Just a stone's throw away is Ågestaverket, the Ågesta plant – also known as R3 or Adam – which was Sweden's first nuclear power station to supply energy to consumers. Most of its output was district heating for Farsta, which earned it the name ‘the nuclear heating plant’. The reactor ran on heavy water and natural uranium. It closed in 1974, but most of it is still standing and has found a new role as a training ground for Stockholm's fire service.

A stone's throw from here lies the Ågesta plant, also known as R3 or Adam, Sweden's first nuclear power station to supply energy to consumers. It mainly provided district heating for Farsta, which earned it the name 'the atomic heating plant'. The reactor ran on heavy water and natural uranium. It closed in 1974 and became a training ground for the Stockholm fire brigade, before Vattenfall dismantled it in 2020–2025.
Ett stenkast härifrån låg Råsunda fotbol: A stone's throw from here stood Råsunda football stadium. The 1958 World Cup final was played there on 29 June, when Brazil beat Sweden 5–2 in front of almost 50,000 spectators. The stadium closed in 2012, once the new national arena in Arenastaden was finished, and the site has since been turned into homes and offices.
Ett stenkast härifrån står Ängbystenen,: A stone's throw from here, on a small knoll in the middle of the houses, stands Ängbystenen, runestone U 60. It gave its name to Runstensvägen, Runestone Road, and the streets around it also have names linked to runes and the Viking Age. A little further on is Björklunds hage, Bromma's best-preserved burial ground from the early Viking Age, and the Stora Ängby manor, whose main house dates from the very end of the 1600s.
Ett stycke härifrån slingrar sig Bällsta: Not far from here winds the Bällstaån stream, also called Spångaån in its upper reaches. It rises on a hill in Viksjö and goes on quite an adventure: under Spånga it runs through a tunnel about 1.4 kilometres long, and further on it crosses the Solvalla trotting track end to end, right through the green infield.

Exakt 50 år senare publicerade DN en ann: Exactly 50 years later the newspaper DN published another version. According to one of the court chauffeurs, Prince Gustaf Adolf's car tried to overtake the king's, and chauffeur Gösta Ledin said "We'll take him" and put his foot down. Instead of getting past, they ended up in the ditch.

Exactly 50 years later the newspaper DN published another version: the King's car had supposedly been racing Prince Gustaf Adolf's. The King loved speed and was annoyed at being overtaken. “We'll have him,” said the chauffeur, and put his foot down.
FFA gick 2001 upp i Totalförsvarets fors: In 2001 the aeronautical research institute FFA was merged into the Swedish Defence Research Agency, FOI. The wind tunnel work carried on for a while, and in 2008 it was taken over by the consultancy Sjöland & Thyselius, which set up a new company, STARCS, to keep it going.
Fabriken består av tre delar: TA där kar: The plant has three parts: TA, where the bodies are assembled; TB, the paint shop; and TC, where the car gets its final assembly. The first two are largely automated, while most of the work in final assembly is done by hand.
Fabriken byggde bostäder åt sina arbetar: The factory built homes for its workers from the 1880s, but the earliest houses have since been demolished or burnt down. In the 1940s four narrow apartment blocks went up to designs by Wejke & Ödéen, and they're still standing today.
Fabriken som byggde orten: The factory that built the town
Fabriken vid Barnhusviken växte snabbt:: The factory at Barnhusviken grew fast: in 1895 it made some 16,000 cream separators, and around the turn of the century the workforce rose from 345 to 1,300. The site eventually covered three hectares. Today only the office building remains.
Fabriksbyggnaden med sin svängda fasad m: The factory building with its curved street façade is still here. The tall chimney was taken down, and in 1985–1990 the building was converted into the Henriksborg serviced offices.
Fagersjö började som en del av Södertörn: Fagersjö started life as part of Södertörns villastad, a planned garden suburb. Nearby is Villa Edvardshäll, the very first villa in the Fagersjö area, built in 1903 just north of what was then the brand-new Nynäs railway. Its builder, the machinist Axel Edvard Samuelsson, named the house after himself – and naming your villa after yourself became something of a tradition among Fagersjö's pioneers.
Fagersjö hade en gång en egen station på: Fagersjö once had its own station on the Nynäs line, but it closed in May 1963. Commuter trains started running ten years later and still pass straight through without stopping.
Fagersjö hade en gång en station på Nynä: Fagersjö once had a station on the Nynäs line, but it closed in May 1963. The commuter trains still run past today – they just don’t stop.
Fagersjö ligger utmed sjön Magelungens n: Fagersjö stretches along the northern shore of Lake Magelungen, and it's home to Högdalstoppen – two of Stockholm's highest points, with sweeping views over the south of the city. The street has its own little story too: Villa Lundin, nicknamed ‘the Castle’, was once at Vildandsvägen 14. In the 1930s the Lundin family are said to have owned one of the only two cars in Fagersjö.
Fagersjö var en del av Södertörns villas: Fagersjö was part of Södertörns villastad, a garden suburb laid out by two businessmen in the early 1900s. Business went badly, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought up the company's land. Another house named after its owner is Villa Lindhov, built in 1910 for Harald Lind.

Fagersjö was part of the Södertörn garden suburb, but business was poor, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought the land. The first house in the Fagersjö section was Villa Edvardshäll from 1903, which machinist Edvard Samuelsson named after himself.
Fagersjös landmärke är Högdalsreservoare: Fagersjö's landmark is the Högdalen reservoir, a water tower from 1958 designed by the architect Nils Sterner. The Stockholm City Museum rates it as highly important to the cityscape.
Fagersjös landmärke är vattentornet Högd: Fagersjö's landmark is the Högdalen reservoir water tower from 1958, designed by Nils Sterner. The Stockholm City Museum considers it highly important to the cityscape.
Fagersjöskogen has unusually large trees. The spruces measure over three metres round the trunk, and there are aspens of around two metres – considered rare. Goshawks and black woodpeckers nest in the woods.
Faggens krog är en nästan musealt bevara: Faggens krog is an 18th-century townhouse preserved almost like a museum. Carl Michael Bellman sang about it, and over the years it has been both a tavern and a cloth factory. Just below the music pavilion on Vita bergen stood Ceders Café, where the Ceder family served summer fika – coffee and cake – from the 1910s onwards. The building was later used by the youth club Vitabergsklubben, led by the author Per Anders Fogelström, until arsonists destroyed it in 1969 and 1970.
Falutorget fick 1883 sitt namn efter Fal: Falutorget was named in 1883 after Falun, the town at the far end of the Bergslagsbanan railway, and until the 1860s this ground was reed bed on the edge of the Göta älv river. For many years the square was overshadowed by Gasklockan, the gasholder – an 86-metre-tall round structure you could see from much of Gothenburg. It was taken out of use in 1993 and finally demolished in 2017, after delays caused in part by nesting peregrine falcons.
Falutorget fick sitt namn 1883 efter Fal: Falutorget was named in 1883 after Falun, the far end of the Bergslagsbanan railway, whose station building stood nearby. Until the 1860s this was all reed beds, part of the Göta älv river, until dredging created new land. For many years the Gasklockan gasholder towered over the area: 86 metres tall and visible from much of the city. It was taken out of use in 1993, and when it was finally demolished in 2017, the work was held up by – among other things – nesting peregrine falcons.
Familjehotellet har fyra höghus och fler: The family hotel has four tower blocks and several low-rise buildings, with 340 flats in all. A 750-metre corridor links everything together, so you can walk to the dining hall without getting your feet wet, whatever the weather.
Familjehotellets hus binds ihop av ett 7: The family hotel's buildings are linked by a 750-metre corridor system. The idea was that residents could reach the dining room and the building's other facilities in any weather without getting their feet wet.
Familjen Jansson bodde i Storgården och: The Jansson family lived at Storgården and farmed the land from the 1790s right up to 1974, when the last harvest was brought in. By then, building work on the new district had already started the year before.
The Jansson family lived at Storgården and farmed the land from the 1790s right up until 1974, when the last harvest was brought in. Work on the new district had already started the year before.
Familjen Widstrand kallade sitt hem ”Vil: The Widstrand family called their home ‘Villa Skoga’. That same year, 1906, the business partner Per Karl Wahlström moved to Storängen, and the artist Gottfrid Kallstenius became a neighbour. In the 1960s the Saltsjöbaden road cut off the villa’s path down to the lake.
Farsta Centrum var den första platsen i: Farsta Centrum was the first place in Stockholm where you could use a parking disc. It made its debut on 1 December 1993.
Farsta brandstation har en särskild styr: Farsta fire station has a special sea rescue unit that carries out rescues and fights fires at sea, flown out by helicopter. The station was renamed from Enskede fire station when Farsta parish was formed in 1957.
Farsta centrum invigdes den 23 oktober 1: Farsta Centre opened on 23 October 1960 and was big for its day, escalators and all. Its car park, with space for 4,000 cars, was one of the largest in Europe, and moving walkways were installed to carry shoppers from their cars to the shops. Farsta was hailed as the southern suburbs' answer to Vällingby.
Farsta gård: Farsta gård, the old Farsta manor farm
Farsta gård nämns i ett pergamentsbrev f: Farsta gård is mentioned in a parchment letter from 1384, when it was owned by the powerful nobleman Bo Jonsson Grip. Its lands covered what are now Fagersjö, Hökarängen, Larsboda, Farsta, Farstanäset, Farsta Strand and parts of Sköndal.
Farsta gård och Farstastenen: Farsta gård and the Farsta runestone
Farsta gård vid Magelungen har rötter än: Farsta gård, on the shores of Lake Magelungen, has roots that go all the way back to the 14th century. Today the farm is run by the Farsta association council, an umbrella group of around 70 local clubs and societies. Here you'll also find Farstastenen, the only surviving runestone in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. It was put back up in 1875 and stands beside the footpath from the farm down to Farstabadet.
Farsta torg, ett par minuter härifrån, a: A couple of minutes from here is Farsta torg, laid out like an Italian piazza and opened on 23 October 1960. The long square measures 180 by 100 metres, and its gently curving shape may have been inspired by Piazza delle Erbe in Verona. Most days there's a market selling fruit and flowers. Next door is the former Farsta gymnasium, a secondary school that's now home to the Adolf Fredrik music classes.
Farstastenen minns en bror: The Farsta stone remembers a brother
Farstastenen pryds av en runorm lagd i e: The Farsta Stone is decorated with a rune serpent coiled in a figure of eight, with a braided ring cross in the upper loop. Tore and Sven raised it in memory of their brother Vinut, Helga’s son. In the 19th century the stone lay flat between the farm buildings, and it was raised again in 1875.
Farstastenen är från 1000-talet. Ornamen: The Farsta Stone dates from the 11th century. It’s decorated with a rune serpent coiled in a figure of eight, with a braided ring cross in the upper loop. In the 19th century the stone lay flat between the farm buildings, and it was raised again in 1875.
Farstaviken sträcker sig från Baggensfjä: Farstaviken bay reaches in from Baggensfjärden towards Gustavsberg, the main town of Värmdö municipality, about 20 kilometres east of Stockholm. Here nature itself has redrawn the map: as the land has slowly risen since the Ice Age, the islands of Farstalandet and Ormingelandet have joined together. Meanwhile, places like Mörtnäs, Hemmesta and Torsby have merged with Gustavsberg.
Fartygen blev för stora för slussen: Ships too big for the lock
Fartyget byggdes på Lövholmsvarvet i Sto: The ship was built at the Lövholmen shipyard in Stockholm. Because it would carry oil, it had to be completely tight, so the hull around the cargo hold was fastened with double rows of rivets.
Fartygsdieslar var på sin tid en svensk: Marine diesel engines were in their day a Swedish product sold worldwide, and they were test-run here. When production in Sickla ended in 1951, the last diesel engine was delivered to Slite.
Fasaden mot Perstorpsvägen är smyckad me: The façade facing Perstorpsvägen is decorated with playful brick motifs. Look out for a sailing boat, a witch, a Christmas goat, a girl skipping and the short poem 'a b c – 1953'.
Fasaderna är klädda i gult tegel. Hallen: The façades are clad in yellow brick. The hall's vaulted roof rests on arches of steel and concrete with a clear span of 48.5 metres, and bands of skylights let in the daylight.
Fasaderna är klädda med lackerade alumin: The facades are clad in lacquered aluminium panels in bright colours chosen by the artist Gert Marcus, so that each group of buildings would have its own identity. The buildings were partly cast as whole tunnels, with walls and floors in a single piece – a method that attracted international attention.
Fascinate målades sommaren 1989 av Circl: Fascinate was painted in summer 1989 by Circle and Tarik Saleh, who were seventeen at the time. The mural was 13 metres wide and 8 metres high, and was done with the property owner's permission – but with no payment for either the work or the paint.
Fascinate var 13 meter bred och 8 meter: Fascinate was 13 metres wide and 8 metres high. It was painted on the outside wall of an industrial building from 1970 – with the owner's permission, but without payment for either the work or the paint.
Fastighetsborgarrådet Walfrid Frank kall: City property commissioner Walfrid Frank called Hagsätra a calm and human-scale centre, where the architects had ‘abandoned the heaven-storming’. He meant that it had no tall building as a landmark, which was common at the time.
Fastighetsdirektören Axel Dahlberg bilda: In 1926 the city's property director Axel Dahlberg set up the Small Cottage Office, which organised self-build housing. The following year work started on 200 small cottages in Olovslund and here in Pungpinan. Today the area is considered a cultural environment of national interest.

Ferdinand Bobergs gasverk byggdes av röt: Ferdinand Boberg’s gasworks was built of red brick from the Haga brickworks outside Enköping. Typical touches are the round-arched windows and the patterned bands of brown and yellow brick beneath the eaves. The plan showed four gasholders in his style, but only two were built.
Feskekôrka, räkmacka vid vattnet: Feskekôrka fish market – and a prawn sandwich by the water

Festivalen som startade allt: The festival that started it all
Festpaviljongen vid stranden byggdes om: The party pavilion by the shore was rebuilt as a surprise for one of Gustav III's visits – though whether the King ever came here is unclear. Inside stands one of Sweden's tallest tiled stoves, 4.65 metres high.
Filmhuset: Filmhuset, home of the Swedish Film Institute
Filmstaden Kista har elva salonger i tre: Filmstaden Kista has eleven screens in three sizes, the largest seating 202 people. The cinema is a big part of Kista Galleria, and in summer 2012 the foyer got a complete makeover.
Filmstaden Kista invigdes den 27 novembe: Filmstaden Kista was opened on 27 November 2002 by the actors Josephine Bornebusch and Fares Fares. The cinema has eleven screens, the largest seating 202.
Filmstaden byggdes 1919–1920 på mark där: Filmstaden was built in 1919–1920 on land that had once been an ostrich farm – feathered hats were all the rage back then. The site was chosen for peace and quiet away from the noise of the city, and the studio became the largest in Europe by area.
Filmstaden i Råsunda: Filmstaden in Råsunda, the old film studios
Filmstjärnor på biodörrarna: Film stars on the cinema doors
Filmstudio på en strutsfarm: A film studio on an ostrich farm
Finansmannen Ernest Thiel lät Ferdinand: The financier Ernest Thiel commissioned Ferdinand Boberg to design him a villa in the Viennese Art Nouveau style, and since 1924 it has been an art museum, Thielska galleriet – the Thiel Gallery. On its walls you'll find Bruno Liljefors, Ernst Josephson, Carl Larsson, August Strindberg and Anders Zorn, alongside Edvard Munch, Paul Gauguin and Toulouse-Lautrec. Just next to it, on a south-facing slope at Blockhusudden, is Gravitational Ripples by Lea Porsager, the memorial to the victims of the 2004 tsunami.
Finnboda var från början ett torp, och n: Finnboda started life as a croft, and the name is thought to come from its role as a harbour for boats from Finland. In the early 1700s tar was produced here in a pitch works. The works manager's house is the only building left from that time.
Finnboda varv anlades 1874 som filial ti: The Finnboda shipyard was founded in 1874 as an offshoot of the Bergsund yard. Since then the old shipyard has become a mixed neighbourhood. Its old workshops – the joinery, the steam engine shop and the canteen – now house flats, offices and shops. The shipyard workers used to live on the surrounding hills, Finnbodaberget, Skatberget and Finnberget among them.
Fiskebäck är stadsdelen där Göteborg möt: Fiskebäck is where Gothenburg meets the sea, by the southern archipelago. The district covers 561 hectares and borders Hinsholmen and Långedrag to the north and Önnered to the south. Its name – 'fish brook' – gives away what once mattered most here, and life by the water still shapes the area today.
Fisksätra, inklämt mellan Lännerstasunde: Fisksätra, squeezed in between the Lännerstasundet strait and the Nacka forests, is Sweden's most densely populated urban area, with 7,724 people per square kilometre. Lännerstasundet is an arm of the Baltic on the border between the Boo and Nacka districts. Fisksätra is also home to the Toy and Collectors' Museum, a museum devoted entirely to toys and play.
Fittja bro blev klar 1669, byggd av Erik: Fittja Bridge was completed in 1669 by Erik Dahlbergh's fortification troops, the final link in a new southbound highway first planned in 1622. In 1677 Dahlbergh had the site fortified because of its strategic importance.
Fjällstugan är byggd i trä med spånbeklä: Fjällstugan is built of wood with shingle cladding, and has several projecting sections and roofs pitched at different angles. Inside there's an 18th-century tiled stove that may have come from Gustav III's opera house.
Fjärde kyrkan på platsen: The fourth church on the site
Fjärden mellan Södertörn och Ekerön: The bay between Södertörn and Ekerön
Flamingoparken ovanpå tunnelbanan: Flamingo Park on top of the metro
Flatenbadet är stadens största friluftsb: Flatenbadet is the city's biggest outdoor swimming spot, and Stockholm Vatten, the water company, reckons Lake Flaten is the cleanest lake in Stockholm. The buildings were designed by the architect Paul Hedqvist, and the bathing place opened on 23 June 1934. All around it is the Flaten nature reserve, the largest in Stockholm, which even has a racetrack for radio-controlled model cars.
Flemingsbergs industriområde anlades på: Flemingsberg's industrial area was laid out in the 1960s, and Billman-Regulator's factory from the early part of that decade is still standing; the street name Regulatorvägen remembers the electronics firm. Serious culture may be on its way, too: the municipality is planning space for the activities the Royal Swedish Opera and Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, currently have in Nacka. This is also home to the Labour Movement Archives and Library, the oldest of its kind in the world.
Flemingsbergs kyrkas altartavla är skulp: The altarpiece in Flemingsberg church was carved in pine by Per Nilsson-Öst. It shows Jesus on the shore of the Sea of Tiberias while the disciples struggle to haul in nets heavy with fish.
Flera av Säbys torp finns kvar i Järvafä: Several of Säby's crofts survive in the Järvafältet nature reserve. Tånglöt is mentioned as early as 1589, when the crofter was called Mårthen. Granskog, also mentioned in 1589, is now the clubhouse of the Järfälla orienteering club.
Flera av godsets gamla hus finns kvar. T: Several of the estate’s old buildings survive. The Bergholm croft is now a summer café, the old smithy belongs to a nursery garden, and the farmworkers’ row has been turned into terraced houses. The red granary is counted among Stockholm’s best-preserved 19th-century farm buildings.
Flera fotbollsspelare har vuxit upp här,: Several footballers grew up here, among them David Frölund, Mikael Dyrestam and Carlos Strandberg. The hip-hop artist Sarettii is from Hisings Backa too.
Flera gator i Veddesta är uppkallade eft: Several streets in Veddesta are named after office and invoicing terms: Kontorsvägen (Office Road), Saldovägen (Balance Road), Fakturavägen (Invoice Road) and Girovägen (Giro Road).
Flera gator i trakten har fått sina namn: Several streets in this area are named after a sawmill. Sörensens gata honours the sawmill owner Nils Georg Sörensen, whose company, Säfveåns AB, also lent its name to Hyvelsågsgatan, Klyvsågsgatan and Stabbetorget. On a hill by Stabbetorget stands Björkekärr Church. And a little further on is Queen Silvia Children's Hospital, the biggest children's hospital in Sweden.
Flera kända personer kommer från Hjällbo: Several well-known names grew up in Hjällbo, including the singer and actor Jennifer Brown, the singer Javiera Muñoz and the athlete Khaddi Sagnia, who competes in the triple jump and long jump.
Flera människor begravdes i den cirka fy: Several people were buried in the coffin, which was around four metres long. At least one was buried without being cremated first, and another's bones were placed in a clay pot. On top lay the burnt bones of a small child, and the grave goods included flint arrowheads and scrapers.
Flickan hade en riktig förebild: The girl had a real-life model
Flyghamnen hette först Göteborgs Flygham: The airport was first called Göteborgs Flyghamn and had a seaplane harbour too. The plans were ambitious: airships were meant to be able to dock here. When the airfield closed in 1977, it was one of the oldest in Europe with scheduled flights.
Flyghamnen skulle invigas den 4 augusti: The airport was due to open on 4 August 1923, but bad weather put it off by a day. On 5 August Crown Prince Gustav Adolf opened the airfield – the same year Gothenburg celebrated its 300th anniversary with the Jubilee Exhibition.
Flysta är i huvudsak en villastadsdel, m: Flysta is mostly villas, but it has a small mystery of its own. A Viking Age runestone, known as Uppland runic inscription 70, once stood here. People have searched for it several times without success, and it's probably lost for good. Neighbouring Sundby counts as part of Old Spånga, and its name goes all the way back to 1312.
Flytdockan for till Mexiko: The floating dock went to Mexico
Folk kallade platsen Masthuggstullen eft: People called this spot Masthuggstullen, after a customs house. Later it became Bierhalleplatsen, after an open-air beer garden serving German-style beer, which Johan Albrecht Pripp had started brewing.
Folket röstade fram ett kafé: The people voted for a café
Folkets hus blev House of Possibilitas: From Folkets hus to House of Possibilitas
Folketshusföreningen bildades 1899, och: The Folkets hus association, which runs the local community hall, was formed in 1899, and the building was opened by the Social Democrat leader Hjalmar Branting. In 1930 the association moved to a bigger building facing Sturegatan with a cinema and theatre, but that was sold in 1999 and the association returned to the old building in the courtyard.
