The Rex cinema opened here on 13 September 1940 and showed films until 1958. But that wasn't the end of the big screen: in 1992 Folkets Hus Backa bio opened in the same premises.
I närheten ligger Näsbydal, ett bostadso: Nearby is Näsbydal, an egg-shaped housing estate with 900 flats, ranging from studios with a sleeping alcove to seven-room flats on two floors. The residents' association has its own tennis court, basketball court, boules court and barbecue area. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, a faint and partly worn-away runic inscription on a slab of rock, discovered by the author Jan Fridegård in 1943.
I närheten låg Fjällbohemmet, ett vårdhe: Nearby was Fjällbohemmet, a care home in Utby from 1939 to 1983. It then became sheltered housing for older people, until it was closed down around 1990. But Utby's history goes back much further: the old Utby parish was absorbed into Partille parish as early as 1571, after its church was destroyed in 1566.
I och runt ravinen står många naturvärde: In and around the ravine stand many veteran trees at least 200 years old. On eastern Henriksdalsberget 35 red-listed species have been found, including the black jewel beetle and the relict longhorn beetle. A footpath with a metal staircase leads through the ravine down to Svindersviken bay.
I oktober 1904 fick Karlsrofältet en rik: In October 1904 the Karlsro field got a proper football pitch, giving the newly founded IFK Göteborg a ground of its own. That autumn the team won four friendlies with a combined score of 8–2. In 1982 the club put up a memorial stone on the spot.
I oktober 1989 hade Stand Up Comedy Klub: In October 1989 the Stand Up Comedy Klubben opened at Norra Brunn – a milestone for Swedish stand-up comedy. The TV show Släng dig i brunnen was recorded here every year from 1990 to 1997.
I oktober 2005 stängde Guldhyttan, den s: In October 2005 Guldhyttan closed – the last shop that had been there since the centre opened in 1965. The metro station and bus terminal were opened by King Carl XVI Gustaf on 21 August 1975.
I området Kristinedal en bit härifrån ka: In Kristinedal, a short way from here, you can see the 1960s dream of a home of your own. Around a hundred detached, terraced and linked houses were finished in 1964, single-storey and split-level homes in facing brick. It was in small-house areas like this one that the carport made its debut. Neighbouring Sjövalla is older – villas began going up there as early as the 1920s and 1930s.
I området Kummelby låg förr en gård, och: There was once a farm in Kummelby, and on its site the first Kummelby Church was built in 1956–57. It was so small that it could only hold 50 people, which is why it was sometimes called Kummelby's little church. A new church was consecrated just before Christmas 2000. Beside it stands Kummelbystenen, the Kummelby Stone, a runestone from the late 11th century.
I området finns Mariakyrkan i Hammarkull: Round here you'll find Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church, in Hammarkullen. It used to be called Tomaskyrkan, and – unusually – it's shared by two churches: the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan, and Angered parish. In the other direction is Hjällbo centrum, built in 1969, with a fruit and vegetable market hall, a library and a church grouped around the square.

In this area is St Mary's Church in Hammarkullen, formerly St Thomas's, which – unusually – is shared by the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan, and Angered parish. The mould-damaged church building has been abandoned and is to be replaced by a new one, so services and activities have moved into temporary huts next door. In the other direction is Hjällbo centrum, built in 1969, with a fruit and vegetable market hall, a library and a church around the square.
I området ligger Atlantisområdet, en rad: This area includes the Atlantis estate, a little village of terraced houses designed in the early 1950s by the architects Bertil Karlén, Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist. The houses drew attention from abroad, and today they carry the City Museum's highest heritage rating. From 1968 to 1983, one of them was home to Lisbeth and Olof Palme – the future prime minister – and their three sons.
I området ligger Glose, där betade stran: The area includes Glose, where grazed shore meadows meet the shallow waters of Ryskärsfjorden. Birds and plants both thrive here, and the fjord and Glose's meadows are part of the Nordre älv estuary, a vast nature reserve. The six-kilometre Glose å stream also flows out into the fjord.
I området ligger Gunnestorps mosse, en b: The area includes Gunnestorps mosse, a mix of lake, fen and bog in Hisingsparken, Hisingen's big park. Reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow here alongside cranberries, sundews and cotton grass. North of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, now part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground.
I området ligger Helgered, med drygt 240: The area includes Helgered, with just over 240 households on either side of Björlandavägen. In its north-eastern corner is Klare mosse, a lovely place for a walk, where the Osbäcken stream has its source. Helgered also borders the Hisingsparken and Svarte mosse nature areas, so forest and bog are never far away from here.
I området ligger Hisingsparken, Göteborg: This is the area of Hisingsparken, Gothenburg's largest park at around 320 hectares, though it only became an official park in 1980. Its oldest part is S.A. Hedlunds park, laid out in the late 1800s. Runners can choose from four trails, from the 2.8-kilometre blue route to the green one, a full 11.1 kilometres. In the northern part of the park is Kättilsröd 4H farm.
I området ligger Mölnlycke, centralorten: This area includes Mölnlycke, the main town of Härryda municipality, about ten kilometres south-east of central Gothenburg. The Mölndalsån river runs through the centre on its way from Lake Landvettersjön to Lake Rådasjön. Since 2023 the village of Öjersjö in neighbouring Partille has also counted as part of the same urban area, so Mölnlycke has now spilled over the municipal border.
I området ligger Vidkärr, som under mång: The area takes in Vidkärr, for many years the end of the line for tram number 1, until it was extended to Östra sjukhuset hospital in 1982. The first two houses in Vidkärr's garden suburb were finished on 24 January 1922. Right next door is Sävenäs station, where commuter trains stood idle from December 2024 to August 2026 while work went on along the Western Main Line.
I området ligger den lilla sjön Skåtte m: The area includes Skåtte mosse, a small lake about 55 metres above sea level, whose water drains away through the Glose å stream. Not far away is Kärna bokskog, a beech forest that has been a nature reserve since 2008, where the rare wood fescue grass and several red-listed lichens thrive. Parts of the forest have been made accessible.
I området runt omkring, ett par kilomete: Around here, a couple of kilometres south of central Mölndal, is the residential area of Rävekärr. It's known for its grey, square terraced houses, aptly nicknamed ‘lådhus’ – box houses. South-east of the houses, two lakes glitter: Horsikan and Rävekärrs Långevatten.
I området, vid Agnesbergs industriområde: It was here, by the Agnesberg industrial estate, that the riverbank gave way on 14 April 1993. The Agnesberg landslide covered an area of roughly 80 by 30 metres along the Göta älv river. A few hours after the first slide, an eight-metre-wide section broke away further back, and several smaller slides followed during the day. It was one of many landslides in western Sweden after the war.
I parken finns roller derby-banan Rullev: The park has the Rullevi roller derby track, urban gardening plots and the outdoor classroom "Näsan i blöt", created by Santiago Cirugeda of the Spanish architects Recetas Urbanas. Look out too for a large mural by the Dutch artists Haas & Hahn.
I parken ligger Brygghuset, där gårdens: In the park stands Brygghuset, where the estate’s washing was once boiled before being rinsed down by the shore. The singer Magnus Rudbeck turned it into a home in 1946, and today it’s a summer café – perfect for a fika, the Swedish coffee break.
I parken vid Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, e: In the grounds of Jakobsberg Folk High School, a short way from here, stand two runestones that originally stood on the land of Vibble farm, the old name for Jakobsberg. They've been here for about a hundred years. One of them tells us that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised. Nearby also stood Jakobsberg Mill, a windmill from the 1840s that burned down no fewer than three times: in 1980, 1997 and 2005.

In the park by Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the folk high school just up the road, are two runestones that originally stood on the land of Vibble gård – the old name for Jakobsberg. They've been in their present spot since 1926. One of them tells us that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised. Nearby also stood Jakobsberg mill, a windmill from the 1840s that burned down no fewer than three times: in 1980, 1997 and 2005.
I parkens förtrollade skog finns ett häx: The park’s enchanted forest has a witch’s house that doubles as a slide, a roundabout shaped like a fly agaric toadstool and a spider to climb on. The ground under the swings looks like a rug, so swinging feels like riding a flying carpet.
I parkens södra ände står kopior av Per: At the southern end of the park stand copies of Per Hasselberg's statues Tjusningen (Enchantment) and Snöklockan (The Snowdrop). The Snowdrop was the first sculpture in Stockholm put up purely as decoration – earlier monuments generally honoured people or events.
I postala sammanhang heter stadsdelen Hi: The district's postal name is Hisings Kärra, and it covers 1,438 hectares. A little further away is Larsered, whose name is a bit of a mystery. It clearly refers to someone called Lars, but nobody knows who he was. The ending '-red' means cleared woodland, so perhaps it was Lars who once cleared the land.
I reservatets sydvästra del finns en kul: In the south-west of the reserve is a historic relic: a defensive position made of stone walls, along with the remains of other stone walls.
I rondellen vid infarten till Lidingö st: In the roundabout at the entrance to Lidingö stands Till en annan värld, To Another World. Carl Milles only ever made it as a bronze sketch just 66 centimetres high, and it wasn't cast at full size until 2008, long after his death. The municipality commissioned it as a symbol of Lidingö's focus on health and wellbeing, and the 240-centimetre version was created by computer-scanning the original. A little further on is Lidingö town hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson.
I ruinens nordvästra hörn sitter en sten: In the north-west corner of the ruin is a stone carved with two heads, probably St Halvard and the woman he tried to save. Legend has it that the world will end when the stone reaches the ground. The walls are slowly sinking, so without protective measures it really will get there.
I rusningstrafik går omkring 120 spårvag: At rush hour, around 120 trams and 130 buses an hour leave from Brunnsparken’s ten stops. That probably makes it Sweden’s second-busiest interchange by number of departures, after T-Centralen in Stockholm.
I samma hus som Världslitteraturhuset fi: Sharing the building with Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature, is Berättarministeriet – the Ministry of Stories – which works to spark children's love of storytelling. The auditorium on the fourth floor seats 60.
I sjöns nordvästra hörn, i Gröndal, ligg: In the north-west corner of the lake, in Gröndal, is Trekantenbadet, which opened in 1972. It has a little sandy beach, a big grassy slope for sunbathing, a floating jetty and an outdoor shower.
I skogarna en bit härifrån ligger Natura: Out in the forests not far from here is the Natura 2000 site Maderna-Haketjärn, with small lakes such as Haketjärnen and Långevatten. Haketjärnen is shared between the municipalities of Härryda and Partille and is just over seven metres deep. Lilla Långevatten covers only 0.03 square kilometres, yet it's almost ten metres deep. Partille is also home to Partille SC, the oldest field hockey club in Sweden that's still going.
I skogen en bit härifrån ligger Södra Lu: In the woods not far from here is Södra Lundtjärnen, a small lake with a quirky detail: the coordinates given for it actually point to a nameless lake just south of the real one. In the other direction is the village of Pinntorp, near Tahult, where the road-racing motorcyclist Kent Andersson has lived.
I skogen en kort promenad härifrån låg s: In the woods a short walk from here stood Kappsta, a summer villa also known as Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. The house burned down in 1931, but its foundations are still there in Kappsta nature reserve, along with a memorial by Gustav and Ulla Kraitz called Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W. Nearby are Villa Ekbacken, built in 1912–1913 for Gustaf Dalén, and Skärsätra water tower from 1912.

In the woods a short walk from here stood the summer villa Kappsta, also known as the Wising villa, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. It burned down in the early 1930s, but its foundations survive in the Kappsta nature reserve, along with the memorial 'Attaché Case R.W.' by Gustav and Ulla Kraitz. The reserve also holds the foundations of Villa Nidaros, Trondheim's pavilion from the 1897 Stockholm Exhibition.
I skogen mellan Fisksätra och Igelboda,: In the woods between Fisksätra and Igelboda, just south of the Saltsjöbanan railway, you can still find the stone foundations of Vinterbrinken, a lineman's cottage where a railway worker lived with his family. The last to live here were the Nordgrens: first Ludvig, his wife Kristina and their five children, and then their son Ragnar, a station hand, with his own family until the end of the 1920s. The name lives on in Vinterbrinksvägen.
I skogens södra del byggdes 2018–2019 tr: In 2018–2019 three nature playgrounds were built in the southern part of the forest. One of them has a gigantic flying ant and concrete ant eggs to climb on – a nod to the second half of the name Svedmyra, myra being Swedish for ant.
I slottet finns en praktfull sandstenssp: The castle has a magnificent sandstone fireplace said to have been brought here as war booty from Prague in the mid-1600s. The same room has a ceiling painted in grisaille.
I slottsparken ligger Brygghuset, där gå: In the palace grounds stands Brygghuset, where the estate's laundry was once boiled before being rinsed down at the shore. The singer Magnus Rudbeck converted it into a home in 1946, and today it's a summer café.
I slutet av 1700-talet besöktes dårhuset: In the late 18th century the asylum was visited by Francisco de Miranda, who fought for the independence of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador. In his diary he wrote that the building was comfortably and thoughtfully designed.
I slutet av 1800-talet blev Curmanska vi: In the late 1800s the Curman villa became a hub of Stockholm's cultural social life. The Curman family owned the house until the 1950s. Today it's the Thai embassy, while the neighbouring villa at number 1 houses Malaysia's.
I slutet av 1800-talet bodde Johan Augus: In the late 19th century Johan August Löf, known as Lötgubben, lived alone by the lake in a home-made earth hut with windows facing the water. The walls were papered with the newspaper Stockholms-Tidningen. He called it Löfhyddan and lived there for almost 30 years.
I slutet av 1800-talet stod vid torget e: In the late 1800s a wooden house on the square was known as Lilla Helvetet, "Little Hell" – a corruption of the property's old name, Hellewe. Opposite, where Bangatan begins, stood a small house popularly called Himmelriket, "Heaven". Both were pulled down when the square was enlarged in the 1880s.
I slutet av 1960-talet bodde cirka 5 000: By the late 1960s around 5,000 people lived in Grindtorp. The streets have heavenly names: alongside Grindtorpsvägen there are Kometvägen and Meteorvägen – Comet Road and Meteor Road.
I slutet av 2019 började arbetet med att: At the end of 2019 work began on laying track for the Kista branch of the Tvärbanan light rail, which will have a stop on Rissne torg.
I socknen finns omkring 170 fornlämninga: The parish has around 170 ancient sites, roughly 100 of them Stone Age settlements. At Tumlehed there are rock paintings of four ships, a deer and four fish, probably also from the Stone Age.
I stadsarkitekten Albert Lilienbergs pla: In city architect Albert Lilienberg's 1916 plan, the Majvivan block was to be built around a large enclosed courtyard. But it wasn't built until the mid-1930s, when Functionalism had taken hold, so instead it got an open courtyard between two long rows of buildings.
I taket på Midsommarkransens station hän: Hanging from the ceiling of Midsommarkransen station is a wooden midsummer wreath, made in 1979 by local residents under the guidance of three students from Konstfack, the University of Arts, Crafts and Design. The station also has Lisbet Lindholm's Blommor till Midsommarkransen (Flowers for Midsommarkransen) from 1990 and a painted wooden relief by Dag Wallin.
I torgets södra hörn låg biografen Focus: The Focus cinema stood in the southern corner of the square from 1960. In 1992 the building became Hagsätra Chapel, now Hagsätra Church, and films were shown in a smaller auditorium until 2005. Until the 1990s there was a petrol station with a garage under the square.

The Focus cinema, designed by Kampmann and opened in 1960, stood in the square's southern corner. The building was converted into Hagsätra Chapel, consecrated in 1992, and the cinema carried on in a much-reduced auditorium until 2005.
I trakten finns gott om natur. En bit hä: There's plenty of nature round here. Not far away is the Älta mosse – Strålsjön reserve, created in 1995 and owned and run by Nacka municipality. In the other direction is Stensö, named after the peninsula that used to be an island in Lake Ältasjön, with a swimming spot at its tip.
I trakten finns gott om runor. Vid Sundb: This area is rich in runes. At Sundby is U 80, a large, elaborately carved rock slab, with an unfinished one, U 81, right beside it. Flysta had a Viking Age runestone too, but despite several searches it has never been found and is probably lost. And in the Bromsten industrial area was Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large-scale graffiti painting – until the wall was torn down in early December 2021.
I trakten flyter Lärjeån, som börjar nor: The Lärjeån river runs through the area, rising north of Gråbo and flowing into the Göta älv at Lärjeholm. On the eastern bank of the Göta älv, by the E45 road and the Bergslagsbanan railway, is Agnesberg, an old coaching inn that belonged to Angered municipality until 1967. The railway station arrived in 1880, and industry soon followed.
I trakten ligger Långsjö gård, som på 16: In this area is Långsjö gård. In the 17th century it was a croft belonging to Långbro farm, and it later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö. Nearby runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows the old Göta landsväg – the highway travellers once took heading south from Stockholm.
I trädgården vid Stocksundstorps gård fi: In the garden at Stocksundstorp farm is Agape, a multi-faith meditation space with art from Buddhist, Jewish, Hindu and Islamic traditions. There has also been a permanent sculpture park here since 2009.
I trähuset i backen har Djurgårdsskolan: Djurgårdsskolan has been in the wooden house on the slope since 1878, making it one of Stockholm's oldest schools. Not far off stand Karl Johans-ekarna, the Karl Johan oaks, where tradition has it the king rested in the 1820s. Slätten, the meadow here, used to attract a colourful crowd, and according to the national librarian Rydqvist, Gustav III himself came here incognito. The poet Bellman is said to have sat beneath an oak, improvising songs on his mandolin.
I ungdomshotellet fanns 70 rum för kvinn: The youth hotel had 70 rooms for women and 67 for men. To limit contact between the sections, the lift only stopped at every third floor. Tenants had to be aged 15–21 and could stay on until they turned 24.
I vattentornsbyggnaden fanns två cistern: At the top of the water tower building were two tanks holding 35 cubic metres each, and the water was pumped up from Bällstaviken. The building also housed offices, switchgear and overnight rooms, and the wood-panelled section is still used for overnight stays.
I vattenvaktarstugan bodde förr en vakt: The water keeper's cottage was once home to a watchman whose job was to keep Stockholm's main water pipeline running smoothly between Norsborg waterworks and Nybohov reservoir. The first pipeline was laid in 1902–1904, and it's still one of the city's most important drinking-water mains. Not far away, in Gömmaren nature reserve, there are also the remains of a farm from the middle Iron Age.
I vändslingan framför Hotel Eggers har S: The tram loop in front of Hotel Eggers is the regular stop for the Ringlinien tramway society. In summer and around Christmas you can ride a vintage tram from here to the Liseberg amusement park on the Liseberg line.
I västra Birka ligger Birkahöjden, ett b: In western Birka rises Birkahöjden, a rocky hill of just over two hectares. Two-thirds of it is covered in pine growing on bare rock, and the rest is open slabs. Several pines and oaks here are considered especially worth protecting.
I växthusen växer påsköträdet, Sophora t: The glasshouses are home to the toromiro, Sophora toromiro, from Easter Island. Extinct in the wild, it has survived in cultivation – thanks in part to the Gothenburg Botanical Garden.
I Årsta har gatorna fått namn efter sven: In Årsta the streets are named after Swedish lakes, like Skagern and Hjälmaren, so a stroll here is almost a geography lesson. Vättersparken used to have a supervised playground, Vättersdälden, which closed in 1992 – but the paddling pool, swings and sandpits are still there. A little further on stands Skagershuset, a block of flats with a wooden façade that was named Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2014.
I århundraden gick färjor från Färjenäs: For centuries ferries crossed from Färjenäs to Klippan. Then, at 9 am on 1 April 1967, the last one – the John E. Olson – cast off. The Älvsborg Bridge had opened. The ferry was later converted into a container crane.
I östra Högdalen står traditionella folk: In eastern Högdalen stand traditional folkhem buildings from the era of the Swedish welfare state: narrow three-storey blocks around planted courtyards. To the west things get bigger, with tower blocks. Here you can see how 1950s suburban planning moved from small-scale to modern.
I östra delen omges Högalidsgatan av fem: At its eastern end, Högalidsgatan is flanked on both sides by natural stone walls five to seven metres high. They create a streetscape typical of this part of Stockholm, and the street's diagonal line breaks up the grid.
I övergången mellan stadsdelarna vid San: Where the districts meet at Sannaplan, rows of free-standing landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical stone-and-wood tenements – were built without courtyards. They were the last of their kind before functionalism took over.
IKEA var först på plats i Kållered köpst: IKEA was the first to arrive at Kållered’s shopping area in 1972, drawing customers from all over western Götaland and Halland. More shops soon sprang up around the store, and in 2023 IKEA opened a brand-new one.
Idrottshallen som aldrig byggdes: The sports hall that never was
Idrottsmuseet har en Hall of Fame med 14: The Sports Museum has a Hall of Fame honouring 148 Gothenburg sporting figures. Besides the objects, it holds around 30,000 photographs and a library with more than 70 metres of shelves of sports literature.
Idrottsplatsen vid Kyrkvikens inre del h: The sports ground at the head of Kyrkviken bay has everything from athletics to ice hockey. But walk a little further and you'll come to Lidingö's oldest farm, Bo gård, whose history goes all the way back to the late Iron Age. Right next to it are the Trisshusen from 1909 – an early type of terraced housing designed by Jacob Gate.
Idén att lyfta bort våningarna kom från: The idea of lifting off the upper floors came from Helmut Junkers, head of development at the housing company Göteborgshem. The removed building elements were reused in the houses on the Båtsmansgatorna streets in Backatorp, and new buildings on Vegagatan in Linnéstaden were given façade panels from here.
Idén föddes 1983 när kommunen ville skap: The idea came about in 1983, when the city wanted to create jobs and optimism in the region and Skanska wanted to strengthen its position as a builder. Built in 1986–1989, the building served as Skanska's Gothenburg headquarters. Today it is owned by Vasakronan.
Igelbäcken rinner förbi alldeles i närhe: The Igelbäcken stream winds past close by on its 10.5-kilometre journey from Lake Säbysjön to Edsviken bay, and its valley is one of Stockholm's ‘green wedges’ of open countryside reaching into the city. A short way off is Akalla village, a name known since the Middle Ages. The oldest house, Storgården, dates from the 17th century, and today the village has a 4H farm, a café and bike hire – in one of the best-preserved village settings in the Stockholm area.
Igelbäcken är känd för den lilla fisken: Igelbäcken stream is known for the stone loach, a little fish that's rare in these parts. Its discovery in 1985 sparked the idea of a nature reserve. Stockholm Vatten has promised to pump drinking water into the stream during prolonged droughts.
Ikeas andra svenska varuhus, efter det i: IKEA's second store in Sweden, after the original in Älmhult, opened here on 18 June 1965. Its round original section was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York, and after later rebuilding and extensions it became the second-largest IKEA in the world by floor space. One of its very first neighbours was the Esso Motorhotell from 1968 – today the Scandic Kungens Kurva hotel.
Ikeas fastighet fick namnet Kurvan och E: IKEA's property was named Kurvan (the Curve) and the Esso hotel Radien (the Radius). The neighbouring blocks carried on the geometric theme with names such as Diagonalen, Kvadraten (the Square), Sekanten and Pyramiden, and the streets include Modulvägen and Tangentvägen.

IKEA's property was named Kurvan (the Curve) and the Esso hotel Radien (the Radius). Then came blocks such as Diagonalen, Kvadraten (the Square), Pyramiden and Sekanten (the Secant), and streets like Modulvägen and Tangentvägen.
Imam Ali-moskén har ett bibliotek med öv: The Imam Ali Mosque has a lending library of more than 3,000 books in several languages. At an open house for local residents in 2017, visitors were treated to calligraphy, an art exhibition, a guided tour and a meze buffet, among other things.
In på 1950-talet sa man Frölanns socken: Into the 1950s people still said Frölanns socken, and the locals were called frölänningar; well into the 1800s they were nicknamed koljenackar, 'haddock necks'. From the 1200s until 1658, Frölunda and Askim were the only part of mainland Sweden that reached the North Sea.
Industrimannen Carl Frans Lundström köpt: The industrialist Carl Frans Lundström bought the plot for his daughter, Calla Curman. Afraid a big apartment block would block the view, he bought the plot opposite too and allowed only a smaller, villa-style house there. That became Villa Sandrew.
Industriområdet delades först upp i fyra: The industrial estate was first divided into four blocks with fitting names: Fabriken (the Factory), Förrådet (the Store), Verkstaden (the Workshop) and Hantverket (the Craft). Later additions include Brandstegen (the Fire Escape), Lagret (the Warehouse), Axeln (the Axle) and Tonfisken (the Tuna).
Inflyttningen började den 7 november 195: The first residents moved in on 7 November 1953, on Månadsgatan and Kalendervägen. While building was under way, delegations came from all over the world, fascinated that ordinary people were getting homes with bathrooms, fully fitted kitchens and parquet floors.
Inför 1980 debatterades om Björn Borg ku: Ahead of the 1980 tournament, people debated whether Björn Borg could win on the hall's fast surface. A temporary carpet was laid, and in a classic final against McEnroe, Borg became the tournament's first Swedish champion.
Inför invigningen byggdes en tredje läkt: For the unveiling a third grandstand was built, with tickets costing a couple of days' wages, so ordinary people could barely see a thing. Young men started smashing up the stand, and in the end the Life Guards charged the crowd on horseback. Several people were hurt, but the ceremony went ahead anyway.
Inför riksdagsvalet 1962 släpptes den så: Ahead of the 1962 general election came what was dubbed the Järva bombshell: homes for 160,000 people were promised on the Järva field within eight years. Tensta centrum opened just in time for the Christmas shopping in 1969.
Inför sammanslagningen med Stockholm 194: Ahead of the merger with Stockholm in 1949, street names that resembled names elsewhere in the city were weeded out. Strandvägen became Hässelby strandväg, and every street named after birds or Norse mythology vanished.
Ingemar Frodbom var källarmästare på Kas: Ingemar Frodbom was cellar master at Kastenhof, the tavern under Norrmalm's town hall. By the end of the 17th century he also owned a house on Drottninggatan, where he ran the Tre Tunnor (Three Barrels) tavern.
Ingemarsgatan har troligen fått sitt nam: Ingemarsgatan is probably named after Ingemar Frodbom, a wine merchant who ran an inn at the Ingemarshof country house in the 1700s. When he died, he left a plot of land to his loyal head waiter, Clas Browall, who in 1731 opened his own inn, Browallshof – today the Clas på Hörnet hotel and restaurant. Incidentally, the surrounding area was nicknamed Siberia, because moving this far out of town felt like being sent into exile.
Ingen bild av livet i Olskroken: No portrait of life in Olskroken
Ingen säger Köpstadsö. I dagligt tal het: Nobody actually says Köpstadsö. Everyone calls the island Kössö, and it's famous for its wheelbarrows. Just over a square kilometre in size, with 129 year-round residents in 2020, it's part of Gothenburg's southern archipelago. Look out for the wheelbarrows when you step ashore – they're the island's trademark.
Ingen vet exakt när Landsnora kvarn bygg: No one knows exactly when Landsnora mill was built, but its load-bearing beams date from 1632. The mill and sawmill are considered Sollentuna’s oldest secular buildings – the oldest, that is, apart from churches.
Ingen vet hur gammal Stuvsta gårds kvarn: Nobody knows how old Stuvsta farm's mill was or what it looked like, though it was surely a post mill. It was built without permission, so there are no drawings. Two millstones are set into the footpath by Kvarnbergsgården.
Ingen vet hur gammal kvarnen var eller h: Nobody knows how old the windmill was or what it looked like, but it was certainly a post mill. It was built without permission, so there are no drawings. The mill is said to have fallen into ruin during the 19th century.
Nobody knows how old the mill was or what it looked like, though it was certainly a post mill. Because it was built without permission, no drawings exist.
Ingen vet var Knuts bro låg. Troligen gi: No one knows where Knut's bridge stood. It probably crossed the low-lying, once marshy land between Jakobsberg and Viksjö, where the Bällstaån stream has its source.
Ingmar Bergman gick på Palmgrenska samsk: Ingmar Bergman went to Palmgrenska samskolan and wrote about its teachers in his memoir ‘The Magic Lantern’. The film ‘Hets’ (‘Torment’) is autobiographical and is about the school. Its teachers included Oskar Lindberg and Eric Ericson, and among its pupils was the journalist Ester Blenda Nordström.
Inloppet till Göteborg har länge bevakat: For centuries, this area has guarded the approach to Gothenburg. On Lilla Billingen, a headland a short way off, you can still see an angular fortification from 1741–1742, and in 1789 a square redoubt was added, with batteries facing the river. Gothenburg's saluting station was here too. The neighbouring hill, Stora Billingen, has military chambers blasted into the rock.
Innan Frösunda började bebyggas på 1990-: Before Frösunda started to be built up in the 1990s, the area was given over to the military, home to the Signal Regiment and the Svea Engineer Regiment. In its final years it was known as the Frösunda detachment and housed, among others, the units that served as the royal guard. A little further off is Annelunds gård, where Per Henrik Ling, the father of Swedish gymnastics, lived from 1822 to 1839.
Innan Landvetter flygplats byggdes 1977: Before Landvetter Airport was built in 1977, Gothenburg’s main airport was at Torslanda.
Innan Långsjöbadet invigdes 1938 var pla: Before the Långsjöbadet bathing place opened in 1938, the site was marshland with sewage ditches and big alders, and the shore was an impenetrable mass of reeds. Today there's a sandy beach about 50 metres long and a few bathing jetties.
Innan Sankt Eriksmässan hade en egen hal: Before the Sankt Erik trade fair had a hall of its own, the tennis hall was rented for exhibitions. At the fair in September 1944, the Volvo PV 444 was shown here for the very first time.
Innan Torslanda flög man från Kvibergs h: Before Torslanda airport, planes took off from Kvibergs hed, an open heath. It was there, on 23 March 1911, that the Belgian René Cozic made a five-minute test flight in a biplane he had built himself. It needed just 30 metres to take off and land.
Innan den första riktiga kyrkan invigdes: Before the first proper church was consecrated in 1633, a temporary one stood here: Brädekyrkan, the Plank Church, one of the city's very first buildings. Gustav II Adolf paid for the building work with a barrel of grain from every church farm in Västergötland, for several years running.
Innan det renade vattnet når Saltsjön pa: Before the treated water reaches the Saltsjön, it passes through the Norrenergi heat-pump plant at Bällstaviken. There the residual heat is captured and turned into district heating and cooling for Solna and Sundbyberg.
Innan gatan fick namnet Scheelegatan 188: Before it was named Scheelegatan in 1885, the street was called Trädgårdsgatan (Garden Street) because of the many gardens here. As a cross street it was also known as tvärgränden, "the cross alley", or simply gränden. It wasn't extended north to Barnhusbron bridge until the 1970s.
Innan husen kom fanns här en parkering,: Before the houses arrived, there was a car park, a clubhouse and a small patch of green next to Skarpnäck's football pitch. The city wanted to grow inwards, placing new homes within existing neighbourhoods. The plot was just under 3,000 square metres.
Innan kyrkan byggdes 1972 höll man gudst: Before the church was built in 1972, services were held in a grey wooden hut known as Edsbergsgården. The 2004 altarpiece is a painted steel cross surrounded by coloured glass, designed by the architect Lars Olof Torstensson and his son Jonas.
Innan kyrkan byggdes användes en proviso: Before the church was built, the congregation used a temporary church from 1965 – the first 'travelling church' in Sweden, designed to be moved. Once Brunnsbo Church was finished in 1972, it was taken down and rebuilt elsewhere as Furåsen Church.
Innan kyrkan byggdes hölls gudstjänstern: Before the church was built, services had been held since around 1960 in a grey wooden hut called Edsbergsgården. The organ was built in 1972 in Hillerød, Denmark, and is the first the church has ever had.
Innan sjösänkningen låg Hammarby sjö och: Before the water level was lowered, Hammarby sjö and Sicklasjön were at the same height. Until 1913 the steam launch Nackanäs ran from Södermalm to the popular Nackanäs inn. When the inn lost its licence to sell spirits, the service stopped.
Innan tunnelbanan kom stannade spårvagns: Before the metro came, tram line 19 stopped here, at Enskedefältet. On 9 September 1951 the tram stop gave way to the metro station, and today the trains cross Sockenvägen on a viaduct. Next door is Enskedefältets skola, a school designed by Paul Hedqvist and built in 1933. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, where in 2016 the district council decided to build a viewpoint.
Innan tunnelbanan tog över trafikerades: Before the metro took over, the line was served from 1956 by trams, routes 14 and 17. An aerial photo from the early 1960s shows the station under construction and the trams' turning loop.
Innanför lekplatsen vid korsningen Jätte: Just beyond the playground at the corner of Jättestensgatan and Baltzersgatan are älvkvarnar, ancient cup marks carved into the rock – prehistoric remains right in the middle of the housing estate.
Inne i Fredhällsberget, alldeles intill,: Right beside us, the Essingeleden motorway roars through the Fredhäll tunnel deep inside Fredhällsberget hill, then carries straight on over the 270-metre Fredhäll bridge across the Mariebergssundet strait. Up above ground it's much calmer. Leafy Rudbecksparken is full of oak trees, and Fredhäll primary school, designed by Paul Hedqvist and opened in 1938, has been given a green listing for its heritage value by the City Museum.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån döljer sig: Hidden away inside the rock not far from here is Aeroseum, an aviation experience centre in an underground cavern. It was once the rock hangar of the Göta Wing, one of only five ever built for the Swedish Air Force. Since 2000, visitors have been able to head down into the bunker and get up close to aviation history.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån gömmer sig: Hidden inside the rock nearby is Vargen, the Wolf, a secret nuclear-proof command centre from the 1970s with room for 200 people. It was built to shelter the leaders of Stockholm and Huddinge in the event of war, but it was eventually decommissioned and turned into a data centre. North of Stockholm it has an almost identical twin called Elefanten, the Elephant. Nearby Lake Lissmasjön has shrunk to a third of its original size after several attempts to drain it.
Inne i kyrkan dominerar det blåmålade ta: Inside the church, the eye is drawn to the blue-painted ceiling and the blue glass mosaic on the chancel wall by Elsa Hansson-Winnberg. The altar and font are made of white concrete and marble.
Inne möts puts, stål och glas av stavlim: Inside, render and steel meet walls of glued laminated pine and a floor of grey limestone. The benches have steel frames and pine bodies, upholstered in chrome-tanned leather.
Inom Härryda kommun ligger Göteborg-Land: Härryda municipality is home to Göteborg Landvetter Airport, Sweden's second-largest international airport – and the municipality's biggest workplace.
Inredningen från stora salen och ett för: The interiors of the great hall and a drawing room were donated to the Röhsska Museum of design and applied art, where they stayed from 1916. In 1994 the rooms were moved back to the manor. For a time the house was also a boarding school for girls, run by the Misses Zander until 1871.
Insekterna har det lyxigt i Kikås. Vid K: In Kikås, the insects live in luxury. By the lake Kikås Långvatten is Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel, built to boost biodiversity, especially for wild bees, butterflies and birds. Kikås is the name of the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and Fågelberg church is not far from here.
Inskriften lyder i översättning: \"Spjal: Translated, the inscription reads: 'Spjallbode and Une had the stone raised in memory of Tidkume, Ingetora's (husband).' Together with U 89, it's known as the Häradsvägen runestones.
Inskriften lyder ungefär: Åfrid lät hugg: The inscription reads roughly: “Åfrid had the slab carved in memory of Svarthövde and Igulfast, her sons, and of Åsgöt.” A rune animal in the carving suggests it was made in the late 11th century.
Inskriften på Kistastenen lyder i översä: Translated, the inscription on the Kista Stone reads: 'Sigvid had this stone raised in memory of his father Egvid and his mother Holmfrid, and Jovurfrid.' The woman's name Jovurfrid is very rare and known almost only from here.
Inspektorsbostaden byggdes troligen 1785: The inspector's residence was probably built in 1785–1787 for the palace gardener Johan Daniel Happée, who worked at Drottningholm for no less than 45 years, from 1770 to 1815.
Inte en enda av gravarna på Edsängen har: Not one of the graves at Edsängen has been excavated by archaeologists. The burial ground probably came into use as early as the Early Iron Age.
Inte långt härifrån ligger Anstalten Sag: Not far from here is Anstalten Sagsjön, a women's prison in Lindome. It takes its name from Sagsjön, a little further on – a tiny, very shallow lake, just 1.5 metres deep, that sits 20 metres above sea level and drains into the Kungsbackaån river basin.
Inte långt härifrån reser sig tre konstg: Not far from here rise three man-made hills, built up from demolition rubble and bulky rubbish. The first, Högdalstoppen, was finished in 1964, and the rock on that spot had previously been the highest point in Högdalen and Fagersjö. Today the summits are an outdoor recreation area with a skatepark and a disc golf course. Högdalstoppen 3 is still growing, topped up with soil dug out during road building.

Invalidkyrkogården: Invalidkyrkogården, the old military veterans' cemetery
Invigd av kronprinsen 1923: Opened by the Crown Prince in 1923
Invigningen av Sveriges då största stads: The opening of what was then Sweden's largest district centre drew more than 100,000 people. Among the 1,200 specially invited guests were Princesses Sibylla and Margaretha.
Invigt av kungaparet: Opened by the King and Queen
Ishallen en bit härifrån blev känd i hel: The ice rink a short way from here became famous across Sweden thanks to the TV series HCZ. It has changed its name several times: first Dalénhallen, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén and the nearby AGA factory, then Danske Bank Hallen, and now Childhood Hallen. Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club play here, and figure skaters train here too.
Isklassad kryssare blev hamnbåt: From ice-class cruiser to harbour boat
Islandstorget fick sitt namn 1936, men d: Islandstorget, Iceland Square, got its name in 1936 – but not because of exiled Icelanders or fishmongers. The connection is vaguer than that: when the streets and squares of Norra Ängby were being named, the planners drew inspiration from the ancient remains in the area. From the autumn of 1944, trams on the Ängby line, route 11, turned round here. A short walk away is Björklunds hage, the burial ground of Viking Age Ängby.
Ivar Tengbom ritade också bankhuset för: Ivar Tengbom also designed the Enskilda Bank building and the Stockholm School of Economics. Together with his partner Ernst Torulf he designed the Hagalund water tower in Solna, built in 1911.
Ivar Tengboms blå konserthus från 1926 h: Ivar Tengbom's blue Concert Hall from 1926 turns its classical colonnade towards the bustling square rather than Sveavägen – quite deliberately. It's considered one of the finest examples of Swedish 1920s Classicism. In front of the steps stands Carl Milles' Orpheus group.
J.G. Törnblom tog över Viksjö gård 1870,: J.G. Törnblom took over Viksjö farm in 1870, first as a tenant and then as owner. He invested in the farm, building a new cowshed, a sawmill and a crosscut saw powered by a portable steam engine.
J.V. Svenson ville egentligen bygga bila: J.V. Svenson really wanted to build cars here. But by the time the factory was finished it was harder than expected to keep up with car development, so while waiting for a good design he started making paraffin hot-bulb engines instead, under the name Avance.
Jakobs stege är en trappa med 187 granit: Jakobs stege, or Jacob's Ladder, is a flight of 187 granite steps leading down towards Lake Mälaren, named after the biblical patriarch Jacob's dream of a ladder reaching from earth to heaven. Nearby is Bellmanskällan, a spring that local tradition says is the one the poet Carl Michael Bellman sings about in Fredman's Epistle No. 82, “Vila vid denna källa” – Rest by this spring. The water still trickles out, if slowly, and it's safe to drink.
Jakobsberg är uppkallat efter majoren Ja: Jakobsberg is named after Major Jakob Lilliehöök, who died in October 1657, just six months after marrying Brita Cruus. His widow named the estate Jakobsberg in his honour and lived on there for almost 60 years.

Jakobsberg is named after Major Jakob Lilliehöök, who married Brita Cruus in March 1657 and died just six months later. His widow named the manor Jakobsberg in his honour and lived on there for almost 60 years.
Jakobsbergs Centrum, alldeles intill, är: Right here is Jakobsbergs Centrum, Järfälla's big shopping centre, with around sixty shops as well as homes and offices under the same roof. A couple of minutes away stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, the old station building from 1876, and where Vasavägen meets Ynglingavägen is Maria kyrka, St Mary's Church.
Jakobsbergs centrum är bilfritt. För att: Jakobsberg's town centre is car-free, and concrete sheep are dotted around to keep traffic out. Together with the windmill, the Järfälla sheep is the municipality's best-known symbol – it even appears on the coat of arms.
Jakobsbergs folkhögskola: Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the folk high school
Jakobsbergs gård var från början ett tor: Jakobsbergs gård started life in the early 17th century as a croft belonging to the Sätra estate. The manor-like house was added in the 1750s, when the farm had become a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers, and today the City Museum gives it a blue heritage rating. Down by the water is Mälarhöjdsbadet, a public beach that, despite its name, isn't in Mälarhöjden at all but in Bredäng.
Jakobsbergs kvarn från 1840-talet hade o: Jakobsberg's windmill from the 1840s had no luck with fire: it burned in 1980, 1997 and 2005, and after that third blaze it was never rebuilt. Next to it, in the buildings of the old manor, is Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, a folk high school for adult education. Two runestones in the park were moved here from the lands of Vibble farm, and one of them tells us that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised.
Jakobsbergs sporthall stod klar 1967 och: Jakobsberg sports hall was completed in 1967 and is home to teams including Järfälla Basket. The club was founded in 1973, and its men's team was already playing in the top division, Elitserien, by 1981, with the women's team following a year later. Since a refurbishment in 2009, the main hall holds about 1,100 people. A stone's throw away is Järfällabadet, the swimming centre that opened in 2018.
Jaktplan och skyddsrum i berget: Fighter planes and a shelter in the rock
James Turrells ljusverk Dawning från 199: James Turrell's light installation Dawning from 1992 was, until 2020, the only artwork on permanent display at Magasin III. Since 2017 the museum has also had a permanent satellite exhibition space in Jaffa.
Jarlabankes sten berättar att Häming och: Jarlabanke's stone tells how Häming and Jarlabanke cleared a road and built bridges in memory of their father, and how Estrid did the same for her sons Ingefast and Ingvar. The stone ends with the words: May God help their souls.
Jarlabergs vattentorn är 47,5 meter högt: Jarlaberg water tower stands 47.5 metres tall and has been a landmark in south-east Stockholm ever since it was finished in 1987. A little further on, in Augustendal, Johan Victor Svenson bought two old summer houses in 1899, planning to build a car factory. But car technology was moving too fast, so he made paraffin engines instead, sold under the name Avance – and they soon became a hit.
Johan Oliveholm köpte 1774 en del av Skä: In 1774 Johan Oliveholm bought part of Skälltorps Östergård, the land where the private Friedländer burial ground was later laid out. After 1800, Bäckebol belonged to three related families: the Lindqvists, the Friedländers and the Bratts.
Johan Wedberg från Nora kom till Stockho: Johan Wedberg from Nora came to Stockholm at 17 and found work as an assistant in a grocer's shop. In 1822 he married Anna Gustava Lundblad, heiress to the estate, and Lidingsberg has belonged to the Wedberg family ever since.
Johannebergs vattentorn från 1924 byggde: The Johanneberg water tower from 1924 was turned into housing in 1995, with just two flats on each floor. The top floor is 134 metres above sea level, and for many years these were the highest homes in Gothenburg – until Karlatornet took the record in 2023. All around is Chalmers, a university of technology founded back in 1829.
Jonsered var ett säteri som från 1830-ta: Jonsered was a noble estate that grew into a mill town under the Gibson family from the 1830s onwards. The brick buildings from its industrial heyday still shape the place, and the Swedish National Heritage Board has designated Jonsered a heritage site of national interest. Nearby is Göta Bio, where the film society Götas Vänner has been running the screenings since 1996.
Josephson inredde huset i 1700-talsstil: Josephson furnished the house in 18th-century style with details rescued from demolitions, including door overpieces from the Gustavian opera house. He had his architect's office on the ground floor and his home above it, and lived here until his death in 1929.
Jubileumsparken anlades till Göteborgs 4: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park, was created for Gothenburg's 400th anniversary. There's a public sauna and a place to swim in the river, and the park is a testing ground for ideas for the new district due to be built around Frihamnen.
Jubileumsparken i Frihamnen växte fram i: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park in Frihamnen, grew up in the run-up to Gothenburg's 400th anniversary as an experiment in city planning. It's home to Hamnbadet, also known as Pöl Harbour, with saltwater pools and a diving tower, and to Allmänna bastun, the public sauna. The sauna is built from recycled materials, its changing rooms are made of 12,000 glass bottles, and it stands four metres above the water. Plans for 5,000 homes on nearby Bananpiren, the Banana Pier, were dropped in 2020 because the ground was too poor to build on.
Jubileumsparken med bastu och bad: Jubileumsparken park, with sauna and swimming
Jungfruplatsen och husen runt torget rit: Jungfruplatsen and the buildings around the square were designed by Johannes Olivegren. When the square opened in 1959, 120 new flats in the area were ready at the same time. It also had a post office, which stayed from 1959 right up until 1996.
Jungfruplatsen, några hundra meter bort,: Jungfruplatsen, a few hundred metres away, was named in 1958 after the constellation Virgo – Jungfrun in Swedish – and opened on 6 December 1959. Built by Wallenstam, it was Mölndal's first proper shopping centre. It's also home to Mölndal's first piece of public outdoor art, Bossanova by Bertil Lundgren, unveiled in 1964. All around, the streets of Bifrost have names linked to farming.
Jungfrusund hette tidigare Jungfruhamn,: Jungfrusund used to be called Jungfruhamn, and the strait was a narrow channel between Gällstaö and Ekerön that has since disappeared. The "jungfru" (maiden) part of the name suggests an ancient pagan site here.

Jungfrusund used to be called Jungfruhamn, and the strait was a narrow channel between Gällstaö and Ekerön that has since vanished. The first part of the name, ‘jungfru’ (maiden), suggests there was once an ancient pagan site here.
Jungfrusund är både bostadsområde och ha: Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden bay, on the east side of the island of Ekerön. Just offshore are the Jungfruholmarna, two islets that belong to the Göta Sailing Society. The club began leasing them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built its own clubhouse there in 1955. They lie about six nautical miles from Stockholm out into Lake Mälaren.

Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden, on the east side of Ekerön. Out in the water are the Jungfruholmarna, two islands belonging to the Göta sailing club. The club leased them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built a clubhouse in 1955. The Ekerö ferry also crosses the bay here.
Juringe gård var en gång utgård till det: Juringe gård was once an outlying farm belonging to the large Vårby estate. The old main house was pulled down in 2001 and replaced by a lookalike, which is now a preschool. Still standing from the farm's working days are the storehouse, a laundry and dairy shed, and the farmhands' house, Väderluven. The croft of Nytorp was also here, beside the new road of 1673 that replaced the old Götha vägen route.
Järfälla gymnasium har funnits här nära: Järfälla gymnasium, an upper secondary school, has stood here near Jakobsberg centre under various names since 1962, and in 2020 it had just over 1,000 students. Among the schools once based here was SAM-gymnasiet, which offered social sciences with specialisms ranging all the way to football. Close by is the Imam Ali Mosque, considered the largest Shia Muslim congregation in the Nordic countries.
Järfälla är en kommun där det mesta är b: Most of Järfälla is built up, and that has led to some creative ways of saving what nature is left. The Norra Igelbäcken nature reserve, for instance, includes an old airfield – and a metro line is being built underneath it. Otherwise, the municipality is best known for shopping, thanks to the Barkarby retail park.
Järfälla är rikt på runor. I Skylsta fin: Järfälla is rich in runes. At Skylsta there's a Viking Age inscription carved straight into the rock, while a fragment of a runestone that, according to Richard Dybeck, stood on the same hill has vanished without a trace. A little further on, on the Stockholm side, is Backlura, where every street is named after a flower or plant.
Järfällabadet har en 50 meter lång bassä: Järfällabadet has a 50-metre pool, a 3-metre diving tower, two water slides and two multi-purpose pools with floors that can be raised and lowered. It replaced the old Jakobsberg swimming baths.
Järfällabadet, en bit härifrån, invigdes: Järfällabadet, a short way from here, opened on 14 April 2018. It has a 50-by-25-metre pool, two water slides and pools with floors that can be raised and lowered. It replaced the Jakobsberg swimming baths, which opened on a Monday in August 1971 and had a 48-metre water slide. The old building was originally going to be demolished but will instead be turned into a space for leisure activities.
Järfällas sydligaste kommundel heter Bar: Järfälla's southernmost district, Barkarby-Skälby, had about 12,000 residents in 2011. It's home to Kyrkbyn, the old church village, with the Gästgivargården coaching inn – in recent years known as Wärdshuset Lasse-Maja – and the old courthouse. Closer to the sports ground is the manor of Skälby gård, whose current main building dates from 1802.
Järla gård är en riktigt anrik herrgård:: Järla gård is a manor with deep roots: the first farm called Järla is believed to have been built around the year 900. It appears in Stockholm's court records in 1453, and a map from 1690 shows it on the northern shore of Lake Järlasjön. Industry later grew up all around it, and branch lines once ran from Saltsjö-Järla station to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works.
Järla har anor från vikingatiden, då led: Järla goes back to the Viking Age, when the route to Birka ran through Lake Järlasjön. The first farm here was probably built around the year 900. Both Sten Sture the Elder and Gustav Vasa have owned Järla farm.
Järnbrottsmotet i närheten är en ovanlig: The nearby Järnbrottsmotet is an unusual type of motorway junction, known as a double trumpet interchange. It was built in the 1990s on the site of the Europa roundabout, a gigantic roundabout with the Söderleden road cutting straight through it at traffic lights. In the wall of Västra Frölunda cemetery next door there are still iron rings where churchgoers once tethered their horses.
Järnbrottsmotet är helt planskilt och i: The Järnbrottsmotet interchange is fully grade-separated and essentially a true motorway junction, yet none of its roads is signposted as a motorway. The Europa roundabout that stood here before it dated from the 1970s.
Järnbärarna bar stångjärnet mellan vågar: The iron porters carried bar iron between the weighing scales on an iron hook resting on their backs. They were paid a share of the weighing fees, and a good porter could earn up to 1,700 riksdaler a year. The team was led by an alderman who swore an oath of loyalty to the king.
Järnkrok på ryggen: An iron hook on the back
Järntorget har fått sitt namn av järnet: Järntorget, Iron Square, is named after the iron that was once weighed and shipped from here. The fountain in the middle dates from 1927 and depicts the world's five continents. This is where the old working-class districts begin. To the south is Haga, with its cafés and landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys – and to the west run the Långgatorna streets, packed with vintage shops and bars.
Järnvägen har gått genom Årstaberg sedan: The railway has run through Årstaberg since the Årstabron bridge opened in 1929, but there was no station then. The commuter rail station didn't open until January 2006, with a platform squeezed between the existing tracks on two parallel viaducts – which is why it's rather narrow for so many passengers.
Järnvågen började byggas 1624 på en holm: Work on Järnvågen, the iron weigh house, began in 1624 on an islet in the Stora Hamnkanalen canal, where Brunnsparken is today. The last remains of the old weigh house burnt down in the great fire of 1813.
Järnvågen i Göteborg var den sista i Sve: Gothenburg’s iron weighhouse, the Järnvågen, was the last in Sweden to close. The guild of iron porters was dissolved in 1893, and they are remembered by the sculpture ‘Järnbärare’ (‘Iron Porters’) on Olof Palmes plats, at the northern end of Järntorget.
Järnåldersbyn Hogslaby består av sex små: The Iron Age village of Hogslaby is made up of six small wooden houses by Lake Aspen. Pupils felt sheep's wool, spin yarn and dye it with plants, bake bread and shape pots and jewellery from clay that's fired the Iron Age way.
Järnåldersgravar på backen: Iron Age graves on the hillside
Järva krog var en vägkrog cirka 3,5 kilo: Järva krog was a roadside inn on the Uppsala road, about 3.5 kilometres north of Norrtull, Stockholm's northern gateway. Its name lives on in the motorway junction. A short walk away is something far older: the Mellanjärva burial ground. With around 175 visible graves, it's one of the largest farm burial grounds in the Stockholm area.
Järvastaden är ett stadsbyggnadsprojekt: Järvastaden is a building project that's taking its time. The first residents moved in in September 2007, and once it's finished it's planned to be home to more than 15,000 people. The ninth and last phase won't happen until after 2030, though, because a high-voltage power line has to be moved first. To the east is the neighbouring residential area of Agnesberg.
Jättekast och kyrkvaktarstuga: A giant's throw and a sexton's cottage
KV konstskola började som en studiecirke: KV konstskola began as an evening drawing class led by the Valand student Wivi Bark, and it quickly became popular. In 1970 the school moved into Valand's old premises in Guldheden, but in 2023 it moved to Lindholmen.
Kafé i tvättstugan: A café in the old laundry
Kafé uppkallat efter en fisk: A café named after a fish
Kakelugnen som flyttat två gånger: The tiled stove that moved twice
Kalifen lade grundstenen: The Caliph laid the foundation stone
Kallhäll ligger intill Mälaren i Järfäll: Kallhäll lies on Lake Mälaren in northern Järfälla, and at its centre is the Folkets hus community centre, with a cinema and a library. A little further away is Stockholm Mejeri, Arla Foods' big dairy, which began production in 1984. Beneath the library is the Bolinder Museum, displaying products from Bolinders Mekaniska Verkstad, the Bolinder engineering works.
Kammeckers kvarn var en holländare där b: Kammecker's mill was a Dutch-style windmill, where only the cap turned to face the wind. It was torn down in 1794, but in 1810 a new one was built to grind grain for the Crown distilleries on Ladugårdslandet. On 29 November 1854 it burned down, bringing the era of mills on the hills to an end.
Kampementsbadet invigdes den 26 juli 196: Kampementsbadet opened on 26 July 1962 and cost 510,000 kronor. The low entrance building was designed by city gardener Holger Blom, and the name comes from the nearby Kampementsbacken hill.
Kaninburarna och biografen: The rabbit hutches and the cinema
Kanske skrevs svensk kungahistoria i när: Swedish royal history may well have been made just near here. Korseberget, a little village on the northern bank of the Nordre älv river close to its mouth, could be the same place as Horsaberg – where King Magnus Ladulås held peace talks with his brother Valdemar on 26 June 1274. A small community with a possibly big place in the history books.
Kanske uppkallat efter tre gubbar: Perhaps named after three old men
Kanton var en liten hantverksby som Lovi: Kanton was a little craft village that Queen Lovisa Ulrika and King Adolf Fredrik had built beside Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion. Craftspeople here made ironwork and lace and wove silk ribbons. The queen even tried her hand at silk farming, but the mulberry trees didn't take to the cold and the venture lasted only about ten years. Today the houses are private homes, and they're regarded as a forerunner of the Swedish garden city.
Kapellet byggdes av Sällskapet för Främj: The chapel was built by a society devoted to promoting pastoral care, which wanted to help people who had moved to the city from the countryside. It built cheap housing and small churches on a Danish model, and Stefanskapellet from 1900 was its first church.
Kapellet i Vasastaden var bara tillfälli: The chapel in Vasastaden was only temporary and was due to be demolished to make way for housing. But Brännkyrka parish bought it for 37,000 kronor, because the growing industrial area of Liljeholmen needed a church.
Kapellet invigdes 1970 och ritades av ar: The chapel was consecrated in 1970 and designed by architect Wolfgang Huebner in brick, patinated steel and glass. The plan is mirrored, with low entrances and lofty chapels. The gold and silver interior decoration is by Professor Olle Nyman.
Kapellet som flyttade till Aspudden: The chapel that moved to Aspudden
Kapellet är en monteringsfärdig träbyggn: The chapel is a prefabricated timber building with an octagonal nave, designed by the architect Erik Otto Ulrich in the Gothic Revival style, complete with a tower and a roof turret.
Kapplandsgatan intill känns igen på sina: Kapplandsgatan next door is easy to spot by its red three-storey buildings, and at the southern end of the street is Högsbo Hospital. The nearest square is Axel Dahlströms torg, which stands out with a 16-storey tower block from 1956 and a marble inlay by Endre Nemes on the community centre. Along Marklandsgatan you'll find a pizzeria, a bakery and a grill.
Karl Johansgatan fick sitt namn 1882 eft: Karl Johansgatan was named in 1882 after King Karl XIV Johan. The stretch between Stigbergstorget and Carl Johan’s Church is often called Hängmattan – the Hammock – because it dips through a hollow between two hills.
Karl XII står i brons och pekar mot Ryss: Karl XII stands in bronze, pointing towards Russia – a reminder of his wars. Johan Peter Molin's statue was unveiled on 30 November 1868, the 150th anniversary of the king's death. It was cast on Kungsholmen and weighs two and a half tonnes. The mortars around the plinth are war trophies from Riga. The Green Party has put forward a proposal to move the statue.
Karl XIV Johans tandläkare Jean Baptiste: Jean Baptiste Dubost, dentist to Karl XIV Johan, bought the Lilla Ersta estate in 1817 and in 1827 built an 18-metre lookout tower on the hill. Locals nicknamed it Tandpetaren, "the Toothpick" – a nod to his profession. The tower stood until around 1870.
Karl XV, som hade Ulriksdals slott från: King Karl XV, who had Ulriksdal Palace from 1857, leased Bergshamra farm for experimental agriculture and built summer villas for his friends. Dairy farmers hung on in southern Bergshamra until 1965.
Karlsro var kanske stadens mest svårspel: Karlsro was perhaps the trickiest pitch in town: its eastern side rose so steeply that playing down the wings was a struggle. Players changed in the open air, and the pioneers remembered all the time they spent hunting for the ball – usually the only one they had – in the rye fields south of the pitch.
Karolinsk herrgård vid Magelungen: A Caroline manor by Lake Magelungen
Karolinska Institutet grundades 1810 bla: Karolinska Institutet was founded in 1810, partly to train more surgeons for the army. During the war of 1808–09, young men with very little knowledge had been given crash courses and sent out as assistant doctors – which prompted the physician Eric Carl Trafvenfelt to propose an institute.
Kasernerna ritades av arkitekten Erik Jo: The barracks were designed by architect Erik Josephson in Baltic brick Gothic, inspired by medieval castle architecture. Every building has red-brick walls and a black metal roof, grouped around a lower, an upper and a rear barrack yard.
Kasernområdet hade både vinterstall, som: The barracks had winter stables, summer stables and a riding hall, and new stable buildings were added in 1903–1905. Today the Kviberg market is held in the former stables.
Katt och råtta över porten: Cat and mouse above the door
Kattuntillverkaren som ägde torpet: The calico maker who owned the croft
Keillers park och utsikten från Ramberge: Keillers park and the view from Ramberget hill
Kejsarens hotell i en roman: The Emperor's Hotel in a novel
Kent och The Hives på 44:an: Kent and The Hives at the 44
Kika in på Malmstens möbelskola: Peek into Malmstens, the furniture-making school
Kikås är den höga åsen vid Stensjöns söd: Kikås is the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and it's home to Sweden's biggest free-standing insect hotel, where wild bees and butterflies check in. Not far from here is Södra Långevattnet, a long, narrow lake with clear water, surrounded by rocky hills and wooded ridges. It's a popular place for a swim – but if you want to fish, you'll need a licence.
Kiosken och taxistationen: The kiosk and the taxi stand
Kista Centrum invigdes 1977 av kung Carl: Kista Centrum was opened in 1977 by King Carl XVI Gustaf and Queen Silvia. After major extensions it was renamed Kista Galleria in 2009, and the following year it was Stockholm’s most visited shopping centre.
Kista Nod, alldeles intill, kostade 700: Kista Nod, right next door, cost 700 million kronor and was completed in 2014. Stockholm University carries out research there in computer and systems sciences. The area is also home to the Electrum laboratory, with a complete production line for semiconductor chips. And, rather more discreetly, Kista houses Försvarsunderrättelsedomstolen, the Defence Intelligence Court, which decides on permits for signals intelligence.
Kista brandstation i gult tegel ritades: Kista's yellow-brick fire station was designed by Hans Borgström. Its seven-level training tower, just over 17 metres high, is identical to the one at Brännkyrka fire station, which Borgström designed at the same time. Both opened in 1980.
Kista torn blev klart 2016 och är Stockh: Completed in 2016, Kista Torn is Stockholm’s second-tallest residential building, with 35 floors of flats. Its little brother, K2, is 60 metres tall. Together the towers hold 362 homes, and the project was nominated for Construction of the Year 2017.
Kista tunnelbanestation är den enda på b: Kista is the only station on the blue line that's above ground. It sits on a viaduct 1,120 metres long – the longest anywhere on the metro. When the station was being named, the naming committee first wanted to add 'Gård', meaning farm, so that nobody would think of a 'likkista', a coffin. Rising above the shopping centre is Kista torn, the Kista Tower, 120 metres tall.
Kista är fullt av forskning. Rise SICS,: Kista is packed with research. Rise SICS, formerly the Swedish Institute of Computer Science, does non-profit computer science research to help Swedish companies compete. The Electrum Laboratory, part of the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, has a complete production line for semiconductor circuits and carries out research in micro- and nanotechnology.
Kistas tunnelbanestation är den enda på: Kista is the only station on the blue metro line that's above ground. The trains glide in along a 1,120-metre viaduct – the longest bridge on the whole metro network. Near the centre you'll also find the eight-sided Kista Church, and on Kista torg is Kista folkhögskola, Sweden's first folk high school – a kind of adult education college – with a Muslim profile.
Kistastenen står inte på sin ursprunglig: The Kista stone isn't in its original location. It was moved here during road works around 1900, and nobody knows where it first stood. The top is decorated with a ring cross with four equal arms.
Klaffbron från 1973 öppnade för trafik s: The bascule bridge from 1973 opened to traffic on the same day as the Nockeby and Drottningholm bridges. In 2023 it was due to be replaced by a new swing bridge as part of the Förbifart Stockholm bypass. With the bridge closed, the clearance for boats is six metres.
Klaffbron från 1973 öppnades samtidigt s: The 1973 bascule bridge opened at the same time as the Nockeby and Drottningholm bridges. As part of the Stockholm Bypass road project it is being replaced by a brand-new, wider swing bridge. Incidentally, Tappström was a town in its own right until 1975.
Klareberg i Kärra är en plats där bussar: Klareberg in Kärra is where the buses get to catch their breath. Drivers like to take their breaks here, and the big bus stop serves routes to Kungälv, Angered and Gothenburg. But the area is also popular with riders and dog owners, who come here to ride and train their dogs.
Klassiska Göteborg på en förmiddag. Kult: Classic Gothenburg in a morning: Götaplatsen, the city's cultural square, a stroll down the Avenyn boulevard and cinnamon buns in Haga.
Klingska huset, i hörnet av Älvsjövägen: Klingska huset, on the corner of Älvsjövägen and Johan Skyttes väg, is the oldest surviving block of rented flats in Solberga. Built between 1923 and 1925 in a town-style design, it was Älvsjö's first piece of town-centre development. A couple of hundred metres away is Älvkvarnstenen, an ancient cup-marked stone that has been moved twice and has stood next to Lerkrogen since 1994.
Klippan är en av Göteborgs äldsta miljöe: Klippan is one of Gothenburg's oldest neighbourhoods, with old seamen's cottages and the remains of the earlier Älvsborg fortress. Right beside it towers the Älvsborg Bridge, and beneath the bridge is the Röda Sten art centre.
Klippan är fullt av historia. Här låg Ga: Klippan is steeped in history. This was the site of Gamla Älvsborg, a mighty fortress from the 1300s to the 1600s that's now a ruin. The old sugar refinery, Sockerbruket, was home to 24 kvadrat, Sweden's smallest dance stage. And Klippans värdshus, the inn from 1762, was made famous by the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg in his book Min son på galejan, 'My Son on the Galley'. The trams sleep in the Majorna tram depot next door.
Klippans sommarteater byggdes 1923 och l: Klippan's summer theatre was built in 1923 in a beautiful spot overlooking Strömmen. Siegfried Fischer was its first director and also appeared on stage. The theatre closed after 1942, but the block name Friluftsteatern – 'the open-air theatre' – keeps its memory alive.
Klippans värdshus arrenderades 1762–1770: The Klippan inn was leased from 1762 to 1770 by James Carnegie, who then moved into Gothenburg and ran a coffee house on Köpmansgatan next to the German Church. The house had wallpaper, five tiled stoves, and a bread oven in one of the kitchens.
Kliv av i Vällingby och se biografen Fon: Hop off in Vällingby to see the Fontänen cinema on the square (2 min), then take the steps through the Trappan civic centre (3 min). Both opened in 1956 and were designed by Backström & Reinius.
Kliv av och gå fram till Eriksbergskrane: Hop off and walk over to the Eriksberg crane (3 min). The gantry crane from 1969 stands just over 70 metres tall and almost 110 metres wide. It's a listed structure and a symbol of the city's lost shipbuilding era.
Kliv av och se dig om bland stjärnhusen: Hop off and take a look around the star-shaped blocks of Gröndal. Sweden's first were built here, designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, and the buildings have become internationally famous.
Kliv av och titta på Krokslätts fabriker: Hop off and take a look at Krokslätts fabriker (2 min), old textile mills that now house businesses, restaurants and flats.
Kliv av vid Finnboda hamn och strosa bla: Hop off at Finnboda hamn and wander among the old shipyard buildings (5 min). Finnboda shipyard was founded in 1874, and its joinery, steam-engine works and canteen now house homes, offices and shops.
Kliv av vid Luma och gå till Lumaparken: Get off at Luma and walk to Lumaparken and the waterfront promenade along Hammarby sjö (2 min). The big functionalist building is the Luma factory, where light bulbs were once made.
Kliv ner i Rinkeby tunnelbanestation och: Step down into Rinkeby metro station and you'll find yourself in a Viking treasure chamber. The artist Nisse Zetterberg took small Viking Age objects dug up in the area and blew them up into huge mosaics on brick-red walls, with gold inlays and runes. The station opened in 1975, when the blue line was launched.
Kliv rakt in i 1950-talet på Kortedala m: Step straight into the 1950s at Kortedala museum (2 min), a two-room flat preserved just as it was when working-class families moved in. Citytorget square next door was built in 1955–1957.
Kliv rakt in i 1950-talet! Ett stenkast: Step straight back into the 1950s! A stone's throw away is Kortedala museum, a completely ordinary two-room flat with a kitchen, kept just as it was when the working-class families first moved in. It's so authentic that it's been used as a set for period films. Citytorget, the square right next to it, was built at the same time, between 1955 and 1957, with tower blocks, rows of shops and a street kiosk.
Klockan som berättade nyheter: The bell that told the news
Klockan som inte alltid går rätt: The clock that isn't always right
Klockaren på 1600-talet sålde enligt käl: According to the records, the 17th-century parish clerk sold beer and schnapps. This competed with the coaching inn in Barkarby and drew criticism from the congregation.
Klockaren som sålde brännvin: The parish clerk who sold schnapps
Klockargården vid kyrkan är känd från 16: The parish clerk's farm by the church dates back to at least the 1620s. According to the records, the 17th-century clerk sold beer and schnapps, competing with the coaching inn in Barkarby and drawing criticism from the congregation.
Klockstapel på smäckra ben: A bell tower on slender legs
Klockstapel som en kub på ben: A bell tower like a cube on legs
Klockstapeln från 1821 står högt uppe på: The bell tower, from 1821, stands high on a rocky hill west of the churchyard. Its bell is older still, cast in Stralsund in 1656. Inside the church, the pulpit dates from 1627 and still has its 17th-century hourglass.
Klotter som gav dödsstraff: Graffiti that earned a death sentence
Klubben som kör på banan sedan 1984 är e: The club that has raced on the track since 1984 is a youth branch of the Motorists' Total Abstinence Association. The tarmac circuit is 330 metres long and the gravel one 340 metres. In winter, electric cars race on an indoor track.
Klättra upp till stångmärket Valen: Climb up to the Valen pole beacon
Knappnålen är gjord av glasfiberarmerad: Knappnålen, "the Pin", is made of glass-fibre-reinforced plastic and stainless steel, and the arms of its cross point north–south and east–west. It went up in 2006 but wasn't officially unveiled until 2007. In 2008 an identical sculpture was raised in Kumla.
Knarrholmen var en present till arbetare: Knarrholmen was a gift to the workers. In 1940 the shipowner Axel Ax:son Johnson donated the island to the shipyard workers at Götaverken, and summer cottages went up here after 1945. In 2014 the trade unions sold the island, with its 33 cottages, restaurant and village shop. Neighbouring Sillfarsholmen was bought by the Aeolus sailing club in 1935 for a single krona.

Knutpunkt för spårvagnar och Mälaröbussa: A hub for trams and Mälaren island buses
