Knuttehaket som blev film: The biker café that made it into a film
Kolla in Flatenbanan för radiostyrda bil: Check out Flatenbanan, the track for radio-controlled cars
Kolla utställningen i biblioteket: Check out the exhibition at the library
Kollektivhuset Sockenstugan är ett gemen: Sockenstugan is a cohousing block for people in the second half of life – one of many created in Stockholm after a political decision in 1980. One report called it a real success story. Right next door is Gränsberget park, an old moraine hill shared between the districts of Enskededalen and Kärrtorp.
Komettorget fick sitt namn 1965 som del: Komettorget, Comet Square, got its name in 1965 as part of a group of names on the theme of space and the universe. That's why the streets around it include Meteorgatan, Nebulosagatan and Kometgatan.
Kommunalhus med polisfinka: A town hall with a police cell
Kommunalvägen löper genom Huddinges hjär: Kommunalvägen runs right through the heart of Huddinge, with the station, the shopping centre, the church and the municipal offices all along its 1.3 kilometres. There's been news here recently too: Sjödalsgymnasiet, an upper secondary school that opened in 1994, closed in 2026. In its final year it had 185 students, compared with 608 just three years before.
Kommunalvägen var tidigare en del av Hud: Kommunalvägen was once part of Huddingevägen, the first direct road between Huddinge and Skanstull. When the new Huddingevägen was built west of the tracks in the 1960s, it became a local street and was named after the municipal hall.
Kommundelen Tibble rymmer både Täby cent: The Tibble district is home both to Täby Centrum and to the church that has been called the Cathedral of Roslagen. Täby Centrum has 215 shops and, since 2022, the official name Westfield Täby Centrum. Its library holds a Viking Age runestone fragment found at Lissby in 1930. A piece found at the same time turned out to belong to a different stone.

The Tibble district is home to both Täby centrum, the shopping centre, and the church that's been nicknamed “the Cathedral of Roslagen”. The shopping centre has 215 shops, and since 2022 its official name has been Westfield Täby Centrum. Its library keeps two fragments of Viking Age runestones that were found in Lissby in 1930 – though it later turned out that several of the pieces actually belonged to a different stone.
Kommunen består mest av skog. Mölndalsån: The municipality is mostly forest. The Mölndalsån river runs through it from east to west, passing Västra Nedsjön, Landvettersjön and Rådasjön lakes. There are several nature reserves too, among them Klippan, Risbohult and Gallhålan.
Kommunen som växte ur sina lokaler: The council that outgrew its offices
Kommunens centrala delar följer Säveåns: The heart of the municipality follows the valley of the Säveån river, hemmed in by steep rocky slopes. Up on the heights grows pine forest on bare rock, here and there mixed with oak and beech. To the south-west lies the Knipeflågsbergen nature reserve, an untouched rocky plateau with natural woodland.
Kommunens största arbetsplats är en flyg: The biggest employer is an airport
Komplexet ritades av Carl-Axel Acking oc: The complex was designed by Carl-Axel Acking and has 340 flats in four tower blocks and several low-rise buildings around four courtyards. They range from 25-square-metre studios with their own little garden to six-room flats with roof terraces looking out over Lake Mälaren.
Konditori i en konstnärsvilla: A patisserie in an artists’ villa
Konditoriet som blev filmkuliss: The café that became a film set
Konditoriet som blev knuttehak: The café that became a bikers' haunt
Kongahälla Center invigdes i mars 2019 o: Kongahälla Center opened in March 2019 and spreads across 37,000 square metres. As well as the express buses in the story, the travel centre next door is also served by the X4, among others.
Konkavt torn med koppartupp: A concave tower with a copper cockerel
Konserter i filmmannens villa: Concerts in the film man's villa
Konsten på Västra skogens station är gjo: The art at Västra skogen station is by Sivert Lindblom, who was inspired by the mystery of the old name Ingentingskogen – the ‘Nothing Forest’. Look out for the tiled shapes along the walls, and for the artist’s own profile, which pops up in several places.
Konsthallen Accelerator har sina utställ: The Accelerator art gallery has its exhibition halls in a former underground lab for accelerator physics, and it opened in 2019 with a work by Tino Sehgal. Its neighbour is Villa Frescati, designed by Louis Jean Desprez in 1791–1792 as a summer retreat for Gustaf Mauritz Armfelt, facing Gustav III's pavilion across the water. And at the Swedish Museum of Natural History is Cosmonova, Sweden's only domed IMAX cinema.
Konstnären Axel Törneman flyttade till J: The artist Axel Törneman moved to Johannisberg in 1924, the year before he died. From his time here there's a large mural in the entrance hall of the main house, which he painted together with his friend Isaac Grünewald.
Konstnären Olle Olsson Hagalund bodde he: The artist Olle Olsson Hagalund spent his whole life in the same wooden house, built in 1897 by the master carpenter Carl Jakob Brolin. Today it's a museum, both for his art and for the old shanty town of Hagalund, which was demolished in the 1960s to make way for the Blåkulla tower blocks. Inside you'll find a model of old Hagalund. Nearby stands Hagalund water tower from 1912.
Konstnären Sivert Lindblom inspirerades: The artist Sivert Lindblom was inspired by the mystery in the name 'Ingentingskogen' – the Forest of Nothing. The walls are decorated with tiled shapes, and a tile pattern runs along the platform edges. Look closely and you'll spot the artist's own profile in several places.
Konstnären Tor Svae, som byggt sagomiljö: The artist Tor Svae, who built the fairy-tale settings at Junibacken, created the park together with George Johansson and Jens Ahlbom, the creators of Mulle Meck. Here you'll find Mulle and his dog Buffa, the Linlyftet lift, Daisy Diesel's garage and Restaurant Chez Nous.
Konstprojektet Det mekaniska undret har: The art project Det mekaniska undret made music about a ride on the number 11 tram. The song Mariaplan, featuring Svartbjörn, was voted one of Göteborgs-Posten's 130 best songs in 2011. The folk singer Clas Kristiansson wrote the ballad "Sommar på Mariaplan".
Konstsamlaren på slottet: The art collector at the manor
Konstverket som tappade ringar: The artwork that lost its rings
Konsums Samköp-bandet var ett av tidens: Konsum's Samköp-bandet was one of the largest self-service shops of its day. On your way to work you dropped your order slip into a box on the facade, then collected your groceries in the evening, by 6.30 pm at the latest. You could also buy goods from vending machines with 390 compartments. Today it's home to the Cafe Chateau patisserie.
Kontorshusen vid Solna strand står på ga: The office blocks at Solna strand stand on old industrial land – the area used to be called Vretens industriområde. Granite was once quarried nearby: from 1875 the City of Stockholm leased Huvudsta quarry on Lake Ulvsundasjön to make cobblestones, but by the early 1880s the rock was considered worked out. And the metro station here sits in a rock cavern a full 28 metres underground.
Kontorsjätte vid Cityterminalen: An office giant by the City Terminal
Kontorsområdet hette förr Virebergs indu: This office district used to be called Virebergs industriområde, the Vireberg industrial estate. It was planned in the 1950s by Valvet, a Wallenberg-owned property company that had bought the land from Huvudsta gård in 1947. Being close to the railway, with a siding of its own, was a big selling point, but building didn't really get going until the 1960s. Next door is Löfströms gymnasium, an upper secondary school that takes in just over 55 elite athletes a year in football, ice hockey and floorball.
Kooperativa förbundet byggde kafferoster: The Swedish Co-operative Union built the coffee roastery in 1969–1970, in brick with a red-orange metal front facing the bay. The coffee was sold as Cirkelkaffe. In spring 2013 the Royal Opera also opened a small stage here, Scen Gäddviken.
Kopparhusen byggdes som rena kontorshus: The copper-clad buildings were built purely as offices, with shops on the ground floor. In the early 2000s the two southern buildings were converted into owner-occupied flats, and the copper façade was given glazed balconies.
Kopparhusen har fått sitt namn av fasade: Kopparhusen, the Copper Houses, get their name from the copper panels on their facades. They were designed by Gunnar Jacobson and Olof Strömberg, and the consulting firm Jacobson & Widmark had its head office in one of them. At street level there were once both the town library and Systembolaget, the state-run off-licence.
Koppartak och mahognyfönster: A copper roof and mahogany windows
Kornhall är en liten hamnby vid Nordre ä: Kornhall is a little harbour village on the Nordre älv river, with a small shipyard and a marina. From here, the Kornhall ferry – a cable ferry – crosses the river to Brunstorpsnäs on Hisingen. The crossing dates back to 1850, and it got its first motor ferry in 1951, when traffic had grown because the route made the journey to Gothenburg so much shorter.
Korsvägen är porten till Göteborgs evene: Korsvägen is the gateway to Gothenburg's events district. Here you'll find the Liseberg amusement park, opened in 1923, the Universeum science centre and the Museum of World Culture – and Svenska Mässan, the Swedish Exhibition and Congress Centre, is right next door.
A short hop south along the park.
Kort hopp till S:t Eriksplan, där du byt: A short hop to S:t Eriksplan, where you change to bus 3.
A short ride via Trekanten to Gröndal.
Kortedala byggdes på 1950-talet som en m: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as a modern suburb with everything close at hand – homes, a square, schools and green spaces. A lot of the architecture from that era is still here today.
Kortedala byggdes som Göteborgs första f: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as Gothenburg's first suburb, on the city's north-eastern outskirts, where until then there had been little more than crofters' cottages. A few farms hung on right into the 1960s. Not far from here, at the entrance to Bergsjön, the long blocks of flats on Siriusgatan stand in a row along a hilltop, a landmark for the whole area.
Kortedala was built as Gothenburg's first suburb. The square itself was finished in 1955.
Kortedala har sin motsvarighet i Välling: Kortedala's counterpart in Stockholm is Vällingby, and both were called satellite towns back when satellites like Sputnik were circling the Earth. For a taste of the 1950s, visit Kortedala Museum on Adventsvägen.
Kortedala torg, en bit härifrån, hette f: Kortedala torg, just along from here, was originally called Kortedalstorget. But Göteborgs Spårvägar, the Gothenburg tramways company, pointed out that everyone actually said 'Kortedalatorget', and that the official name was a mouthful. The city council voted 24 to 17, and in 1959 the square got the name it has today. That same year the Forum cinema opened on the square – only to close at the end of 1965.
Kovikshamn ligger vid havet, strax norr: Kovikshamn lies by the sea just north of where the Nordre älv river flows out, and it has not one but two marinas. The northern one, Kovikshamns Norra Småbåtshamn, is privately owned and the bigger of the two. Since 2015 Kovikshamn has officially counted as an urban area, and at the same time the neighbouring villages of Sundhammar and Tofta, along with Brunnefjäll, were merged into it.
Kring 1750 byggdes ett sockerbruk öster: Around 1750 a sugar refinery designed by Carl Hårleman was built east of the islet. It stood until 1841, and parts of its foundations still lie beneath Hotel Palace.
Kring Bromma kyrka ligger en liten klung: Around Bromma Church is a small cluster of old rectory buildings with a long history. The red Sockenstugan, the 17th-century parish cottage, was the vicar's home right up until 1850, when the new rectory was finished. On the same plot is a tithe barn, where the priest once collected the Bromma farmers' taxes – paid in produce rather than cash. And up on Kråsberget hill, north of Sockenstugan, stands the church's bell tower.
Kring förra sekelskiftet byggdes sommarv: Around 1900 summer villas sprang up here, drawn by the views of Lake Mälaren and the steamboat jetty. At the same time a steam-powered sawmill operated at Jungfrusund, and charcoal stacks smouldered on Gällstaö to keep it supplied with energy.
Kring förra sekelskiftet fanns flera trä: Around the turn of the 20th century, the Malmvik estate had several gardens and orchards alongside its farmland. There were smaller orchards here at Betlehem and at Lindö too.
Kring förra sekelskiftet köpte grosshand: Around 1900 the wholesale merchants Fredric Althainz and Carl Bengtsson bought land here to build an exclusive suburb, Södertörns villastad. Plots sold slowly and only a handful of houses were built. In 1912 the land was sold to the City of Stockholm.
Kring köpcentrumet i norra Botkyrka finn: The area around this shopping centre in northern Botkyrka has an unusually close-knit cluster of churches. Botkyrka folkhögskola, a folk high school – a kind of adult education college – founded in 1997, is owned by five Christian congregations, three of them Syriac Orthodox, yet it's open to everyone, whatever their faith. Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, on Tomtbergavägen, sits right next to the Syriac Orthodox Church of St Peter and St Paul, while Hallundakyrkan is practically wall to wall with the shopping centre.
Kring år 1800 hade operadansösen Sophie: Around 1800 the estate belonged to the opera dancer Sophie Hagman, best known as the mistress of Prince Fredrik Adolf. During her time large sums were spent beautifying it, and a double avenue of lime trees was planted down to the water.
Kritiken var enhällig när kyrkan invigde: The critics were unanimous when the church was consecrated in 1859. The writer Viktor Rydberg noted that its tower was lower than those of the German Church and the cathedral, but "more powerful, more resolute, more devout than they".

Krogen Draken och en bitter fejd: The Draken inn and a bitter feud
Krogen grundades 1626 av proviantmästare: The inn was founded in 1626 by the quartermaster Henrik Olofsson, who was granted the right by King Gustav II Adolf to run a hostelry on the highway between Stockholm and Uppsala. A copy of the charter – the first of its kind – hangs in the entrance.
Krogen med dåligt rykte: The tavern with a bad reputation
Krogen med kungligt tillstånd: An inn with a royal charter
Krogen som gynnades av tullen: The inn that profited from the toll
Krogen stängde 1872 när gästerna blev fö: The inn closed in 1872 when customers dried up. The building then became a primary school and later housing for statare, the contracted farm labourers. On Walpurgis Eve 1983 Christer Lingström reopened it as a restaurant, since it was Sweden's oldest surviving inn building.
Krogen vid vägskälet: The inn at the fork in the road
Krokslätts fabriker är gamla industribyg: Krokslätts fabriker are old industrial buildings where textiles were once made. Today they're home to businesses, restaurants and flats – a good example of old factories getting a new lease of life.
Krokängsparken var folkpark mellan 1903: Krokängsparken was a folkpark – a popular open-air entertainment park – from 1903 to 1934. On Sunday mornings people marched with music and banners from the ferry landing to the festival ground, where there were political speeches, a dance floor, a carousel, a shooting gallery and hot dogs. In the end the competition from Liseberg proved too stiff, and in 1934 the company went bankrupt.
Krokängsparken, en promenadpark på cirka: Krokängsparken, a park for walking of about 7.5 hectares, was laid out as far back as 1902 between Bratteråsberget hill and Pölsebo. A little further on, towards the river, towers the Eriksberg crane, a gantry crane from 1969 that's just over 70 metres tall and almost 110 metres wide. It's a listed structure and a symbol of the shipyard era, when everything about shipbuilding was on a giant scale.
Kronprins Gustav Adolf invigde flyghamne: Crown Prince Gustav Adolf opened the airport on 5 August 1923, the same year Gothenburg celebrated its 300th anniversary. Bad weather pushed the ceremony back by a day. The airfield was laid out on land belonging to the farms of Amhult Uppegård, Röd Sörgård and Amhult Nedergård.
Kronprinsen invigde i regnet: The Crown Prince opened it in the rain
Krontorpet Hökmossen nämns första gången: Hökmossen, a croft owned by the Crown, is first mentioned in 1748 in a document in the Military Archives. Back then it was called Hökmåsen, after a bog north of the farm that has since disappeared. A little way off, in an old co-op building in the villa suburb of Långbro, was the restaurant Aloë, which served luxurious tasting menus from 2015 to 2025 and earned two Michelin stars.

The crown croft of Hökmossen is first mentioned in 1748, in a document in the Military Archives, where it's called Hökmåsen. The name comes from a bog (mosse) north of the farm that has since disappeared.
Krossgatan ligger i Vinsta industriområd: Krossgatan runs through the Vinsta industrial area, where Vällingby fire station opened in December 1964. Its firefighters have special training in roof ventilation and climbing at height. Johannelund metro station was built as an 'industrial station' with two side platforms – the only one like it on the Stockholm metro – and until October 1997 it opened only at rush hour. The Vinsta district takes its name from the old village of Vinsta.
Krucifixet som fick färg: The crucifix that was given colour
Krusboda byggdes under åren 1970–1975 oc: Krusboda was built between 1970 and 1975 and has its own school. Not far away, on Lake Albysjön, is Nyfors, a well-preserved 1940s holiday-cottage area where more and more people now live all year round. Between the branches of the Wättinge stream lies Bullerholmen – ‘Noisy Islet’ – which, despite its name, is now completely uninhabited. North of the cottages begins the Alby nature reserve.
Kryddhandlaren Carl Peter Eneroth hade a: The spice merchant Carl Peter Eneroth had a shop at Västerlånggatan 45 and grew up on Kevinge farm. His godfather was Zacharias Strindberg, grandfather of August Strindberg. Klimpen was the rocky knoll where Calle cast his fishing rod.

Kräftpremiär i sjöpaviljongen: Crayfish season in the lake pavilion
Krögaren Eric Nordström, som gjorde krog: The innkeeper Eric Nordström, who made the inn more profitable than the garden, had once been a garden hand at the house where Bellman was born. He was also the father-in-law of Maria Kristina Kiellström, better known as Ulla Winblad in Bellman's Epistles.
Krögaren och kocken Mikael Öster värvade: Restaurateur and chef Mikael Öster was brought in to run Westra Piren. Upstairs was the gourmet restaurant, seating 70, where the kitchen cooked in the classic French tradition. Downstairs there was a bar and a brasserie.
Kulan på kullen är Bällsta radartorn, i: The ball on the hill is the Bällsta radar tower, nicknamed the Golf Ball, standing between Bromma Airport and Solvalla. The Solvalla trotting track opened in 1927, holds 35,000 spectators and hosts the Elitloppet race every year. In Bällsta itself, around 200 cottages were built by their owners with their own hands, using materials and instructions from the city's small-house office.
The ball-bearing giant SKF has deep roots here. Not far away in Gamlestaden was Mariedal's landeri, a small country estate, where SKF had its office from 1910 to 1914. Nearby was also Torpavallen, the old home ground of Qviding FIF, with two gravel pitches and a grass pitch with a stand. Where footballs once rolled, the Torpavallen shopping centre now stands.
Kullen är cirka 20 meter högre än den ur: The hill is about 20 metres higher than the original gravel ridge, because slalom slopes were planned on its north side. They were never built. From the top you can see the Globe, Högdalstoppen, Söder Torn and the Wenner-Gren Center, though trees now hide some of the view.
Kultur i oväntade lokaler finns en bit h: Culture in unexpected places awaits a short way from here in Fullersta. Fullersta bio is now an art gallery and theatre, housed in former Konsum co-op shops and an old cinema. And since 2009, the manor house Fullersta gård – once the centre of an estate whose lands covered the whole area – has been home to a contemporary art gallery.
Kulturhuset Bergsjön: Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house
Kumla allé är cirka 850 meter lång och l: Kumla allé is about 850 metres long and still leads up to the manor house. The old line of trees survives along its southern stretch. At the northern end of the avenue is Alléplan, generally known as Trollbäcken's centre.
Kung Oscar II invigde gasverket den 25 n: King Oscar II opened the gasworks on 25 November 1893, together with Crown Prince Gustaf and Princes Carl and Eugen. A special train ran from Central Station right onto the works' own tracks. Boberg was awarded the Order of Vasa for his work.
Kungakrönt huvud och hiss: A crowned head and a lift
Kungarnas Stockholm: slottet som ersatte: Royal Stockholm: the palace that replaced Tre Kronor Castle, the House of Nobility and Riddarholmen Church, and Gustav III’s Haga, with its Finnish Cottages and the remains of a palace and a stable block that were never finished.

Kungen var på väg hem från jakt och hade: The King was on his way home from a hunt in tall hunting boots, so he made it ashore with dry feet while everyone else got theirs wet. He took it calmly, smoked a cigarette and said it was "a blessing in disguise".
Kungen var på väg hem från jakt vid Tull: The King was on his way home from hunting at Tullgarn. Thanks to his tall hunting boots he stepped ashore dry-shod, while everyone else got wet feet. He smoked a cigarette and declared it "a blessing in disguise".

Kungens kurva har fått namn efter att Gu: Kungens kurva, "the King's Curve", got its name after Gustaf V's Cadillac ended up in the ditch here on 28 September 1946, on the way home from a hunt. The car slid into a waterlogged ditch, and Dagens Nyheter reported that the King "stepped out dry-shod after car tumble into marshy pool".
Kungens kurva har fått sitt namn från en: Kungens kurva, 'the King's Curve', is named after a real accident. On 28 September 1946, King Gustaf V's chauffeur came off Södertäljevägen near here and ended up stuck in a water-filled ditch – and the name stuck too. IKEA opened its second store here in 1965, and the round building was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York.
Kungens trädgårdsmästare från Haag: The King's gardener from The Hague
Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien lät bygga S: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences built Stockholm's old observatory in 1753 to designs by Carl Hårleman. Research here covered astronomy, geography and meteorology. Astronomy moved out to Saltsjöbaden in 1931, and the building became a geography department.
Kungliga tennishallen: Kungliga tennishallen, the Royal Tennis Hall
Kungsgatan 65 har levt många liv. Biogra: Kungsgatan 65 has worn many hats. The Palladium cinema opened here in 1918, with the Bal Palais dance restaurant in the basement. Later it became the Heaven nightclub, and from 2003 to 2025 it was Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern from 1906, a listed theatre named after King Oscar II. The same building is home to Fasching, Scandinavia's largest jazz club since 1977.
Kungshamra planerades bilfritt, med park: Kungshamra was planned to be car-free, with parking kept outside. Landscape architect Gunnar Martinsson argued that no purpose-built playgrounds were needed, since the whole area could serve as one big outdoor playroom. Kitchens in the family flats face the courtyards so parents can keep an eye on the children.
Kungshamra planerades bilfritt. Landskap: Kungshamra was planned to be car-free. Landscape architect Gunnar Martinsson saw no need for playgrounds – the whole area was meant to work as one big space for play and outdoor living.
Kungsholms folkskola var Sveriges störst: Kungsholms folkskola was Sweden's biggest primary school and one of the largest in the world, with room for 4,000 pupils. Only the northern part survives today, home among other things to Stockholm's arts school. This neighbourhood is full of firsts: Kungsholmen's crèche was the first of its kind in Sweden, and Kvinnohuset, a fourteen-storey cooperative block of flats for women, opened here in 1947.
Kungsladugård har den största sammanhäng: Kungsladugård has the largest continuous area of landshövdingehus, Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses. They were built between 1916 and 1938, and the area was planned by the chief city engineer, Albert Lilienberg. The town plan is of national interest.
Kungsladugård är tidigt bostadsbyggande: Kungsladugård is an early chapter in Gothenburg's housing history. The Svärdsliljan block from 1927 was one of HSB's first blocks of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors. The district also has a bronze statue, Ung man, Young Man, made by Astrid Noack in 1948 and set up on the corner of Ståthållaregatan and Fågelfängaregatan in 1968. Kungsladugård Church is just a short walk away.
Kungsladugårdsgatan är bred av en anledn: There's a reason Kungsladugårdsgatan is so wide. In Albert Lilienberg's town plan of 1916, it was drawn at double width to leave room for a future railway between the harbour and the city. The name comes from Älvsborgs Kungsladugård, the royal farm that supplied Älvsborg Castle with horses and grain. Along the street stands the Broström Foundation's building from 1924, listed since 2017.
Kungsporten låg ungefär där Kungsportsbr: The King’s Gate, Kungsporten, stood roughly where Kungsportsbron bridge is today. This was where people and goods were checked and customs duties collected. The gatehouse also housed the town watch, with a lock-up on the first floor. The gate was made of wood from 1621 to 1653, and of stone after that.
Kungspudeln och Bulldoggen: The King Poodle and the Bulldog
Kungssten lies close to the mouth of the Göta älv river. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was the longest suspension bridge in Sweden when it opened in 1966. Out in the estuary is the 17th-century New Älvsborg Fortress, built to defend the city against the Danes. Down by the water is Klippan, with old seamen's cottages and the remains of the older Älvsborg Fortress.
Kungsstol i röd sammet: A royal seat in red velvet
Kungsträdgården var från början kungens: Kungsträdgården, the King's Garden, began life as the royal kitchen garden. Today it's one of the city's best-loved parks, and in spring its cherry trees burst into pink and white blossom.
Kusinen som var präst här: The cousin who was vicar here
Kvarnen bakom en storbrand: The mill behind a great fire
Kvarnen byggdes av fogden Henrik Olofsso: The mill was built by the bailiff Henrik Olofsson, who also put up Edsberg manor and founded the Edsbacka inn in 1626. In 1638 the estate and mill were owned by Count Gabriel Bengtsson Oxenstierna.
Kvarnen på Vårdkaseberget brann ned till: The windmill on Vårdkaseberget burnt to the ground at Easter 1939. The miller's house survives and is used by the scouts, and every year the Walpurgis Night bonfire on 30 April is lit where the mill once stood.
Kvarnen som brann tre gånger: The windmill that burned three times
Kvarnen som dödade en ko: The windmill that killed a cow
Kvarnen som flyttade från stan: The windmill that moved out of town
Kvarnen som malde i 300 år: The mill that ground for 300 years
Kvarnen som står här i dag byggdes 1855: The windmill that stands here today was built in 1855 for the farmer Knut Bennet of Bällsta farm, about three kilometres north-west of here. It was designed by his 19-year-old nephew Karl Abraham Saxenberg, who was given a gold watch as thanks. The weathervane still reads "KB 1855".
Kvarnen var ett svartbygge: The mill was built without permission
Kvarnen är blåmärkt av Stadsmuseet, den: The windmill is marked blue by the Stockholm City Museum, the highest heritage rating. It has been restored but now stands without its sails.
Kvarnen är en stolpkvarn, där hela byggn: This is a post mill, where the entire building is turned to face the wind. The name Stampan hints that it may have pounded flax and hemp for rope and sails, but there's no record of that.
Kvarnen är i dag renoverad, men saknar v: The windmill has been restored, but it has no sails. It stands among the houses of Solhem, far from its original hill in the inner city.
Kvarngatan på Södermalm har fått sitt na: Kvarngatan in Södermalm is named after the windmills that stood here in the 17th and 18th centuries. It was probably Christian Hansson's mill that started the great Katarina fire of 1723.
Kvarnholmen var en gång en ö full av mjö: Kvarnholmen, ‘Mill Island’, was once all about flour and bread. The Tre Kronor mill started up in 1897, and there was also a macaroni factory, an oat mill and a crispbread bakery. Today people live in the old silos – when Silo III was turned into flats, for a while nothing but its outer walls was left standing. The old bakery, Bageriet, is now Kvarnholmen's centre, and the oat mill, Havrekvarnen, has been listed since 2016.
Kvarnholmen var från början en ö, men su: Kvarnholmen used to be an island, until the channel separating it was filled in during the 1970s to give the factories a better transport link. This was home to the Tre Kronor flour mill, and its oat mill, Havrekvarnen, built in 1927–28, is now a listed building. Around Tre Kronors väg the company built a model village for its workers, with terraced houses, narrow blocks of flats and its very own Konsum co-op store, open from 1935 to 1977. The Munspelet office building from 1966 – nicknamed “the Harmonica” – is listed for its striking modernist architecture.
Kvarnholmens centrum ligger i Bageriet,: Kvarnholmen's centre is Bageriet, the Bakery – the old crispbread factory, whose earliest drawings date from 1929. Today people live where the crispbread used to be baked. Right next door is Disponentvillan, the manager's villa, built in 1931 for the head of Kvarnen Tre Kronor, the Three Crowns Mill. Makaronifabriken, the macaroni factory, is still here too, and the Lilla Kvarnholmen playground is themed on the island's old industrial buildings.
Kvarnskolan bekostades av Edvard Witte p: Kvarnskolan was paid for by Edvard Witte of Gåshaga farm, who wanted to give the parish's girls a school for reading and handicrafts. Boys were admitted as early as 1890. The building also housed a poorhouse, and the schoolmistress lived in the miller's cottage by the mill.
Kvarnstenen fick ny plats: A new home for the millstone
Kvarnstenen vid Gymnasievägen är av sand: The millstone on Gymnasievägen is made of sandstone and measures about 1.25 metres across. Grooves in the stone channelled the flour out to the edge, where it could be collected. It was moved here in 2013 following a suggestion from a local resident.
Kvarnstenen är av sandsten, cirka 1,25 m: The millstone is made of sandstone and measures about 1.25 metres across. Its radiating grooves carried the ground grain out to the edge, where the flour could be collected.
Kvarter och gator i Husby är uppkallade: Husby's blocks and streets are named after Norwegian places and people, such as Oslogatan, Trondheimsgatan and Edvard Griegsgången. Cars and pedestrians are kept apart on separate levels, with footbridges spanning the sunken roads.
Kvarteren i Annedal har fått namn efter: The blocks in Annedal are named after Swedish children's books: Kulla-Gulla, Lasse Liten, Skalman, Kusin Vitamin, Tant Brun, Tant Grön and Tant Gredelin. The first tenants moved in in February 2011, on Pippi Långstrumps gata – Pippi Longstocking Street.
Kvarteren i Solna strand har fått namn e: The blocks in Solna strand are named after fruit, berries, nuts and vegetables – Smultronet (the Wild Strawberry), Päronet (the Pear), Aprikosen (the Apricot) and Apelsinen (the Orange), for example. In summer the electric boat E/S Movitz sails from here to Klara Mälarstrand.
Kvarteren runt Wieselgrensplatsen består: The blocks around Wieselgrensplatsen are made up of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's tenements with a stone ground floor and two wooden storeys above – and Lundby Hospital stands on the square.
Kvarteren vid Åkerbyvägen hör till HSB:s: The blocks along Åkerbyvägen are part of HSB's low-rise housing in Tibble, one of the areas built in the 1950s and 60s. A little further away is Täby centrum, with the Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, which has five screens and 516 seats. In the other direction is Ensta station on the Roslagsbanan railway, where around 500 people get on on an ordinary winter weekday.

The blocks along Åkerbyvägen are part of HSB's low-rise housing in Tibble, one of the areas built in the 1950s and 1960s. A little way off is Täby Centrum, with the Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, which has five screens and 516 seats. The Roslagsbanan railway has no fewer than three stations in Tibble, so the train is never far away.
Kvarteret Gamlebo, intill Svedmyra tunne: The Gamlebo block, beside Svedmyra metro station, was originally built as Gamlebo, the City of Stockholm's old people's home, later known as Gammelbyn. Its ten original residential buildings are now owner-occupied flats. Much closer, on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen, was the Corso cinema, which opened in 1938 as Tusse-Bio and closed in 1969.
Kvarteret Holmia bildades 1906 av det ny: The Holmia district was founded in 1906 by a newly formed company, AB Lidingö Villastad, and its early 20th-century character is still beautifully preserved, with villas in National Romantic, Art Nouveau and Art Nouveau Baroque styles. Here you'll find Lidingö museum, in the former Villa Fornboda from 1907, with exhibitions on 20th-century Lidingö and a turn-of-the-century salon. It's run by Lidingö's local heritage society – one of the largest in Sweden – which among other things organises Bellman Day.
Kvarteret Kabbelekan består av sex hus i: The Kabbelekan block consists of six buildings in 1920s Classicism, designed by Allan Berglund in 1924. The central building facing Mariagatan has three gables crowned with spires, and the dormers have half-moon windows.
Kvarteret Lojo är uppkallat efter Liding: The Lojo block is named after Lidingö’s twin town Lohja (Lojo in Swedish) in Finland. Its 24 houses have facades of brick and wood panelling in red or yellow – one colour per terrace – and white balconies. They sit carefully placed in the rocky, pine-covered terrain.
Kvarteret Loket har fått namn efter Atla: The Loket block – ‘the Locomotive’ – takes its name from the Atlas area, where AB Atlas made locomotives among other things. The neighbouring blocks are called Lokstallet, Tendern and Kolven (the engine shed, the tender and the piston). On the porcelain side, they’re called Fajansen, Leran and Terrakottan instead – faience, clay and terracotta.
Kvarteret Malmgården vid platsens västra: The Malmgården block on the western side of the square consists of two five-storey buildings from 1914, designed by Oscar W Nilsson. With their reddish-brown brick, steep tiled roofs and small-paned windows, they're a fine example of the National Romantic style.
Kvarteret Plankan var länge ett skräpigt: For years the Plankan block was a scruffy area of little workshops in sheds. In 1964–68 a single continuous building designed by Lars Bryde was put up, filling the entire block. The same architect designed the buildings in Drakenberg opposite.
Kvarteret Rosteriet har fått namn efter: The Rosteriet block – ‘the Roastery’ – is named after a German firm that roasted coffee substitute here from 1913 to 1920. Pharmacia then made medicines on the site, and in the 1950s and 60s AB Atomenergi produced fuel rods here for Swedish research reactors. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill is Brännkyrka's old parish hall from the 1920s, which since 2003 has been home to Nordic Music, an upper secondary school.
Kvarteret Sörgården öster om Spånga kyrk: The Sörgården block east of Spånga Church is Tensta's only original area of small houses. Its 76 terraced houses from 1969–1970 were built by the residents themselves, with pale render and red timber cladding.
Kvarteret heter Klamparen efter en gamma: The block is called Klamparen after an old trade: a foreman who sorted timber at a lumber yard. In the second half of the 19th century there were large lumber yards here.
Kvarterets praktfullaste hus är Villa Ol: The grandest house in the block is Villa Oldenburg from 1909–1910, designed by town planner Per Olof Hallman for the notary public Uno Oldenburg. Look for his initials on the cartouche in the gable facing Lejonvägen.
Kvastekulla griftegård, en bit härifrån,: Kvastekulla cemetery, not far from here, was designed by the Finnish architects Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander, who won a Nordic architecture competition. Their idea was to keep the beautiful landscape intact and disturb nature as little as possible. Planning began in 1952, the cemetery opened in 1959, and the chapel followed four years later.
Kvibergs kaserner var militärförläggning: The Kviberg barracks were an army base from 1895 to 1994. Today they're listed buildings with a restaurant, museum and market. They're also home to the Sports Museum, Idrottsmuseet, founded in 1983, which has had two Olympic medals among its exhibits. Just to the north is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the largest multi-sports venue in the Nordic countries, with an indoor ski track 1.2 kilometres long.
Kvibergs marknad håller till i det gamla: Kvibergs marknad, the Kviberg market, is held in the old horse stables of the artillery regiment. Every weekend 10,000–15,000 visitors browse 160 stalls for antiques, curios and odds and ends. A little further away is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the biggest multi-sport venue in the Nordic countries, with a full-size football pitch and a 1.2-kilometre indoor ski track.
Kvibergs museum visade bland annat artil: Kviberg Museum displayed artillery, horse-drawn equipment and uniforms, among other things. It closed on 9 April 2013 because of the high rent, and at a ceremony the museum’s colours were handed over to the Air Defence Regiment.
Kvibergsnäs landeri: Kvibergsnäs landeri, a historic country estate
Kville saluhall ritades av Gustav Appell: Kville market hall was designed by Gustav Appell Arkitektkontor. In 2014 it won the Yimby Prize and the award for Gothenburg's best building of the year, and it was nominated for the EU Prize for Contemporary Architecture.

Kville market hall was designed by Gustav Appell Arkitektkontor. In 2014 it won both the Yimby Prize and the award for Gothenburg's best building of the year. It was also nominated for the EU Prize for Contemporary Architecture.
Kvilletorget fick sitt namn redan 1922 o: Kvilletorget was named as long ago as 1922 and lies close to the Kvillebäcken canal. The Salvation Army has premises on the square, and Brämaregården Church and the Gothenburg Mosque are both just round the corner.
Kynäsberget, ett par hundra meter bort,: A couple of hundred metres away is Kynäsberget, a large expanse of forest and rock of national interest for outdoor recreation. Further south, in Lake Trehörningen, lies Storholmen, which was originally an island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots for summer cottages, mostly sold to working people from Stockholm, and the island was linked to the mainland by a footbridge. Today most of it is forest and shoreline that everyone is free to enjoy.
Kyrka och äldreboende i ett: Church and care home in one
Kyrka ritad av en slottsarkitekt: A church by a palace architect
Kyrkallén fick sin form på 1750-talet, n: Kyrkallén, the Church Avenue, took shape in the 1750s, when the Chinese Pavilion was built: a dead-straight avenue of lime trees some 1,800 metres long. Both Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz and Fredrik Magnus Piper later drew up grand parks around the avenue, but neither plan was carried out.
Kyrkan bakom bostadshuset: The church behind the apartment block
Kyrkan bakom ett höghus: A church behind a block of flats
Kyrkan bestod av ett långhus med ett rak: The church consisted of a nave with a square-ended chancel. Excavations uncovered finely worked, squared ashlar granite in the lowest courses of the walls – a find considered unique in Västergötland.
Kyrkan brann under gudstjänsten: The church that burned during a service
Kyrkan byggdes 1972 för Svenska kyrkan o: The church was built in 1972 for the Church of Sweden and was called Vårfrukyrkan, Our Lady's Church. Fittingly, it was consecrated on Lady Day, 19 March. The Church of Sweden stopped using it in 2007, and in 2009 it was reconsecrated as a Serbian Orthodox church.
Kyrkan byggdes 1974 av Svenska Missionsf: The church was built in 1974 by the Mission Covenant Church of Sweden and was originally called Tomaskyrkan, St Thomas’s Church. In 2011 the Church of Sweden and the Uniting Church in Sweden formed a joint church here, and it was renamed Mariakyrkan, St Mary’s Church.
Kyrkan byggdes på privat initiativ med i: The church was a private initiative, built with donated funds in 1920–1921, and the first service was held on 19 June 1921. At first the chapel was run by volunteers, until it was handed over to Säve parish in 1928.
Kyrkan byggdes under förra hälften eller: The church was built in the first half or middle of the 12th century, with a nave and a square-ended chancel. Excavations revealed finely worked, squared ashlar blocks of greystone in the lower walls – something considered completely unique in Västergötland.
Kyrkan byggdes under första halvan av 11: The church was built in the first half of the 1100s, and the memorial stone calls the ruin Gothenburg's oldest Christian monument. It was excavated and restored in 1925.
Kyrkan där prästgården stod: A church where the vicarage stood
Kyrkan hamnade på stadens lägsta punkt,: The cathedral ended up on the lowest point in the city, which had to be raised with at least two metres of fill. Bedrock lies about 30 metres down. A proposal to build between the Otterhällorna rocks was dropped, partly because the site was thought too out of the way.
Kyrkan i logens ställe: A church in place of a barn
Kyrkan i slutet av Värmlandsgatan bär ku: The church at the end of Värmlandsgatan carries King Oscar II's full name, and the king himself came to visit in 1898 and signed the guestbook. Round the corner runs Nordhemsgatan, with the Briggen food hall. The area is also home to SS Manhem, Gothenburg's biggest chess club, with more than 400 members – one of the top clubs in Sweden.
Kyrkan i spårvagnens vändslinga: A church in the tram loop
Kyrkan invigdes den 19 december 1970. På: The church was consecrated on 19 December 1970. On the chancel wall hangs the altarpiece Varde ljus (Let There Be Light) from 1986: 35 gleaming silver aluminium reliefs covering a full 40 square metres, by the sculptor Bertil Berggren Askenström. The pulpit is built of brick.
Kyrkan kallades länge Sankt Halvards kyr: For a long time the church was known as St Halvard's. Halvard, patron saint of seafarers, was a merchant from Drammen who drowned trying to save a woman. He was also the patron saint of Oslo Cathedral, under which Ytterby fell at the time.
Kyrkan med de två tornen här bredvid är: The church with the twin towers right beside us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. Keep watching now, because we'll soon be heading up onto Västerbron, the bridge with one of the best views in Stockholm.
Kyrkan med prinsen bland gästerna: A church with a prince among the guests
Kyrkan nämns första gången 1388, när bis: The church is first mentioned in 1388, when Bishop Eystein came on a visitation. The fifteen oak roof trusses over the nave are the only known medieval ones to survive in Bohuslän, and may be as old as the church itself.
Kyrkan placerades högt uppe på ett berg: The church was placed high on a rocky hill in Aspudden, with views over Trekanten lake, Gröndal and the inner city. That view was cut short when the Essingeleden motorway was built in the 1960s.
The church was set high on a hill beside the old winter road, with views over Trekanten, Gröndal and the inner city. The view was cut short when the Essingeleden motorway was built in the 1960s.
Kyrkan på prästgårdens plats: A church where the vicarage stood
Kyrkan på prästgårdens tomt: A church on the vicarage plot
Kyrkan ritades av Hans Wieland i mörkröt: Designed by Hans Wieland in dark red brick, the church is 15 metres long, 15 metres wide and 15 metres high. A band of windows runs all the way round just beneath the flat roof.
Kyrkan ritades av Helena Tallius Myhrman: Designed by Helena Tallius Myhrman, the church has a square plan with curving lines and sharp, drawn-out corners. On its turf roof sits an almond-shaped lantern that lets in light from the south. Bishop Eva Brunne consecrated the church on 5 December 2010.
Kyrkan ritades av Sidney White och invig: The church was designed by Sidney White and consecrated in 1973, in the same style as the rest of the 1970s centre. The square worship space had no separate chancel, and in front of the entrance stood a bell tower shaped like a cube on slender legs.

The church was designed by Sidney White and consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent 1973. In front of the entrance stands a free-standing bell tower clad in brown and white panelling – a cube perched on slender legs.

Designed by Sidney White, the church was consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent 1973. The worship space was square with no separate chancel, and in front of the entrance stood a cube-shaped bell tower on slender legs.
Kyrkan ritades av arkitekten Theodor Wåh: The church was designed by architect Theodor Wåhlin in the National Romantic style. Hamburgsund Chapel and Nösund Chapel were built to almost identical plans. Its tall, pointed tower is clad in copper and topped with a gilded cross.
Kyrkan som revs: The church that was torn down
The church stands on an old vicarage plot. The first vicarage was built early in the 19th century and paid for by the Riksbank, Sweden’s central bank, which owned the paper mill. People wanted a chapel in Tumba as early as the 1920s, but the Second World War, among other things, pushed the plans back.
Kyrkan tog vändslingans plats: The church took the turning loop's place
Kyrkan visade sig vara svårt mögelskadad: The church turned out to be badly damaged by mould and has been abandoned. The plan is to demolish it and build a care home with a church in the same building, ready in 2029. In the meantime, services and activities carry on in temporary buildings next door.
Kyrkan är byggd i brunt tegel mitt i Fle: Designed by Gunnar Cedervall, the church is built of brown brick in the heart of Flemingsberg centre. The base of its silver communion chalice has the same shape as the free-standing bell tower outside the main entrance.
Kyrkan är byggd i trä på betonggrund run: The church is built of wood on a concrete base around an atrium courtyard. A large dark cross adorns the pale façade, and the walls of the nave are partly limewashed, grey-toned brick.
Kyrkan är uppförd i gjuten naturbetong o: Designed by the architect Johan Tuvert, the church is built of cast, unfinished concrete. Daylight enters through four low bands of windows in the roof. Inside, the church keeps a fragment of the relics of Saint Nektarios of Aegina.
Kyrkans dopfunt från 1200-talet gjordes: The church's 13th-century font was made by the font master Thorkillus. The original is kept at the Gothenburg City Museum, and a newly carved stone copy has taken its place.
Kyrkans långhus bärs av femton takstolar: The nave is held up by fifteen oak roof trusses – the only medieval ones known to survive in Bohuslän. They may be as old as the church itself, which was probably built sometime between the late 1100s and the mid-1200s.
Kyrkans trätak målades 1710 av Erik Erik: The church's wooden ceiling was painted in 1710 by Erik Eriksson Grijs – his last known church painting. It shows the name of God in Hebrew letters, the Transfiguration of Jesus and the Last Judgement, and the paintings seem never to have been painted over.
Kyrkans votivskepp från 1600-talet är un: The church's 17th-century votive ship is unique because it has a crew on board. The trumpeting angel in the chancel dates from the same century.
Kyrkans äldsta föremål är dopfunten från: The church's oldest object is the font from the medieval church, carved in soapstone some time after 1250. Its original base is missing, so the current one was made in 1934. A memorial stone in the churchyard marks where the medieval chancel stood.
Kyrkbytorget fick sitt namn 1948. Husen: Kyrkbytorget got its name in 1948. The buildings went up in 1955–1956 to designs by Tuvert Arkitektkontor, and in 2002 a courtyard street was added to link the properties around the square.
Kyrkbytorgets hus byggdes i mitten av 19: The buildings around Kyrkbytorget square went up in the mid-1950s, and the Roxy cinema here showed films from 1956 to 1965. The library opened the same autumn as the cinema, in November 1956, and much of its 1950s interior was kept when it was renovated for its 60th anniversary. Nearby runs the Lundby Tunnel, which at 2,060 metres is one of Sweden's longer road tunnels.
Kyrkeby och Nereby är ett gott exempel p: Kyrkeby and Nereby are a good example of how statisticians keep redrawing the map. Before 2015, there was a small settlement here officially called Nereby and Sjöhed. When the boundaries were redrawn, a larger built-up area was marked out instead and named Kyrkeby and Nereby. A little way off is the church village of Kyrkeby, with Harestad Church.
Kyrkklockan, som väger 300 kilo, skänkte: The 300-kilo church bell was donated by a private individual in 1926. The church has two fonts; the newer one, from 1966, was made in clay by Märta Taube-Ivarson, with reliefs of biblical scenes.
Kyrkklockorna skänktes 1882 och göts vid: The church bells were donated in 1882 and cast at the Götaverken works. The great bell weighs 2,367 kilos, and the 49-metre tower is topped by a three-metre cross of gilded copper.
Kyrkogården gjordes i ordning på 1830-ta: The churchyard was laid out in the 1830s, but the first burial didn't take place until 1855, when Hanna Nordwall from Lunda was laid to rest. Her gravestone is still there.
Kyrkogården har medeltida ursprung. Här: The churchyard dates back to the Middle Ages. The medieval old church of Västra Frölunda stood here until it was demolished in the 1860s.
Kyrkogården kom till när Karl XIV Johan: The cemetery came about when King Karl XIV Johan made Ulriksdal Palace available in 1822 as a home for veterans of the wars of 1788–1814. Around 200 of them were buried here. The memorial from 1824 reads: "H H (Here rest) invalids from the wars of the years 1788–1814."
Kyrkogården som bytte namn: The cemetery that changed its name
Kyrkogården utvidgades söderut under 192: The churchyard was extended southwards in the 1920s and 1940s, and most recently in 1987. Today it holds 1,247 graves across 1.5 hectares.
Kyrkoruinen kallas Göteborgs äldsta kris: The church ruin is called Gothenburg's oldest Christian monument and dates from the 12th century. In 1528 King Gustav Vasa ordered the church demolished, because it stood so close to the town that enemies could make use of it in wartime. Its stones went into building the church in Nya Lödöse instead.
Kyrkorummet har ett platt trätak med tre: The nave has a flat wooden ceiling with three cross beams. Filip Månsson's decorative paintings in grey, blue and red create the illusion of beams running lengthwise too. The same artist decorated the small apse of the chancel.
Kyrkorummet är ljust med grå toner och h: The church interior is light, in grey tones, with high-set windows. On the chancel wall hangs a cross with a Christ monogram in fused art glass. The space seats 200.
Kyrksal i femtio år: A church hall for fifty years
Kyrkstolar av PET-flaskor: Church chairs made from plastic bottles
Kyrktuppen i förgylld aluminium formgavs: The gilded aluminium weathercock was designed by the sculptor Arne Jones. It was voted Sweden's Church Weathercock of the Year in 1997 and has become Högdalen's emblem.
Kyrkvaktmästaren blev lärare: The church caretaker became the teacher
Kyrkvägen 16 byggdes 1922 av fjärdingsma: Kyrkvägen 16 was built in 1922 by the parish constable John Lif. He became well known as the local policeman, as a writer for Järfälla-Bygden and for his many photographs of the parish.
Källan vid stranden tog in saltvatten, s: The spring on the shore let in salt water, so a new well was drilled about 80 metres further up. The well house's doorway came from the 18th-century tavern Källaren Druvan in Gamla stan.
Källarmästaren med flera krogar: The cellar master with several taverns
Källö, officiellt Stora Källö, har fått: Källö, officially Stora Källö, is named after a pothole on the island – a ‘giant's kettle’ worn into the rock. Islanders once made their living from fishing and farming, and the oldest houses date from the 1700s. In 1932 Gothenburg's motorboat club bought land here and built a jetty, a dance floor and a kiosk. Today there are around 30 summer cottages on the island.
Kälvesta gravhögar är Stockholms kommuns: The Kälvesta burial mounds form the largest burial ground in Stockholm municipality, with around 145 ancient remains: mounds, about a hundred round stone settings, three-pointed settings and three ship-shaped stone settings.
Kälvesta kan kallas ett ”horisontellt” m: Kälvesta could be called a “horizontal” Million Programme estate – part of Sweden's big 1965–1975 housing drive – with around 2,000 single-family homes. The architects Höjer & Ljungqvist helped plan its terraced and linked houses, and building went on from 1966 to the mid-1970s.
Kälvesta kvarn kallas också Lilla Stampa: Kälvesta mill is also known as Lilla Stampan and Lunda mill. In 1884 it was moved from Observatoriegatan to Lunda, and in 1892 on to its present spot on Skestavägen in Solhem.
Kälvesta kvarn är en stolpkvarn. Det bet: Kälvesta windmill is a post mill, which means the entire mill building is turned to face into the wind.
Kälvestas radhus och villor har en helt: Kälvesta, with its terraced houses and villas, has a very different neighbour to the north-east: Lunda, a district taken up mostly by a large business and industrial estate just south of Hjulsta and west of Spånga. Two very different worlds, then, at a comfortable distance from each other – a good example of how varied Västerort, Stockholm's western suburbs, can be.
Käppalaställningen började byggas 1939 o: Work on the Käppala battery began in 1939. Its 75-millimetre anti-aircraft guns were among the most powerful around Stockholm. Today a gun donated by Bofors is on display here, and all the emplacements survive intact.
Kärleksstigen vid Isbladskärret: Kärleksstigen, the Lovers' Path, by Isbladskärret
Kärleksstigen är bara cirka 390 meter lå: Kärleksstigen, the Love Path, is only about 390 metres long, and not everyone liked it. The columnist Cecilia Hagen called the idea "utterly daft" and wondered whether WWF perhaps saw royals as an endangered species.
Kärna bokskog ligger nära, ett naturrese: Kärna beech forest is close by: a nature reserve of about 18 hectares, created in 2008 and managed by the West Coast Foundation. The rare wood fescue grass grows among the beeches, along with several red-listed lichens. Parts of the reserve have been made accessible, so the forest isn't just for seasoned hikers.
Kärnan i Flygtekniska försöksanstaltens: Wind-tunnel testing was at the heart of the Aeronautical Research Institute's work and was used extensively when Swedish aircraft were being designed. The first tunnel was built in 1940. Supersonic tunnels followed in time, and in 1960 the first hypersonic tunnel came into use.
Kärra hörde till Säve socken, som tillhö: Kärra was part of Säve parish, which belonged to Norway until 1658. The area was ravaged by many wars, and Orrekulla redoubt was built here in the late 1600s. It was strengthened in 1719 but then left to decay.
Kärra kyrka alldeles intill hette faktis: Kärra church, right next to us, was actually known as Kärra chapel right up until 2001. North of the church is a parish hall from 1978. And Kärra was once a place of justice: from 1824 to 1887 the district court for the Askim area held its sessions here.
Kärrdal hör till Östra Sjöberg, en kommu: Kärrdal is part of Östra Sjöberg, a district tucked between Edsviken bay, Lake Rösjön and the Rinkeby forest. Further on, on the eastern shore of Edsviken, is Bergendals herrgård, Bergendal Manor. The site is known from the 1650s, when the croft of Snickartorpet stood here, and the grand manor house was built in 1913 at the initiative of landowner Ragnar Liljenroth. Today it's a hotel and conference venue. Along the same road is Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Kärringstan är inget officiellt namn, me: Kärringstan – roughly 'Old Wives' Town' – isn't an official name, but this villa area has earned it. The streets are named after famous women, and the blocks have names like Baderskan, Barnjungfrun, Kallskänkan and Tvätterskan: the Bath Attendant, the Nursemaid, the Cold-Kitchen Maid and the Washerwoman. So the Barnmorskan block, the Midwife, fits right in – its terraced houses won Stockholm's Building of the Year award in 2011. Just around the corner is Modellvillan 21, which took the same title in 2017.
Kåhög är ett litet villasamhälle vid Säv: Kåhög is a small village of houses on the Säveån river, with the Western Main Line railway to the south. At the bridge in Kåhög begins the Jonsereds strömmar nature reserve, the Jonsered Rapids, which follows the Säveån valley all the way to Lake Aspen. With a bit of luck you might spot kingfishers and dippers.
Kåkstaden utan vatten och vägar: The shanty town without water or roads
Kållered ligger precis vid gränsen till: Kållered lies right on the border with the province of Halland. It used to be farming country, but today western Kållered is dominated by hypermarkets. A short distance away is Kållered station – the first station here opened back in 1891 – and the area also has the Shopping Park Kållered retail park.
Kållered ligger vid gränsen mot Halland: Kållered sits on the border with the province of Halland and was once farming country. Today it has big out-of-town stores such as IKEA, a small hotel and a golf course beside the Torrekulla nature reserve. Not far from here is Kållered Church, the oldest building in Mölndal municipality.
Kållered var en gång lantbruksbygd, men: Kållered was once farming country, but today western Kållered is all about big-box retail. Shopping Park Kållered is right here, and nearby was EkenCenter, a shopping centre from 1990 with about 25 shops. The competition proved too tough, the building was demolished in 2013, and yet another retail building went up in its place.
Kållereds socken hörde till Askims härad: Kållered parish was part of the old Askim district and existed long before any motorways were built through here. Its parish church, Kållered Church, stands on a hill in the village and is in fact the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. This area was also once home to the EkenCenter shopping centre, which was demolished in 2013.
Kållereds station har haft två liv. Den: Kållered station has had two lives. The first station opened in 1891 but closed in 1972. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka came back, a new station opened on 17 August 1992, and in the rush hour there are now trains every fifteen minutes in each direction.
Kårhuset ritades i funkisstil av Paul He: The student union building was designed in functionalist style by Paul Hedqvist, and Prince Eugen contributed decorations to the interiors. From 1976 to 1988 it housed the music venue Glädjehuset, and after the student union moved out, the building was converted for the Stockholm School of Economics.
Kölnan från 1763 är ett av bruksområdets: The kiln house from 1763 is one of the oldest buildings on the site, built eight years after the works opened in 1755. The fire station from 1926 served the works and now houses an exhibition on fire safety, complete with a fire engine from the 1940s.
Köpcentret Allum har ett namn från forns: The Allum shopping centre has an Old Swedish name: it's the dative form of ‘alla’, all, and means roughly ‘for everyone’. It opened in 2006 and spans the E20 motorway with shops and a walkway. Not far away, Partille herrgård – the manor house locals call Slottet, the Castle – sits on a hill overlooking the Säveån river valley. It has been listed since 1995.
Köpcentret Allum, alldeles intill, har e: The Allum shopping centre, right beside us, has a name with a story. Allum, or allom, is an Old Swedish dative form of 'all', meaning something like 'for everyone'. Work began in September 2004, and it opened in April 2006. A building with shops and a passageway spans the E20 motorway, linking the northern and southern halves.
Köpcentret Stinsen invigdes 1995 av Ingv: The Stinsen shopping centre was opened in 1995 by the TV presenter Ingvar Oldsberg, in a former car showroom where Mercedes-Benz cars used to be sold. One reminder of those days remains: the two big car lifts are still in use, now as goods lifts. The centre was extended in stages and reopened in 2009.
Köpcentret här hette Mörby Centrum ända: The shopping centre here was called Mörby Centrum until May 2026, when it was renamed Danderyds Centrum – though the metro station in the northern part of the building kept the old name. It opened on 29 January 1978. Not far off is Villa Markelius, which the architect Sven Markelius designed in 1945 for himself and his family. And down by Edsviken bay stands Berzelii ek, Berzelius' Oak, today what's known as an oak ruin.
Köpmannen Erik Larsson planterade två li: The merchant Erik Larsson planted two lime trees at Malmvik in 1618. When he was ennobled in 1631, he took the name von der Linde – 'of the lime tree' – after the farm and its trees. One of the limes survived until 1999, when it blew down in a November storm.
Köpmannen Robert Ditzinger köpte Långsjö: The merchant Robert Ditzinger bought Långsjö farm in 1881, and the following year he built two identical, mirror-image manor-style houses for his two sons. The style was inspired by the decorative timber architecture of the day, typical of wealthy Stockholmers' summer villas. Both houses still stand.
Köpmannen Robert Ditzinger köpte gården: The merchant Robert Ditzinger bought the farm in 1881, and the following year he had two identical, mirror-image manor-style houses built for his two sons. They're in the wooden panelled style typical of summer villas outside the city, and both are still standing.
Köpt för silver och två oxar: Bought for silver and two oxen
Körkarlen kom först, men sist: The Phantom Carriage came first – and last
Körsbärsträden kom på 90-talet: The cherry trees came in the 90s
L.M. Ericsson testade ny teknik på gårde: L.M. Ericsson tried out new technology at the estate. Hågelby had its own power station and was self-sufficient in electricity into the 1930s. There was also an apiary for pollination and honey, and a water tower with a viewing platform on the hill.
Ladan som blev dansställe: The barn that became a dance hall
Landala kapell, ritat av Carl Fahlström,: Landala Chapel, designed by Carl Fahlström, was consecrated right here on 11 October 1885. In 1919 the little wooden church was physically moved closer to what became Chalmers. The tower burnt in 1960 but was rebuilt.
Landshövdingehus i kvarteren runt omkrin: Landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses – in the blocks around
Landshövdingehusen i kvarteret Renen, lä: The landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses – in the Renen block, along the north-west side of the square, were due to be demolished in the 1970s. After widespread protests they were sold instead and renovated in the 1980s.
Landsnoravägen börjar vid Edsbacka Wärds: Landsnoravägen starts at Edsbacka Wärdshus, an inn founded in 1626. At Landsnora mill the road bends sharply and squeezes between the mill building and the miller's cottage – a passage so narrow that it's controlled by traffic lights.
Landstingshus blev Hotel Gio: From county offices to Hotel Gio
Landstingshuset, där Region Stockholms p: Landstingshuset, where Region Stockholm's politicians meet today, spent more than 150 years as a military hospital, Garnisonssjukhuset, from 1811 to 1969. Next to it stands Graverska huset, built in 1754 as a home for the tanner Jacob Graver. And for food lovers: at Bergsgatan 33, the chef Mathias Dahlgren ran the restaurant Bon Lloc – Catalan for “good place” – which held a Michelin star from 1997 to 2005.
Lasse and Maja have moved to Skogås! Härbreparken, nearby, is a themed play park inspired by Valleby, the fictional little town where the children's detective agency Lasse-Majas detektivbyrå solves its mysteries. The park won Huddinge's architecture award in 2020. In the middle of Skogås centrum, on Yttertorget, stands Mariakyrkan, the parish church of Trångsund-Skogås.
Leden räknades förr som motorväg. På 199: The road used to be classed as a motorway. In the 1990s the city took it over and had the motorway status removed, as it wanted to avoid urban motorways. Plenty of road maps still show it as a motorway, though, and a few green motorway signs remain.
Leden är uppkallad efter FN:s generalsek: The road is named after UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld, who died in a plane crash in Africa in 1961. Shortly after his death the city council decided on the name, at first as Dag Hammarskjölds Väg. The road got its current name in 1968.
Ledningen går förbi Botkyrka kyrka, unde: The pipeline runs past Botkyrka Church, under the strait at Fittja and on through Vårby gård, Segeltorp, Herrängen and Midsommarkransen to Nybohov by Lake Trekanten. With few exceptions it follows Gamla Södertäljevägen, the old Södertälje road.
Leif Dahlén planerade en stor utbyggnad,: Leif Dahlén planned a major expansion, including a 150-metre tower for conference accommodation. But when the dot-com bubble burst and rents doubled, the exhibition centre stopped paying its way.
Lemmingvallen heter fotbollsanläggningen: Lemmingvallen, the Lemming Ground, is the football ground a stone's throw away – a name that makes many people think of little mountain rodents. Here in Utby, in eastern Gothenburg, there's a grass pitch and an artificial pitch for eleven-a-side, plus two gravel pitches for seven-a-side. Utby Church is close by too.
Lerkrogen är ett hus som har flyttat. De: Lerkrogen is a house that has moved. The old tavern first stood near Brännkyrka Church, but it was taken down in 1968 to make way for new roads and the Stockholmsmässan exhibition centre. In 1986 it was put back up near Älvsjö station, and today local heritage societies use it. Next to it is the Älvkvarn stone, an ancient cup-mark stone that has also been moved twice.
Leta upp Fågel Rock med tre ägg vid viad: Find the sculpture Fågel Rock med tre ägg, Bird Rock with Three Eggs, by the viaduct
Leta upp Lidingös kortaste väg vid Lidin: Find Lidingö's shortest road at Lidingsberg
Leta upp betongsnigeln i Snigelparken: Find the concrete snail in Snigelparken
Leta upp runristningen U 52 i berghällen: Track down the U 52 rune carving on the rock slab
Leta upp statyn Ung man: Find the statue Ung man, Young Man
Lettlands ambassad upprättades 1919 men: Latvia's embassy was established in 1919 but closed in 1940. After independence from the Soviet Union it reopened in 1992. Before moving to Odengatan it was at addresses including Birger Jarlsgatan 24, Valhallavägen 74 and Storgatan 38.
Lexby var landsbygd ända tills radhusen: Lexby was open countryside right up until the terraced houses arrived in the 1950s, followed by the Vintergäcken estate in the late 1960s. The actor and director Sissela Kyle grew up here and writes about it in her memoir. Partille IF and the rugby club Spartacus both play their home games in Lexby, and a little further away is Partille Arena.
Lidingö Arena har långa fönsterband med: Lidingö Arena has long ribbons of windows with red-painted metal sun shades, and the red is echoed in the reddish-brown brick and the sheet-metal details. The building has an eight-storey section to the west and a lower, three-storey section to the east.
Lidingö centrum, kommunens största centr: Lidingö Centre, the island's biggest shopping area, opened in 1995 and combines shops with owner-occupied flats. Next door is Lidingö Town Hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson and given the blue rating for its high architectural and historical value. The Grand cinema, which opened in autumn 1993, is the only cinema in the whole municipality.
Lidingö friförsamling bildades 1888 och: Lidingö's free church congregation was founded in 1888 and in 1895 got its first mission house, Emanuelsberg, paid for with collected donations. Ansgarskyrkan was its third church. The architect Janne Feldt designed more than 50 churches, and this was one of his last.
Lidingö har bara tre vattentorn, och ett: Lidingö has just three water towers, and one of them stands a short walk from here, at the end of Tallbergsvägen. Käppala water tower is sometimes called Brevik water tower, even though it's actually in western Käppala. The area also has Villa Brevik from 1920, which for many years hosted HSB's in-house training courses.
Lidingö har en lång radhustradition. De: Lidingö has a long tradition of terraced housing. The Canada Houses at Bo, built in 1908–1909, are counted among the very first terraced houses in Sweden.
Lidingö villastad byggde inte bara villo: Lidingö villastad built not just villas but also "linked single-family houses", an early kind of terraced house – making Lidingö the first place in Sweden with terraced housing. The oldest are in the Canada block, from 1907–1908.
Lidingöbanan går över Lidingöbron, länge: The Lidingöbanan line crosses Lidingöbron, for many years the only road link to the island.
Lidingöbanan och båten hem: The Lidingö line and the boat home
Lidingövallen började anläggas 1936. Eft: Work on Lidingövallen began in 1936. After a major rebuild, the "new Lidingövallen" opened on 11 September 2021, and the running track was extended to 400 metres from the previous 369.
Liljeholmens station låg exakt mitt emel: Liljeholmen station sat exactly halfway between Älvsjö and Stockholm Central, four kilometres in each direction. The railway embankment across Liljeholmsviken bay was 270 metres long and only three metres above the water.
Lilla Bommen och Göteborgsoperan: Lilla Bommen and the Gothenburg Opera
Lilla Ursvik har en oväntad industrihist: Lilla Ursvik has a surprising industrial past. In 1906 the brothers Alexander and Patrick Graham founded their lift company, Graham Brothers, here, and from 1929 it made neon signs as well. A new factory went up in 1937. Lifts were still being made here until the late 1970s, by which time the Finnish company Kone had taken over.
Lilla Varholmen är porten till Öckeröarn: Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. It's linked to Hisingen by a bridge, and from here the car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality on two routes, the Björkö ferry and the Hönö ferry. The Björkö crossing is only about 900 metres long and takes roughly five minutes. The island has its own lighthouses too: the leading lights that guide ships in today date from 1927.

Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. A bridge links it to Hisingen, and from here the car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality on both the Björkö and Hönö routes. The Björkö route is only about 900 metres long, and the crossing takes roughly five minutes. The island has lighthouses too: the first light station came as early as 1889.
Lilla Ösbysjön är bara 4,1 meter djup oc: A couple of minutes away, in the middle of the villa area, is Lilla Ösbysjön, a small lake only 4.1 metres deep. Close by is Vendevägen station on Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway. It opened in 1912 as Parkvägen and didn't change its name until 1956. The waiting shelter was designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt.
Lilleby vid havet på Hisingen var länge: Lilleby, by the sea on Hisingen, was pure countryside for a long time and belonged to Björlanda parish until it became part of Gothenburg in 1967. As early as 1846, the farmland here was redistributed in a land reform. Today the housing areas are growing fast. The district covers 1,330 hectares and is also home to Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside holiday colony with its cabins preserved from the 1950s.
Lillstugan byggdes 1919 av slaktare Joha: Lillstugan was built in 1919 by Johansson the butcher for his daughter Margareta, who wanted to open a café. Later on its customers were mostly soldiers, lorry drivers and bikers, and it appears as a bikers' haunt in the 1952 film Farlig kurva ('Dangerous Curve') with Varg-Olle Nygren.
Lillstugan byggdes 1919 åt slaktardotter: Lillstugan was built in 1919 for the butcher's daughter Margareta, who wanted to open a café. Later on its customers were mostly soldiers, lorry drivers and bikers. It appears as a bikers' haunt in the 1952 film Farlig kurva ('Dangerous Curve'), with Varg-Olle Nygren.
Lillstugan byggdes 1919 åt slaktarens do: Lillstugan was built in 1919 for the butcher's daughter Margareta, who wanted to open a café and bakery. Later its customers were mostly soldiers, lorry drivers and bikers, and it appears as a biker hangout in the 1952 film Farlig kurva. In the 1980s it was extended into an inn.
Lillängen har 161 villor, de flesta i tr: Lillängen has 161 villas, most of them timber-clad and one or two storeys high. The plots are small and the houses often stand well forward, close to the road. The road layout and plot divisions survive from the start.
Lillängen nämns första gången 1653 och v: Lillängen is first mentioned in 1653, when it was a grazing and hay meadow belonging to the Järla estate. The villa area was planned in 1937, and the first families moved into their new houses that same autumn. The same year, the area got its own stop on the Saltsjöbanan railway, and the functionalist waiting shelter from 1937 – green with white corners – is still standing today.
Lind och en varnande gravsten: A linden and a warning gravestone
Lindarna som gav ön namn: The lime trees behind the name
Linden på Torslanda kyrkogård är minst 8: The linden tree in Torslanda churchyard is at least 800 years old. Beside it stands the gravestone of the vicar Arfwid Gren, who died in 1799. Its inscription ends: “Touch not this Stone. For Death Dwells within.”
Linden på kyrkogården är minst 800 år ga: The linden tree in the churchyard is at least 800 years old. Beside it stands the 1799 gravestone of the vicar Arfwid Gren, which ends: "Gnag ey de Dödas Ben Förvara Deras Minne. Rör ey vid denna Sten. Ty Döden Bor där inne." – roughly, "Gnaw not the bones of the dead, keep their memory. Touch not this stone, for Death dwells within."
Lindevägen fick sitt namn 1917, och vill: Lindevägen got its name in 1917, and the villa area along it was first known as Nya Enskede, 'New Enskede', or Palmeska förstaden, 'the Palme suburb'. The name Linde comes from a croft, an inn and a coaching station that stood nearby from 1762. Since 2012 the metro station has been decorated with Maria Miesenberger's Ögonblick i rörelse, 'Moments in Motion', with granite-ceramic walls and aluminium sculptures.
Lindholmen nämns första gången 1333, då: Lindholmen is first mentioned in 1333, when King Magnus Eriksson dated a letter at his fortified Lindholmen. The castle on what is now Slottsberget had stood since at least 1250 and was given to Queen Blanka as a morning gift, the bride's present on the day after the wedding. By 1410 it had fallen into such disrepair that no one could live there.
Lindholmen var länge ett av Göteborgs st: For many years Lindholmen was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. Where ships once took shape, you'll now find Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology. From the quay there's a view straight across the river to the city centre.
Lindholmspiren ligger vid den gamla varv: Lindholmspiren is in the old shipyard district of Lindholmen, where ships were built for more than a hundred years. Today it's home to Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology, and from the quay you can look straight across the river to the city centre.
Lindome ligger cirka 15 kilometer söder: Lindome lies about 15 kilometres south of Gothenburg, but still counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. It's the church village of Lindome parish, in the province of Halland, wedged between the E6 motorway and the West Coast Line. A short way off is Lindome station, where commuter trains call and buses have a larger stop.
Lindome socken är stor, hela 81,7 kvadra: Lindome parish is a big one, covering a full 81.7 square kilometres, and it takes in both the town of Hällesåker and Lindome itself, with its parish church. Lindome Church is a short walk from here. The parish used to belong to the province of Halland and the old Fjäre district, but since 1998 it has been part of Västra Götaland County.
Lindome station har varit död och återup: Lindome station has died and come back to life. It opened on 1 September 1888, when the Gothenburg–Halland railway was completed, but passenger trains stopped calling in 1970, and in 1989 the station shut altogether. Then, when commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka started up again, it made a comeback on 17 August 1992. In 2012 it was rebuilt to take longer trains.
Lindome station öppnade redan 1888. Pers: Lindome station first opened as far back as 1888. Passenger services were withdrawn in 1970, and in 1989 the station closed altogether. When commuter trains started running between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka, it reopened on 17 August 1992.
Lindomesnickarnas möbeltorg: Furniture market of the Lindome joiners
Lindvreten var ett torp under Vårby gård: Lindvreten was a croft belonging to Vårby gård, and its name probably means 'the patch of land with the lime trees'. Nearby was the croft of Månskär, whose curious name has nothing to do with the moon. It comes from Måns, one of its first tenants, and kärr, the Swedish word for wetland. This is also where you'll find Södra djursjukhuset, an animal hospital that started out in 1967 with two people working from a villa.
Lindötunneln går genom en klippa på östr: The Lindö tunnel runs 178 metres through a rock outcrop on the east side of Lindö. Before, the road wound through a couple of sharp, narrow bends between Tillflykten and Lindö lada. The new route brought both fewer accidents and shorter queues.
Ling begravdes på udden norr om gården,: Per Henrik Ling, father of Swedish gymnastics, was buried on the headland north of the farm, where a 3.5-metre standing stone bears the inscription Ling 1776–1839. His grandson Alarik Liedbeck, Alfred Nobel's closest collaborator, also lies here.
