Reningsverket i berget: A treatment works inside the rock
Resecentret invigdes den 11 april 2003 o: The travel centre opened on 11 April 2003 and the following year won the Svenska Stadskärnor award for good design. The team behind it included the architect Gert Wingårdh and the artist Mats Theselius.
Reservatet är ett typiskt mellansvenskt: The reserve is a typical central Swedish rift-valley landscape. The hill to the south is covered in pine and spruce forest, while the northern part is flat clay. A map from the 1700s shows that the lower areas were once meadow and pasture.
Restaurang Sturehof har serverat fisk oc: Restaurant Sturehof has been serving fish and seafood since 1897. A stone’s throw away is Sturebadet, a bathhouse opened in 1885. Where East stands today was once the Brända tomten restaurant, which closed in 1987.
Restaurang i 1680-talshus: A restaurant in a house from the 1680s
Restaurangen Gässlingen på Brännkyrkagat: The restaurant Gässlingen on Brännkyrkagatan was started in the early 1970s by a man who collected leaded windows from old houses being torn down, and built them into the interior. Later the kitchen took on an Alsatian flavour.
Restaurangen låg i en villa som byggts s: The restaurant was in a villa built as a show home, to demonstrate what the new garden suburb might look like. After a rebuild in 1895 it had pointed towers with pale green roofs and views over Stora Värtan.
Restaurant Löwenbräu ligger vid Fridhems: Restaurant Löwenbräu has been at Fridhemsplan since 1970, when it moved from Jacobsgatan. The old Draken cinema was also here.
Restauranten var också namnet på en håll: The restaurant also gave its name to a stop on the Djursholm railway, opened in 1890. It only became Djursholms torg in 1968 – and the line closed as soon as 1976. The restaurant building itself was burned down by the fire brigade in 1963.
Rester av bergen finns kvar inne i kvart: Remnants of the old rocky hills survive inside the blocks along Nybrogatan, which is why the buildings are often six storeys high on the street side but only three on the courtyard side. You can see it in the courtyard of Nybrogatan 72, for example.
Rialto hade 496 platser, varav 126 på lä: The Rialto had 496 seats, 126 of them in the balcony. As early as 1922 the owners went bankrupt, and the Norwegian Odd Biörnstad bought the cinema. It became the first in the Ri-Teatrarna chain.
Riddarfjärden är Mälarens östligaste fjä: Riddarfjärden is the easternmost bay of Lake Mälaren, and the border between the provinces of Uppland and Södermanland actually runs right through the middle span of Västerbron bridge. On the Kungsholmen shore, Mälarbadet opened in 1906. At the time it was the biggest and most exclusive indoor bathhouse in Scandinavia, with pools beneath large skylights. Street names around here remember the tanners who once worked in the area – Garvar Lundins gränd, for example, is named after the tannery owner Anders Wilhelm Lundin.
Riddarholmen och utsikten över Riddarfjä: Riddarholmen and the view over Riddarfjärden
Riksantikvarieämbetet kallar Canadakvart: The Swedish National Heritage Board calls the Canada block groundbreaking. Even so, it wasn't until the 1950s that terraced houses really caught on in Sweden. The block has been a listed building since 1981.
Riksdagen beslutade 1905 att garnisonen: In 1905 parliament decided that the garrison should move its exercises from Gärdet to Järvafältet. At its largest the training ground covered 5,000 hectares. At first the soldiers of the Svea Life Guards had to make their way out here all the way from their barracks on Linnégatan in central Stockholm.
Riksdagsmannen och handlanden Johan Jaco: The merchant and member of parliament Johan Jacob Ekman lived in the villa. In 1890 he sold the Kviberg estate to the Crown for 323,000 kronor, and the barracks of the Göta Artillery Regiment were built on the land.
Riksgränsen går genom fabriken: The national border runs through the factory
Ringdahl Leg Optiker har funnits på Flem: Ringdahl Leg Optiker has been at Fleminggatan 36 since 1946. When new owners took over in autumn 2007, they kept both the company name and the well-known signs, which had already been included in the City Museum's survey of neon signs in 1998.
Ringen som aldrig byggdes: The ring that was never built
Rinkeby i Danderyd ska inte förväxlas me: Rinkeby in Danderyd shouldn't be confused with the Rinkeby district in northern Stockholm – this one is an old farm and a housing area. A fragment of a Viking Age runestone, U 132, was once found here, but it vanished without trace in the second half of the 1800s. Nobody knows where it went.
Rinkeby är äldre än många tror. Byn omta: Rinkeby is older than many people think. The village is mentioned as early as 1347, when it was made up of several farms. Modern Rinkeby was built from 1968 onwards as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive of the 1960s and 70s. Rinkebytorget, the square, now has a small shopping centre and Folkets hus, the community centre, and it's a good place to pick up fruit and veg.
Rinkebybocken – stor som en tia: The Rinkeby goat – the size of a coin
Rissne station togs i bruk den 19 august: Rissne station opened on 19 August 1985 and is 10.4 kilometres from Kungsträdgården, the terminus of the blue line. The ticket hall is beneath the square.
Rissne är den enda tunnelbanestationen i: Rissne is the only metro station in Stockholm with its name carved in runes. The name also appears on a runestone in Sigtuna, raised in memory of 'Gunnar's son in Risnö'. In 1640 Rissne gård was bought by Reinhold Goevert Leuhusen, secretary of the Admiralty board. Today the old farm is a restaurant and conference venue.
Ristningen i Törnby är gjord direkt i et: The Törnby inscription is carved straight into an earth-fast boulder of reddish granite. The stone is 1.2 metres high and the runes are 9–10 centimetres tall.
Ristningen på U 101 sitter på stenens pl: The carving on U 101 is on the stone's flat upper surface and covers about 1.85 by 1.50 metres, with runes 7–16 centimetres high. It's one of the Jarlabanke stones and was described by Richard Dybeck in the 1860s.
Ristningen är inte signerad. Runforskare: The carving isn't signed. Even so, the runologist Elias Wessén believed it was probably the work of the famous rune master Fot, since the careful craftsmanship, spelling and rune forms are similar to his other stones.
Ritad för film från start: Designed for film from the start
Ritorp anlades redan på 1600-talet som e: Ritorp goes back to the 1600s, when it was a croft belonging to the village of Nederjärva, just south of the country road to Enköping. Today's farmhouse dates from the 1770s. It's a private home, but Stockholm County Museum calls it irreplaceable. Two thousand years ago this spot was under water: the bay of Fröfjärden linked the Baltic waters of Saltsjön with Lake Mälaren, and the shoreline of Brunnsviken was about ten metres higher than it is today.
Ritorp började som ett torp på 1600-tale: Ritorp started out as a croft in the 17th century, and the current farmhouse from the 1770s is described by Stockholm County Museum as irreplaceable. The buildings around it have charming nicknames: the Tower Villa from 1903, the Majhill house from 1911 and the Horseshoe Stable from 1929, which was moved in 1993. And in the northern part, look out for the houses known as Rödingarna, 'the Red Ones'.
Rivs på Gustav Vasas order: Torn down on Gustav Vasa's orders
Robert Carlsson köpte kvarnen 1924 och d: Robert Carlsson bought the mill in 1924 and ran it and the sawmill into the 1950s. After that everything fell into disrepair until the municipality took over in 1983. The miller's cottage, the millpond and the stone-lined channel are still there.
Robinia på taket av tunneln: Locust trees on the tunnel roof
Roller derby och Näsan i blöt: Roller derby and an outdoor classroom
Rondellen vid Brommaplan är 100 meter i: The roundabout at Brommaplan is 100 metres across, with six streets feeding into it. This is where Drottningholmsvägen turns off south towards Drottningholm and Ekerö, and county road 275 becomes Bergslagsvägen.
Ropsten har blivit större med åren. Sprä: Ropsten has grown over the years. Blasted rock has been dumped into Lilla Värtan ever since 1884, most recently around 2005–2007 for the park-and-ride. On top of that, post-glacial land rise since a painting from 1795 amounts to the sea sitting about a metre lower.
Ropsten har fått sitt namn efter en lite: Ropsten takes its name from a tiny islet off Ropudden, known as Roparstenen, Rope Sten or Roop Sten – the stone where you stood and shouted for the ferry on the other side. The islet was only about 4–6 metres wide above the waterline.
Rosens och Liljans kapell: The chapels of the Rose and the Lily
Roslags Näsby är Roslagsbanans stora väg: Roslags Näsby is the main junction on the Roslagsbanan railway, where the line splits towards Kårsta – formerly Rimbo – and towards Österskär. The station has two island platforms, reached by a footbridge over the tracks. Not far away is Kvarntorpshällen, a rock with a runic inscription discovered in 1943 by the writer Jan Fridegård while he was living in Täby. It contains an unusual word: styvsöner, stepsons.
Roslagsbanan nådde Lahäll 1928, när linj: Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, reached Lahäll in 1928 with the opening of the line from Altorp, and in 1937 it was extended to Näsbypark. Further on, by Näsbyviken bay, is Näsby Castle, today a conference hotel with a restaurant. And to the south, in Djursholm, lies the Svalnäs burial ground, with graves from around 500 to 1000 AD – one of the largest and most impressive in Danderyd.
Roslagsbanan nådde hit 1937, när Stockho: The Roslagsbanan railway arrived in 1937, when the Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar company extended the line from Lahäll, and this is where that branch ends. Näsbypark is known as one of Täby's more exclusive neighbourhoods, with villas and terraced houses close to the water at Stora Värtan bay. Right next to the station is Näsbypark Church, part of Täby parish.
Rud var jordbruksbygd ända tills jordbru: Rud was farming country right up until farming stopped in the 1960s and housing estates sprang up. Grimmered village, first mentioned in 1546, has been preserved with two complete farmsteads, three farmhouses and a few outbuildings.
Rudbecksskolan invigdes den 8 juni 1970: Rudbecksskolan was opened on 8 June 1970 by Ingvar Carlsson, then Minister of Education. The school is named after Reinhold Rudbeck and is Sollentuna's largest workplace.
Rudboda har fått sitt namn efter Rudboda: Rudboda takes its name from Rudboda gård, a farm first mentioned in writing in 1381. The area includes the Lojo block, built in 1970–1973 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive – though the municipality describes it as a smaller-scale, higher-quality version. Out on Bosön there's a student campus from 1998–1999, built to show what the Olympic Village might have looked like had Stockholm won its bid for the 2004 Summer Games. It didn't.

Rudboda is named after Rudboda farm, mentioned in writing as early as 1381. The Lojo block was built between 1970 and 1973 during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, and the municipality calls it an excellent example of the programme's ideas applied on a smaller scale. On Bosön, student flats were built to show what an Olympic village might look like – ahead of the 2004 Summer Games, which Stockholm never got.
Rudboda kyrka från 1972 är en monterbar: Rudboda Church, from 1972, is a prefabricated "travelling church" that can be dismantled. Services stopped in 2009, and in 2021 the municipality decided it should be demolished or partly relocated. On the square next to it stands the fountain sculpture Winged Cube from 1969.
Ruinen visar en enkel kyrka med långhus: The ruin reveals a simple church with a nave and a square-ended chancel. Excavations turned up finely worked, squared fieldstone in the lowest courses of the walls – a find thought to be completely unique in Västergötland. The remains were dug out and restored in 1925.
Runhällarna U 80 och U 81: The rune-carved rock slabs U 80 and U 81
Runhällen U 80 berättar: \"Andvätt och G: The rune-carved rock U 80 says: "Andvätt and Gärdar had these runes carved in memory of their father Sven, and Kättilvi in memory of her husband." The carving and its winding ornament are cut so deep that they're easy to see, even though they haven't been repainted for a long time.
Runhällen U 90 söder om gården har inskr: The runic rock U 90, south of the farm, bears the inscription: "Vilfrid had this rock carved in memory of his brother Tärv, and Munde in memory of his brother-in-law."
Runhällen är inte signerad, men runforsk: The rune-inscribed rock isn't signed, but the runologist Elias Wessén believed it was probably made by the well-known rune master Fot. The careful craftsmanship, the spelling and the rune forms all resemble his other work.
Runorna i berghällen i Skylsta säger: ”S: The runes on the rock face at Skylsta say: "Sven had the runes carved in memory of Torbjörn, his brother." The inscription is 1.7 metres long and the runes are six centimetres high.
Runorna lyder: Helga lät resa stenen eft: The runes read: ‘Helga had the stone raised in memory of Svärting, her husband, and of Östen and Häming, her sons. And Igulfast carved.’ The stone was found on 20 October 1953 during digging for fill.
Runorna på Farstastenen lyder: Tore och: The runes on the Farsta stone read: Tore and Sven had the stone raised for Vinut, their brother, Helga's son. The stone is thought to belong together with the Ågesta stone on the other side of Lake Magelungen.
Runorna på U 89 berättar att Helga och H: The runes on U 89 tell us that Helga and Holmfrid had the stone raised in memory of Holmfast, their father. The runes are 7–9 centimetres high, and the carving is well cut and fairly well preserved.
Runorna på berghällen i Skylsta lyder i: Translated, the runes on the rock face at Skylsta read: ‘Sven had the runes carved in memory of Torbjörn, his brother.’
Runristaren hette Öpir: The rune carver was called Öpir
Runstenen U 121 säger: \"Jobjörn och Sve: Runestone U 121 reads: "Jobjörn and Sven (or Sten) raised the stone in memory of Torfred, Ingetora's husband." It is 1.8 metres tall and originally stood in a burial ground that was cleared when the Hagalund tunnel and Solna station were built.
Runstenen U 122 tecknades av Johannes Bu: Runestone U 122 was drawn by Johannes Bureus in the early 1600s, and even then the top of the stone was missing. The last recorded sighting was in 1763, when the antiquarian Nils Reinhold Brocman noted it on his way to Hälsingland.
Runstenen U 32 är känd från teckningar p: Runestone U 32 is known from drawings made in the 1600s but then disappeared. In the mid-1800s Richard Dybeck found it lying across a drainage ditch, runes facing down. The name Botne on the stone isn't found on any other known runic inscription.
Runstenen U 79 stod från början vid Skes: Runestone U 79 originally stood at Skesta, three kilometres away. The banker Carl Gustaf Cervin had it moved here in the 1860s – reportedly without permission and against the wishes of the people of Skesta. The stone was raised by Gy and Sven in memory of their father Bärsa and carved by Ärnfast.
Runstenen U 88 i Skälby, en bit härifrån: Runestone U 88 in Skälby, not far from here, has had an eventful life. For at least part of the 19th century it served as a doorstep in Lindal, so people walked over the Vikings' words every day. Then it disappeared for a while, until it was found in 1938 at Skälby Farm, lying on a burial mound. Today it stands beside its companion, U 89.
Runstenen i Eneby är delvis skadad, men: The Eneby runestone is partly damaged, but what can be read runs roughly: Asbjörn ... Gunnälv had the stone raised in memory of Åsulv, their father.
Runstenen i Troxhammar bär en kort men g: The runestone at Troxhammar bears a short but moving inscription: "Kjulak had the stone raised for Kvig, his good son." It dates from the Viking Age, and the runes are 5–6 centimetres tall.
Runstenen i Troxhammar säger: Kjulak lät: The runestone at Troxhammar says: “Kjulak had the stone raised in memory of Kvig, his good son.” The runes are 5–6 centimetres tall. The name Kjulak also appears on another runestone, Sö 339.
Runstenen som blev grindstolpe: The runestone that became a gatepost
Runstenen som flyttades i smyg: The runestone moved on the quiet
Runstenen säger: ”Sibbe och Jorun och To: The runestone reads: 'Sibbe and Jorun and Torgun and Ingegärd, the siblings, had this stone raised in memory of Tjarve, their father, and Gudmod in memory of her husband.' The name Tjarve also appears on a runestone in Uttran, only about 3 km away – perhaps the same man.
Runstenen utanför hembygdsmuseet bär ins: The runestone outside the local history museum bears the inscription: Björn and Fulluge had the stone cut ... their. The rest of the text has been lost.
Runstenen utanför museet flyttades hit i: The runestone outside the museum was moved here in October 1988. The inscription says that Björn and Fulluge had the stone carved in memory of someone, but that part of the text is missing.
Runstenen vid hembygdsmuseet bär inskrif: The runestone by the local history museum reads "Björn and Fulluge had the stone carved ... their". The end is damaged, so we don't know who it was raised for.
Runstenen vid slottets infart: The runestone at the palace entrance
Runt 14 000 studenter läser vid Södertör: Around 14,000 students attend Södertörn University, which offers police training and teacher training with an intercultural focus, among other things. Much of the research here is about the Baltic Sea and Eastern Europe, backed by Östersjöstiftelsen, the Foundation for Baltic and East European Studies, which the government set up in 1994. The library is open to everyone, and right next to it is Flemingsberg Park, winner of Huddinge's building award in 2021.
Runt 1900 köpte staden husen för att riv: Around 1900 the city bought up the houses to demolish them under the Lindhagen plan, and Ringvägen was supposed to end here. That it didn't is largely thanks to Anna Lindhagen, daughter of the plan's author Albert Lindhagen, who as early as the 1910s was campaigning to preserve old Stockholm neighbourhoods.
Runt 1950 fanns mer än 100 växthus i sta: Around 1950 there were more than 100 greenhouses in the district. The market gardens were sold off one by one, and the last, Solbackens Handelsträdgård, closed in 2006. Houses now stand on the land.
Runt Järfälla kyrka har runstenar kommit: Runestones have a habit of coming and going around Järfälla Church. In 1728 Olof Celsius the Elder found one inside the church, probably used as a step. It then vanished until seven fragments turned up in 1939. Another stone lay outside the porch door and was already described back then as lost and worn – it's still missing today. Next door is Kyrkbyn, the church village, once known as Järfälla gård.
Runt Rådasjön breder ett naturreservat u: A nature reserve surrounds Lake Rådasjön, with pastures, broadleaf woodland and alder swamp forest teeming with wildlife. The area around Mölnlycke is famous for its masses of wood anemones, which turn the ground white in spring. Also by the lake is Råda säteri, a manor with wings and farm buildings, listed since 1969.
Runt för att slippa hörn: Round, so there were no corners
Runt hörnet ligger kvarteren Kampö och H: Around the corner are the Kampö and Hartsö blocks, terraced houses from the late 1950s that the City Museum has marked green as especially valuable. A short way off rise the offices of Televerket, the old national telecoms agency – the headquarters of Telia Company until 2016. They were designed by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award.
Runt sekelskiftet 1900 byggdes sommarvil: Around the turn of the 20th century summer villas were built here, drawn by the views over Lake Mälaren and the steamboats to Stockholm. At the time a steam-powered sawmill stood by the strait, and on Gällstaö charcoal stacks smouldered to fuel it.
Runt sjön går en 1,8 kilometer lång slin: A 1.8-kilometre loop called Lugna promenaden, the 'calm walk', runs around the lake and is easy going even if you have limited mobility. The lake is 5.6 metres deep at its deepest.
Runt sjön går ”Lugna promenaden”, en 1,8: The "Lugna promenaden", the Easy Walk, circles the lake: a 1.8-kilometre loop that's easy going even if you have limited mobility. There are picnic spots along the way, and you can both swim and fish in the lake.
Runt torget låg en gång flera varuhus: N: Several department stores once stood around the square: Nordiska Kompaniet, Kvickly and Tempo. By 2008 only Åhléns, the former Tempo, was left. In 2000 a link was built between the old NK and Tempo buildings.
Runt torget står vita skivhus på elva vå: The square is ringed by white eleven-storey slab blocks. Tallest of all is Frölunda Specialist Hospital, at 55 metres and 17 floors.
Rutschbanorna som lockade: The slides that drew the crowds
Rya skog är känd för sitt fågelliv, och: Rya Forest is known for its birdlife, and species such as the lesser spotted woodpecker still breed here. In spring 1849 a pair of white storks built a nest in an oak here, and in the second half of the 1800s hobbies are also said to have nested in the woods.
Rylander & Rudolphs främsta produkt var: Rylander & Rudolph's main product was manganese dioxide batteries, made under the Frenchman Georges Leclanché's patent. About half the workers were women, and some ten children in their early teens also worked at the factory.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970 och är hjärtat i: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970 and is the heart of Bergsjön, where the streets are named after space and the universe – Tellusgatan, for instance. On the square is Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, café, studios, an exhibition hall and even a music studio. It offers everything from music and art to crafts and children's events.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970, och gatunamnen: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970, and the streets around it keep up the space theme, with names such as Tellusgatan and Merkuriusgatan. On the square is the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, a music studio, artists' studios and an exhibition hall, offering a mix of concerts, crafts and activities for children.
Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Uni: Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan, Meteorgatan – Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön, the street names are straight out of outer space. Just up the road is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, home to Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the local cultural centre. It has a library, café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, with everything from music and art to events for children.
Rysk empir med stenar i putsen: Russian Empire style with pebbled render
Ryska ikoner i skogsbacken: Russian icons on a wooded hillside
Ryska revolutionen gav företaget en kris: The Russian Revolution plunged the company into a crisis that ended in bankruptcy in 1922. After several mergers and name changes, it's now Volvo Construction Equipment. The old factory buildings are used for trade fairs and events.
Räddat av planerarens egen dotter: Saved by the planner's own daughter
Rävekärr byggdes 1969–1974. Förut gick o: Rävekärr was built between 1969 and 1974. The area used to stop at Alebäcken stream in the south, but the new housing went up on the far side of it too. The first tenants moved in in 1973, and the school and nursery were finished in December 1974.
Rävekärr har fått sitt namn efter hemman: Rävekärr takes its name from the old Rävekärr homestead in Fässberg parish. One of its farms was the Rävekärr vicarage, on the site where Fågelbergskyrkan church stands today. The last vicar moved out in 1978, and the vicarage was demolished in January 1984.
Rådan is first mentioned in 1599 as a croft. It went on to be a farm foreman's residence, a manor, a boarding school in 1890, military quarters in the 1940s and a police academy in 1970. Silverdal farm, for its part, was an inn until 1860 and then a village shop until the late 1950s.
Rådsparken, alldeles i närheten, har båd: Just nearby is Rådsparken, a park with both an animal park and a sports ground, next to Huddinge Church, which has been the parish church since the Middle Ages. A fragment of a runestone is set into the church's outer wall, and just east of the church lay the assembly site of Tomtabergh, mentioned as early as 1433. The church school close by opened in 1914 and was threatened with demolition in the 1950s, but it survived – today the parish choirs rehearse there.
Rågsved är en stadsdel med två ansikten,: Rågsved is a district with two faces, split down the middle by the metro. On one side is the iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre; on the other, the buildings climb up a hill. The station opened in 1959 and is about 8.5 kilometres from Slussen.
Rågsved är känt för sin ikoniska hästsko: Rågsved is known for its iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre, and the metro station was the end of the line when it opened in 1959. On the platform stands the bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Green Bird, by the artist Björn Selder. A little further away in Högdalen is Cyklopen, a self-run cultural centre staffed entirely by volunteers. Its first building was destroyed in 2008 in an arson attack thought to be the work of Nazis, but the association simply built a new one.
Rågsveds station öppnade den 14 november: Rågsved station opened on 14 November 1959 and was the terminus until 1960. From here it's 8.5 kilometres to Slussen.
Råsunda smygöppnade den 18 april 1937 nä: Råsunda had a soft opening on 18 April 1937, when AIK beat Malmö FF 4–0. At the official opening on 17 May, King Gustaf V cut the ribbon before the international against England – which also ended 4–0, but to England.
Råsunda vattentorn, ritat av Sigge Crons: Råsunda water tower, designed by Sigge Cronstedt, opened in 1910 and was taken out of service in the early 1950s. Since 1994 it's been a home – the tower has been converted into flats. On a rocky hill by Näckrosparken, the Water Lily Park, stands Råsunda Church. And on the southern shore of Lake Råstasjön is Råstahällen, Solna's only natural monument, a slab of bedrock where you can see three criss-crossing sets of scratches left by the ice during the last Ice Age.
Råsunda är en av bara två arenor i värld: Råsunda is one of only two stadiums in the world to have staged both the men’s and the women’s World Cup final. Norway won the 1995 women’s final, beating Germany 2–0. The other stadium is the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.

Råsunda is one of just two stadiums in the world to have hosted both the men’s and the women’s World Cup final. In 1958 Brazil beat Sweden 5–2, and in 1995 Norway beat Germany 2–0. The other stadium is the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.
Råsundavägen hette från början Stockholm: Råsundavägen was originally called Stockholmsvägen and was built as an embankment between rocky ridges so the tram line to Råsunda and Sundbyberg could be laid. Most of it was built by Kreuger & Toll, as one of the company's first contracts.
Röda Korsets Högskola: Röda Korsets Högskola, the Swedish Red Cross University
Röda Sten konsthall: Röda Sten konsthall, the art centre
Röda Sten konsthall under Älvsborgsbron: Röda Sten art centre, beneath the Älvsborg Bridge
Röda skolan från 1903 hade åtta lärosala: The Red School from 1903 had eight classrooms: one for each year of the seven-year elementary school, plus a room for cardboard crafts. At first the school was lit by paraffin lamps and heated with iron stoves. Today Örby library occupies part of the ground floor.
Rödakorssystrar till kriget: Red Cross nurses off to war
Rödingarna byggdes som bostäder åt SJ:s: The Röding houses were built for Swedish Railways staff at Ulriksdal station. When two of them were threatened by a new road ramp, Solna decided to move them instead. They then sat propped up on beams beside Ulriksdal golf course until November 2020.
Rödkinda barnhem är en stor rödfärgad tr: Rödkinda children's home is a large red-painted wooden villa with a mansard roof, built in 1916–1917 to designs by Kellgren & Hammarling. It sits on a hill sloping down towards Lake Magelungen. In 1924, eleven children lived here and were taught the ordinary elementary school curriculum.
Röhsska museet för design och konsthantv: Röhsska museet, the museum of design and craft
Rökstenen på stationsväggen: The Rök runestone on the station wall
Rörstrands slott har kvar sin 1600-talsk: Rörstrand Castle has kept its 17th-century character, with smooth rendered facades and black-glazed roof tiles. Inside are some of the Rörstrand factory's finest tiled stoves – and a castle café for a fika, a coffee and cake.
Röset som gav sjön namn: The cairn that named the lake
Rösjön anses ha fått sitt namn efter ett: Rösjön is thought to be named after a cairn (röse) on an island in the southern part of the lake. The cairn marked the boundary between the old districts of Danderyd skeppslag and Sollentuna hundare.
Rösjön är cirka 1 500 meter lång och 300: Rösjön is about 1,500 metres long and 300 metres wide. Its waters are home to perch, pike, roach, bream, tench, burbot, rudd and bleak, among others, and there are crayfish too. The lake drains through the Fjätursbäcken stream into Lake Fjäturen.
Rösjön lake is about 1,500 metres long and 300 metres wide. It's home to perch, pike, roach, silver bream, common bream, tench, burbot, rudd and bleak – and crayfish too.
Rösjön är en avlång sjö, 7,3 meter djup,: Rösjön is a long, narrow lake, 7.3 metres deep. Most of it belongs to Sollentuna, with a smaller part in Danderyd – while Täby, right next door on the eastern side, doesn't get a single metre of shoreline. A little further on, Landsnoravägen runs for about three kilometres past Edsberg Palace and Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Rösträtt och åttatimmarsdag: Votes for all and the eight-hour day
Rött och gult, en färg per länga: Red and yellow, one colour per row
S.A. Hedlund var huvudredaktör för Göteb: S.A. Hedlund was editor-in-chief of Göteborgs Handels- och Sjöfartstidning and a leading cultural figure in the city. Around 1860 he had Slätta damm pond created, and today it's home to many species of birds.
S:t Eriksgatan, kaféer och butiker: S:t Eriksgatan, for cafés and shops
S:t Tomas kyrka murades på Celsings förs: At the suggestion of the architect Peter Celsing, S:t Tomas church was built by trainee bricklayers. This kept costs down and gave the walls a more irregular, lively surface. The façades have no eaves, plinth or drainpipes.
SF lanserade Fontänen som premiärbiograf: SF launched Fontänen as a premiere cinema, screening the same new releases as the cinemas in the city centre. During the 1960s the premieres dwindled, and Fontänen became an ordinary suburban cinema.
SF lämnade Reflexen 1977, och sedan dess: The SF cinema chain left Reflexen in 1977, and since then it has been run by a non-profit cultural association. During the 2006 renovation the old neon sign went back up after many years' absence and received an honourable mention as Sign of the Year. SF's old projectors kept running until 2013.
SIAB levererade sina hus i storelement s: SIAB delivered its houses as large prefabricated panels assembled on site, while Skånska Cementgjuteriet built its houses on the spot. Skånska's areas ended up more varied and better suited to the terrain. Because of state loans, no house could be larger than 140 square metres.
SJ skaffade byggmark genom att fylla ut: The state railways, SJ, created building land by filling in Årstaviken bay with rock blasted from the Nyboda tunnel and from a rocky knoll that was blown away – and that's where Marievik stands today. Next door was Maryvik's felt factory, which made lubricating pads and boiler felt.
SKF började med Wingquist och 15 anställ: SKF started out with Wingquist and 15 employees. By 1909 it already had branches in Copenhagen, Paris and Milan, and warehouses as far away as Melbourne and Yokohama. By 1912 the workforce had reached 1,300.
SKF:s allra första kullagerorder kom frå: SKF's very first ball-bearing order came from ASEA in Västerås and is dated 16 March 1907. Just four years later the company opened its first factory abroad, in Luton, England.
SVT Väst lät folk rösta fram namn. Bastu: Swedish broadcaster SVT Väst let the public vote on names. The sauna became Svettekörka (Svettekôrka in local dialect – roughly 'Sweat Church'). In the vote for the pool, Pöl Harbour won, with Inälvsbadet and Kallhalla coming second and third.
Salems centrala bebyggelse hette förr Sa: The centre of Salem used to be known as Salemstaden. For a long time the area was crofters' land belonging to the Fågelsta farm. One of the crofts, Bergfana, was built in the late 1840s, and the first to move in were Eric Ode – a former soldier who worked on the estate – and his family. When the railway arrived in 1860, Bergfana became one of Salem's four lineman's cottages, where the people who kept watch over the track lived.
Salems kyrka står på en udde söder om Bo: Salem Church stands on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, surrounded by great oaks, limes and birches. The old Södertälje road, Gamla Södertäljevägen, runs right past, and the whole area is rich in ancient remains. Follow the road east and you'll reach St Botvid's Spring, a cold-water spring at the south-eastern tip of the lake. About fifty metres from the spring stands the Söderby runestone.

Salem Church stands on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, framed by big oaks, limes and birches. The old Södertälje road, Gamla Södertäljevägen, runs past the church, and the whole area is rich in ancient remains. Follow the road east and you'll reach Sankt Botvid's spring, a cold spring at the south-eastern tip of Bornsjön. About fifty metres from it stands the old Söderby runestone.
Salen som bär arkitektens namn: The hall named after its architect
Salong för kulturlivet: A salon for the cultural set
Salongen hade kraftig lutning och 375 få: The auditorium had a steep rake and 375 blue-upholstered armchairs, and the screen could show CinemaScope. The curtain was designed by the artist Tor Hörlin and showed the view from his studio at Kornhamnstorg.
Salthandlaren Gustav R. Setterberg byggd: The salt merchant Gustav R. Setterberg built a villa out of old salt barges. It's said to have been the first villa in Arendal, probably from the 1870s, and was later rebuilt by a paediatrician who bought it in 1903.
Salthandlaren Gustav R. Setterbergs vill: The salt merchant Gustav R. Setterberg's villa was built from old salt barges and was probably the first house at Arendal. The neighbouring villa, Rosenborg, appears in Berndt Lindholm's painting Arendal 1879, with a funny little tower that still had a flat roof back then.
Saltsjö-Järla station invigdes 1894 unde: Saltsjö-Järla station opened in 1894 under the old-fashioned name Jerla, and branch lines once ran from here to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works. Today the old industrial buildings by Lake Järlasjön have been reborn as Järla sjö, with around 700 homes, shops and restaurants, and about 1,200 people working there. In 2004 the area won the Urban Environment Council's award for improving the townscape.
The Saltsjöbanan railway station here opened in 1894. While the new Slussen was being built, Henriksdal served as the line's city-end terminus from 2016 until the end of 2022. Large parts of the line have been closed since 2023, and the stretch to Slussen isn't expected to reopen until 2028 at the earliest. Danvikstull was once home to the Klippan summer theatre, where audiences laughed along with John Elfström and Arthur Fischer.
Saltsjöbanans station invigdes 1894, då: The station on the Saltsjöbanan railway opened in 1894, when the name was spelled Jerla. Branch lines ran from here to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works. Here's a fun fact: Anna Book was a pupil at Nacka music school when she sang “ABC” in Melodifestivalen, Sweden's Eurovision selection, in 1986. And from 2030 you'll be able to change to the blue metro line at a new station here.
Saltsjön, Djurgården och Nackareservatet: Saltsjön, Djurgården and the Nacka reserve
Saltsjötunneln är borrad 50 meter under: The Saltsjö tunnel is bored 50 metres beneath the city and measures 3.5 metres across. The tunnel boring machine that dug it was called Ormen Långe, the Long Serpent. Its outlet is in the harbour off Kastellholmen, about 250 metres from the shore.
Samariten öppnade 1890 som Nya barnsjukh: Samariten opened in 1890 as the New Children's Hospital, at a time when people pouring into Stockholm meant cramped housing and the spread of childhood diseases. It closed in 1974 and every building except the administration block was demolished. That building is now a nursery school.
Samma dag som Skarpnäck öppnade 1994 inv: On the same day Skarpnäck station opened in 1994, Bagarmossen's new underground station opened too. Bagarmossen's old station at ground level had closed a few months earlier.
Samma år som arenan öppnade, 2013, spela: In 2013, the year the arena opened, Swedish Television filmed parts of the show Summercamp at Angered Arena and Angeredsvallen.
Sammanlagt har det funnits fyra slussar: There have been four locks here in all: Queen Kristina's lock, Christopher Polhem's lock, Nils Ericson's lock and the Karl Johan lock. The new lock channel is called Victoriaslussen and is expected to open to boats in 2027.
Sandbäck är ingen ny plats. Redan på 155: Sandbäck is no newcomer. As early as the 1550s – more than four hundred years ago – there were two farmsteads here. Today it's in the south-western part of Östra Mölndal, and a little way off is the Pepparred nature reserve, with old pastures and broadleaf trees, protected since 1925.
Sandsborg låg där den gamla vägen mot Da: Sandsborg stood where the old road to Dalarö and the country road to Tyresö parted ways – a fitting spot for an inn. It opened in 1803 in the farm's main house and became a popular, well-known place during the 19th century.
Sandås ligger i Askim, och namnet Askim: Sandås is in Askim – and Askim, by the way, is actually pronounced “Ashim”. The parish dates back to the Middle Ages. To the south, Sandås borders Skintebo, a residential area by the coast that was farmland until the 1970s. It has car-free footpaths, båtmansgårdar – a sort of boatswain's cottage – and, more surprisingly, a copy of the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm.
Sankt Georgios stod klar 1890 i nygotisk: St Georgios was completed in 1890 in the Gothic Revival style, with machine-made red brick, pointed-arch windows and a tall copper-clad spire. The Greek Orthodox congregation added an iconostasis and stone altar, while the organ was removed in the 1970s.
Sankt Olofs kyrka, Täby: Sankt Olofs kyrka, St Olaf's Church, Täby
Sankt Olofs kyrka, en kort bit bort, hör: St Olof's Church, a short way off, belongs to Täby parish. Through neighbouring Hägernäs runs the E18 motorway, completed on the Danderyd–Ullna stretch in 1957, cutting straight through the area. A little further north is Rönninge, which has no built-up areas at all – just the Rönninge by-Skavlöten nature reserve and the Skavlöten outdoor recreation area.
Sankt Pauli kyrka: St Paul's Church, Sankt Pauli kyrka
Sankt Pauli kyrka, delvis i romansk stil: St Paul's Church (Sankt Pauli kyrka), partly in Romanesque style, was consecrated in 1882 and paid for entirely with private money. The hill it stands on is called Höga Lyckan. Its working name was Redbergskyrkan until the city council settled on the name in 1881.
Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka alldeles i: Right next door is the Church of Saint Paul of the Cross, Angered's Catholic parish church. A short walk away stands Alexander Calder's steel sculpture The Three Wings, which spent twelve years on Götaplatsen before it was finally allowed to move to Angered in 1979. Since 2013 it has stood on an open lawn in the town park.
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka, St Sigfrid's Church
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka är en monteringsfär: St Sigfrid's Church is a prefabricated timber building with an octagonal nave, designed by Erik Otto Ulrich. It was due to be torn down once the stone-built Stefanskyrkan was finished in Vasastaden, but was bought for 37,000 kronor to serve the growing industrial district of Liljeholmen.
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka är en riktig flyttf: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka has done some travelling. The red wooden church originally stood in Vasastaden and was moved here in 1904, when it was called Sankt Stefans kapell. Designed to be portable, it looks a lot like the flat-pack timber villas of the period, and it has been a listed building since 1993. Further along Hägerstensvägen is the Aspen cinema – when it opened in 1952, it was the first privately run cinema to open in Stockholm since 1943.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church
Sankta Birgitta kyrka byggdes 1960–1962: Saint Birgitta's Church was built between 1960 and 1962 and consecrated in December 1962. The architect Rolf Bergh designed the church, its bell tower and the parish hall next door. And here in Nockeby, the architect Sven Markelius built his own villa in 1930 – one of the very first houses designed to the new ideals of functionalism.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka byggdes på marken: Sankta Birgitta church was built on the land where the tram's old terminus and turning loop used to be. The loop was no longer needed once modern trams had a driver's cab at each end, so it was removed in 1960 and the Källviken stop took over the name Nockeby.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka i Nockeby står på: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church in Nockeby, stands where the trams used to turn round. This was the old terminus of the number 12, with its turning loop, until work on the church began in November 1960. It was consecrated on 9 December 1962. All around, Nockebyhov is lined with terraced houses from the late 1940s that the City Museum has marked blue for their exceptional cultural and historical value.
Sankta Birgitta kyrkas fristående klockt: The free-standing bell tower of St Birgitta's Church was built for four bells but has only two: Syster Trofast and Broder Barfot, Sister Faithful and Brother Barefoot. The tower is 39 metres tall, with the cross adding another eight, and was meant as a landmark for both land and sea, visible far and wide.
Sanna betyder ungefär sandmark. Här i nä: Sanna means something like 'sandy ground'. Close by is Plaskis – or Älvsborgsdammen, to give it its proper name. In summer, families paddle in 20 to 45 centimetres of water, and when the pond is drained, the skateboarders move in. At the edge is the sculpture Boll, 'Ball': a two-metre blue steel sphere that looks like a giant beach ball.
Sannegårdshamnen invigdes i januari 1914: Sannegårdshamnen, the Sannegården harbour, opened in January 1914, though these days the name usually means the residential area around it. Culture has moved into the old industrial buildings: Backa teater, one of Sweden's leading theatres for children and young people, performs in a converted sheet-metal workshop on Lindholmen. And a stone's throw away is Aftonstjärnan, a cinema and theatre that has been a listed building since 1995.
Satellitstad i Sputniks tid: A satellite town in the Sputnik age
Saxe nöjde sig inte med en sten. Ristnin: Saxe wasn't content with just a stone. The carving at Törnby says he had the stone cut and a bridge built in memory of his mother. The man who carved the runes signed it too: Sven carved.
Scandic Talk Hotel är 19 våningar och 72: Scandic Talk Hotel has 19 storeys and stands 72 metres tall, making it the third-tallest hotel building in Sweden. The tower is made up of two offset volumes, one with screen-printed glass façades and the other clad in boldly textured aluminium panels.
Scandinavium invigdes 1971. Läs om Abba,: Scandinavium opened in 1971. Read about ABBA, Eurovision and Kiss at the arena.
Scenen 24 kvadrat drevs av koreografen G: The stage Scenen 24 kvadrat was run by choreographer Gun Lund and Lars Persson of the company E=mc2 danskonst. On this little stage in Sockerbruket, the old sugar refinery, they welcomed dancers from some twenty countries.
Scheelegatan hette förr Trädgårdsgatan,: Scheelegatan used to be called Trädgårdsgatan, but in 1885 it was renamed after the chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele. On the corner of Fleminggatan and Pipersgatan is Separatorhuset, built around 1900 as the head office of AB Separator – later Alfa Laval – whose factory once filled the whole large site by Barnhusviken bay. The City Museum has now given the building its blue heritage rating.
Schering Rosenhane gjorde Säby till säte: Schering Rosenhane made Säby a manor estate in the 1630s and, in the 1650s, had the Carolean-style main house built that still stands today. The architect may have been Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, but Rosenhane was himself keen on architecture and probably had a big say.
Schmidt lät också bygga en stor kringbyg: Schmidt also had a large barn built around a courtyard, made of timber from Norrland in northern Sweden. Until the Second World War it housed some forty cows. After that, ‘Fittja loge’ became a popular spot for dances and parties for young people from the area and from Stockholm.

Se AGA:s gula optiktorn på nära håll (1: Take a close look at AGA's yellow optics tower (1 min), built in 1943 to make periscopes for submarines, among other things. The area is called Dalénum, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén.

Sedan 1916 visar Tornbergs klocka tiden: Since 1916 Tornberg's clock has been telling the time on Nybroplan – though not always accurately. Trams have stopped here since 1877, apart from a break from 1967 to 1991.
Sedan 1946 har Lundbergs konditori legat: Lundbergs konditori has stood on the same corner of Gröndalsvägen since 1946, with the same name and in the same premises, making it a true fika classic – fika being Sweden's beloved coffee-and-cake break. Up on the Sannadal plateau rise the point blocks of Ljuskronan, Ljussaxen and Lyktan, built between 1958 and 1972 and now a familiar part of Gröndal's skyline. The light-themed block names – the Chandelier, the Candle Snuffer and the Lantern – suit the hilltop nicely.
Sedan 1970 står vattentornet Fornborgsre: Since 1970 the Fornborgsreservoaren water tower has stood right in the middle of the ancient hillfort. Parts of the fort were investigated when it was built, but no objects were found. Up on the plateau there are also a few holiday cottages.
Sedan 1975 är Hågelby en folkpark med ca: Since 1975 Hågelby has been a folkpark – a traditional Swedish people's park – with a café, a 4-H farm, a dance floor and a stage. Hågelbyparken is the only folkpark to have won Folk Park of the Year twice, in 1989 and 2000.
Sedan 1986 drivs Tellus av en ideell kul: Since 1986 Tellus has been run by a non-profit cultural association with around fifty members, who do everything from baking cakes to repairing the film projectors.
Sedan 1998 finns Ekebyhovs Äppelgenbank: Since 1998 the palace has been home to Ekebyhov's apple gene bank. The main building, the park and the building known as the Citadel have been listed since 1970.
Sedan 2005 pryds entréhallen och platsen: Since 2005 the entrance hall and the area facing the bus station have been decorated with Fredrik Landergren's art: inlaid glass mosaics of human heads. The station building is also green-listed by the City Museum.
Sedan 2006 skyddas knappt sex hektar tal: Since 2006, just under six hectares of pine and broadleaf woodland at Malmvik have been protected by a 50-year conservation agreement. Look out for trees with a painted white ring and an N above it – they mark the edge of the area.
Sedan 2016 kan man läsa serieskapande på: Since 2016 you can study comics at Skarpnäck folk high school, now under the name Comics, Illustration and Animation. The school also runs a course in Spanish and development cooperation, held in Barcelona and in South American countries.
Sedan 2019 är Aspen biograf igen och des: Since 2019 Aspen has been a cinema again, as well as a local arts centre. After a thorough renovation it has two screens, a stage and a bistro.
Sedan Citybanan öppnade 2017 använder pe: Since the Citybanan rail tunnel opened in 2017, commuter trains have used the two northern tracks. In the summers of 2018–2020, because of engineering works, Södra station took over from Central Station for eight weeks as the starting point and terminus for long-distance trains heading south.
Sedan den 16 augusti 2015 är Stenpiren e: Since 16 August 2015, Stenpiren has been a transport hub with a terminal building for trams, buses and boats. The new track cut four minutes off the journey from Brunnsparken to Järntorget, and in 2017 the scheme won the Siena Prize for landscape architecture.
Sedan den 18 augusti 2014 är Solna stati: Since 18 August 2014 Solna station has been the terminus of the Tvärbanan light rail's Solna branch. On an ordinary winter weekday about 3,100 people board here. From the northern end of the stop it's about 150 metres to the railway station entrance.
Sedan hösten 2017 byggs torget om under: Since autumn 2017 the square has been redeveloped under the name Selma stad. The plan includes 1,000 new homes, offices, shops and a new district centre with space for culture. A tram line past the square is also planned for the future.
Sedan våren 2009 står verket Ur väggen a: Since spring 2009 the square has been home to ‘Ur väggen’ (‘Out of the Wall’), a work by Yvonne T. Larsson. Its geometric angles were inspired by Endre Nemes’s marble wall from 1955.
Sedan våren 2022 heter huset House of Po: Since spring 2022 the old community hall has been called House of Possibilitas, after the cultural company that took over the premises and focuses mainly on performing arts and music. Inside are rehearsal rooms, studios and stages for shows – though the building is still owned by the City of Gothenburg.

Since spring 2022 the building has been called House of Possibilitas, after a production company working in theatre, dance and music took it over. It has rehearsal rooms for dance and theatre, artists' studios and rooms for local clubs, and puts on performances, talks and film screenings.
Segeltorp har inget med segel att göra: Segeltorp has nothing to do with sails
Segertorp var dagsverkstorp under Vårby: Segertorp was a croft whose tenants owed labour to the Vårby estate. In 1846 it consisted of a main house with two wings and three farm buildings, and in 1862 it became an independent farm.
Separatorhuset är fullt av symboler: mer: Separatorhuset is full of symbols: a caduceus, Hermes' winged helmet and an anchor above the main entrance, and above the portico a separator, a spade and a pitchfork. The corner tower has two tower clocks and a copper-clad cap.
Ser du tunnlarna från söder går tåg mot: Looking at the tunnels from the south, trains to Stockholm use the right-hand one, while the middle one – the very first, from 1911 – takes trains heading north. Furthest west is a single-track freight tunnel that merges with its neighbour inside the rock.
Sessionssalen var först klar och fick vä: The council chamber was finished first and was decorated with murals by Sven "X:et" Erixson. In the airy main staircase hang caricatures by Ewert Karlsson.
Setterwallska villan har höga murar av g: The Setterwall villa has tall walls of yellow-red Dutch brick on a sandstone base, with a tower, a lantern and bay windows on the outside. Inside are oak panelling, silk wallpaper and open fireplaces of Italian marble. Even so, the Setterwalls only lived there in summer.
Setterwallska villan har murar av gulröt: The Setterwall villa has walls of yellowish-red Dutch brick on a high sandstone base, with a tower, bay windows, a terrace and a veranda. Inside are tall oak panels, silk wallpaper in the drawing room and fireplaces of Italian marble.
Sex våningar mot gatan, tre mot gården: Six storeys to the street, three to the yard
Sextio skulpturer och ett åttkantigt hus: Sixty sculptures and an octagonal building
Shopping Park Kållered var från början t: Shopping Park Kållered was originally meant for audio and video shops, and was called Ljud & Bild-huset – the Sound & Vision House. When it opened in 1986 it had nine shops, most of them selling home electronics. Since then it has also gone by the names K-Center and K-gallerian.
Shopping i gamla flyghangarer! Köpcentre: Shopping in old aircraft hangars! The Bromma Blocks shopping centre is housed in Bromma Airport's hangars, which were the largest in northern Europe in their day. The architect Paul Hedqvist designed them in a chunky, block-like functionalist style – hence the name. And out in Bällstaviken bay is an islet that's actually a shipwreck: an old cargo ship that sank and has slowly been taken over by greenery.
Shoppingen här sker i Bromma flygplats g: The shopping here takes place in Bromma Airport's old hangars, which were once the biggest in northern Europe. In 1972 the first hypermarket moved into one of them, and in September 2010 the converted Hangar 3 opened, with around 80 shops under one roof. The name Bromma Blocks is a nod to the boxy functionalist architecture.
Shoppingsugen? Bäckebol Center rymmer et: Fancy some shopping? Bäckebol Center has around twenty shops spread over 95,000 square metres. The area has changed hands several times, and in 2008 Media Markt – later Power – opened its second Gothenburg store in Coop Bygg's old premises. A short walk away is the Lärjeån river, which gave its name to the whole Lärjedalen valley.
Sibirien har inga officiella gränser. En: Sibirien, "Siberia", has no official boundaries. By one account the border runs through the courtyards on the north side of Odengatan – so people living in the street-front buildings aren't in Siberia, but their neighbours in the courtyard buildings are.
Sickla har länge varit en plats där bruk: Sickla has a long history of industrial workers living close to their jobs. As early as the late 1890s, homes went up in Tallbacken for workers and foremen at AB Diesels Motorer. Then, in 1947–48, the Sickla strand housing area was built for employees of Atlas Diesel – later Atlas Copco – to designs by the architects Erik and Tore Ahlsén. The name Sickla itself roughly means a low-lying spot where water wells up.
Sickla kanal skiljer Södra Hammarbyhamne: The Sickla canal divides Södra Hammarbyhamnen from Nacka. The industrial past is easy to see here: in the 1920s Atlas Diesel, later Atlas Copco, moved its entire operation to Sickla, and the company's head office is still here. The factories kept going until the late 1980s, and in 1994 the area was transformed into the Sickla shopping quarter.
Sickla kanal öppnades 1931 för att båtar: Sickla canal opened in 1931 so that boats could reach Sicklasjön lake after the water level had been lowered. When two low road bridges were built in 1999–2003, another lock was needed, so today boats pass through two.
Sieverts Kabelverk grundades av Max Siev: Sieverts Kabelverk, the cable works, was founded by Max Sievert in 1888 and was originally called Trådfabriken, the Wire Factory. For many years it was Sundbyberg's biggest employer. Today the Signalfabriken quarter, with homes, restaurants and hotels, has grown up among the old industrial buildings. Just nearby, Bällsta bro, the Bällsta bridge, crosses Bällstaån stream, which marks the boundary between Sundbyberg and Stockholm.
Sigurd och Brynhild på gatuskylten: Sigurd and Brynhild on the street signs
Sikreno låter italienskt, men namnet har: Sikreno sounds Italian, but the name has nothing to do with its neighbours Frescati and Albano. According to one unconfirmed theory, it's actually an anagram based on the name Erikson! This is also where you'll find the Stocksund Inn, built between 1814 and 1816 by what was once the end of the Stocksund Bridge. The inn closed in 1938, and today the building is divided into homes.
Sikttavla på andra sidan dalen: A sighting board across the valley
Sillrök, gjuteri och fångar: Smoked herring, a foundry and prisoners
Sillviks Havskoloni bildades när Burgård: Sillvik’s seaside allotment colony was founded when the Burgården colony in central Gothenburg was cleared to make way for the Valhalla swimming baths. The colony has just over 120 cottages, a shared clubhouse and a beach café.
Silverdals griftegård anlades 1914 som g: Silverdal cemetery was laid out in 1914 as the burial ground for the Stockholm garrison, and Sollentuna parish took it over in 1960. A crematorium and a funeral chapel were added later. The area now called Silverdal was once home to two crofts, Rådan and Silverdal, which in time grew into farms.
Silverdals griftegård var fram till 1960: Until 1960 Silverdal cemetery was the garrison cemetery of the Svea Life Guards. The author Harry Martinson and the singer Ted Gärdestad are buried here. The chapel, designed by Lage Knape, was consecrated in 1969.
Silverdals gård har varit krog, tingshus: Silverdal farm has been an inn, a courthouse and a village shop. The inn ran until 1860, and the shop closed in the late 1950s. All that's left of the large farm today is the main house and the little smithy.
Silverpilen var ett soptåg: The Silver Arrow was a rubbish train
Silverskatten är från 900-talet och blan: The silver hoard dates from the 10th century and mixes Nordic jewellery with objects from both west and east. Two genuine Arabic coins and four imitations had been made into pendants, and there's also a necklace of 42 beads. Today the hoard is on display at the Swedish History Museum.
Sim- och sporthallen invigdes 1973 och a: The swimming and sports centre opened in 1973, and two years later its architects, Gustaf Rosenberg and Olle Stål, won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, for it. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Edsberg Palace from 1760, home to the Rudbeck family for almost 200 years. Up on the stable hill, until 2019, was Edsvik konsthall, an art gallery that put on twelve exhibitions a year.
Simbassäng i källaren: A swimming pool in the basement
Sisjöns industriområde ligger runt hörne: The Sisjön industrial area is just around the corner, directly south of the Söderleden road. It grew up as an industrial area in the 1960s but has gradually turned into a shopping area. Frölunda torg is just over two kilometres away, and Mölndal's town centre four.
Sista biten till Saltholmen, där skärgår: The last stretch to Saltholmen, where the archipelago boats leave from.
Sista björnen sköts 1750: The last bear was shot in 1750
Sista butiken från starten: The last shop from opening day
Sista landskampen 2012 var en repris av: The last international at the stadium in 2012 was a replay of the World Cup final – and Brazil won again, 3–0. On 25 November that year there was an open day, and visitors got to start the demolition by taking seats and turf home as souvenirs.
Sista matchen, samma lag: The last match, the same teams
Sista motorn till Slite: The last engine went to Slite
Sista utposten mot öster: The last outpost to the east
Sju rader med skivhus på en höjd, det är: Seven rows of slab blocks on a hillside – that's Siriusgatan, a real landmark as you enter Bergsjön. From some of the flats you can see all the way out to the island of Vinga! It's the most populous street in Gothenburg. The façades were originally grey and yellow, but during an eco-minded renovation in 1992, the anthroposophist Fritz Fuchs gave the buildings a new palette of light, soft shades.
Sju rum och vaktmästarbostad: Seven rooms and a caretaker's flat
Sju värmepumpar på totalt 225 MW tar var: Seven heat pumps with a combined 225 MW recover the energy in treated wastewater from the Henriksdal treatment works. The heat goes into southern Stockholm's district heating network, the chilled water becomes district cooling – and since the water still has some head of fall, it finally generates electricity in a turbine.
Sjukhemmet byggdes 1891–92 i sten, tre v: The nursing home was built in stone in 1891–92, three storeys high, with a park and an open view over Ulvsundasjön lake. From the very start it had central heating and electric light, and its water came from a diamond-drilled well.
Sjukhuset i Babels hus: The hospital in The House of Babel
Sjukhuset ritades av Melchior Wernstedt: The hospital was designed by Melchior Wernstedt and opened in 1935. It came with around 70 hectares of land for farming and gardening as therapy, along with a chapel, smithy, bakery, laundry and even an open-air dance floor.
Sjukhuset som aldrig användes: The hospital that was never used
Sjukhusets renovering skulle ha varit kl: The hospital's renovation was meant to be finished in spring 2018. Damp and mould in the foundation slab, along with delayed deliveries, pushed the opening back again and again, until 15 January 2020. The main building is an eight-storey slab surrounded by nine single-storey sections.
Själva Byälvsvägen byggdes runt 1970 och: Byälvsvägen itself dates from around 1970 and is the odd one out in Bagarmossen, otherwise a well-preserved 1950s suburb. The district won international praise for keeping pedestrians and cars strictly apart and for buildings that follow the lie of the land. A little further on, the Nacka nature reserve begins, with forest along the southern shore of Lake Sicklasjön and historic surroundings at Lilla Sickla.
Själva diket och en bit av den gamla väg: The ditch itself and a stretch of the old road embankment survive in a patch of woodland about 200 metres north of the Circle K petrol station. DN found the spot in 1985 with the help of the man who recovered the car. The Cadillac was hauled out by a lorry from Wårby Bryggerier brewery.
Själva olycksdiket och en bit av gamla S: The ditch where the accident happened, along with a stretch of the old Södertäljevägen embankment, was still there in 2018, in a patch of woodland on the Scandic hotel's grounds. The name Kungens kurva ("the King's Curve") was first given to two Esso petrol stations by their owner, Tore Jakobson.
Sjättenovembervägen hette tidigare Torsv: Sjättenovembervägen – Sixth of November Road – used to be called Torsvägen, and most of it follows the old Göta landsväg, the historic highway south. The long log causeway that gave Långbro its name – “long bridge” – back in the 1400s probably lay where the northern end of the street runs today. The district of Älvsjö was formed in 1932, and at the time it also took in what are now Rågsved, Solberga and Hagsätra.
Sjöberg har fått namn efter Sjöbergs går: Sjöberg takes its name from Sjöberg farm on Edsviken. A croft stood there first, also known as Skeppartorp or Ålänningstorp. The present main house was built in the 1850s for a palace steward at Haga and Ulriksdal.
Sjöberg ligger inklämt mellan tre naturo: Sjöberg is squeezed between three green areas: Edsviken, Rösjön and Rinkebyskogen. A little further away is Rösjön, a long, narrow lake 7.3 metres deep and 6.3 metres above sea level. Most of it belongs to Sollentuna and a smaller part to Danderyd – while Täby, right next door, doesn't touch its shores at all.
Sjöbergs fornborg ligger på en hög platå: Sjöberg's hill fort sits on a high plateau and measures about 210 by 100 metres. Archaeologists examined it in the 1980s and dated the wall to AD 400–550, but also found traces of even older settlements. The fort has given its name to Borgvägen along Edsviken.
Sjödalsgymnasiet var en riktig mästare i: Sjödalsgymnasiet was a true champion in Junior Achievement, the student enterprise programme. The school won the Swedish championship in 2001, 2002, 2004, 2005 and 2009, and once even took European gold. In 2019 it was named the best Junior Achievement school in the Stockholm region.
Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet: Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet, the Maritime Museum and Aquarium
Sjökaptenen bakom namnet: The sea captain behind the name
Sjökrogen som blev varvskontor: The waterside inn that became a shipyard office
Sjön Bergsjön, som gett stadsdelen sitt: Lake Bergsjön, which gave the district its name, is very close by – though it's tiny, to say the least. It covers just 0.0257 square kilometres, roughly two and a half hectares. It does sit high up, though, at 101.7 metres above sea level, and its water drains into the Göta älv river.
Sjön Grötfatet ligger bara några hundra: Lake Grötfatet – 'the porridge bowl' – is only a few hundred metres away, and the name tends to raise a smile. Fisksätra Church beside the square is a little out of the ordinary: it belongs to Nacka parish but is also used regularly by the Catholic parish of Saint Konrad, as part of the Guds hus, or God's House, project.
Sjön Trekanten hette Trehörningen fram t: Lake Trekanten was known as Trehörningen until the mid-19th century. On its north shore lay Nynäs, a ramshackle working-class suburb with a tannery, a coffee roastery, workshops and a bakery famous locally for its Nynäs loaf. Once the houses had fallen into disrepair, they became the backdrop for Bo Widerberg's 1970 film Joe Hill, standing in for the 'Lumberyard' and the 'Saloon'. The last of them were demolished in 1980.
Sjön anses ha fått sitt namn efter ett r: The lake is thought to take its name from a cairn ('röse') on an island in its southern part. The cairn marked the boundary between Danderyd's 'skeppslag' and Sollentuna's 'hundare', two old administrative districts.
Sjön har fått namn efter torpet Källtorp: The lake is named after the croft Källtorp, known since 1610. From 1723 it was a parsonage, and the present house was built in 1783. Källtorpssjön is a fissure-valley lake stretching about 1.5 kilometres from east to west.
Sjön planteras med öring och regnbåge, o: The lake is stocked with brown and rainbow trout, and you can fish here with a fishing permit. In winter the council clears a circular skating track on the ice, and a 1.75-kilometre walking trail loops around the lake.
Sjön var djup: vid provborrningar i den: The lake was deep: test drilling in the dried-up lakebed hasn't reached bedrock even at 40 metres down. On Georg Biurman's map from 1750, the lake is almost as big as Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Sjöräddningens station vid Hammarbysluss: The sea rescue station by the Hammarbyslussen lock
Sjöstugan, även kallad Stora Sjötullen 3: From the mid-18th century to the late 19th century, Sjöstugan – also known as Stora Sjötullen 3 – was an inn and brewhouse. Seafarers who had to wait for a customs inspection could get refreshments here.
Sjötorp var ett torp under Balingsta går: Sjötorp was a croft belonging to Balingsta gård, on the Flemingsbergsviken inlet. Its main building was put up in 1904 by the Ersta Deaconess Society as a home for what were then called “wayward girls”. Since 1998 it has been a private house, set in the middle of the Orlången nature reserve. A couple of hundred metres away is Stensättra gård, an old manor estate in an area that was probably first settled in the Viking Age.
Sjövillan är ett panelat trähus i en vån: Sjövillan is a single-storey, timber-clad house in the Gustavian style, with a mansard hipped roof and an Empire-style porch on columns. Two Gustavian tiled stoves led museum man Gösta Selling to date the house to the late 1700s, while the City Museum believes it's from the early 1700s.
Sjöängen söder om Brännkyrka kyrka ansåg: Sjöängen, the meadow south of Brännkyrka Church, was long considered almost impossible to build on. Since 2007 there have been plans for housing and a park, and in 2009 it was decided the area would get an artificial lake recreating a small part of the old Lake Brännkyrkasjön.
Skalden Carl Michael Bellman tillbringad: The poet Carl Michael Bellman spent the summer of 1773 at Fållan by Lake Magelungen, where his relatives the Zetterman family had their summer home. That's why four lime trees beside the old house foundations are known as Bellmanslindarna, the Bellman Limes. The houses themselves were pulled down around 1840. Closer to the stop is Magelungsfortet, a fort wedged between Nynäsvägen and Gamla Nynäsvägen. It's a remnant of the Southern Front, a ring of defences built to protect Stockholm around the time of the First World War.
Skalden Elias Sehlstedt var stamgäst och: The poet Elias Sehlstedt was a regular and wrote about happy times at Nackanäs. In summer 1950 the feature film ‘När syrenerna blomma’ (‘When the Lilacs Bloom’) was shot, and the inn was one of the locations.
Skandalen som ändrade reglerna: The scandal that changed the rules
Skandiahamnen intill är Sveriges största: Next door is Skandiahamnen, Sweden's largest container port, with 2,200 metres of quays. Huge container ships and car carriers sail from here. A little further away is Arendalsbanan, the old speedway track of the team Kaparna. Its attendance record of 5,940 was set in 2002, and the lap record belongs to none other than Tony Rickardsson, from 2004.
Skandiahamnen öppnades 1966. Den skapade: Skandiahamnen opened in 1966. It was created by enclosing and filling in 1.3 million square metres of the Älvsborg fjord.
Skansen Kronan, utsikt över staden: Skansen Kronan fort, with views over the city
Skansen öppnade 1891 och är världens äld: Skansen opened in 1891 and is the oldest open-air museum in the world. It has old farmsteads from all over Sweden, Nordic animals and a wide view over Stockholm.
Skanstull har fått sitt namn efter Söder: Skanstull gets its name from Söder skans, a fort between Årstaviken bay and Hammarby sjö lake. It was built in 1645 and later enlarged to plans by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, and the last traces weren't cleared away until the 1920s. These days the spot is watched over by Folksamhuset, a 27-storey tower that has been called an indispensable part of Stockholm's skyline since it went up in 1960. Down at Hammarbyslussen lock is the Swedish Sea Rescue Society's floating station, opened by Prince Carl Philip in 2019.
Skanstull har fått sitt namn efter en sk: Skanstull is named after a skans, a small fortification, and the toll gate at the city's southern entrance. From here the Skanstullsbron bridge heads south towards Johanneshov, and across the water you can see the big white dome of the Globen area. Götgatan, Södermalm's main street, starts just north of here.

Skanstull is named after a skans, a small fortification, and the tull, or toll gate, at the city's southern entrance. From here the Skanstull bridge heads south, and across the water you can see the big white dome of the Globen area.
Skarpa by nämns för första gången redan: The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as far back as 1318. The Skarpnäck manor was established in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace, but its golden age came under the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, who built the main house between 1865 and 1867. In 1922 his descendants sold the farm and its land to the City of Stockholm.
Skarpa by nämns första gången redan 1318: The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as far back as 1318, and the Skarpnäck manor estate was created in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace. The present main house was built in the 1860s by the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, and under his ownership the estate enjoyed its golden age. The district itself was formed in 1963 from Pungpinan and Skarpnäck. Its metro station, opened in 1994, lies in a rock cavern 25 metres underground.
Skarpnäck blev tunnelbanans 100:e statio: Skarpnäck became the metro's 100th station and is the easternmost on the whole network. The artist Richard Nonas has decorated it with 17 bench-like sculptures in dark granite.
Skarpnäck är den östligaste stationen i: Skarpnäck is the easternmost station on the whole metro network and the end of line 17. Richard Nonas's bench-like sculptures are made of dark granite.
Skarpnäcks koloniområde från 1936 har 55: Skarpnäck's allotments, from 1936, have 554 plots, most of them at least 300 square metres with cabins of around 25 square metres. With just over 184,000 square metres under cultivation, it's one of the largest allotment areas in Europe.
Skarpnäcks tunnelbanestation, en kort pr: Skarpnäck metro station, a short walk away, became the hundredth station on the network when it opened on 15 August 1994. It sits in a rock cavern 25 metres underground, decorated by the artist Richard Nonas with 17 sculptures that look like benches. Even closer is Skarpnäcks folkhögskola, the largest folk high school in Stockholm.
Skarpnäcksfältet var förr ett flygfält,: Skarpnäcksfältet was once an airfield, and for many years it hosted the Skarpnäcksloppet motor race. The last air show took place in August 1980, and during the 1980s a new residential area grew up on the field. Today Australian rules football is played at The Jordo Cricket Ground, where the very first match, between the Södermalm Blues and the Norrtälje Dockers, took place on 6 August 2012.
Skarpnäcksloppet startade 1950 och körde: The Skarpnäck race started in 1950 and ran over 15 laps. In May 1967 Reine Wisell won the Formula 3 class, while Ronnie Peterson finished seventh. Peterson got his revenge, winning in both 1968 and 1969.
Skarpäng har fått sitt namn av ett dagsv: Skarpäng takes its name from a day labourer's croft on the Ella farm, built in 1715. In the 1920s land began to be divided into plots for holiday homes, and by 1940 around 550 had been sold. Neighbouring Ella park got its name in the early 1930s, when what was then northern Ella was split up. Today it's a purely residential area of large villas.
Skatten inspirerade keramikern Mari Påru: The treasure inspired ceramicist Mari Pårup's relief Vårbyskatter ('Vårby Treasures') on the Vårbyhuset building, unveiled in 2008. Over a hundred glazed hemispheres on the brick wall form a giant necklace, the largest bead around 50 cm across.
Skepp och fiskar på berget: Ships and fish on the rock
Skeppsholmen var länge flottans ö. I dag: For a long time Skeppsholmen was the navy's island. Today it's home to Moderna museet, the Museum of Modern Art, and to the old sailing ship af Chapman, now a youth hostel. From the shore you get one of the best views across to Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Skidbacken Ekebyhovsbacken är hemmabacke: Ekebyhovsbacken is the home slope of Mälaröarnas Alpina Skidklubb, the local alpine ski club, and from the top you get a sweeping view over Ekerö and Lake Mälaren. A little further on, on Gällstaö, grows the Gällstaö oak, which may be between 400 and 500 years old. By volume it's Sweden's second-largest broadleaf tree, beaten only by the Ekebyhov oak.
Skinngruppen heter i dag Store. Sedan om: Skinngruppen is now called Store. Since around 2020 the company has been owned by Nordiska Kompaniet and trades under that brand.
Skintebo finns omnämnt redan 1567, som S: Skintebo is mentioned as early as 1567, as Skinteboda or simply Skintan. The name may mean good soil, but it could also mean a furrow, hollow, ditch or sunken track. Skinta in the sense of good soil appears in several places around Askim.
Skintebo finns som bynamn redan 1567, då: Skintebo appears as a village name as early as 1567, then spelt Skinteboda or simply Skintan. The name may mean good soil, but it could also mean furrow, pit, ditch or sunken lane. The word 'skinta' in the sense of good soil turns up in several places around Askim.
Skintebodalen var jordbruksmark fram til: Skintebodalen was farmland until the 1970s. The new estate was given car-free footpaths, terraced houses, two-storey timber homes and "båtmansgårdar", a cross between a terrace and a detached house. It won the prize for Gothenburg's best building of the year in 1975.
Skivhusen på Siriusgatan står i sju rade: The slab blocks on Siriusgatan stand in seven rows on a hillside, a landmark as you come into Bergsjön. From some of the flats you can see all the way out to Vinga lighthouse! It's Gothenburg's most populous street, with 3,199 residents in 2021. The facades were originally grey and yellow, but during a renovation in 1992 the anthroposophist Fritz Fuchs was given the job of repainting them in a range of pale shades.
Skivhuset ritades av Andreas Carstens, ä: This slab block was designed by Andreas Carstens, is about 300 metres long and was completed in 1964. It has 9 or 10 storeys depending on which side you approach from, and holds 421 flats. Bands of red brick and white balcony fronts make it look even longer.
Skjortfabrikören Simon Berendt köpte Bjö: The shirt manufacturer Simon Berendt bought Björken 18 when it was newly built, and the house stayed in the family for four generations, until 1986. Today it's a listed building.
Skog och berg dominerar i den här delen: This part of Huddinge is all forest and rocky hills. Not far from here, Kynäsberget stretches out to the south-west of Lake Magelungen – an area of woods and crags considered of national importance for outdoor recreation, and there are plans to protect its northern part as a nature reserve. In the other direction is Björkängen sports ground, home to the ice hockey team Huddinge IK.
Skog och berg tar över en bit härifrån:: Not far from here, forest and rock take over. Kynäsberget, south-west of Lake Magelungen, is of national importance for outdoor recreation, and its northern part may become a nature reserve. Further off, on the Stockholm border, is the Rågsved open space, also called Kräppladalen – just over 100 hectares of rift-valley landscape, with ridges, steep slopes and clay-filled valleys.
Skogarna här hör till Nackareservatet, e: The forests here are part of Nackareservatet, a large nature reserve and outdoor recreation area shared by Stockholm and Nacka. A little further on is Lake Källtorpssjön, 7.6 metres deep, with the Hellasgården outdoor sports centre on its shore. Test fishing in the lake has turned up perch, white bream, common bream, ruffe and roach.
Skogen här är full av små sjöar. Örtjärn: The forest here is dotted with little lakes. Örtjärnen, a few hundred metres away, is a full ten metres deep despite its small size, and its water drains out through the Finnebäcken stream. A little further away is Västra Kroppedammen, just 0.006 square kilometres – a real dwarf among lakes.
Skogen som bytte namn: The forest that changed its name
Skogskapellet var det allra första kapel: Skogskapellet, the Woodland Chapel, was the very first chapel at Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. Gunnar Asplund designed it, and it was built in 1919–20. Close by stands the Resurrection Monument, a bronze group of six figures that John Lundqvist worked on from 1928 to 1941. The new crematorium, designed by Johan Celsing, has also won acclaim, picking up the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 2013.
Skogskyrkogården skapades av Gunnar Aspl: Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, was created by Gunnar Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz on a pine-covered gravel ridge, and it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994. On the roof above the entrance to the Woodland Chapel stands Carl Milles' small gilded Angel of Death – the only time Milles and Asplund worked together. The angel sparked a debate in the city council, as some priests found it offensive and indecent!
Skogås sträcker sig från Mörtvik i norr: Skogås stretches from Mörtvik in the north to Gräsvreten in the south, with Lake Drevviken along its eastern edge.
