On Mörtviken, a bay of the lake, is Mörtviks gård, a group of buildings that still feels like a farm even though several of the houses have been heavily rebuilt. Closer to the stop is Östra gymnasiet, an upper secondary school that was named one of the buildings of the year in 2005.
Skola kring ett torg: A school built round a square
Skola och statarbostad emellan: A school and farmworkers' homes in between
Skola, statarbostad och krog igen: School, farmworkers' homes – then an inn again
Skolan byggdes 1952–1953 för drygt 300 e: The school was built in 1952–1953 for just over 300 pupils in 21 classes. Cyrillus Johansson split it into three connected buildings around the playground. On the main building is the relief Noah's Ark by the artist Allan Wallberg.
Skolan började som Olofskolans verkstad,: The school began as the workshop of Olofskolan, the school Carl Malmsten founded in 1930. For 60 years it was on Södermalm. One of its best-known heads was the guitar maker Professor Georg Bolin.
Skolan driver också hotell, konferens oc: The school also runs a hotel, conference centre and hostel all year round, with some 160 hostel beds in summer. Its owner, the temperance organisation IOGT-NTO, changed its name to Movendi Sverige in 2025 after a merger.
Skolan följer gamla allén: The school follows the old avenue
Skolan har fått sitt namn efter klockarg: The school is named after the klockargården, where the bell-ringer of Lidingö Church lived. In the late 19th century the school day ran from 8 am to 3 pm, with a fifteen-minute break between lessons. Lunch also lasted a quarter of an hour, and pupils ate packed food they had brought from home.
Skolan ordnar \"öppen kroki\", lärarlösa: The school runs "open kroki" – untutored evening and weekend life-drawing sessions with a model. There's no need to book; you just pay at the door.
Skolan ritades av Åke E. Lindqvist och i: Designed by Åke E. Lindqvist, the school opened in 1973. The buildings were planned around a square, with each function given its own design, and façades of yellow-red brick and timber with exposed concrete elements.
Skolan som tog EM-guld: The school that won European gold
Skolan startade i januari 2007 som filia: The school opened in January 2007 as a branch of Göteborgs folkhögskola, a folk high school for adult learners. In 2010 it became independent as Agnesbergs folkhögskola, named after its first premises, and in 2011 it moved to Bergsjön. Since 2021 the Finnish Multicultural Folk High School on Gärdsås torg has taken over its students.
Skolan var från början en del av Olofsko: The school was originally part of Olofskolan, founded by Carl Malmsten in 1930, and was known as Olofskolans Verkstad, the Olofskolan Workshop. It was based on Södermalm for 60 years, and one of its best-known heads was the guitar maker Professor Georg Bolin.
Skolan var först med att erbjuda slöjd v: The school was the first to offer handicrafts alongside academic subjects. It closed on 10 June 1977 after its 100th end-of-year ceremony. In 1988 the French state bought the building on Kommendörsgatan and converted it into an embassy.
Skolan är uppkallad efter Johan Skytte,: The school is named after Johan Skytte, and its main building, begun in 1946, was designed by the architect Paul Hedqvist. Close by is Långbrodal School, whose 2017 extension attracted a lot of attention. And further off was Långbro Hospital, a psychiatric hospital built between 1905 and 1910 and closed in 1997.
Skolan öppnade 1982 som Botvidsgymnasiet: The school opened in 1982 as Botvidsgymnasiet, offering mainly technical vocational courses. In 2000 it moved from Slagsta to Hallunda and took its present name. Today students from all over the country apply for its contemporary circus programme.
Skolan öppnade den 10 maj 1846, men den: The school opened on 10 May 1846, but the intended teacher was still in training. So for the first year lessons were given by the church caretaker, Erik Mellberg. In April 1847 the parish clerk and organist Ludvig Ulric Öberg took over.
Skolarkitekten Georg A. Nilsson tog fram: The school architect Georg A. Nilsson drew almost identical plans for three schools – Långbrodalsskolan, Enskede skola and Örbyskolan – all built around 1915. You'll recognise them by the projecting stairwell with a giant clock. The style is National Romantic, harking back to the plain stone houses of the 1600s.
Skoldag med kvartsraster: A school day with quarter-hour breaks
Skolhus i båtsmanstorpet: A schoolhouse in the sailor’s croft
Skolhuset från 1901 hade en folkskolesal: The 1901 schoolhouse had a primary classroom for 64 children and an infant classroom for 36. It also had a teacher's flat, a council room that doubled as a woodwork room, and a dental clinic with a treatment room and waiting room.
Skolscenen har tvååriga utbildningar i t: The school stage runs two-year programmes in theatre and musical theatre. Since 1989 it has put on a New Year revue every January and February. The theatre, built in 2002, seats 223.
Skomakarens torp blev kronjuvel: The cobbler's croft became the crown jewel
Skorstenen i gult och blått: The chimney in yellow and blue
Skotten och engelska sättet: The Scot and the English method
Skrapan är 86 meter hög med 22 våningar: The Skyscraper is 86 metres tall, with 22 storeys, and was designed by Ralph Erskine together with White Architects. Gothenburg's soft clay called for stabilising piles up to 90 metres long – longer than the building is tall.
Skruven var inget vanligt torp utan bost: Skruven was no ordinary croft but housing for Säby's estate craftsmen, above all the blacksmith. Shoemakers and tailors lived there too, and an inn served travellers on the through road until 1809.
Skrönan om Gustav III:s gåva: The tall tale of Gustav III’s gift
Skulpturen Arbetarhustru: The sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife
Skulpturen Arbetarhustru gjordes av Elma: The sculpture Arbetarhustru ('Worker's Wife') is by Elma Oijens and came about at the initiative of Gamla Landalapojkar, an association of old Landala boys, who raised the money. It was unveiled on 11 October 1980, and the poem on the plinth was written by Holger Oijens.
Skulpturen Boll är gjord av Berit Lindfe: The sculpture ‘Boll’ (‘Ball’) is by Berit Lindfeldt and was installed in 2007. The sphere was first polished to a mirror finish, then partly painted light blue, with shiny dots left unpainted.
Skulpturen Fosterbröderna: The sculpture Fosterbröderna, the Foster Brothers
Skulpturer och meditationsplats: Sculptures and a place to meditate
Skulptörens sista år i Solna: The sculptor's last years in Solna
Skuru var från början namnet på en gård,: Skuru was originally the name of a farm, and that farm lives on today as Solsunda. In the 1500s King Gustav Vasa gave it to Danvik's hospital, and in the early 1900s it belonged to Stockholms sjukhem, a nursing home. The area also has Bastusjön, a lake you can swim in, and a little further off is Glasbrukssjön, which is small but a surprising 13 metres deep.

Skuru started out as the name of a farm, and today the area is mostly villas and semi-detached houses surrounded by nature. Not far from here, on the shore of Saltsjön, is Stora Nyckelviken, a manor from the mid-1700s – and as early as the 1600s there was a sailors' inn on the spot. Around the manor lies the Nyckelviken nature conservation area, 171 hectares of hilly, historic farmland.
Skvalta var ursprungligen en sjö, och va: Skvalta was originally a lake, and the water flowing out through Vikdalen powered several 'skvaltkvarnar', small horizontal water mills – which is where the name comes from. A little further on, in the villa suburb of Storängen, are two genuine artists' homes. Villa Bergh was home to the painter Richard Bergh from 1904 to 1919, and next door is Villa Pauli, where the artists Georg and Hanna Pauli lived. Both were designed in 1904 by the architect Albin Brag.
Skvaltan, barackcentrumet: Skvaltan, the shopping centre in huts
SkyView, gondolen upp på kupolen: SkyView – the gondola ride up the dome
Skyddsrum blev däckfirma: From air-raid shelter to tyre shop
Skälby är ett villaområde i södra delen: Skälby is a residential area of villas in southern Järfälla, part of the Stockholm urban area, and in 2005 it had 6,336 residents. The name comes from Skälby gård, a manor dating back to the 16th century. To the south, across the municipal boundary, begins Kälvesta, a Stockholm neighbourhood of terraced houses and villas.
Skälby, villaområdet runt omkring, har f: Skälby, the residential area all around us, is named after Skälby gård, a manor house not far from here. It's a former noble estate in Järfälla parish dating back to the 1500s, though the current main house was built in 1802. It's also in an unusual spot – right in the middle of four ancient burial grounds.
Skälltorp, området här intill, omfattar: The neighbouring area, Skälltorp, takes in northern Backa with Selma Lagerlöfs torg square, as well as Backadalen, Blå staden, Åketorp and Backatorp. A little further on is Sophie Elkans gata, named in 1992 after the Gothenburg-born writer Sophie Elkan – best remembered as Selma Lagerlöf's close friend. So here, the two friends meet again in the street names.
Skär, ekskog och strandängar: Skerries, oak woods and shore meadows
Skärgård där bilarna kör: An archipelago where cars now drive
Skärholmen har en egen liten bergbana. S: Skärholmen has a little funicular of its own. The inclined lift between Skärholmen and Ekholmshöjden is 63 metres long, holds about 30 people and takes around a minute – and there's no driver on board. Also nearby is Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is part of Kulturhuset Stadsteatern, the city's culture house and theatre.
Skärholmen hörde till Huddinge ända fram: Skärholmen was part of Huddinge until 1963, when it was transferred to Stockholm along with Vårberg. Down on the metro platform you can take a little trip to America: in 1990 the artist Ulf Wahlberg painted a spot in New Mexico in a series of 23 pictures, from sunrise to sunset. And close by, a funicular carries passengers up to Ekholmshöjden.
Skärholmens gård, vid Mälaren en bit här: Skärholmens gård, down by Lake Mälaren, started out as a simple croft belonging to Vårby gård. In the mid-18th century it was rebuilt as a summer retreat for wealthy Stockholmers. The City of Stockholm has owned it since 1945, and the City Museum has given it a blue listing, meaning its buildings are judged to be of exceptional cultural and historical value.
Skärsätra gård, alldeles intill, har get: Skärsätra gård, the farm right next to us, gave its name to the whole district, and its old main house is still standing, though it has been altered over the years. The villas round about make for a nice little architecture walk: there's Villa Bergtomta, an Art Nouveau house from 1910; Apelsinvillan, the Orange Villa, by Lake Kottlasjön, listed since 1982; and Villa Smith, which the architect Nils Tesch designed for himself in 1959 but never actually moved into.
Skådespelaren Gustaf Fredriksons far köp: The actor Gustaf Fredrikson's father bought Charlottenburg in 1854, and his son later wrote about his childhood memories of "the grand old Charlottenburg". From 1931 Sven G. Hellström, family doctor to the people of Råsunda, had his surgery in the wing.
Skål i Gustav III:s glas: A toast in Gustav III's glass
Skårsgatan har fått namn efter gården Sk: Skårsgatan is named after the farm of Skår – 'skår' means a notch or ledge in the rock – and the name appears, spelt Shor, in a court letter as early as 1496. Sankt Sigfridsgatan, next to it, is named after the patron saint of Västergötland. And on that street you'll find Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, which since 1924 has been baking citrus-scented gingerbread biscuits to a secret recipe.
Sköndal blev en egen stadsdel 1932 och h: Sköndal became a district in its own right in 1932, and there's plenty of architecture to discover. The architect Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl in 1955 as his own home, and Sköndalsskolan, the school opened in 1953, is the work of none other than Cyrillus Johansson. A little further on, Stora Sköndal Church sits proudly on a rocky outcrop near Lake Drevviken.
Sköndalsbro var en gång ett torp, och hu: Sköndalsbro was once a croft, and its main building probably dates from somewhere between 1700 and 1750, or perhaps later. The blocks around it are like a small open-air museum of architecture. Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl as his own home, and the architect couple Hanna and Roy Victorson built Villa Victorson. The two houses, from 1955 and 1958, are marked blue by the City Museum, meaning they're of exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Sköndalsskolans fasad mot Perstorpsvägen: Sköndalsskolan's façade facing Perstorpsvägen is full of playful brick motifs: a sailing boat, a witch, a Yule goat, a girl skipping, and the short poem "a b c – 1953". The main entrance is framed in yellow brick with patterned brick flowers.
Slagsta gård har anor ända från 1300-tal: Slagsta farm dates back to the 14th century. In the 1650s it became a manorial estate, and county governor Frans Crusebjörn lived here with his wife Gunilla Rosenstjerna, who had inherited it from her father.
Slalombacken som aldrig blev: The ski slope that never was
Slas och klubbtidningen Utropstecknet: Slas and the club magazine Utropstecknet
Slottet av tre gårdar: A manor made of three farms
Slottet byggdes 1750 av affärsmannen And: The manor was built in 1750 by the businessman Anders Plomgren. In 1834 it was moved, because its owner, the Russian ambassador Peter van Suchtelen, wanted to build a new main house. The old building became home to four families of servants.
Slottet byggdes i U-form i förenklad fra: The palace was built in a U shape in a simplified French Rococo style, with round dormers known as oeil-de-boeuf windows. The drawings are unsigned, but the builders probably followed one of Carl Wijnbladh's model designs for manor houses.
Slottet mitt i orten: A palace in the middle of town
Slottet ritades av en rysk arkitekt i Al: The manor was designed by a Russian architect in the Empire style of Alexander I's day. The outer walls of the ground floor are studded with small round stones pressed into the render, a technique found in Russian architecture at the time.
Slottet som kanske aldrig ägde den: The castle that may never have owned it
Slottets balkong mot sjön: The castle's balcony over the lake
Slottets mest kända herre var Carl Rober: The manor's best-known owner was Carl Robert Lamm, whose large art collection included works by Bruno Liljefors and Anders Zorn. His company also began building homes in the area in the 1920s.
Slussen som gick med förlust: The lock that ran at a loss
Slussen är platsen där Mälaren möter Sal: Slussen is where Lake Mälaren meets Saltsjön, the inlet of the Baltic, and where Södermalm meets Gamla stan, the Old Town. There have been locks here since the 17th century, and right now the whole area is being rebuilt in one of Stockholm's biggest construction projects. From the quays you can look out over Gamla stan, Skeppsholmen and Djurgården.
Slussvaktarstugan från tidigt 1900-tal s: The lock-keeper's cottage from the early 1900s is still standing. The Swedish Security Service once kept watch for Nazis from here, because the German consulate had rented space in the Post Office building across the lock.
Slutade röka för lägre skatt: Gave up smoking to pay less tax
Slutstation för tre spårvagnslinjer: End of the line for three trams
Slutstation i ett år: End of the line for a year
Släktforskare, spetsa öronen! Alldeles i: Calling all family historians! Right next door is the home of Genealogiska Föreningen, the Genealogical Society. Founded in 1933, it's a national association and one of Sweden's oldest in the field of family history. A stone's throw away is Jungfrudansen, now a housing area with culturally valuable Million Programme buildings but once a festival ground. The Huvudsta quarry was here too.
Slättens gård är ett före detta torp som: Slättens gård is a former croft that originally belonged to Sätra manor, and it's one of the few buildings left from before the Mälarhöjden villa suburb was built. Today its three houses are managed by AB Stadsholmen. A little further on is Mälarhöjden sports ground, known locally as Myren, which – despite its name – is actually in Fruängen.
Smista allé fick sitt namn efter Smista: Smista allé is named after Smista farm, which stood where Skärholmen's shopping centre is today, on the other side of the motorway. The Smistabron footbridge and cycle bridge crosses the E4/E20 to Sätra.
Smycketorget i närheten anlades på 1960-: Nearby Smycketorget was built in the 1960s on two levels: shops and a hairdresser upstairs, an Asian restaurant and a pizzeria downstairs. A little further away is Frölunda torg, opened by Olof Palme on 8 September 1966. Seven years in the making, it was then the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries.
Små kyrkor efter dansk modell: Small churches on a Danish model
Småstad med Trosa som förebild: A small town modelled on Trosa
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ab: We'll soon reach the final stop, Abrahamsberg. Here's a little naming quirk: Abrahamsberg metro station isn't actually in Abrahamsberg at all, but in Riksby. Before the metro, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals in glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are a nod to the tiled stations of the tram days. Close by is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg Church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ak: We'll soon reach the final stop, Akalla. Akalla's main walkway, Sibeliusgången, is named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius and runs for 900 metres, with Bertil Johnson's fountains from 1976 bubbling away along the route. Yet the name Akalla goes back to the Middle Ages. In Akalla village stands Storgården, a 17th-century farm in one of the best-preserved village settings around Stockholm, now with a 4-H children's farm and a café. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Al: We'll soon reach the final stop, Alvik. Alvik is an interchange where the Tvärbanan and Nockebybanan light rail lines meet the metro. From here you can head out into Bromma, with its villa neighbourhoods and the shores of Lake Mälaren. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Alviks strand. Alvik's old industrial area once lined the shore of Lake Mälaren; today it's mostly offices and a few restaurants. Nearby is Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, an events venue where the TV competition Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail plunges into the rock through the Alvik tunnel, about 250 metres long, then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the 400-metre Alvik bridge, finished in 2000. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Am: We'll soon reach the final stop, Amhult Resecentrum. A few hundred metres from here in Amhult was Torslanda airfield, Gothenburg's airport from 1923 right up until 1977, when Landvetter took over. It was originally called Göteborgs Flyghamn and had a seaplane harbour too. When it closed, it was one of the oldest airfields in Europe with scheduled flights. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen An: We'll soon reach the final stop, Angered Centrum. Angered was built in the 1970s, and today it's one of Gothenburg's most international districts. It's home to the Blå Stället cultural centre, and all around are large stretches of countryside with lakes and forest. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Angereds Storåsväg. Not far from here is Hammarkulletorget, built in 1971, which got new colours and a new shape during a renovation in 1997. You can reach it by tram, getting off at what's been called Gothenburg's only underground station. Closer to this stop is Eriksbo, part of the Hjällbo district. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ap: We'll soon reach the final stop, Aprilgatan. Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, is better known to many as Norra or Norra centrum, and it's the little hub of northern Kortedala. There's a health centre, a pizzeria, tobacconists and a pâtisserie if you fancy a fika – a Swedish coffee-and-cake break – plus a pub close by. Local clubs and associations have their premises on the square too. It sits on tram line six, by the end of the line. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ar: We'll soon reach the final stop, Arendal Portal. Right next door is the Arken combi terminal at Skandiahamnen, the Skandia Harbour, where semi-trailers are transferred between ships and trains. It replaced the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to make way for the Västlänken rail tunnel. Work started in January 2018, and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen As: We'll soon reach the final stop, Askims Svartmosse. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ax: We'll soon reach the final stop, Axel Dahlströms Torg. The square is dominated by a 16-storey tower block completed in 1956, and the community centre is decorated with a marble-inlay mural by the artist Endre Nemes. The same year Högsboskolan, the Högsbo school, opened right next door, built for around 1,000 pupils. The school is gone now, though – it was demolished in 2013. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ba: We'll soon reach the final stop, Backlura. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bagarmossen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bagartorp södra. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Balingsnäs. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby handelsplats. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby station övre. Barkarby is a place being transformed. The commuter rail station took on its present form on 10 October 2016, with four tracks and a ticket hall up on the Barkarbybron bridge. Meanwhile, a new metro station is being built underground, and once everything's finished, a new entrance at the north end of the station will become the main way in. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby station. It's about 14.5 kilometres from here into Stockholm Central, and the commuter train station has four tracks so that freight and long-distance trains can race straight through. In 1728, Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone in Järfälla church – it had probably been used as a step. It later went missing, but in 1939 seven fragments turned up, and today they're kept at the Swedish History Museum. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barnängen. Per Anders Fogelström brought the old factory district of Barnängen, on the shore of Hammarby sjö, to life in his novel Vävarnas barn, 'The Weavers' Children' – and this is also where Hammarby IF football club has its roots. Barnängsparken slopes down to the waterfront with lawns and a ferry pier facing Hammarby sjöstad. A little further on is Leksaksmuseet, the Toy Museum, with everything from 19th-century dolls to Lego, Barbie and Star Wars. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Be: We'll soon reach the final stop, Beatrice Lesslies Gata. A few hundred metres from here is Studio Fredman, the recording studio Fredrik Nordström set up in 1990. A long list of Swedish metal bands have recorded here – In Flames, Hammerfall, Opeth, Dark Tranquillity and Soilwork among them – as well as the British band Bring Me the Horizon. Just beyond is Radiotorget, the first square built for a Swedish satellite town, opened in 1954. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Björknäs centrum. Björknäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436, and takes its name from Stora Björknäs farm. It sits at the eastern end of the Skuru bridges, where the Skurusundet strait marks the boundary between two historic provinces: Södermanland to the west and Uppland to the east. Bridges have been built here three times – in 1915, 1957 and 2023. When the newest one opened, it took over the name Skurubron, and the older ones became Gamla Skurubron, the Old Skuru Bridge. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Björnbo. Elfviksvägen has two villas by the architect Ralph Erskine: Villa Gadelius, designed in 1961 for the businessman Knut Saburo Gadelius, and Villa Molin from 1947, built for the garden designer and editor Ulla Molin. A little further on is the Kanada block. Its terraced houses, along with those in Gamla Enskede, are thought to be the very first in Sweden, and they have been listed since 1981. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Björnkulla. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Blackebergs gård. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Blockhusudden. This headland is named after a blockhouse of timber and stone, built in Gustav Vasa's day to guard the approach to Stockholm. Later it became a customs post for incoming boats, and the old customs houses at Stora Sjötullen are now private homes. Out here you'll also find Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, an art museum on Djurgården. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Bockkranen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Borås resecentrum. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bosön. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Br: We'll soon reach the final stop, Bredäng. Bredäng is seriously hilly: Bredängsskolan, the school, sits 62 metres above sea level, and Bredängshemmet, the care home, a full 67 metres. Bredängsparken, next to the centre, is one of the biggest parks in the district, and drinking alcohol has been banned there because things used to get rowdy. Bredäng Church doesn't have a building of its own – it's in a parish hall at one end of the shopping centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Bromma flygplats. The building on Ulvsundavägen went up in 1946 as the head office of the airline ABA and was later used by SAS. It was designed by Paul Hedqvist, the architect behind several of the airport's hangars, too – in their day the biggest in northern Europe. These days the hangars house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brommaplan. By the metro viaduct stands the sculpture ‘Bird Rock with Three Eggs’, made by Berndt Helleberg in 1969. The viaduct is actually older than the metro: it opened in 1944, when trams ran across it. The art in the station, in sheet metal, glass and photographs, tells the story of Bromma and of aviation. The 16-storey Brommahöjden tower block is a newcomer by comparison – it only arrived in 2008. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brunnsparken. Brunnsparken is the beating heart of the city's public transport – almost every tram line passes through here. Right next to it is Gustaf Adolfs torg, with a statue of the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers, and that's why Gothenburg has canals: the Dutch knew how to build on clay. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brännö Rödsten. Brännö is a car-free island in Gothenburg's southern archipelago. Its summer dances on the jetty are famous all over Gothenburg, and the island has lovely rocks to swim from. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Burö färjeläge. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ce: We'll soon reach the final stop, Centralen. At Vasagatan 7 was the bar Tre Remmare, with a casino and nightclub under the same roof. It was one of the few places in Stockholm allowed to stay open until five in the morning, and it became notorious for heavy drinking and drug abuse. It lost its licence and closed in 2007, and the Bishops Arms pub has taken over the premises. Across the street stands the World Trade Center, designed by Ralph Erskine. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ci: We'll soon reach the final stop, Cityterminalen. Kungsgatan 65 has had quite a few incarnations. The Palladium cinema opened here in 1918, with the Bal Palais dance restaurant in the basement. Later it became the Heaven nightclub, and from 2003 to 2025 it was Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern, the Oscar Theatre, from 1906 – named after King Oscar II and now a listed building. The same building houses Fasching, which since 1977 has been Scandinavia's biggest jazz venue. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Da: We'll soon reach the final stop, Dalens sjukhus. Dalen hospital, completed in 1977, is a well-preserved example of the late modernist architecture of its day and an important piece of urban planning history. A little further away, on the Nytorps gärde field, stood the croft of Nytorp, which belonged to the Hammarby estate. It disappeared in the early 1960s to make way for the Nytorpsbadet pool. The residential area of Dalen is made up of 14 blocks, and the Stockholm City Museum has classed the whole of it as culturally valuable. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Danderyds sjukhus. Over in Inverness, the Inverness brunn mineral water works was in business from 1929 to 1945 – among other things, it made Sweden's first soda water. The spring is still there on the shore of Stocksundet, though the water isn't fit to drink and tastes salty. Closer to the stop stood Mörby gård, an 18th-century farm that gave the area its name. It was listed in 1944, but burned down in 1976. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Dj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Djurgårdsbrunn. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Djursholms torg. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Djurstensvägen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Do: We'll soon reach the final stop, Doktor Sydows Gata. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Dr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Drottningtorget. Drottningtorget sits right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings still in use in Sweden. Much of the largest tram network in the Nordic countries fans out from here. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902 – and while many other Swedish cities scrapped their trams, Gothenburg chose to keep them. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Du: We'll soon reach the final stop, Duvbo. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ek: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekensberg. Ekensberg is named after the Ekensberg inn, built in the early 18th century and still standing at Gröndalsvägen 184. Between 1926 and 1934, most of what we now call Gröndal went by the name of Ekensberg. The headland sits between Mörtviken bay and the Essingesundet strait. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekensbergsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekerö centrum. From Tappström, commuter boat line 89 runs all the way into Stockholm to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay, with boats such as M/S Lux. The Tappström strait, which separates the islands of Lovön and Ekerön, also has a guest harbour for visiting leisure boats. A little further away was Tappsund brickworks, founded in the late 19th century and closed in 1959. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Eketrägatan. The street is named after the noble Eketrä family, who owned the Västra Pilegården estate – right where the asphalt is today – from the 18th century until 1875. This is also where the Bräcke tram line turned south. The line closed in 1968 and was dismantled in the 1980s, but its old trackbed is still almost untouched, like a trace from another age. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekstubben. Ältavägen is 8.1 kilometres long, and its route was laid out in 1934. Most of it runs through unspoilt countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. The Flaten nature reserve has an unusual attraction: a racetrack for radio-controlled model cars, at Ältavägen 301 in the Flaten area. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ektorps centrum. Much of neighbouring Ekängen was built in the 1940s as a neighbourhood of small family houses, and it's still a quiet residential area just north of Saltsjö-Duvnäs. A little further on you'll find Långsjön, a small forest lake that has been a nature reserve since 2005. There's a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail all the way round – perfect if you fancy swapping the town centre for a lap of the lake. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen El: We'll soon reach the final stop, Elfvik. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen En: We'll soon reach the final stop, Enbacksskolan. Bussenhus, the little cottage next to Spånga Church, was a soldier's croft with an unusual sideline: in the 1740s, the cavalryman who lived here was allowed to run a tavern. It crops up now and then in the records of the Sollentuna district court, after various brawls. Inside the church you'll find fragments of Viking Age runestones, and one of them is built into the church's outer wall. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Eq: We'll soon reach the final stop, Equmeniakyrkan. Every spring, Björkö turns blue. At Bovik there's an area called Pjonken, famous for the masses of hepaticas, or blue anemones, that flower there. The island lies in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, and the village is home to around 1,400 people. A short way from here stands Björkö Church, which belongs to Öckerö parish. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Er: We'll soon reach the final stop, Eriksbo Östergärde. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Es: We'll soon reach the final stop, Essingetorget. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Farsta centrum. Farsta Centre opened on 23 October 1960 and was huge for its day – escalators and all. Its car park, with room for 4,000 cars, was one of the largest in Europe, and to save shoppers the long walk, moving walkways carried them from their cars to the shops. Farsta was billed as the southern suburbs' answer to Vällingby. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Farsta strand. The square by the station is named after the crime writer Stieg Trenter, who was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery by the railway station – then called Södertörns villastad – and young Stieg sometimes lent a hand in the shop. His crime novel Träff i helfigur is set in the streets around here. The planned garden suburb never really took off, though: the plots were slow to sell, mostly because transport links were so poor. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fi: We'll soon reach the final stop, Finnberget. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Fiskebäcks Småbåtshamn. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Fittja. At the metro station you'll find a copy of Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd's sculpture The Knotted Gun, also known as Non-Violence – the most famous version stands outside the UN headquarters in New York. A couple of hundred metres away is Fittja gård. In the 17th and 18th centuries its inn was one of the biggest coaching inns in Sweden, and one of the buildings served as the district courthouse right up until 1916. Today the farm is home to the Multicultural Centre. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Fjällsyran. Rannebergen Centrum was built in 1974 and has its own swimming pool, and just across the street the Bohusleden trail and the Vättlefjäll hills are waiting, with lovely lakes for swimming and fishing. Close by, the Lärjeån Valley nature reserve begins too. It was protected in 2026 and covers more than 1,100 hectares. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Framnäs. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Fredriksdal. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Fridhemsplan. Fridhemsplan is one of Kungsholmen's main hubs, with the metro, buses and plenty of shops. In the 16th century, Kungsholmen was known as Munklägret, 'the Monks' Camp', after the monks who owned land here. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Frihamnen. Stockholm's free port opened as a temporary arrangement in 1919 and kept growing right up until the 1970s. Over much the same period, from 1921 to 1952, seaplanes landed at Lindarängen, where the free port stands today. Fordhuset, the Ford Building, was designed by Uno Åhrén and built between 1929 and 1931 to assemble Ford cars – these days it's home to the stock exchange company Nasdaq. The huge Magasin 6 warehouse was less lucky: it went out of date almost as soon as container shipping took over. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Fritidsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Fruängen. At 46.8 metres above sea level, Fruängen is the highest station on the entire metro network. Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady, has an unusual back story: the church centre opened in 1963, but the actual church hall shown on the original plans wasn't begun until 2004. It was finally consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent in 2005. A block away is Triangelhuset, the Triangle House, from 1955 – named after its one-of-a-kind triangular floor plan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Frölunda Torg. Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 and was one of Sweden's first large suburban shopping centres. All around is Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Frösundavik. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Furulund. Furulund Church is a bit unusual: it's shared by EFS, the Evangelical Homeland Foundation, and the parish of Furulund-Öjersjö. Tucked away nearby is Prästtjärnen, a small lake that's a surprising 14 metres deep for its size. It lies just over 108 metres above sea level and drains into the Göta älv river basin. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Furulunds centrum. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fy: We'll soon reach the final stop, Fyrktorget. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ga: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gamlestads Torg. Gamlestaden means just what it says: the old town. Nya Lödöse was founded here in 1473, long before today's Gothenburg was laid out in 1621. Later the area turned industrial, and this is where the ball-bearing company SKF grew up. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gladö kvarn. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Glasbruksgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Go: We'll soon reach the final stop, Godsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Godsterminalen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Grimbo. Nearby is Gunnestorps mosse, a patchwork of lake, fen and bog in Hisingsparken. Reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow here side by side with cranberries, sundews and cotton grass. North of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, an old croft that's now part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Grötö färjeläge. Grötö is tiny: 84 year-round residents on just under two thirds of a square kilometre. Even so, it has something rare in Bohuslän – a sandy beach. You'll find it in the Grötö Knöten nature reserve at the northern tip of the island, while a glacial ridge of rounded stones runs along the west coast. In summer the kiosk in the main harbour is open, and close to the harbour there's both sand and smooth rocks with a swimming ladder. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gubbängens centrum. Gubbängstorget square was once home to the City cinema, which opened in April 1953 and closed twenty years later. In the 1950s the new suburbs were meant to provide every service their residents could need – right down to a cinema of their own. Today the old auditorium has a new lease of life as Moment teater, a theatre that started here in 2000 and won Svenska Dagbladet's Thalia Prize in 2008 for its work with the classics. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Gullmarsplan. Gullmarsplan is named after Gullmarn, a fjord near Lysekil on the west coast in Bohuslän. The square was built in the 1940s along with the surrounding district, and the metro station opened on 1 October 1950 – before that, trams stopped here. Today it's one of Stockholm's busiest interchanges, where the metro, the Tvärbanan light rail and buses all meet. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Gustavsbergs centrum. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gärdsås Torg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gåshaga brygga. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Gåshaga. Behind the houses is the Käppala plant, which has been treating wastewater since 1969 and is considered one of the most efficient of its kind in the world. A little further away is Käppalaställningen, a Second World War anti-aircraft battery that reopened in 1994 as a memorial to Stockholm's air defences – the only one of its kind in Sweden. Nearby you'll also find M/S Soya III, a tanker built in 1936 to carry soya oil and now used as a conference ship. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Görvälns griftegård. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ha: We'll soon reach the final stop, Hagsätra. Just a stone's throw away is Hagsätra centrum, the local shopping centre, which opened in 1960 – the same year the metro arrived. Look out for 'Barnet med käpphästen', the Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist that has become the centre's emblem. A little further on there's an outdoor pool with a confusing name: Älvsjöbadet, which isn't in Älvsjö at all but right here in Hagsätra. It was built in 1937–1938. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hallonbergen. Head down into the metro and it's like stepping into a child's drawing. The artists Elis Eriksson and Gösta Wallmark decorated the station with childlike pictures inspired by their own early years. The station opened on 31 August 1975, along with the blue line's first stretch between T-Centralen and Hjulsta. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hallunda centrum. The area around this shopping centre in northern Botkyrka has an unusually close-knit cluster of churches. Botkyrka folkhögskola, a folk high school – a kind of adult education college – founded in 1997, is owned by five Christian congregations, three of them Syriac Orthodox, yet it's open to everyone, whatever their faith. Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, on Tomtbergavägen, sits right next to the Syriac Orthodox Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul, while Hallundakyrkan, Hallunda Church, is practically wall to wall with the shopping centre. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen He: We'll soon reach the final stop, Heden. When Trädgårn opened as a café in 1858, all its staff were men, and the only spirit on offer was punsch, a sweet Swedish liqueur. The building beside the stop, Exercishuset – the Drill Hall – was completed in 1867, a gift from the merchant Julius Lindström. Schoolchildren came here for gymnastics, and the volunteer rifle corps used it for drill. Heden itself was the army's parade ground, and until 2019 it had a bandy pitch – bandy being a fast-paced cousin of ice hockey, played with a ball. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Helenelunds station. From here it's 10.9 kilometres by commuter train to Stockholm Central, and on a normal winter weekday about 5,400 people get on here. Next door is Eriksberg, a narrow strip squeezed between the E4 motorway and the railway, named after the Eriksberg croft from 1819. A little further on is Silverdal cemetery, laid out in 1914 as the burial ground for the Stockholm garrison. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Henriksdalsberget. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Henriksdalsviadukten. Beneath Henriksdalsberget hill runs a 337-metre tunnel on Saltsjöbanan, the Saltsjö railway, and trains have been rumbling through it since 1893. The land around Henriksborg was once industrial. From 1882 until the late 1950s, the Rylander and Rudolph factory turned out batteries for wind-up telephones and carbon rods for arc lamps, among other things. And the Danvikcenter office building won a European award for its steelwork in 1987. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hi: We'll soon reach the final stop, Himlabacken. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Hinnebäcksgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen. Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen is the main transport hub on Hisingen, Sweden's fourth-largest island, where both ships and cars were once built. Volvo was founded in Gothenburg in 1927, and its head office is still here on Hisingen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hjulsta. A cavern for the metro was blasted out beneath Hjulstaskolan, the local school, and on 31 August 1975 blue line trains started running here, about 14 kilometres from Kungsträdgården. Close by are the green Hjulsta allotments. Their association was founded in 1973, and today they're held up as a model of multicultural gardening. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Hjuvik. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ho: We'll soon reach the final stop, Hornkamsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hovås Nedre. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Askim Church, the parish church of a parish that stretches along the coast south of Gothenburg and became part of Gothenburg municipality in 1974. The marina in Hovås also has a sea rescue station, and its very first boat, in 1983, was the former pilot boat Alice Olsson. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Huddinge sjukhus. Right next door is the Swedish Red Cross University, Röda Korsets Högskola, Sweden's oldest non-religious nursing school. It was founded in 1867 by Emmy Rappe, who had trained under none other than Florence Nightingale in London. The school began in Uppsala and spent many years at Sabbatsberg Hospital before settling here. A short walk away is Flemingsberg Church, consecrated in 1976. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Huddinge station. Commuter trains stop at Huddinge centrum, the heart of the municipality and its main shopping area. Kommunalvägen runs almost parallel to the Western Main Line for about 1.3 kilometres, and along it you'll pass both Huddinge Church and the municipal offices. Close by are traces of Svartlösa domsaga, an old court district. Its courthouse was designed in 1959 by the architect Karl Karlström, yet the district itself lasted just twelve years before it was abolished in the court reform of 1971. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Hultåsen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Häggvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Härlanda. Behind the walls in Härlanda, prisoners were locked up from 1907 to 1997. The old central prison is now a listed building and goes by the name of Härlanda park. The Saga cinema on Sofiagatan closed in 1964, and the following year it reopened as a grocery shop – Saga Hemköp, the first in the Sagabutikerna chain. Among the buildings there's also the ruin of an old church. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hässelby gård. The assembly hall of the local school, Hässelbygårdsskolan, once doubled as the Prisma cinema, open to the public from November 1960 until December 1984. The school even had its own doctor's surgery and swimming pool. A little further on is Hässelby familjehotell, the 'family hotel' that was master builder Olle Engkvist's largest collective housing block when it opened in 1955. Its staffed services closed in 1976, but residents still keep some of the activities going as volunteers. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Höga hallar. Not far from here is Benareby, nestled between four lakes – Nordsjön, Yxsjön, Finnsjön and Gravsjön. Benareby was once known for its wooden barrels, most of which went to the fish-processing industry, and the coopers' craft is still alive here today. There are also lots of old holiday cottages that people now live in all year round. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Högdalen. Not far from here are three man-made hills built from demolition rubble and bulky waste. The first, Högdalstoppen, was completed in 1964; the rock it sits on had once been the highest point in Högdalen and Fagersjö. Today the hilltops are an outdoor recreation area with a skatepark and a disc golf course. Högdalstoppen 3 is still growing, topped up with soil dug out during road building. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Högnäsvägen. Just a short walk away, in the playground of Klockargården school, Carl Milles' elephants are having fun: his sculpture group Playing Elephants has stood here since 1947. The school dates from 1843, which makes it the oldest one in the municipality still in use. Along Stockholmsvägen in Näset, look out for Näsets krog, a well-preserved 18th-century roadside inn, and Villa Nynäs, where Lidingö's first general store opened in the late 19th century. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Högsätra. The ice rink just along from here became famous across Sweden thanks to the TV series HCZ. It has changed names several times: first Dalénhallen, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén and the nearby AGA factory, then Danske Bank Hallen, and now Childhood Hallen. It's home to Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club, and figure skaters train here too. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Högsätrahuset. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hökarängen. Hökarängen was one of the first suburbs to spring up along the new metro after the Second World War, and David Helldén's car-free town centre became a model for suburbs right across Sweden. Next door is Farsta fire station, which started life as Enskede fire station. And look out for the light, arched roof of Gubbängshallen, visible from far across the open Gubbängsfältet. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hökmossen. Hökmossen was once home to the cottage of Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. Not far away is Hägerstensbadet – Personnebadet to the locals, after Personnevägen – an outdoor pool that opened on 21 June 1961. The water is heated by solar panels, and swimming is free. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hönö färjeläge. The Hönö ferry, Hönöleden, carries more vehicles than any other ferry route in Sweden – just over 2.3 million in 2009. The ferries cross between Lilla Varholmen on Hisingen and the island of Hönö, a 2,500-metre trip that takes twelve minutes. Because it officially counts as part of county road 155, the crossing is free. The fleet includes M/S Ada, M/S Beda, M/S Göta and M/S Marie. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen IA: We'll soon reach the final stop, IAC Group. Sörred's name is far from flattering. It's recorded in 1388 as Surfua rudi, and the first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv – a careless man, a slacker, a good-for-nothing. The second part is the Old Swedish ‘ryd’, a clearing. Yet the slacker's clearing turned out to be anything but idle: this is where construction of Volvo's Torslanda Works began in 1960–1961. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen In: We'll soon reach the final stop, Inseros. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ja: We'll soon reach the final stop, Jakobsbergs sjukhus. A couple of minutes away is Aspnässkolan, the very first school of Järfälla's own parish. It opened in 1846 in a manor house the parish had bought, a building that had once been a roadside tavern. The oldest schoolhouse was pulled down in 1959, but it lives on in a surprising way – today it's a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre. The hospital itself belongs to Region Stockholm, and among other things has a health centre and a pharmacy. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Jakobsbergs station. Jakobsberg is named after a dead man. Jakob Lilliehöök inherited the farms in the village of Vibble, and after he died in 1657 his widow, Brita Cruus, built a manor house and named it after him. Today it's home to Jakobsberg folk high school. By the station is Gula villan, the Yellow Villa – the station building from 1876. The windmill, from the 1840s, burned three times and was never rebuilt after the fire in 2005. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Jarlaberg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Jo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Jons väg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ju: We'll soon reach the final stop, Julitavägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Jungfrusund. Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden bay, on the eastern side of Ekerön island. Out in the water are Jungfruholmarna, two islands belonging to the sailing club Göta segelsällskap. The club leased them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built a clubhouse there in 1955. The Ekeröleden car ferry also crosses the bay here. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Jupitervägen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Jä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Järntorget. Järntorget, the Iron Square, is named after the iron that was weighed and shipped out from here. The fountain in the middle dates from 1927 and depicts the world's five continents. This is where Gothenburg's old working-class districts begin. To the south is Haga, with its cafés and landshövdingehus – the city's typical tenements with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys. To the west run the Långgatorna streets, lined with vintage shops and bars. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Järnvågen. The name means 'the iron scales'. This is where iron shipped out through Gothenburg's harbour was weighed – including iron from the ironworks of Värmland. In the 1780s the city's iron weigh-house moved to a plot just north of today's Järntorget, the Iron Square, which was named after it. The iron porters who carried the heavy bars settled in the blocks around it. The scales themselves are long gone. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Järva närsjukhus. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ka: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kallebäcks Källa. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kanehall. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Karolinska institutet västra. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Karolinska sjukhuset norra. Sweden's first cancer clinic, Radiumhemmet, opened in 1910 in a flat on Kungsholmen, and since 1938 it has been part of the hospital here in Solna. Not far away stood Norrbacka inn, one of Stockholm's best-known coaching inns on the road to Uppsala, until it burned down in 1882. There were also plans for a lookout tower in Hagaparken, but work on it never even began. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kastellholmsbron. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ki: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kippholmen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kista centrum. Kista is the only station on the blue line above ground. It sits on a 1,120-metre viaduct, the longest on the entire metro network. When the station was being named, the naming committee first wanted to add 'Gård', meaning farm, so that nobody would think of a likkista – a coffin. Rising above the shopping centre is Kista torn, the Kista Tower, 120 metres tall. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Klara Mälarstrand. From the quay beside City Hall, Strömma's boats head out onto Lake Mälaren – to Drottningholm and the Viking town of Birka, as well as on lunch and dinner cruises. They run from May until the end of October. Right nearby is the mouth of Klara sjö, the canal that separates Kungsholmen from Norrmalm and links Barnhusviken bay with Riddarfjärden. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Klareberg. Klareberg in Kärra is where the buses get a breather. Drivers like to take their break here, and the big bus stop serves routes to Kungälv, Angered and Gothenburg. But the area is also popular with horse riders and dog owners, who come here to ride and to train their dogs. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Klippans Färjeläge. Klippan takes its name from Skinnareklippan, the rock on which St Birgitta's Chapel stands. The chapel was consecrated in 1857 and designed by A W Edelsvärd, using drawings of a Scottish church that the brewer David Carnegie had brought back with him. Carnegie's brewery is a hotel today. You'll also find the remains of the Gamla Älvsborg fortress here, which Sweden bought back from the Danes in 1619. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Klubbacken. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kn: We'll soon reach the final stop, Knalleborg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ko: We'll soon reach the final stop, Komettorget. Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan, Meteorgatan – that's Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön, the street names come straight from outer space. Close by is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, with the Bergsjön culture centre. It has a library, a café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, with everything on offer from music and art to children's activities. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kongahällagatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kornhalls Färja. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Korseberget. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kottla station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ku: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungsbacka station. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungssten. Kungssten is close to the mouth of Göta älv, the Göta River. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966. Out in the estuary is the 17th-century Nya Älvsborg fortress, which guarded the city against the Danes. Down by the water is Klippan, with old seamen's cottages and the ruins of the earlier Älvsborg fortress. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungälv resecentrum. Buses for Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsund and Tjörn pull in at the travel centre, and right next door is Kongahälla Center, a shopping centre opened in 2019 with around a hundred shops and restaurants. The E6 motorway roars past just alongside. A little further on is Oasen, a swimming pool and ice rink built after the old baths burned down. Inside there's a 25-metre pool and a warmer pool for rehabilitation. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungälvs sjukhus södra. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kv: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kvarnhagen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kvarter 13. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Källbrinks idrottsplats. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kärna bussterminal. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kärrtorp. From Kärrtorp you can walk all the way to the Nacka nature reserve, Nackareservatet, so the forest is never far away. Closer by are the Reflexen cinema, which has been showing films since 1961, and Kärrtorpshallen, a sports hall from the early 1960s designed by Kjell Ödeen and recognised by the City Museum as a building of heritage value. Kärrtorpsparken, the local park, only got its present name in 2009, but at its southern end you'll find the old crofter's cottage that gave the whole district its name. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kållered station. Kållered station has had two lives. The first opened in 1891 and closed in 1972. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka came back, a new station opened on 17 August 1992, and in the rush hour there are now trains every fifteen minutes in each direction. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kålleredgården. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kålsered. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Körkarlens gata. On 3 April 1973, OBS opened in Bäckebol – 30,000 square metres and, at the time, the biggest hypermarket in the country. Long before that, Bäckebol was a farm. Work on its stone manor house began in 1764 under the weighmaster Johan Oliveholm, and it has been a listed building since 1969. The owners of the estate even have their own private burial ground, in use since the mid-1700s. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen La: We'll soon reach the final stop, Landvetter resecentrum. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Larsberg. Up on the hill are the Larsberg blocks, with their brick-red façades, green metal roofs and white balconies – classic 1960s style. Just over 1,200 flats were finished here in 1969, all designed by the architect Bengt Gate. Down below is Malmstens, where students learn furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery. The old hospital building in Högsätra was due to be demolished during 2025 to make room for a new district, Kärnan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Le: We'll soon reach the final stop, Lektorsstigen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Li: We'll soon reach the final stop, Liljeholmen. The Rosteriet block takes its name from a German roastery that produced coffee substitute here from 1913 to 1920. Pharmacia later made medicines on the site, and in the 1950s and 60s AB Atomenergi manufactured fuel rods for Swedish research reactors. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill is Brännkyrka's old parish hall from the 1920s, which since 2003 has been home to Nordiska Musikgymnasiet, a music high school. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Lilla Dalens begravningsplats. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lilla Varholmen. Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. A bridge links it to Hisingen, and from here car ferries set off for the islands of Öckerö municipality, on both the Björkö route and the Hönö route. The Björkö crossing is only about 900 metres and takes around five minutes. The island has lighthouses too – the leading lights in use today date from 1927. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lillebyvägen. Lilleby, by the sea on Hisingen, was farmland for a long time and belonged to the parish of Björlanda until it became part of Gothenburg in 1967. As early as 1846 the land was reorganised here under the great Swedish land reform known as laga skifte. Today new housing is springing up fast. The district covers 1,330 hectares and is also home to Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside holiday colony whose 1950s cabins have been preserved. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Lillövägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lindholmen. For many years Lindholmen was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. Where ships were once built, you'll now find Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology. From the quay there's a view straight across the river to the city centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lindholmspiren. The pier sits by the old shipyards on Lindholmen, where ships were built for more than a hundred years. Today it's home to Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology, and from the quay you can look straight across the river to the city centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lindome station. Lindome station has died and come back to life. It opened on 1 September 1888, when the Gothenburg–Halland Railway was completed, but passenger trains stopped calling in 1970 and the station shut down altogether in 1989. Then commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka started running again, and on 17 August 1992 it made its comeback. In 2012 it was rebuilt to handle longer trains. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lindvreten. Lindvreten was a croft belonging to Vårby manor, and the name probably means ‘the patch of land with the lime trees’. Nearby was another croft, Månskär. Its odd name has nothing to do with a crescent moon, or ‘månskära’ – it comes from Måns, one of the first tenants, and ‘kärr’, the word for marsh. This is also where you'll find Södra djursjukhuset, the Southern Animal Hospital, which started out in 1967 with two people working in a villa. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Linnéplatsen. Linnéplatsen is the gateway to Slottsskogen, the city's great park, laid out in 1874. It has animals, ponds and the Natural History Museum, home to a stuffed blue whale from 1865. In the other direction runs Linnégatan, one of Gothenburg's best-loved streets for eating out. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Lise Meitners gata. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Liseberg Station. We're on the north side of Liseberg. The amusement park opened in 1923 as part of the city's anniversary exhibition, and today it's one of the most visited in the Nordic region. At Christmas it turns into a Christmas market glittering with millions of lights. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Lj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ljungkullen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Ljusterögatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Lu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Lunda industri. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lundbystrand. Götaverken once built ships here, and its old shipyard halls have found some surprising new uses. Curling has been played in a former workshop since 2001, and the old sheet-metal shop is now Lundbystrandshallen, a sports hall with five handball courts. The glass building by the water, Kanalhuset, was built for the camera maker Hasselblad, which soon moved out. Today it's where SVT and Sveriges Radio, Sweden's public television and radio, broadcast from. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Luxgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Lå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Långsjö torg. The businessman Robert Ditzinger was a considerate father. In 1882 he had two identical main houses built on Långsjö farm, one for each of his two sons. The farm later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö, which stretches down to Långsjön lake on the Huddinge side. Not far from here runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows Göta landsväg, the old highway south. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ma: We'll soon reach the final stop, Marklandsgatan. The street is named after 'markland', an old unit used to value land. Right next door is Frölundaborg, the ice hockey arena, which opened in 1967 with a friendly in which Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national team 4–3. And past Slottsskogsvallen, where high jumpers like Patrik Sjöberg and Stefan Holm trained, winds Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Way. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Masthugget. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Me: We'll soon reach the final stop, Merkuriusgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Mo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Moa Martinsons torg. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Mossvägen. Stora Ursvik borders Kymlinge, Lilla Ursvik, Rissne and Rinkeby. Not far from here, on a hill by the Rissne interchange, stands the Stora Stampan windmill. Its neighbour, Holländskan, burned down in 1989, but Stora Stampan was restored over the winter of 2019–2020 and now has new sails. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Motalavägen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Mö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Mölndals Innerstad. Welcome to Mölndal. Along the rapids in Mölndals kvarnby, the mill village, water power has driven mills and factories for several hundred years. Today the mill village is a heritage area with a museum and cafés. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Mölndals bro. Mölndal means 'mill valley', and the rapids behind the name are just nearby. Mills have stood by the rapids in Kvarnbyn, the Mill Village, since the 14th century, and until the 17th century most of them belonged to the Crown. The falls stretch for around 800 metres and drop about 45 to 48 metres. Their power later drove local industry, and today Kvarnbyn is protected as a heritage site of national interest, with the Mölndal City Museum right beside the rapids. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Mölnlycke resecentrum. Trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop at Mölnlycke station – but it hasn't always been in this spot. When it opened in 1894 it stood about 350 metres further east, and it only moved to where it is now in 2003. The old station building was pulled down in 2013. Not far away is Wallenstam Arena, where the floorball team Pixbo Wallenstam IBK play their home games in front of crowds of up to 1,600. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Mörby station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Na: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nacka Forum. Nacka Forum opened on 1 March 1989, taking over from a makeshift shopping centre in prefab huts that had had to do for years. Right next to it begins Storängen, an idyllic area of villas, where Villa Wållgren from 1907 has been judged irreplaceable. A stone's throw away is Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg and built in 1907 for the future city commissioner and his wife Elin, née Bonnier. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Nacka gymnasium. You won't be short of classrooms around here. Nacka gymnasium is one of Sweden's biggest sixth-form schools, and next door Eklidens skola is one of the largest secondary schools in the country, with an ice rink and a swimming pool right beside it. The name Järla comes from jarl, the old Norse title for an earl. In nearby Vikdalen, Stockholm families built summer villas in the late 1800s, arriving by steamboat. Then the car engine factory opened in Augustendal, workers moved in, and the villas became workers' homes. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Nacka sjukhus. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Nacka strand. For a long time Nacka strand went by the name Augustendal. The industrial pioneer J.V. Svenson bought the land in 1899, and by 1916 his engine factory employed 500 people, making it one of the biggest workplaces in Sweden. The company went bankrupt in 1922 and Handelsbanken took it over. Offices and flats followed in the 1980s, and in 1988 the area was renamed Nacka strand. Down in the marina, look out for Carl Milles' sculpture God the Father on the Rainbow, which has been sending an arc of water out over Saltsjön bay since 1995. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ni: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nils Ericson Terminalen. Gothenburg will soon have a brand-new station right beneath your feet. The glass terminal itself was designed by the Norwegian architect Niels Torp and won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 1996. Over in the Nordstan shopping centre is Emotrappan, the Emo Stairs, where punks and hard rockers were hanging out as far back as the 1980s. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Nils Ericsonsplatsen. Nils Ericsonsplatsen is named after Nils Ericson, the man who built Sweden's first main railway lines – and the brother of the inventor John Ericsson. Deep beneath us, Västlänken, the West Link, is under construction: a railway tunnel running under central Gothenburg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen No: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nockeby. St Birgitta's Church was built in 1960–62 and consecrated in December 1962. The architect Rolf Bergh designed the church, its bell tower and the parish hall beside it. Here in Nockeby, the architect Sven Markelius also built his own villa in 1930 – one of the first homes built in the new functionalist style. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Nockebyhov. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Norsborg. This is as far west as the metro goes: Norsborg is the westernmost station on the whole network and has been the end of the red line since 1975. A short walk away is the Botkyrka poorhouse. Built in 1798, it took in the poor until 1911 and then served as an old people's home and nursing home. Since 1998 it has been full of schoolchildren again, as the independent school Botkyrka friskola holds its lessons here. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ny: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nybroplan. Here at Nybroplan stands Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, opened in 1908. This is where Strandvägen begins, with its grand turn-of-the-century buildings along the waterfront, and from Nybrokajen quay the boats head out into the archipelago. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Nyfors. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Nä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nämdöstigen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Näsbovägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Näsbypark. Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, arrived here in 1937, when the Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar company extended the line from Lahäll, and this is where the branch ends. Näsbypark is known as one of Täby's more exclusive neighbourhoods, with villas and terraced houses close to the water at Stora Värtan bay. Right beside the station is Näsbypark Church, part of Täby parish. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Näset. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Od: We'll soon reach the final stop, Odenplan. Gustav Vasa Church stands on Odenplan. Just a short way off, on Sveavägen, is Stadsbiblioteket, the Stockholm Public Library, designed by Gunnar Asplund and famous for its round lending hall. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Op: We'll soon reach the final stop, Opaltorget. We're in Tynnered, where the streets are named after gemstones: Opaltorget, Smaragdgatan and Briljantgatan – Opal Square, Emerald Street and Diamond Street. From here, it isn't far to the nature reserves and seaside swimming spots of Västra Frölunda. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Or: We'll soon reach the final stop, Orhem. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Paradistorget. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Parksidan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Partille centrum. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pe: We'll soon reach the final stop, Pelikanvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Peppareds torg. Not far from here, an old barn has been turned into a theatre. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is home to six amateur dramatic societies. Since 1998 it has staged revues and comedies, mostly by young people – and there's even an English-language theatre group in the building. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Peppargatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Persiljegatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pi: We'll soon reach the final stop, Pilotvägen. Thank you for riding with us!
