Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Po: We'll soon reach the final stop, Polhemsplatsen. The square was named in 1883 after the inventor Christopher Polhem. This is where you'll find the GP building, which the newspaper Göteborgs-Posten moved into in 1935 and which is still the headquarters of the Stampen media group. A stone's throw away is a statue of Gunnar Gren, one third of the famous Gre-No-Li trio and one of Gothenburg's most successful footballers of the 20th century. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Pumpgatan. The shipbuilding giant Götaverken was based here right up until 1991, and its old shipyard halls now live on as sports halls. Kanalhuset, by the water, was designed for the camera maker Hasselblad, which moved out after only a short time; today SVT and Swedish Radio broadcast from there. And Lundbybadet, the public baths from 1915, became a karate club when the last bath attendant, Ante Melander, hung up his towel in 1973. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ra: We'll soon reach the final stop, Radiohuset. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Rannebergen Centrum. Rannebergen sits high up, right on the edge of nature. Just a few minutes away is Idtjärnet, a woodland lake 109 metres above sea level, and a little further off is Stora Mölnesjön, with a swimming spot and a jetty. The local centre, complete with a swimming pool and a pizzeria, was built in 1974, and the Bohusleden hiking trail and the Vättlefjäll hills are right on its doorstep. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Re: We'll soon reach the final stop, Redbergsplatsen. Redbergsplatsen square was once called Korsvägen and was given its current name in 1883. A public water pump was installed here in 1873, letting people enjoy fresh water from Lake Delsjön. Just north of the square, in the Redbergslid People's Park, a pavilion with a stage for performers went up in 1886. And below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, stands the bronze fountain group Elementens kamp, the Struggle of the Elements, which was moved here from Olskrokstorget in 1968. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Reimersholme. Reimersholme is a small island named after Anders Reimers, who owned it in the 1700s. For many years it had a schnapps distillery, and the name Reimersholms lived on on the bottle labels. Today it's a peaceful residential island with a waterside path all the way around. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ri: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rinkeby centrum. Step down into Rinkeby metro station and you'll find yourself in a Viking treasure chamber. The artist Nisse Zetterberg took small Viking Age finds dug up in the area and blew them up into huge mosaics on brick-red walls, inlaid with gold and runes. The station opened in 1975, when the blue line was inaugurated. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Rissne. Rissne is the only metro station in Stockholm with its name carved in runes. The name also appears on a runestone in Sigtuna, raised in memory of “Gunnar's son in Risnö”. In 1640 the Rissne estate was bought by Reinhold Goevert Leuhusen, secretary to the Admiralty. Today Rissne gård is a restaurant and conference venue. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ro: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rondovägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ropsten. From Ropsten, the Lidingöbanan line runs across the Lidingö Bridge out to Lidingö. The bridge opened in 1925, and for many years it was the only road link to the island. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ru: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ruddammen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Rudsjöterrassen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ry: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rymdtorget Buss. Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970 and is the heart of Bergsjön, where the streets are named after space and the universe – Tellusgatan, for example. On the square is Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the local culture centre, with a library, a café, studios, an exhibition hall and even a music studio. There's everything on offer from music and art to crafts and children's events. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Rö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rörby FRA. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Rörby gård. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen S:: We'll soon reach the final stop, S:t Eriksplan. Behind the triangular park lies one of Stockholm's most talked-about unsolved crimes. On 4 May 1932, Lilly Lindeström was found murdered in her flat at Sankt Eriksplan 11 – the case known as the Vampire Murder. There are happier memories just round the corner: the Capitol cinema, which opened in 1926, closed in 1985 and then came back to life in 2018 as Bio & Bistro Capitol. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Saltholmen – the gateway to Gothenburg's southern archipelago. From here, ferries run out to car-free islands like Brännö, Styrsö and Vrångö, and the boats are covered by the same ticket as the tram. Take a dip at the open-air bathhouse, or hop on the next boat out. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Saltholmen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Saltängen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sankt Sigfrids Plan. Örgryte's old cemetery goes back to the 13th century, and many well-known Gothenburg names are buried here – three bishops among them. The old church is one of the city's favourite places to get married, with around sixty weddings a year. Look out for the bronze statue by the main entrance: it's called Genomkämpat, 'The Struggle Is Over', and the original stands in a cemetery in Berlin. And on the spot where the old ossuary once stood, the merchant Julius Lindström was given a family grave in 1870 – in return for paying for a new ossuary. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Se: We'll soon reach the final stop, Sergels torg. Sergels torg is Stockholm's modern centre, with its black-and-white paved pattern known as Plattan and the glass obelisk rising from the fountain. Kulturhuset, the House of Culture, with its library and exhibitions, stands on the square. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Servicehuset Tor. The Holmia neighbourhood was laid out in 1906 by a newly formed company, AB Lidingö Villastad, and it still looks much as it did in the early 1900s, with villas in the National Romantic, Art Nouveau and Art Nouveau Baroque styles. It's also home to Lidingö Museum, housed in the former Villa Fornboda from 1907, with exhibitions on Lidingö's 20th century and a turn-of-the-century drawing room. The museum is run by the Lidingö local history society – one of the largest in Sweden – which also organises Bellman Day, among other events. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Si: We'll soon reach the final stop, Sickla udde. A hundred years ago, much of the land around Hammarby sjö lake simply wasn't there. In 1925 a new canal was blasted through the Danvik cliffs, and the lake dropped by about five metres. The newly exposed shoreline was built up with blasted rock, and an area of car workshops and small industries called Lugnet grew up on it. Today it's the site of Hammarby sjöstad, a new waterfront district built between 1994 and 2020. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sickla. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sillvik. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sk: We'll soon reach the final stop, Skarpnäck. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skarpnäcks gård. The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as far back as 1318, and in 1660 Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace turned Skarpnäck into a manor estate. The present main house was built in the 1860s by the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, and under his ownership the estate enjoyed its golden age. The district itself was created in 1963 out of Pungpinan and Skarpnäck, and its metro station, opened in 1994, lies in a cavern blasted out of the rock 25 metres underground. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skintebo. Right in the middle of a Swedish seaside villa neighbourhood stands a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm. Skintebo in Billdal was farmland for a long time, but in the 1970s Skintebodalen was built up with car-free paths, terraced houses, two-storey wooden houses and ‘boatswain's houses’ – a quirky cross between a terraced house and a villa. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Skoga äldrecentrum. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Skogome. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skogskyrkogården. Sandsborg, an old farm and inn, gave its name to both a cemetery and a metro station here in Gamla Enskede. A short walk away is the Museum of the Visually Impaired, housed in what was once the Technical Factory for the Blind; its collections trace the history of blind and partially sighted people in Sweden back to the late 18th century. And inside Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, you'll find Almhöjden, the Elm Hill – a mound crowned with weeping elms that looks like something out of a Caspar David Friedrich painting. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skra Bro. The name is said to come from the scraping noise sledge runners made on the bare ground during a thaw. The old bridge over Osbäcken stream is still here, right beside us, but these days it's just a footbridge between the park-and-ride and a supermarket. Cars now cross a larger road bridge north of the roundabout. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skälltorpsvägen. Not far from here is Lillhagsparken hospital, originally Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. It no longer provides any care – the forensic psychiatric unit moved out in 2013. Closer to the stop stood Hökälla, an old manor estate in Skogome. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skärholmen. Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen Centre on 8 September 1968. It was planned as a regional shopping centre serving 250,000 people across southern Greater Stockholm, and it's still one of the largest in Sweden. The centre was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive, and it's listed in the SOS Brutalism database of brutalist concrete architecture. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Skärvik. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skårs Kyrka. Right next to us, it smells like Christmas all year round. Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, was founded in 1924 and these days bakes just one thing: citrus-flavoured ginger biscuits made to a secret recipe. The shop on Sankt Sigfridsgatan still has its original 1940 interior, and the bakery has been awarded a diploma by the Gastronomic Academy for its unrivalled biscuits. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sköndalsbro. Sköndalsbro began as a croft, a small tenant farm, whose main house probably went up sometime between 1700 and 1750 – or perhaps later. The streets around here are a small open-air architecture museum. Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl as his own home, and the husband-and-wife architects Hanna and Roy Victorson built Villa Victorson. Both houses, from 1955 and 1958, are marked blue by the City Museum for their exceptional cultural and historical value. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Slussen. Slussen is where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic waters of Saltsjön, and where Södermalm meets Gamla stan, the Old Town. There have been locks here since the 17th century, and right now the whole area is being rebuilt in one of Stockholm's biggest construction projects. From the quays you can look out over Gamla stan, Skeppsholmen and Djurgården. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Slåttervägen. Right next door is Viksjö gård, a manor and former noble estate held in the 1600s by the Skytte family, among others. The manor sits up on a hill, and modern Viksjö has grown up around it on what used to be its fields. A little further away, in Jakobsberg, the Järfällabadet swimming centre opened in 2018. It replaced the old pool from 1971, which had a 48-metre water slide. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sn: We'll soon reach the final stop, Snipen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen So: We'll soon reach the final stop, Solbacka. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Solgård. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sollentuna station. Ten tower blocks line Malmvägen, with 1,247 flats between them – which is why locals call the street ‘Tian’, ‘the Ten’. The service building, designed by Åke Arell, drew international attention when it opened in 1972, with preschools, shops and rooms for local clubs all on the ground floor. Overlooking the square is the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, which houses the municipal offices and, since 2023, the library too. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Solna centrum. Deep beneath your feet, 27 to 36 metres down in the bedrock, is the metro station, opened in 1975. Above it is one of the biggest shopping centres in the Stockholm region, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants. Across Centralvägen lies Eric Grates park, named after the sculptor who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. That's where you'll find his bronzes Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Solna station. Råsundavägen 45 was once home to a cinema, the Savoy. In 1974 the auditorium became the Marcus Music recording studio – according to Studio Sound magazine, the first in Sweden with a 24-track tape machine. Abba recorded most of The Album here in 1977. Today it's called Soundtrade Studios, and over the years artists such as Robyn and Joey Tempest have recorded here. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Solna strand. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sp: We'll soon reach the final stop, Spånga station. The name Spånga turns up in writing as early as 1300, as 'apud Ecclesiam spangar'. It comes from the old church village and simply means 'footbridges' – a few narrow planks across the water. The station is on the Mälarbanan railway, a little over eleven kilometres from Central Station. A bit further away is Svandammen, the Swan Pond, a park with a swimming spot that's popular with teenagers and families alike. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen St: We'll soon reach the final stop, Stenhuggarevägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Stenpiren. We're now heading down towards Göta älv, the Göta River, and Stenpiren pier. In the 1800s and early 1900s, more than a million Swedes left for a new life in America, and most of them went via Gothenburg. Many boarded their ships right here. Today the Älvsnabben ferry crosses the river from this spot, and your tram ticket covers it too. On the far bank are Lindholmen and Eriksberg, where the city's great shipyards once stood. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sticklinge. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Stockholms östra. Next to the station is Nymble, the engineering students' union building from 1930, designed by Sven Markelius and Uno Åhrén. Ever since, the students have held their gasques – formal student dinners – in Gasqueparken with its fountain. On the other side of Valhallavägen is Lärkstaden, where the architects Per Olof Hallman and Erik Josephson designed villas for themselves around 1910. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Storkällan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Strandbergsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Strömdal. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Stuvsta station. Häradsvägen, which ends a little way from here at the Stuvsta tunnel, was built in the mid-1920s as a public relief project by the road association of Svartlösa härad, the old local district – hence the name. Forest had to be cleared to make way for it, and villas soon sprang up along its length. The tunnel is a curiosity in its own right: its northern entrance is built into a block of flats that straddles the approach. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Styrsö Bratten. Styrsö is one of the largest islands in Gothenburg's southern archipelago. People live here all year round, and the island has sheltered coves for swimming, meadows and old fishing villages. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Styrsö Tången. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Stärtered. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Su: We'll soon reach the final stop, Sundbybergs station. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sundhammar. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sv: We'll soon reach the final stop, Svalnäs Gästhem. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Svarte Mosse. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Svedmyra T-stn. Despite its name, Svedmyra metro station isn't in Svedmyra at all, but in Stureby. A stone's throw away are the Svedmyra baths from 1969, where the water is kept at a toasty 32 to 34 degrees for warm-water exercise. A little further off stood the Enskede ski jump, which opened in 1924 and hosted ski-jumping competitions right up until 1990. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Svingeln. Up on the hill nearby is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Redoubt, a 17th-century fortification crowned with a gilded lion. It was built to protect the city from attack from the east. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Säteriet. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sätra äng. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Säve Depå. Hidden inside the rock not far from here is Aeroseum, an aviation centre in an underground cavern. It was once the rock hangar of the Göta Wing air base, one of only five ever built by the Swedish Air Force. Since 2000, visitors have been able to head down into the bunker and get up close to aviation history. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Säve Flygplats. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Säve Station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Södergarnsvägen. Östra Rudboda was built in the mid-1970s: just over 450 terraced and linked houses grouped around shared courtyards, known locally as ‘tun’. Today the area is recognised as part of the municipality's cultural heritage. Neighbouring Yttringe takes its name from the large meadows that have been there for centuries. A little further on is Gråviken, an important spot for seabirds and a nature area of national interest. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Södersjukhuset. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sörgårdsskolan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sörredsmotet. Western Hisingen is the land of heavy industry and docks. Not far from here is the Preemraff oil refinery, which gets most of its crude oil from the North Sea. In neighbouring Arendal, the Arendal shipyard was in business from 1963 to 1989; today the site is home to Volvo Buses' headquarters, among others. Arendal is so thoroughly industrial that in 2012 only 90 people actually lived there. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sörskogen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen T-: We'll soon reach the final stop, T-Centralen. Down beneath the streets, blue vines and leaves climb across the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and if you look closely among the tendrils you'll spot silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was otherwise best known for his mechanical sculptures, and in 1966 he helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, 'She – a Cathedral'. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ta: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tanto. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Tappström. Tappström is a narrow channel between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön, about one and a half kilometres long and only just over three metres deep. On its shore, the architect Ralph Erskine designed the Ekerö centrum shopping centre, completed in 1991, with a “dot” more than twenty metres tall as its landmark. Erskine lived on Lovön himself and said he enjoyed coming over here to do his shopping. From here, commuter boat 89 runs all the way into central Stockholm, to Stadshuskajen by the City Hall. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Te: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tekniska högskolan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Telefonplan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Tengdahlsgatan. We're in Sofia, the easternmost part of Södermalm. From here you can wander through Vita bergen and SoFo, or head down to the water at Hammarby sjö, Lake Hammarby. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Tensta centrum. If you'd like to step straight back into 1969, visit Kämpingebacken 13, a museum flat rented by the City Museum. The interior has been kept just as it was, showing what life looked like when Tensta was built during the Million Programme housing drive between 1966 and 1972. Tensta konsthall, a centre for contemporary art, is only a couple of minutes away too. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen To: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tomteboda postterminal. This vast postal terminal was once counted among the largest single buildings in Sweden, and mail was sorted here from 1983. When the sorting stopped, new tenants moved in, and in 2021 SL, Stockholm's public transport authority, opened the biggest bus depot in the Nordic countries in part of the building. Two fragments of a Viking Age runestone have been found in the grounds of Tomtebodaskolan, the local school. One of them turned up in 1903 but had most likely gone missing again by 1911. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Torslandakrysset. Not far from here, on the western side of Hisingen island and about 15 kilometres from central Gothenburg, is the old airfield: Torslanda Airport, built in 1923. For more than fifty years it was the city's airport, until Landvetter took over in 1977. Today Torslanda is best known for Volvo's car factory, Torslandaverken. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Torvmossegränd. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Tr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Trekanten. Until the mid-1800s, the lake you can see, Trekanten, was called Trehörningen. On its northern shore lay Nynäs, a rough-and-ready working-class suburb with a tannery, a coffee roastery and workshops, plus a bakery famous locally for its Nynäs loaf. As the buildings fell into decay, they found a new role as a film set for Bo Widerberg's 1970 film Joe Hill, standing in for the “Lumberyard” and the “Saloon”. The last of them were torn down in 1980. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Trollbäckens centrum. Trollbäcken is a borrowed name. The area used to be called Kumla, after the medieval manor on Lake Drevviken, but in 1947 the villa neighbourhoods renamed themselves Trollbäcken to avoid being mixed up with the town of Kumla in Närke. A couple of hundred metres away, beside county road 260, stands Trollbäcken Church. The manor itself is still known as Kumla herrgård, Kumla Manor, and since 2013 it has been home to a restaurant and conference centre. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Tu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tulebohöjd. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Tullinge station södra. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Tumba station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ty: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tyresö centrum. The tall building you can see from miles away is Tyresö View. At 82 metres and 23 storeys, it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County in 2016. Beneath the glass roof of the shopping centre are around 70 shops, the town hall and a library with its own exhibition hall. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Tyresö kyrka. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Tä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Täby centrum. Täby centrum has 215 shops and 34 restaurants and cafés, and since 2022 its official name has been Westfield Täby Centrum. The Filmstaden cinema, which opened in 2013, has five screens and 516 seats in all. And the library holds something a great deal older: fragments of Viking Age runestones found in Lissby in 1930. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ul: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ulriksdals begravningsplats. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Un: We'll soon reach the final stop, Universitetet. Deep under the campus, scientists once carried out research in accelerator physics. Since 2019 the old laboratory has been an art space called Accelerator, opened by the artist Tino Sehgal. The lab is named after Manne Siegbahn, winner of the 1924 Nobel Prize in Physics. Ralph Erskine designed Juristernas hus, the House of Law, as a semicircle wrapped around an old oak – and the same idea of sparing the oaks shaped Aula Magna too. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ur: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ursviks holme. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Va: We'll soon reach the final stop, Varmfrontsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Varvsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Vasaplatsen. We're in Vasastaden, with its grand stone apartment buildings from the late 1800s. Several University of Gothenburg buildings are here too, and Vasaparken, the park with the university's main building, is right next door. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vi: We'll soon reach the final stop, Vikdalsvägen. Jarlaberg water tower stands 47.5 metres tall and has been a landmark in south-east Stockholm ever since it was finished in 1987. A little further on, in Augustendal, Johan Victor Svenson bought two old summer houses in 1899, planning to build a car factory. But car technology was moving too fast, so he made paraffin engines instead, sold under the name Avance – and they soon became a hit. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Virginsgatan. We're coming into Kålltorp, a quiet residential area of villas and flats in eastern Gothenburg. From here it's not far to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve of lakes and forest. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Torslanda PVH. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Torslanda RA. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Torslanda TA. The Torslanda Works, first known as the Volvo Torslanda factory, was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic countries when it opened. Building began in 1960–1961 in the district of Sörred, and the name has an amusing origin. The first part, Sör-, is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a careless man, a slob or a good-for-nothing, while the ending -red comes from Old Swedish ryd, cleared land. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Torslanda TK. The stop is right by Volvo's car plant, Torslandaverken. Building work began on 4 November 1957, and King Gustaf VI Adolf opened the factory on 24 April 1964. The first car off the line was a Volvo Amazon, and the sporty P1800 was built here from the very beginning too. Today the cars made in Torslanda include the XC90. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Tuve L B. At 199 square kilometres, Hisingen accounts for roughly half of Gothenburg municipality. The island is part of Västra Götaland County and is the fifth largest in Sweden. Water surrounds it on every side: Göta älv, Nordre älv and the Kattegat. About a quarter of the island belongs to the province of Västergötland, the rest to Bohuslän. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvohallen. The dome-shaped building is Volvohallen, an exhibition hall built by Volvo Cars in 1975 and designed by the architects Lund & Valentin. Volvo's Torslanda plant, Torslandaverken, was built in the district of Sörred, a village whose name is recorded as early as 1388 as Surfua rudi. Sörred was part of Björlanda parish until it became part of Gothenburg in 1967. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Vrångö. Vrångö is the southernmost inhabited island in the Gothenburg archipelago. It has a nature reserve with sandy beaches and rocky shores facing the open sea. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Väderilsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Vällingby. Vällingby was planned as an 'ABC town', with arbete, bostad and centrum – work, home and town centre – all in one place. It even had its own cinema: Fontänen opened in 1956, named after the fountains in the square. The same year saw the opening of Trappan, the civic centre, built in terraces between a lower and an upper square. Both were designed by the architects Backström & Reinius. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Västra Röd. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Vårbergs sjukhem. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Wa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Waldemarsudde. Waldemarsudde was the home of the artist Prince Eugen, son of King Oscar II and one of the leading landscape painters of his day. Today his waterside villa and garden are an art museum. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Yn: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ynglingagatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Yt: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ytterby station. Just a couple of minutes' walk away are the ruins of Ytterby Old Church. It was built in the 12th century, when this area belonged to Norway, and legend has it that Saint Olaf himself built it. It served as the parish church until 1870. The railway station on the Bohusbanan line is much younger – it opened in 1907. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Äl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Älvnäs. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Älvsjö station. Älvsjö gård has deep roots, with owners known by name from the mid-15th century. One family held the estate for almost two hundred years, right up until 1968. For a long time hardly anyone lived in the area: around 1900 the population was mainly people working on the estate or at the station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Åk: We'll soon reach the final stop, Åkareplatsen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Åkerby industriområde. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen År: We'll soon reach the final stop, Årsringsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Årstaberg. Årstalänken offers an unusual sight. The eastern part of this stretch of motorway has been closed since 2004 – a 'ruin motorway', as it's known – and there are now plans to build housing on it. Årstaberg commuter rail station sees around 8,300 people board on a normal winter weekday, and the Tvärbanan light rail has stopped here since 2000. Along Årstaskogs väg rise the Årstahusen, three residential tower blocks built between 2017 and 2020. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Öc: We'll soon reach the final stop, Öckerö färjeläge. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ös: We'll soon reach the final stop, Österlyckan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Östervägen. Artillerigården, the Artillery Yard, has served the army's gunners since the 1640s, and today it houses the Army Museum. Hidden beneath it are two Second World War air-raid shelters, which are occasionally opened for guided tours. Just round the corner, at Artillerigatan 14, was the Michelin-starred restaurant Gastrologik, where there was no menu – the chefs decided what you ate. Since 2024 the restaurant ergo has taken over the same premises. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Östhammarsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snickarglädje och kupoltorn: Gingerbread trim and a domed tower
Snöklockan, bara för skönhetens skull: The Snowdrop, purely for beauty's sake
Snörom fick troligen sitt namn av att de: Snörom probably got its name because the old country road to Erstavik made a sharp bend here. The croft is known from 1691 and has, among other things, been home to the parish clerk at Nacka's old church.
Sockenstugan och Bromma kyrka: Sockenstugan, the old parish hall, and Bromma Church
Sockerbruket fick bygglov 1763 och växte: The sugar refinery got planning permission in 1763 and grew to six storeys, visible across all of Ladugårdslandet and Norrmalm. Many considered it one of the ugliest buildings in Stockholm. It was later used as a mess hall for the Svea Artillery Regiment and as a store for the Opera's scenery, among other things.
Socknen är småkuperad bergsterräng med o: The parish is a landscape of low, rolling rocky hills with farmland in the hollows and a little archipelago. It has two nature reserves: Sillvik and the Nordre älv estuary, which is part of the EU's Natura 2000 network.
Socknens gamla medeltida kyrka ödelades: The parish's old medieval church was laid waste during the Northern Seven Years' War. Thanks to taxes and generous gifts from the parish's poor, it was rebuilt and completed in 1622. Today the only reminder of the site is a grave marked by a stone slab from 1728.
Sofielundsskolan har ett eget litet kapi: Sofielundsskolan, the school here, has its own small place in local school history: from 1994, the newly founded Sollentuna Fria Gymnasium, an upper secondary school, used it as a temporary base for its academic classes. Right beside it runs Sollentunavägen, which was the main road between Stockholm and Uppsala until the Uppsalavägen highway was expanded in the 1950s. A little further on is Sollentuna Hospital, opened in 1978 and completely renovated between 2015 and 2020.
Solbergaskogen har en rik svampflora, me: Solbergaskogen has a rich variety of fungi, such as pine bracket and cauliflower fungus, which grow only on old pine trees. The red-listed beefsteak fungus has been found on several oaks, and amethyst deceivers grow in the hazel grove.
Solgård var förr främst ett sommarstugeo: Solgård used to be mainly an area of summer cottages. Today the houses often sit on steep plots, seeming to cling to the slopes. Up to the north are early 20th-century villas in the National Romantic style.
Solgård är ett villaområde söder om Hudd: Solgård is a villa area south of Huddinge centrum, and the view here is something special. From the highest hills, about 60 metres above sea level, you can see all the way to the Globe arena in Stockholm. If you're driving, there are only two ways in. And in the woods by Solgårdsvägen there's an ancient hillfort, Solgårds fornborg.
Solgårds fornborg är en av Huddinges ått: Solgård hillfort is one of Huddinge's eight hillforts and was probably used as a place for assemblies or worship. Only small fragments of wall remain on the eastern side. On the hill opposite lies the next one, Visättra hillfort.
Solhems borgarbrandkår bildades 1925 och: Solhem's volunteer fire brigade was formed in 1925 and was called out around 70 times a year. It had two vehicles and three motor pumps – and the firemen had built the fire engines themselves.
Solhem's volunteer fire brigade was formed in 1925 and was called out around 70 times a year. It had two fire engines, which the firefighters had built themselves.

Solhem’s volunteer fire brigade was formed in 1925 to protect the homes of Spånga. It was called out some 70 times a year and had two vehicles, one with a water tank, plus three motor pumps. The firefighters built the fire engines themselves.
Sollentuna Fria Gymnasium grundades 1992: Sollentuna Fria Gymnasium was founded in 1992 by Katarina Forste and Stig Magnusson, who had been colleagues at Rudbecksskolan. The school had room for about 200 students on its arts and social sciences programmes. Sofielundsskolan is now known as Johanssons skola.
Sollentuna centrum invigdes den 13 novem: Sollentuna Centrum was opened on 13 November 1975 by King Carl XVI Gustaf. In 2007–2010 it was expanded to double its size, and in 2011 it won the international ICSC Shopping Centre Awards in Paris.
Sollentuna station, en kort promenad bor: Sollentuna station, a short walk away, is the busiest commuter train station on the line to Märsta, 13.2 kilometres north of Stockholm Central. Tureberg has been the heart of the municipality since the council offices moved here from Norrviken in the 1940s. Today you'll find Tureberg Church, the shopping centre and the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, home to the municipal offices and, since 2023, the library too.
Sollentunas centrum har flyttat. Från bö: Sollentuna's centre has moved around. It started out by the church village at Sollentuna Church, then the local administration grew up in Norrviken, and in the 1940s it all moved to Tureberg. Right next door are Turebergskyrkan church and the remand prison, which opened in 2011 and is part of Rättscentrum Sollentuna, the justice centre. And a couple of hundred metres away stood Sollentunamässan, in its day the third-largest exhibition centre in Sweden.
Sollentunas första egentliga flerbostads: Sollentuna's first proper apartment blocks, from 1943, line Vallarestigen and were nicknamed the rabbit hutches. Helenelund's cinema, from 1936, became a church in the 1960s when the Baptists moved in.
Sollentunas förvaltning hade lokaler frå: From 1946 Sollentuna's council had offices in Tureberg, but by the late 1960s they were no longer big enough and staff had to make do with temporary premises. The answer was Turebergshuset, built in 1974–1976 to designs by Ulf Snellman and Tore Forsman.
Sollentunas förvaltning låg förr i Norrv: Sollentuna's administration used to be based in Norrviken, but in the 1940s it moved here to Tureberg, which has been the natural heart of the municipality ever since. A little further on is Arena Satelliten, opened in 2009, with sports halls, a music studio, a café and a fully equipped theatre stage. And on Malmvägen stands Tian, 'the Ten' – ten tower blocks from the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive.
Sollentunavallen ligger i ett gammalt gr: Sollentunavallen sits in an old gravel pit in the Stockholm esker, a long glacial ridge, and opened for the Swedish Athletics Championships in August 1969. The stands hold about 4,500 people, and in winter the artificial pitch next door becomes a bandy rink for Helenelunds IK. A little further away is Edsbacka krog, the first restaurant in Sweden to win two Michelin stars.
Sollentunavägen var en gång huvudvägen m: Sollentunavägen was once the main road between Stockholm and Uppsala, until Uppsalavägen was widened in the 1950s. Nearby is the fifteen-storey Tureberg Building, Turebergshuset, home to the municipal offices and, since 2023, the library as well. Arena Satelliten, opened in 2009, has sports halls, a media studio and a theatre seating 200.
Solna Centrum invigdes den 18 september: Solna Centrum opened on 18 September 1965 and was then one of the most modern shopping centres in the region. The architect Sture Frölén designed both the plan and every single building, commercial and public alike.
Solna centrum är den femte djupast beläg: Solna centrum is the fifth-deepest station on the whole metro network. The platform lies 16.5 metres below sea level, in the bedrock beneath Skytteholmsparken.
Solna kyrka byggdes på 1180-talet som ru: Solna Church was built in the 1180s as a round church – there are only two others in the Lake Mälaren region, in Bromma and on Munsö. The church itself was on the ground floor, while the two upper floors sheltered people and goods in case of attack.
Solnahallen stod klar 1983, och fasadern: Solnahallen was completed in 1983, and its east and north facades are decorated by the artist Per Olov Ultvedt. AIK plays floorball, handball and basketball here, and in the late 1980s the hall welcomed national teams such as Cuba, Bulgaria and Germany for the Euro Volley volleyball tournament. It's also used for concerts.
Solsunda hette fram till 1922 Skuru gård: Until 1922 Solsunda was known as Skuru gård. In the 16th century King Gustav Vasa gave the farm to Danvik hospital, so that the rent would help cover the hospital's costs. Since the early 20th century the manor house has served as a rest and treatment home. Little Bastusjön lake nearby is home to perch, roach and two kinds of freshwater mussel.
Som 20-årig vandringsman kom L.M. Ericss: As a 20-year-old journeyman, L.M. Ericsson came to Alby and asked for a bed for the night, but was called a ‘useless vagrant’ and sent packing. He swore that one day he would buy the place. A little over 30 years later, in 1895, he did just that.
Som en skärgård på land: begravningsplat: Picture an archipelago on dry land: the cemetery here opened in October 2024 and is laid out as a cluster of small islands, each one its own burial section, with a reflecting pool in the middle. Its neighbour is Granholmstoppen, a former rubbish tip that has grown into a hill 49 metres above sea level. It was built up from earth dug out when the blue metro line and the surrounding districts were built – although, according to the lorry drivers who built it, a bit of everything ended up in there.
Som mest hade Lidingö fyra biografer. Va: At its peak Lidingö had four cinemas. Vasabiografen was in the Vasaborgen building opposite the centre from 1923 to 1962. The old Grand was torn down in the early 1990s, and the Systembolaget off-licence now stands in its place.
Sommarcafé i gammalt torp: A summer café in an old croft
Sommarcafé i magasinet: A summer café in the old storehouse
Sommarcafé i torpet Lugnet: A summer café in the Lugnet croft
Sommaren 1832 besökte Karl XIV Johan sko: In the summer of 1832 King Karl XIV Johan visited the school. The headmaster, Carl Palmstedt, caught the King's interest so thoroughly that he handed over 600 riksdaler from his own purse on the spot and promised an annual grant.
Sommaren 1921 flyttade Malmqvistska barn: In summer 1921 the Malmqvist children's home moved in. By 1924 eleven children lived here and went to ordinary primary-school lessons. The City of Stockholm took over in 1948.
Sommaren 2015 började Göteborgs första e: In summer 2015 Gothenburg's first emission-free electric buses started running here, between Lindholmen Science Park and Johanneberg Science Park. The line was a trial that ended in 2020.
Sommarsalong och gudstjänstlokal: Summer salon and place of worship
Sommarsalongen byggdes åt krigsrådet Car: The summer salon was built for the war councillor Carl Jacob Salomon, who bought Johannisberg in 1834. It also served as a place of worship for people living on the headland, and much of the lavish 1830s interior survives.
Sopanläggningen gav god tillgång på göds: The refuse plant meant a plentiful supply of manure, so plots were sold to market gardeners. Commercial nurseries with greenhouses defined the area for most of the 20th century. At the peak there were more than 100 greenhouses, and the last nursery closed in 2006.
Soporna som byggde stadsdelen: The rubbish that built the neighbourhood
Soppsleven i kartongen: The soup ladle in the box
Sopstationen gav god tillgång på gödsel,: The refuse station meant there was plenty of manure, so plots were readily sold to market gardeners. Market gardens shaped the area for most of the 20th century, and in the 1950s there were more than 100 greenhouses. The last one closed in 2006.
Soya III har hetat Tankman, Shell S-8, R: Soya III has sailed as Tankman, Shell S-8, Rya, Piltank and Grimm. In the late 1990s the Wallenius shipping companies bought her back and restored her original name. Her home port is Gåshaga.
Spana in Tomtehuset vid Vasagatan: Look out for Tomtehuset, the Gnome House, on Vasagatan
Spana in porten till Tofslärkan 6 på Ode: Take a look at the doorway of Tofslärkan 6 at Odengatan 5. Above the half-columns sit two playful stone sculptures: a cat with a rat and a dog with a bone. The keystone in the arch of the doorway is shaped like the house number, 5.
Spana in soffan på möbelhusets tak: Spot the sofa on the furniture store's roof
Spargrisen som slukade slantar: The piggy bank that gobbled coins
Speedwaybanan i Arendal var 336 meter lå: Arendal's speedway track measured 336 metres in length and 12.5 metres across, with bends 17.5 metres wide and a radius of 30 metres.

The speedway track at Arendal was 336 metres long and 12.5 metres wide. Tony Rickardsson set the track record of 60.1 seconds riding for Masarna, and the attendance record came at a meet between Kaparna and Rospiggarna.
Spetsiga hörn och torvtak: Pointed corners and a turf roof
Spionarkiv i källarbaren: Spy archive in the cellar bar
Sporthallen en kort promenad bort, Botky: The sports hall a short walk away, Botkyrkahallen, combines royal glamour with everyday use. King Carl XVI Gustaf opened it in the summer of 2000, and it's also the sports hall for Brunnaskolan school. Balrog IK's men's team play here in front of up to 1,500 spectators. A short way in the other direction is Slagsta gård, a historic manor and former noble estate.
Sprickdal med lerjord och tallar: A fault valley of clay and pines
Spritfabriken kunde verka utan att konku: The distillery could operate without competing with Stockholm's spirits monopoly because the island was in Brännkyrka parish. It traced its roots to Lars Ohlsson Smith's brännvin distillery. What survives today includes the gatehouse by the bridge and an old tank known as Åttingen.
Spritförbud och skolbänkar: A drinks ban and school desks
Sprängningarna började 1861 med fyrverke: Blasting began in 1861 with fireworks, using Nobel's new nitroglycerine. The work took seven years and ran at a loss. Its instigator, Georg von Francken, lost most of his fortune, so people dubbed the gateway "Francken's ruin".
Spånga IP ligger mellan stationen och Te: Spånga IP sports ground lies between the station and Tensta and is used for many sports. But from 1930 to 1954, the Spånga broadcasting station stood where the sports ground is today.
Spånga IP är en riktig allt-i-ett-anlägg: Spånga IP really has it all: an ice rink, an indoor football hall, a bandy rink, street basketball and athletics tracks. In snowy winters they even lay cross-country ski tracks on the running track. A short way off was Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large-scale graffiti painting – until the wall was demolished in December 2021.
Spånga är ett riktigt gammalt namn. Det: Spånga is a truly old name. It appears in writing as early as 1300, in Latin, as apud Ecclesiam spangar, referring to the old church village. The name is simply the plural of spång, a footbridge. Today Spånga is an informal area that roughly covers the districts of Bromsten, Flysta, Solhem, Lunda and Sundby.
Spår av 8 000 år gamla boplatser har hit: Traces of 8,000-year-old settlements have been found 20–25 metres above sea level, on spots that were then the seashore. The area has settlements, camps and workshops from the Stone, Bronze and Iron Ages.
Spårvagn och båt på samma biljett. Åk ut: Tram and boat on the same ticket. Head out to car-free Brännö in the southern archipelago, swim off the rocks and take the boat back.
Trams reached Marklandsgatan in 1962. Between Linnéplatsen and here they shared the tracks of the Särö railway, which was later closed. The following year the tramline was extended towards Frölunda, though along a different route from the train.
Spårvagnarna under Frölunda torg en bit: When Frölunda torg, just up the road, was built in 1966, the trams beneath it ran into a stop that was completely underground – but in 2008 it was partly opened up to the outside. Next to the square stood Frölunda specialist hospital, opened in 1968 and replaced in early 2024 by the new Högsbo local hospital. Closest to us are Tynnered Church and Smycketorget square.
Spårvagnen kom hit redan hösten 1929, in: The tram reached this spot as early as autumn 1929, before the square even existed. The square itself was laid out in the early 1930s as a long, narrow piazza – a classic garden-city square. The town plan was approved in 1932 and bears the signature of Albert Lilienberg. All around is Nockeby, part of the Bromma garden city.
Spårvagnen kom upp till Kapellplatsen 19: The tram reached Kapellplatsen in 1911. In 1956 a large rocky outcrop south of the square was blasted away, mainly so that Caltex Oil could build a petrol station. The station closed in the 1990s.
Spårvagnen rullar över Djurgårdsbron och: The tram rolls across Djurgårdsbron and past the Nordic Museum and the Vasa Museum, home of the royal warship Vasa.
Spårvagnshall blev tunnelbanedepå: From tram shed to metro depot
Spårvagnshållplatsen Nils Ericsonsplatse: The Nils Ericsonsplatsen tram stop used to be called Nordstan. The spot was already an established bus hub before the terminal was built.
Spårvagnshållplatsen invigdes redan 1881: The tram stop opened back in 1881, when the line out towards Getebergsäng was built. Today Korsvägen has six platforms and tram tracks heading off in five directions.
Spårvagnslinje 15 gick mellan Råsundaväg: Tram route 15 ran between Råsundavägen and Fredsgatan; today bus 515 has taken over. Along Tulegatan the Tuletornen towers now rise too – two new 16-storey residential blocks.
Spårvägen hade en svampformad biljettkio: From 1917 the tramways had a mushroom-shaped ticket kiosk at Linnéplatsen. When the large kiosk at Lilla Bommen opened in 1929, ticket sales here stopped and the mushroom was replaced by an advertising column.
Spårvägen nådde Marklandsgatan 1962. Mel: The tramway reached Marklandsgatan in 1962. Between Linnéplatsen and here the trams shared tracks with the Säröbanan railway, which was later closed. The following year the tramway was extended towards Frölunda along a different route.
Spårvägsmuseet i Norra Djurgårdsstaden v: The Tram Museum in Norra Djurgårdsstaden shows how public transport in the Stockholm area has developed from the 1650s right up to the present day, on water as well as land. Right next to it is Husarviken bay, whose name has nothing to do with hussars: it comes from the village of Husarnæ, mentioned in 1288, so the stress falls on the first syllable. These days the bay is spanned by Husarviksbron, a bascule bridge for pedestrians and cyclists.

The Tramway Museum in Norra Djurgårdsstaden tells the story of public transport around Stockholm – on water as well as land – from the 1650s right up to today. Next to it is Husarviken bay, whose name has nothing to do with hussars. It comes from Husarnæ, a village mentioned in 1288, so the stress falls on the first syllable. Since 2018 the bay has been spanned by the Husarviken bridge, an opening bridge for pedestrians and cyclists.
Sst – en kod från telegrafen: Sst – a code from the telegraph age
Staden i sol och ljus: The town of sun and light
Staden köpte Skarpnäck 1922 och reserver: The city bought Skarpnäck in 1922 and set the fields aside for a new civilian airport. But in 1933 Riksby in Bromma was chosen instead. Even so, the Soviet general staff still had the airfield marked on their attack maps well into the 1980s.
Stadens första stora markköp: The city's first big land purchase
Stadens järnvåg låg här: The city's iron weighhouse stood here
Stadion byggdes oerhört snabbt med hjälp: The stadium went up incredibly fast, with the help of Ivar Kreuger's engineers. AIK won the opening match against Malmö FF 4–0, but at the official inauguration Sweden lost to England by the same score.
Stadsarkivet Liljeholmskajen: Stadsarkivet, the City Archives, at Liljeholmskajen
Stadsdelen Backa, ofta kallad Hisings Ba: The district of Backa, often called Hisings Backa, is no small place: 1,473 hectares stretching from Brunnsbo in the south, through Backa in the middle, to Skälltorp in the north. Backa was once a rural municipality of its own in what was then Gothenburg and Bohus County. Not far from here is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, the local centre of northern Backa.
Stadsdelen Gubbängen har fått sitt namn: Gubbängen gets its name from Gubbängens gård, a croft that later became an independent farm and was pulled down in 1965. Nearby is Gubbängsparken, a landscaped park of almost twelve hectares with a staffed playground. And a little further on, south of Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, is the Southern Jewish Cemetery, in use since 1952.
Stadsdelen Larsboda ligger klämd mellan: The Larsboda neighbourhood is squeezed in between Nynäsvägen and Magelungsvägen, and just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, 73 metres high. A little further away, on Lake Drevviken, is Hökarängsbadet, with a sandy beach about 60 metres long, a swimming jetty, a big meadow and rocks to sunbathe on. There's also a barbecue area and a café if you feel like staying a while.
Stadsdelen Rud har ett namn som berättar: The name Rud speaks of hard graft: it comes from Old Swedish rýdh, a clearing. The village is recorded as Rudh as early as 1495. Not far from here is Ruddalens IP, a sports ground with room for 3,000 spectators. The first match was played in 1985, when Västra Frölunda IF took on IFK Malmö, and the ground has hosted several seasons of Allsvenskan, Sweden's top football league.
The district of Syrhåla has an honest name. First recorded in 1550, it means ‘swampy place’ or ‘sour ground’ – a nod to the low, damp land between the hills. Syrhåla became a district of its own in 1957, when Arendal was split in two. Arendal itself is now given over entirely to industry and logistics, and it's where Volvo Buses, among others, has its headquarters.
Stadsdelen Torp har fått sitt namn efter: The district of Torp takes its name from two old farms. Lilla Torp was built in 1748 by Bengt Wilhelm Carlberg, and close by is the manor of Stora Torp, which dates back to the 1550s. Back then the estate was known as Torpit, and its tenant farmers answered to Kärra, the estate of Sten Eriksson Leijonhufvud. After his violent death in 1568, the farm passed to his widow, Gref Ebba.
Stadsdelen Vinsta är en ganska ung skape: Vinsta is a fairly young district. The City of Stockholm bought the land from Spånga in 1949, and four years later the district was created and named after the old village of Vinsta. Its 1.67 square kilometres today take in an industrial area that includes Vällingby fire station, designed by the architect Mårten J. Larsson and opened in 1965.
Stadsdelen bildades 1954 och gränsar öve: The district was created in 1954 and looks across the waters of Lake Mälaren to Ekerö municipality. On Strandliden stand 16 slab blocks from the late 1950s, which the City Museum has green-listed for their cultural, historical and artistic value. Right in the middle of the centre, on Maltesholmstorget, is Hässelby Strand Church.
Stadsdelen domineras av arton höghus som: The district is dominated by eighteen tower blocks standing in a row right through the area, with the centre on the south side. The Stockholm City Museum has rated Akalla one of the most interesting districts from the Million Programme, Sweden's great 1965–1974 housing drive.
Stadsdelen har fått sitt namn efter ett: The district is named after a small croft belonging to Hammarby gård – and the crofter's cottage is still standing in the southern part of Kärrtorpsparken park. Near the square is the Reflexen cinema, opened in 1961. Today volunteers from a cultural association run it, sharing the building with Teater Reflex. Down in the metro station glows Björn Olsén's artwork Ljuslådor med hemliga tecken, Light Boxes with Secret Signs, unveiled in 1994.
Stadsdelen hette först Jakobsberg. Den f: The district was first called Jakobsberg. It was renamed to avoid confusion with Jakobsberg in Järfälla, and the choice fell on Bredäng, a croft dating from the 1780s that was farmed right up to 1949.
Stadshuset invigdes 1923 och är en av St: Stockholm City Hall was inaugurated in 1923 and is one of the city's great symbols. Every December the Nobel Banquet is held here in the Blue Hall, and from the tower there's a sweeping view over Riddarfjärden bay and Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Stadshuset som blev Signalfabriken: The town hall that became Signalfabriken
Stadshusets silverglänsande aluminiumfas: The town hall’s shimmering silver aluminium facade, with its sun-shading louvres, is typical of the high-tech style of its day. The building is essentially made of aluminium, concrete and glass. When it was new, people called it a ‘strange bird’ among Lidingö’s villas.
Stadsplanen från 1962 var mycket noggran: The 1962 town plan was meticulous. The 8–9-storey slab blocks were to be turned 15 degrees clockwise from north–south and stand about 50 metres apart. One side of every building was to be completely car-free.
Stadsplanen för Lärkstaden tillät bara e: The town plan for Lärkstaden allowed only one kitchen per villa, to stop owners letting rooms out. The builders got round this with 'doubles': two-room flats with a bathroom but no kitchen. Piplärkan 8 had three of them.
Stadsplaneraren Per Olof Hallman ogillad: The town planner Per Olof Hallman disliked ruler-straight streets and square blocks. In Röda bergen he followed the lie of the land instead, with curving streets and irregular blocks. In 1922 the press wrote of 'Country life in the middle of Stockholm'.
Stadsporten med häkte: The city gate with a lock-up
Stallbacken är ett passande namn, för hä: Stallbacken – “Stable Hill” – is a fitting name, because this is home to Åby Travgymnasium. Opened in autumn 2005, it's an upper secondary school for young people from all over Sweden and the Nordic countries who want a career in harness racing or riding. It's based at Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track. A little further on, you can swap the sound of hooves for film soundtracks at Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in a converted school hall.
Stallet som blev kafé: The stable that became a café
Stampade den lin och hampa?: Did it pound flax and hemp?
Start framför Centralstationen från 1858: Start in front of the Central Station, built in 1858. At Kungsportsplatsen you'll see Kopparmärra, the 'copper mare' statue, before the tram climbs up Avenyn, Gothenburg's grand boulevard.
Starta vid Odenplan och gå till Stadsbib: Start at Odenplan and walk to the City Library on Sveavägen (5 min), designed by Gunnar Asplund and famous for its round lending hall. Gustav Vasa church also stands on the square.
Starten på en biografkedja: The start of a cinema chain
Statarmuseet, Överjärva gård: Statarmuseet, the farm workers' museum, at Överjärva gård
Stationen hette Vreten: The station used to be called Vreten
Stationen hette först Johanneshov: The station was first called Johanneshov
Stationen hette först Järva: The station was first called Järva
Stationen invigdes den 5 april 1964. Gus: The station opened on 5 April 1964. King Gustaf VI Adolf rode the new line all the way out and was met by Cub Scouts and Brownies and a choir of pupils from the Adolf Fredrik music school.
Stationen ligger 21 meter under den forn: The station lies 21 metres below the old film studios. The artwork is a large collage of texts, stones, pieces of tiled stove and glazed brick from the demolished Strindberg House at Karlaplan, with display cases of film props and photos from Filmstaden. It's also the only metro station with entrances in two municipalities.
Stationen ligger i ett bergrum 20–22 met: The station lies in a rock cavern 20–22 metres underground and opened on 29 January 1978. The art is by Karin Ek and Gösta Wessel: shadow paintings that seem to change colour depending on the angle you see them from.
Stationen ritades av Magnus Ahlgren och: The station was designed by Magnus Ahlgren and is green-listed by the Stockholm City Museum for its heritage value. Since 2005, the entrance hall and the outside wall facing the buses have featured art by Fredrik Landergren: inset glass mosaics of human heads.
Stationen öppnade 1866 när Norra stamban: The station opened in 1866 along with the Northern Main Line, and was then called Järva. The name was changed to Ulriksdal in 1920, partly because it was being confused with Järna and Järle. The racecourse next door had opened the year before.
Stationen öppnade 1890 och fick el redan: The station opened in 1890 and was electrified as early as 1895. In the early 1950s it was the busiest railway station in Sweden, handling around 340 trains a day, freight included, with lines heading off in four directions. The villas round about started going up in 1896, when Djursholms AB began selling plots near the station. In the 1970s and 80s the whole Roslagsbanan railway was under threat of closure.
Stationen öppnade 1890 och hette först D: The station opened in 1890. It was called Djursholm at first, then Ösby, and from 1920 Djursholms Ösby. The line was electrified as early as 1895. With trains running in four directions – around 340 a day, freight included – it was once reckoned to be the busiest railway station in Sweden. The villas round about started going up in 1896, when building plots near the station were put on sale.
Stationen öppnade 1922 som hållplats för: The station opened in 1922 as a stop for local trains on the Northern Main Line. Residents of the growing suburb of detached houses had taken the matter all the way to the government. Today's station came into use in 1994, when the line was widened to four tracks.
Stationen öppnade 1937, när Roslagsbanan: The station opened in 1937, when the Roslagsbanan railway was extended to Näsbypark. At first it was called Alléparken, but the name lasted only four months. The trains here run on a single track with just one platform. Down by the bay of Näsbyviken is Näsby Castle, now a conference venue with a hotel and restaurant.
Stationen öppnade 1944 som spårvagnshåll: The station opened in 1944 as a tram stop on the Ängby line, under the name Färjestadsvägen. It became a metro station in 1952, but it wasn't called Ängbyplan until 1962. Not far from here, as far back as the 16th century, stood Karsvik farm, on the shore of Lake Ängbysjön, which has since disappeared. Today the Mälaren Scouts have their base in Karsvik's meadow. And nearby Ängby torg square only got its official name in 2005.
Stationen öppnade 1946 under namnet Joha: The station opened in 1946 as Johanneshov. But Johanneshov was the postal address for much of southern Stockholm and was thought too broad, so in 1958 the station was renamed Gullmarsplan. Between 1950 and 1964 trolleybuses ran here too.
Stationen öppnade den 5 juni 1977 och li: The station opened on 5 June 1977 and lies 13 kilometres from Kungsträdgården, the terminus at the other end of the blue line. Buses from the neighbouring bus terminal go to Sollentuna, Danderyd, Vällingby and Jakobsberg, among other places.
Stationens första räddningsbåt 1983 var: The station's first rescue boat, in 1983, was the former pilot boat Alice Olsson, built in 1949. In 1987 she was replaced by Gustaf Olsson, a 10.3-metre covered boat with twin engines, donated by Sten A. Olsson.
Stationens konst, Röster från det förflu: The station's artwork, Röster från det förflutna (Voices from the Past) by Göran Dahl, Carl Johan De Geer and Kristina Anshelm, shows fossils and runic inscriptions – among them a complete reproduction of the famous Rök runestone. From the north entrance it's 20 metres down to the platform.
Stationens signatur är Sst, som ska läsa: The station's code is Sst, short for Södra bangården, STockholm. The slightly odd order of the letters goes back to the 19th-century telegraph system.
Stationens tak och väggar är målade i gr: The station's ceiling and walls are painted green and red. Among other things, the artists Karl-Olov Björk and Anders Åberg created scenes of Sweden depicting the country's problems in the 1970s, along with little peep-show boxes to look into.
Stationshuset invigdes den 12 december 1: The station building opened on 12 December 1876, the same day King Oscar II inaugurated the railway between Stockholm and Västerås. It is the only one of Järfälla's four old station buildings on the line still standing; Barkarby, Kallhäll and Stäket have all been demolished.
Stationshuset som ersattes av plåt: A station building replaced by sheet metal
Stationshuset är äldre än hållplatsen: d: The station building is older than the stop itself: it first stood at the steam ferry landing in Herserud and was moved here in 1914. It's in the National Romantic style, with dragon heads on the ends of the gutters.
Stationsnamnet är en ledtråd. En kort bi: The station name gives it away. A short distance from here was Täby Galopp, the biggest gallop racecourse in Scandinavia, opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf in 1960 to replace the Ulriksdal racecourse in Solna. The last race day was 18 May 2016, after which the horses moved to Bro Park. Where the track used to be, a new district, Täby Park, is now taking shape, planned for around 20,000 residents.

The stop's name is a clue: Galoppfältet means 'the gallop field'. A short way off was Täby Galopp, Scandinavia's largest flat-racing track, opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf in 1960 to replace the Ulriksdal racecourse in Solna. The last race day was 18 May 2016, and the horses moved to Bro Park. Where the track once was, the new district of Täby Park is now taking shape, planned for many thousands of residents.
Statyn Avskedet på polarisen: The statue Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice
Statyn Såningskvinnan av Per Hasselberg: Per Hasselberg's statue The Sower was unveiled on Johanna's name day, 21 July 1883, which is why locals call her Johanna. She was cast in bronze in Paris, and the original plaster is in Gothenburg's Museum of Medical History.
Statyn mitt på platsen föreställer Karl: The statue in the middle of the square is King Karl IX – Charles IX – on horseback, but to Gothenburgers it's simply Kopparmärra, the Copper Mare. It went up in 1904. This is where Kungsportsavenyn, the city's grand avenue, begins, and on the canal alongside, the flat Paddan sightseeing boats glide by, ducking under the low bridges. A short distance away is Stora Saluhallen, the big market hall, from 1889.
Statyn som Landalapojkarna samlade till: The statue the Landala boys paid for
Stearinljus vid Mälarstranden: Candles on the shores of Lake Mälaren
Stefanskyrkans fasader är klädda med lju: St Stephen's Church (Stefanskyrkan) is faced with pale sandstone from Närke, and the south gable bears a stone crucifix by the sculptor Carl Eldh. In the chancel stands a triptych-style altarpiece with ten paintings by Einar Forseth, dating from the 1926 refurbishment.
Stenarna är av Göteborgsgnejs och bröts: The stones are Gothenburg gneiss, mostly quarried from a hill 250 metres away. Each weighs 1–2 tonnes, and the roof stone nearly 3 tonnes. Thin flat stones were stacked between the blocks to support the chamber.
Stenbrottet öppnade 1866 och ägdes då av: The quarry opened in 1866, owned at the time by the engineer Johan Adolf Berg. His workforce included some 60 convicts from Långholmen prison. The bluish-grey granite was exported as far as England, and Berg used it for, among other things, the quay by the Nationalmuseum.
Stenen från sprängningarna användes unde: In the second half of the 1800s, rock from the blasting was used to fill in nearby Stora Träsket, the 'Great Swamp'. That created more building plots for the new Östermalm.
Stenen hittades vid odling i Islinge och: The stone turned up during ploughing at Islinge and is mentioned in 1847. In the 1860s it was set up by the main house at Islinge farm, and in 1943 it was moved to the hill at Dalängen so more people could see it.
Stenen saknar helt de djurslingor som an: The stone has none of the animal-shaped ribbons usually seen on runestones in Uppland. Even so, the rune forms suggest it probably dates from the late 11th century. In the summer of 1682 the antiquarian Johan Hadorph and the draughtsman Johan Leitz travelled through Järfälla, drawing every runestone they came across.
Stenen som kan få jorden att gå under: The stone that could end the world
Stenen är från mitten av 1000-talet och: The stone dates from the mid-1000s and its inscription reads roughly: 'Kari and Ingjald and … in memory of Björn, their father. God help …'. The rest was lost along with the missing top.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö m: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö island in the middle of Lake Mälaren, is best known for its disused 19th-century quarry and the industrial village that grew up around it. Neighbouring Törnby is far older: it's first mentioned in 1342, in connection with a land swap with Vårfruberga convent, and has since grown together with Stenhamra.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö,: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö, is best known for its disused 19th-century granite quarry and the company town that grew up around it. If you'd like to go even further back in time, look for runestone U 32, which stands in a patch of woodland just under a kilometre from the centre. Ekerö municipality, by the way, is made up of a cluster of islands in Lake Mälaren long known as Mälaröarna, the Mälaren Islands.
Stenhuggarfamiljernas tjänstebostäder fi: The tied cottages of the stonecutters' families survive in excellent condition. Together with the quarry, the school and the co-op shop, they offer a rare picture of a late-19th-century industrial community, and the area is designated of national interest for cultural heritage.
Stenpiren byggdes 1844–1845 och fick sit: Stenpiren, the Stone Pier, was built in 1844–1845 and got its name in 1883. Before that, this was the site of Träpiren, a wooden jetty half as wide and one of the city's first quays. All the archipelago boats used to depart from here.
Stenskolan hade bassängbad, träslöjdsal: The stone-built school had a swimming pool, a woodwork room and a dining hall on its lower-ground floor. At the top were an art room, a music room and an open-air classroom where pupils with lung disease were taught. All in all there was room for around 470 pupils.
Stensö byggdes under miljonprogrammet, m: Stensö was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, with seven-storey point blocks and eight-storey slab blocks. In eastern Stensö small houses went up, some just 55 square metres, meant for pensioners and people living alone. Before that there were just a few 1920s villas out at the far end.
Stensö har fått sitt namn efter en halvö: Stensö is named after a peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and the Stensö swimming spot is at its tip. Through the area runs Ältavägen, built in 1934, which winds for just over eight kilometres through open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. Not far away, in the Flaten nature reserve, people race radio-controlled model cars.
Sticklinge på nordvästra Lidingö är beka: Anyone who has run Lidingöloppet, the famous cross-country race, will know Sticklinge in north-western Lidingö, because the course runs right through it. South of the houses stretches the Sticklinge nature reserve: 108 hectares of forest, coast and grassland, protected since 2021. By Rödstuguviken bay stands Rödstugan, a house with roots in the 17th century that has been home to crofters, ferrymen and the families of farm labourers.
Stieg Trenter föddes på Magelungsvägen 4: Crime writer Stieg Trenter was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery by Södertörns villastad station – today Farsta strand – where Stieg sometimes lent a hand. Since 1995 a sign on the square has carried a quote from his crime novel Tiga är silver.
Stieg Trenters torg är runt med en fontä: Stieg Trenters torg is a round square with a fountain in the middle. Since 1995 it has had a literary sign quoting from Trenter's 1955 crime novel Tiga är silver (Silence Is Silver).
Stigbergets äldsta kända namn är Galgebæ: Stigberget's oldest known name is Galgebærgith, Gallows Hill, recorded as early as 1545. Once the gallows had been moved away, a lookout tower went up here in 1827, which people jokingly called "the Toothpick on Söder".
Stjärnadressen i Gamla stan: A star address in the Old Town
Stjärnbildsgatan, en bit härifrån, fick: Stjärnbildsgatan, a short way from here, had an unusual makeover: its four-storey blocks were rebuilt so drastically that the top floors were removed altogether, leaving terraced houses around generous courtyards. Nearby is Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the Intercultural Folk High School. It started in 2007 as the first folk high school in the Nordic countries for Roma students and was opened by Crown Princess Victoria.
Stjärnhusen fick åtta våningar eftersom: The star-shaped Stjärnhusen blocks got eight storeys because the fire brigade's ladders reached 22 metres, and a lift was only thought worthwhile if 40 flats shared it. The result was five flats per floor around a pentagonal stairwell.
Stjärnhusen i Gröndal byggdes av Olle En: The Star Houses in Gröndal were built by Olle Engkvist to designs by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, and the architectural historian Fredric Bedoire ranks them among the finest groups of buildings in Stockholm. The area is of national interest and a textbook example of folkhem architecture, from the early days of the Swedish welfare state. And after all that architecture, it's time for fika, the Swedish coffee break: Lundbergs konditori has been on the same corner, under the same name, since 1946.
Stjärnkrogens sista kapitel: The last chapter of a star restaurant
Stockholm är byggt på vatten och omgivet: Stockholm is built on water and surrounded by forest. This route takes the boat out along the Saltsjön to Blockhusudden, continues through the Royal National City Park on Djurgården and ends at Källtorpssjön lake, deep in the Nacka nature reserve.
Stockholm är fullt av musik- och filmmin: Stockholm is packed with memories of music and film. This route runs from Kafé 44 and Cornelisparken on Södermalm, past the studios where ABBA recorded, to Filmstaden in Råsunda, where almost 400 Swedish feature films were shot.
Stockholms frihamn öppnade som ett provi: Frihamnen, Stockholm's free port, opened in 1919 as a temporary solution, yet it kept growing right up until the 1970s. For much of that time, from 1921 to 1952, seaplanes landed at Lindarängen, where the port stands today. The Ford Building, designed by Uno Åhrén, went up between 1929 and 1931 as an assembly plant for Ford cars; these days it's the home of the stock exchange operator Nasdaq. The huge Magasin 6 warehouse had less luck – it was out of date almost as soon as container shipping took over.
Stockholms första södra tull hette Grind: Stockholm's first southern toll gate was called Grinds tull and stood at what is now Östgötagatan/Bondegatan. Around 1660 it moved to the narrow isthmus here. The toll station was abolished in 1857, and nothing of the toll houses survives today.
Stockholms sjukhem köpte gården 1903 som: Stockholms sjukhem bought the farm in 1903 as a convalescent home. In the 1940s it cared for war invalids from the Finnish Winter War, and from 1953 to 1968 for polio patients. The matron, Mathilda Sundelin, bought the farm in 1922 and renamed it Solsunda vilohem, a rest home.
Stockholms stad byggde 1889 en sopstatio: In 1889 the City of Stockholm built a refuse station at Lövsta, and the rubbish came here by rail. All that manure attracted market gardeners, and greenhouses and hotbeds defined the garden suburb for most of the 20th century.
Stockholms stad köpte egendomen Gubbänge: The City of Stockholm bought the Gubbängen estate from the farmer Albin Arvidsson in 1908, but building didn't really get going until the 1940s. The district grew up around two farms, Herrängen and Gubbängen, neither of which survives. The metro arrived on 1 October 1950, when the line from Slussen to Hökarängen opened.
Stockholms stad köpte marken 1885 och by: The City of Stockholm bought the land in 1885 and built the Lövsta refuse station by Lake Mälaren, with the rubbish arriving by train from Spånga. The workers needed homes, so Count Carl Trolle-Bonde of Hässelby Palace began leasing and selling plots.
Stockholms stads småstugebyrå lät bygga: Stockholm City's small-house bureau had 362 small houses of ten different types built in Bagarmossen, with residents building them themselves from standard plans. The town plan was led by Sven Markelius.
Stockholms stadsmuseum bedömde målningen: The Stockholm City Museum judged the mural to be of cultural and historical value, and in 2015 it was decided that the wall would be protected and become the centrepiece of a new park. But in 2020 the decision came to demolish it, as it was in poor condition and at risk of collapse.
Stockholms största koloniområde ligger a: Stockholm's largest allotment area is right nearby, with no fewer than 554 plots, each with its own little cottage. It was laid out in three stages – in 1936, 1939 and 1941 – to replace several allotment areas in the southern suburbs that were cleared during the 1920s and 30s. Also in the neighbourhood is Pungpinan, an area of small cottages, where building began on Lugna Gatan as early as 1927.
