Stockholms tunnelbana är känd för sin ko: The Stockholm metro is famous for its art, but Johannelund – along with S:t Eriksplan and a handful of others – is one of the few stations with no artwork whatsoever.
Stockholms ånglokssällskap: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm steam locomotive society
Stockholms ånglokssällskap bevarar och r: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm Steam Locomotive Society, preserves and restores old railway vehicles. It started out in 1974 with an emergency reserve locomotive bought from SJ, the Swedish state railways. The society was first based at Tomteboda and then in the old slaughterhouse district, but when the Globe arena was about to be built it had to move, in 1988, to an industrial siding here in Västberga. Nearby Midsommarkransens skola was an elementary school from 1915 to 1962.
Stockholmsmässan hette Älvsjömässan fram: Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, was called Älvsjömässan until 1976. Today it's Sweden's largest venue for trade fairs and conferences, with around seventy fairs a year and just over a million visitors. In spring 2020 its halls were put to a very different use, when the Älvsjö field hospital was set up inside.
Stockholmsvägen är en av Lidingös äldsta: Stockholmsvägen is one of Lidingö's oldest roads – the municipality calls it Lidingö's historic lifeline. Along it stand Kopparhusen, the Copper Houses, three tower blocks from the 1950s and 1960s; the oldest has been marked by the city museum as being of very high cultural and historical value. Further on is Lidingö Arena, an office and retail building from the 1970s by the architect Bo Möller, so striking that it has become a local landmark.
Stockholmsåsen löper genom Sollentuna, o: The Stockholm esker runs through Sollentuna, and the road was laid along the dry ridge or its slopes. Older routes followed the ridge even more closely, passing the old farms of Kista and Tuna north of Edsviken.
Stockmos har haft sin fabrik i Stenhamra: Stockmos has had its factory in Stenhamra since 1932. In the 1940s there were 10,000 fruit trees here – the largest orchard in Sweden north of Skåne. Fruit trees are still common in the residential area later built on the land, and many street names recall the orchards.

Stockmos has had its factory in Stenhamra since 1932. In the 1940s there were 10,000 fruit trees here – Sweden's largest orchard north of Skåne. Many fruit trees still stand in the residential area built on the land, and several street names recall the orchards.
Stocksund är rikt på arkitektvillor. Vil: Stocksund is full of architect-designed villas. Villa Gärdsgården was built in 1904–05 to designs by Ragnar Östberg, for the artist Alf Wallander. Villa Tallom was built in 1904–06 by the architect Lars Israel Wahlman as a home for himself and his family, and it has been listed since 1979.
Stocksundet förbinder Lilla Värtan med E: The Stocksundet strait links Lilla Värtan with the bay of Edsviken and marks the border between Danderyd and Solna. Stocksund station used to sit closer to the harbour, with tracks running down to the water so goods could be loaded onto ships. The harbour also had the power station that supplied electricity to the Djursholm railway, and the Långängsbanan tramway started from the station.
Stora Essingen är en 73 hektar stor ö i: Stora Essingen is a 73-hectare island in Lake Mälaren. Its highest point, Kungsklippan, is 41 metres above sea level, and on the second-highest stands Essinge church, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and consecrated in 1959. The local cinema Orkanen opened nearby in 1938. The two apartment buildings on Badstrandsvägen are called Byggindustrihuset, after AB Byggindustri, the construction company that built them.

Stora Essingen is an island of 73 hectares in Lake Mälaren, and its highest point, Kungsklippan, rises 41 metres above sea level. On the island's second-highest point stands Essinge Church, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and consecrated in 1959. Its free-standing bell tower, a 48-metre campanile, is a landmark of southern Stockholm.
Stora Essingens sommarvillor från 1700-t: The 18th-century summer villas on Stora Essingen became year-round homes in the early 20th century, and things really took off when the Essinge bridge opened in 1929. In 1966 came Essingeleden, Sweden's first six-lane motorway, along the island's eastern shore. On 14 October 2005 the floating crane Lodbrok crashed into the bridge, causing massive traffic jams.

The 18th-century summer villas on Stora Essingen became year-round homes in the early 1900s, and things really took off when the Stora Essingen bridge opened in December 1928. In 1966 Essingeleden, Sweden's first six-lane motorway, arrived along the island's eastern shore. On 14 October 2005 the floating crane Lodbrok crashed into the bridge, causing huge tailbacks.
Stora Fågelsången var en av flera små gå: Stora Fågelsången was one of several small farms carved out of the Hägersten estate in the late 1700s, which became manor-like summer retreats. The south wing is the oldest part, referred to as 'the new building' in 1756. The Stockholm City Museum has marked the farm as being of high heritage value.
Stora Förö är genom landhöjningen numera: Thanks to post-glacial land uplift – the land here is still slowly rising after the Ice Age – Stora Förö is now joined to Lilla Förö by a narrow isthmus. The island has a burial cairn and finds from the Stone Age. When the master carpenter Axel Hellqvist came out here on a boat trip in 1927, there wasn't a single tree, because the island had long been used for grazing sheep and cutting timber.
Stora Kåsjön är Partille kommuns största: Stora Kåsjön is the largest lake in Partille municipality, just over a square kilometre in area and a full 32 metres deep. It sits high up, about 109 metres above sea level, and it's also the municipality's source of drinking water. Around it are more small lakes, such as Haketjärnen in the Maderna-Haketjärn Natura 2000 area.
Stora Rödjan var ett kronohemman i Lundb: Stora Rödjan was a Crown farm in Lundby parish and served, among other things, as a colonel's residence. Work on the Ryahamnen oil harbour began here in the 1930s, followed by Skarvikshamnen in the 1950s.
Stora Saluhallen vid Kungstorget: Stora Saluhallen, the market hall on Kungstorget
Stora Sjötullen: Stora Sjötullen, the old customs house
Stora Sköndal var en bondgård redan unde: Stora Sköndal was already a farm in the Iron Age. Near the main building are two burial grounds probably used in the Vendel and Viking periods.
Stora Stampan byggdes på 1670-talet och: Stora Stampan was built in the 1670s and first stood on Observatoriegatan in Stockholm. When the blocks there were laid out in the 1880s there was no room for windmills, so in 1882 it was moved here. Its sister mill, Lilla Stampan, now stands as Kälvesta windmill in Solhem.

Stora Stampan was built in the 1670s and first stood on Observatoriegatan in Stockholm. When the area was to be developed with city blocks in the 1880s there was no room left for windmills, so in 1882 it was moved here to Kvarnbacken. It's probably one of the oldest surviving windmills in Greater Stockholm.
Stora Stampan maldes i till slutet av 19: Stora Stampan was still grinding until the late 1920s. Its sails were taken down during a renovation in 1971, and in winter 2019–2020 the mill was restored and given new ones.
Stora Stampan är en stubbkvarn, där hela: Stora Stampan is a post mill, so the whole mill house turns to face the wind. Holländskan, built in 1885, was an eight-sailed Dutch-style mill where only the cap turned. The name Stampan may suggest that flax and hemp were pounded here for rope and sailcloth, but there's no record of it.
Stora Stampan is a post mill, where the whole mill body turns to face the wind. Holländskan, built here in 1885, was a Dutch-style tower mill where only the cap could turn, and it had eight sails.
Stora Ursvik gränsar mot Kymlinge, Lilla: Stora Ursvik borders Kymlinge, Lilla Ursvik, Rissne and Rinkeby. Not far from here, on a hill by the Rissne interchange, stands the Stora Stampan windmill. Its companion, Holländskan, burned down in 1989, but Stora Stampan was restored over the winter of 2019–20 and now has new sails.
Stora Ursvik var en av flera stora medel: Stora Ursvik was one of several large medieval farms in the area and has a long military history – for many years the defence research agency FOA was based here. Homes only started to be built in 2006.
Stora delar av Hisingen har lerjord som: Much of Hisingen is covered in what's known as "Hisingslera", Hisingen clay. It isn't a particular type of clay; the name simply comes from the fact that it's found almost everywhere on the island. The soil is often very fertile, but can be tricky to build on.
Stora delar av Viksjö gränsar till Görvä: Much of Viksjö borders the Görväln nature reserve along Lake Mälaren, and here you'll find the Hummelmora green space with the Hummelmoraberget hill. As early as 1935 a regional plan proposed making both Görväln and Viksjö nature reserves, but the municipality only wanted to protect Gåsberget.

Much of Viksjö borders the Görväln nature reserve, which follows the shore of Lake Mälaren past spots such as Hummelmora hage and Görvälnsbadet beach. Viksjö also has the green area of Hummelmora, with Hummelmoraberget hill.
Stora delar av grannområdet Ekängen bygg: Much of neighbouring Ekängen was built in the 1940s as a neighbourhood of small family houses, and it's still a quiet residential area just north of Saltsjö-Duvnäs. A little further on you'll find Långsjön, a small forest lake that has been a nature reserve since 2005. There's a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail all the way round – perfect if you fancy swapping the town centre for a lap of the lake.
Storbageri i Peugeots gamla hus: A big bakery in Peugeot's old building
Storholmen i sjön Trehörningen var en gå: Storholmen in Lake Trehörningen was once a proper island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots, most of them sold to workers from Stockholm, and a footbridge was built to the mainland. Around twenty little summer cottages sprang up. Today it's mostly forest and shoreline open to all, and the lake is rich in fish and birdlife – the lesser spotted woodpecker among them – and even bats.
Storhögen på gravfältet är sex meter hög: Storhögen, the great mound on the burial ground, is six metres high and 46 metres across – the second-largest burial mound in Södermanland. When it was excavated in 1939, gold fragments of a sword hilt from around 650–700 were found. That sword is considered more magnificent than those from the boat graves at Vendel and Valsgärde.
Storskogstorget invigdes 1958 och formga: Storskogstorget square opened in 1958. The landscape architect N.H. Orénto designed it very much in the style of the day, with seating, greenery and two ponds. From here you can also get to Näckrosen metro station, the only one on the network with entrances in two different municipalities. A little further on is Filmstaden in Råsunda, the studios where almost 400 Swedish feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973 – a place especially linked with Ingmar Bergman.
Storstugan planerades som ett bågformat: Storstugan was planned as a curved 25-storey building with a restaurant at the top and a day nursery on the middle floors. When it was built in 1970, it ended up with 17 storeys and nothing but flats.
Storängen grundades 1904 av Tjänstemänne: Storängen was founded in 1904 by the Civil Servants' Home Ownership Association. Officials, university lecturers, company directors and artists moved here, drawn by the new Saltsjöbanan railway with its fast trains into Stockholm.
Storängen räknas som ett av Sveriges bäs: Storängen is considered one of Sweden's best-preserved early 20th-century villa suburbs, with large timber houses in the National Romantic style. Gustaf Hugo Sandberg designed the most houses, and since 1987 the area has been designated of national interest for cultural heritage.
Storängen var tidigare ett flackt jordbr: Storängen was once a flat field of farmland. It came into being in 1848, when Lake Trehörningen was lowered to create land for cultivation. The industrial area was built on marshland that had once been a bay of the lake.
Storängens industriområde, alldeles i nä: Building work on the Storängen industrial area, right nearby, began in the early 1950s, just under a kilometre south-east of Huddinge centrum. Now the area is about to change. Under a plan from 2009, it will eventually become a mixed neighbourhood, mostly homes plus businesses that sit comfortably alongside residents. It's also where you'll find Storängshallen, a hall for athletics and gymnastics.
Storängshallen alldeles intill, invigd 2: Right next door is Storängshallen, opened in 2007, a hall mainly for athletics and gymnastics. The area has an amusing history. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård launched Huddinge villastad, a scheme for a brand-new garden suburb of villas. Only a handful of the old villas are left, and Huddinge centrum now stands right where the villa town was supposed to be.
Storängshallen är 94,5 meter lång och ha: Storängshallen is 94.5 metres long, with a vaulted roof that spans the entire hall without a single pillar and rises 14 metres high. Inside are a 200-metre track and a 60-metre sprint straight. Back in the 1970s, the old sports ground here was covered by an inflatable plastic dome instead.
Strawberry Arena, som invigdes under nam: Strawberry Arena, which opened as Friends Arena, is Sweden's national stadium, home to the men's football team, and since 2013 it has hosted the final of Melodifestivalen, the contest that picks Sweden's Eurovision entry. For concerts it holds up to 65,000 people. Next door is a 25-storey hotel with round windows designed to look like footballs, and Mall of Scandinavia has an IMAX cinema with the biggest screen in Sweden, almost 22 metres wide.
Strax efter Akalla passerar stråket Akal: Just past Akalla, the trail passes Akalla village, one of the best-preserved 18th-century farming villages in the Stockholm area, with roots going back to the Bronze Age. At Hästa farm, one of the largest urban farms in the world, the land has been worked since the Viking Age.
Strax efter mitten av 1870-talet blev Ar: Soon after the mid-1870s, Arendal became a seaside resort. Wholesale merchants, shipowners, an eye doctor and a salt trader had summer retreats here, with villas such as Rosenborg, Tjällstorp and Fjordhem.
Strax före återinvigningen 1992 härjades: Shortly before the reopening in 1992, a major fire swept through several of the centre's buildings, delaying the opening.
Strax härifrån ligger Hammarkulletorget,: Just up the road is Hammarkulletorget, a square designed by White Architects and built in 1971. Beneath it lies the only completely underground tram stop in Sweden. It was modelled on the Stockholm metro – because in the 1970s there really were plans for a metro all the way out to Angered. That's why it's sometimes called Gothenburg's only metro station.
Strax intill inträffade Tuveraset, en av: It was right near here that the Tuve landslide struck – one of the worst natural disasters in modern Swedish history. At 4.09 pm on 30 November 1977, the ground in Tuve gave way in a massive landslide that claimed nine lives. It's also known as Raset i Tuve or Tuveskredet.
Strax intill ligger Arken kombiterminal: Right beside us is the Arken combi terminal in Skandia Harbour, where semi-trailers are switched between ships and trains. It replaced the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to move to make way for the Västlänken rail tunnel. Work started in January 2018, and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019.
Strax intill ligger Fässbergs kyrkogård,: Right next to it is Fässberg cemetery, with 4,800 graves and a chapel from 1936. A little further on is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema run by the municipality in the converted Fässbergssalen assembly hall, which opened in January 2013. The upper secondary school that houses the hall was once one of Sweden's 20 schools with specialist elite programmes.
Strax intill ligger Hult Åsens naturvård: Right beside it is the Hult Åsen nature conservation area, a stretch of high ground with pine, birch and bare rock. Set aside in 1994, it covers ten hectares and is looked after by the City of Gothenburg. A little further away is Askims torg, the square at the heart of Askim, a district facing Askimsfjorden bay.
Strax intill ligger Kvibergsnäs landeri,: Right next door is Kvibergsnäs landeri, a country estate between Kviberg and Gamlestaden. Its present buildings date from the first half of the 19th century. Kvibergsnäs is something of a survivor: it's the only country estate in Gothenburg where both the house and the barns are still standing.
Strax intill ligger Lillhagsparkens sjuk: Right beside us is Lillhagsparken hospital, originally named Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. There's no longer any care here – the forensic psychiatric unit moved to Rågården in 2013.
Strax intill ligger Mariakyrkan i Hammar: Right next to us is Mariakyrkan in Hammarkullen, formerly known as Tomaskyrkan, a church shared by the Uniting Church in Sweden and Angered parish. Close by there was also Hammarkullens Folkets Hus Bio, a 200-seat cinema. And a short walk away is Hammarkulletorget – the place to go for Gothenburg's only underground tram stop.

Right next door is St Mary's Church in Hammarkullen, formerly St Thomas's, shared by the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan, and Angered parish. The building has been abandoned because of mould and is to be replaced by a new one. Nearby was also Hammarkullens Folkets Hus Bio, a cinema seating 200. And a short walk away is Hammarkulletorget, where the tram stops at what is jokingly called Gothenburg's only underground station.
Strax intill ligger Motorbranschens tekn: Right next door is the Motor Industry Technical Upper Secondary School, where the focus is on vehicles and transport. A short way from here is Västra Frölunda Cemetery, with medieval roots; the old Västra Frölunda Church stood here until it was pulled down in the 1860s. Iron rings for tethering horses are still set into the cemetery wall – a kind of car park from days gone by.
Strax intill ligger Mörby verkstäder, in: Right next door are the Mörby workshops, designed by Sigge Cronstedt and opened in 1906. The great workshop hall has stepped gables and roof lanterns that let in daylight, and trains on the Roslagsbanan line are still serviced here. In 1944, 144 people worked here; by 2011 there were just 15.
Strax intill ligger Nylöse kyrka, som ti: Right next to it is Nylöse Church, which used to be called Gamlestadens kapell. A little further along Gamlestadsvägen is the Gothenburg Hospital Cemetery, which dates back to the late 1500s. Only the odd gravestone is left today, but the site is protected by law as a heritage site, and a Franciscan friary also once stood here.
Strax intill ligger Rudboda gård, ett ti: Close by is Rudboda gård, a former croft that gave its name to the whole district. On Elfviksvägen stands Villa Molin, designed by Ralph Erskine in 1947 for the garden architect Ulla Molin. Not far off is Kyrkviken, once called Koltorpsviken, the narrow inlet of the sea that splits Lidingö into a northern and a southern half.
Strax intill ligger Råda säteri, en herr: Right next door is Råda säteri, a manor on Lake Rådasjön with a main house, wings and old farm buildings, all listed since 1969. The lake is up to 23 metres deep and supplies Mölndal with its drinking water. The Mölndalsån river runs straight through it and changes its name further downstream to Gullbergsån, so the water here flows all the way into Gothenburg.
Strax intill ligger Solvalla, Sveriges n: Right next to us is Solvalla, Sweden's national harness racing stadium and the largest trotting track in the Nordic countries. Every year it hosts Elitloppet, one of the world's biggest trotting races, and the stands hold 35,000 spectators. The track opened on 31 July 1927, and twelve races were held in its first year.
Strax intill ligger Tuve kyrka, en av Gö: Right beside us is Tuve Church, one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Since 2010 it has been part of Tuve-Säve parish. The old parish of Tuve belonged to the province of Västergötland and the Östra Hising hundred, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000 the parish had just over 10,000 residents.
Strax intill låg Karlsrofältet, en idrot: Right beside us was Karlsrofältet, a sports ground for almost sixty years. The name goes back to the iron porter Carl Jonsson and appears as Carlsro as early as 1834. A little further on begins the Botanical Garden, which opened in 1923 in time for the Jubilee Exhibition but wasn't considered finished until 1948. Its emblem is a wood anemone, and it has two stars in the Michelin travel guide.
Strax intill reser sig Fässbergs kyrka p: Right nearby, Fässberg Church stands on its hill. From 1922 to 1976 it was called Mölndal Church, because in 1922 the old Fässberg parish became the town of Mölndal. The parish goes back to the Middle Ages, and Gunnebo House lies within it too. A stone's throw away is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in a converted assembly hall.
Strax intill rinner Tappström, sundet me: Right beside us is Tappström, the channel between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön. It's about one and a half kilometres long but only 3.2 metres deep. On the Ekerö side there's a guest harbour for visiting boats, and the bridge here carries Ekerövägen, county road 261, all the way towards Brommaplan. So this is where one island ends and the next begins.
Strax intill studsar basketbollarna i Go: Right next door, basketballs are bouncing in Gothia Arena – home of Högsbo Basket and the only club-owned sports hall in Gothenburg. On match days it holds a thousand people. This whole area was once part of the parish of Västra Frölunda, which had around 13,500 residents in 1944 and became part of the City of Gothenburg the following year.
Strax intill står Akalla värmeverk, ett: Right beside us is Akalla värmeverk, a district heating plant from the mid-1970s. It may not sound thrilling, but the Stockholm City Museum rates two of its buildings as especially valuable to the city's cultural heritage. A little further away, in Akalla centrum, is a church with an unusual story. Consecrated in 1976, it was first shared by the Church of Sweden and EFS, a Lutheran revival movement. In 2020 it was sold to the Catholic diocese and is now the home church of the Syriac Catholic community.
Strax intill står Gibraltar herrgård, fa: Right next to us is Gibraltar herrgård, the old Chalmers family manor that gave Gibraltargatan its name. The wooden main house, in the Empire style, was built in 1847, and since 2024 it has stood in a new spot on Orrspelsgatan, south of the Chalmers University campus. One of the old estate manager's houses served as the Chalmers students' union building from 1948 to 1952.
Strax intill står Nacka kyrka, byggd 189: Right next door is Nacka Church, built in 1891 in Gothic Revival style, which gained a new funeral chapel in 1908–1909. It belongs to the old parish of Nacka, which had just 1,708 inhabitants in 1887 and became the town of Nacka in 1949. Across Kyrkviken bay, the Nysätra headland juts out into the water. The Nackanäs Inn welcomed guests there until it burned down in 1960.
Strax norr om kyrkan möter Tuve kyrkväg: Just north of the church, Tuve kyrkväg meets Holmvägen, the local road leading to Stora Holm's skid-training track, Stora Holm Manor and the Säve depot, among other places.
Strax norr om stationen finns en larmad: Just north of the station is an alarmed hall where metro trains are parked, with four tracks and room for six full-length trains. The station has only one way out, plus an emergency exit by the hall.
Strax norr om stationen grenade en hemli: Just north of the station, a secret branch line curved off to the west from 1941 until the late 1980s. Known as Krutbanan, the 'Gunpowder Line', it was three kilometres long and used for military purposes.
Strax norr om statyn står 13 stora almar: Just north of the statue stand 13 large elm trees that were going to be cut down for a new metro entrance. Thousands of Stockholmers protested, and in May 1971 the site was occupied for a week with hammocks and a tent camp. The elms are still standing.
Strax söder om Barkarby ligger Vålberga,: Just south of Barkarby lies Vålberga, a housing area built around 1963, made up mostly of long rows of terraced houses around a sports field. A little further away is Barkarby Villastad, with the neighbourhoods of Tingsbyn and Kyrkbyn – regarded as one of Järfälla's most valuable historic environments.
Strax söder om centrum, vid Stävholmsgrä: Just south of the centre, at Stävholmsgränd, lay a burial ground from the Bronze and Iron Ages. Excavations in 1966–1967 showed that people had lived here since the Stone Age. Its stone circle was unique in Stockholm, so the outer ring of stones was rebuilt when the rest made way for terraced houses.
Strax söder om kyrkans plats anlade Pete: Just south of where the church now stands, Peter Jonas Bergius laid out a botanic garden, Bergielund, in 1759. In 1885 it moved to Frescati, north of the inner city, and was renamed Bergianska trädgården, the Bergius Botanic Garden.
Strax utanför kusten ligger ön Trälen, o: Just off the coast lies the island of Trälen, which has had its moment as a TV star. In autumn 2006, TV4 aired a reality show called Trälen every weekday, in which wealthy inner-city Stockholmers and some less well-off suburbanites lived together on the island for 40 days. Half a million viewers tuned in for the first episode, but the numbers soon dropped off. The winner was Serhan Sören Erdal.
Strax väster om Danderyds kyrka, en bit: Just west of Danderyd Church, a little way from here, the runestone U 131 stands between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall. The Danderyd district is bordered by the Edsviken inlet to the south and west, and just over 11,000 people live here, most of them west of the E18.
Strax väster om gården ligger det välbev: Just west of the farm is Lugnet, a well-preserved croft – a red-painted double cottage with green shutters. Today it’s a summer café, and south of the farm some 15 apple trees survive from the old orchard.
Strax öster om Filipstadsbacken reser si: Just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, a 73-metre hill named after Burmanstorp. Around 1900, the land towards Lake Magelungen was meant to become Södertörns villastad, a garden suburb with almost 600 plots for well-to-do Stockholmers. But the plots were slow to sell, mostly because transport links were poor, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought out the whole company.
Strax öster om Holm ligger Stora Holms s: Just east of Holm lies the Stora Holm estate. In 1974 the playwright Ellen Bergman founded the Gothenburg Chamber Theatre here, in the house where she also lived, combining food and theatre in one evening. It closed in 1986.
Stridsvagnshindren från andra världskrig: The anti-tank barriers from the Second World War were left standing at Kungsportsplatsen until 5 March 1952.
Strosa förbi Engelska radhusen i kvarter: Stroll past Engelska radhusen, the English terraces, in the Drivbänken block
Strosa i Ekerö centrum och leta upp den: Wander round Ekerö centrum and find the giant 'dot'
Strosa i Järla sjö bland gamla industrih: Wander around Järla sjö among old industrial buildings
Strålsjön är en näringsfattig skogssjö s: Strålsjön is a nutrient-poor forest lake that's sensitive to acidification. Bog myrtle grows along the south-western shore, and just off the water's edge you'll find white and yellow water lilies and bulrushes.
Strålsjön är liten men hela 7,4 meter dj: Strålsjön is small but a full 7.4 metres deep, and it lies 34.8 metres above sea level. At its south-eastern end there's a bathing spot with a jetty, and the Sörmlandsleden trail passes by here too.
Studenthuset Fyrtalet heter så för att m: The student residence Fyrtalet – 'the Foursome' – got its name because four identical buildings were planned, though only one was ever built. It was designed by the architect Léonie Geisendorf. On Furusundsgatan stands YK-huset, built in 1939 as a collective housing block for the Professional Women's Club, complete with a nursery, restaurant and gym. And Värtan's station building from 1882 has a blue rating – the highest level of protection the City Museum awards.
Studentområdet Kungshamra har ett kungli: The Kungshamra student village has a royal name for good reason: the land was a gift from King Gustaf VI Adolf. The buildings went up between 1965 and 1967, and today there are 1,383 student homes here. A short walk away, in a patch of woodland, is Invalidkyrkogården, the Invalids' Cemetery – a burial ground opened in 1824, where the last burial took place in 1905.
Studion användes också för jazz. I febru: The studio was used for jazz too. In February 1995 Herbie Hancock dropped by to play piano on drummer Peter Johannesson's album Sixtus.
Studion fick 2011 namnet Ingrid efter In: In 2011 the studio was named Ingrid, after Ingrid Bergman and the venue's past as a cinema. When the City Museum documented it in 2019, the red velvet cinema seats were still in place.
Stugan som var skola: The cottage that was a school
Stureby började byggas 1921 och hette då: Building started in Stureby in 1921, when it was called Ersta Villastad, but after protests it was renamed in 1926 – and Stureby is a made-up name. Nearby is the Vivstavarvsvägen terrace, 36 terraced houses from the early 1950s designed by Erik F. Dahl, and the only housing in Stureby marked blue by the City Museum. And Sockenvägen, which links up the northern part of Brännkyrka parish, is no less than 5,450 metres long.
Stureplan var Sveriges dyraste plats för: Stureplan was the most expensive place in Sweden for illuminated advertising. In the 1950s a property owner with four or five signs could earn around 50,000 kronor a year. Brands lit up here included Marabou, Pommac, Osram and Lipton's tea.
Stureplan var en livlig bytespunkt med t: Stureplan was a busy interchange with a newsstand beneath Svampen, the Mushroom shelter. When Sweden switched to driving on the right on 3 September 1967, the trams disappeared and the square became a sterile island surrounded by traffic.
Stureplan är Östermalms livliga mötespla: Stureplan is Östermalm's buzzing meeting place. In the middle of the square stands Svampen, the Mushroom, a concrete rain shelter from the 1930s that has become the classic place to meet up.
Stuvsta gårds kvarn, Kvarnberget: The Stuvsta gård windmill on Kvarnberget
Stuvsta och Snättringe var fram till 201: Until 2018, Stuvsta and Snättringe were a single municipal district of just over 16,000 people, before being split in two. Not far from here, Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, and several of its millstones survive. The municipality has placed one of them on Gymnasievägen, where Huddingegymnasiet, the sixth-form school, occupies a building listed among the municipality's most valuable.
Stuvsta sträcker sig hela vägen från Hag: Stuvsta stretches all the way from Hagsätra in the north down to Tomtberga and Hörningsnäs farm in the south, and east to Lake Trehörningen. Not far from here, the Stuvstaleden road runs through the Kungsklippan rock in the Stuvsta tunnel, opened in 1994. Its northern entrance is built into a block of flats that straddles the approach road.
Stuvstatunneln är 193 meter lång och går: The 193-metre Stuvsta tunnel has run through the Kungsklippan rock since 1994. Before that the road went right through Stuvsta, causing noise problems. A new bridge over the railway was built at the same time.
Styrsö är en av de största öarna i södra: Styrsö is one of the largest islands in the southern archipelago. People live here all year round, and the island has sheltered swimming coves, meadows and old fishing villages.
Stäven som bröt isen: The bow that broke the ice
Stålbolag i glashuset: Steel companies in the glass house
Större delen av Skintebo ligger i en dal: Most of Skintebo lies in a hollow surrounded by hills. A narrow valley leads you down to the sea, half a kilometre to the west. The land that couldn't be farmed had already been built on with houses.
Största hyresgästen i Lidingö Arena är e: The biggest tenant in Lidingö Arena is a 31-room hotel that moved in in 1996. An arcade runs along the street, and there's a car park underneath.
Subtopia, en kort promenad bort, hette t: A short walk away is Subtopia, formerly known as Kulturhuset Rotemannen. Today it's a production hub for the arts, with studios, workshops and rehearsal spaces, and it has been a long-standing supporter of the circus world. Further on is Fittja farm, whose inn was one of the largest coaching inns in Sweden in the 17th and 18th centuries. Since 1987 the farm has been home to the Multicultural Centre.
Subtopias hus byggdes i början av 1900-t: The Subtopia building was put up in the early 1900s by telephone magnate Lars Magnus Ericsson as an experimental cowshed for Alby farm. It was built of concrete and – naturally – had a telephone. Among other things, Ericsson tested how to get cows to give milk evenly all year round.
Sundbyberg är Sveriges till ytan minsta: Sundbyberg is the smallest municipality in Sweden by area, at just 8.79 square kilometres. On Esplanaden you'll find the library, Det Nya Museet – the New Museum – and a bust of the town's founder, Anders Petter Löfström. Right next door is the Bristol cinema, which opened on New Year's Eve 1939 and now doubles as an arts venue.
Sundbyberg är en av Stockholms äldsta fö: Sundbyberg is one of Stockholm's oldest suburbs. It became a market town, a köping, in 1888, and was granted town status in 1927. The railway station is older still: it opened in 1876 on the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen railway. And 26 metres beneath your feet, deep in the rock, is the metro station, decorated with sculptures of building façades and the human senses.
Sundbybergs gamla stadshus vid torget ri: Sundbyberg's old town hall on the square was designed in 1932 by Nils Malmborg and Sven Ahlbom. Today it's part of Signalfabriken, but Ture Tideblad's municipal coat of arms still sits above the old main entrance.
Sundbybergs kommun köpte säteriet 1961 o: Sundbyberg municipality bought the manor in 1961 and let it as a residence, to the politicians Sven Andersson and Sven Aspling among others. In 2001 it was bought by Lennart Ehrenlood, who restored it and wrote a book about the estate. In 2017 the municipality bought it back for almost 20 million kronor.

Sundbyberg municipality bought the manor in 1961 and let it out as a home, to tenants including the government ministers Sven Andersson and Sven Aspling. In 2001 it was bought by Lennart Ehrenlood, who wrote a book about the estate. The municipality bought it back in 2017 for almost 20 million kronor.
Sundbybergs stadsmuseum berättar histori: Sundbyberg City Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb from the 1860s onwards. Its collection includes burnt bones from a Viking Age grave, excavated on the spot where the Sieverts cable works later stood. You can also see parts of the runestone U 78, which went missing in the 18th century. Two pieces were found in Ursvik, spent many years in the porch of Solna Church, and finally came to the museum in 1976.
Sundbybergs viktigaste landmärke, det nu: Sundbyberg's best-known landmark is its water tower, no longer in use. It was designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912 as a symbol of a growing, modern Sundbyberg. Around it lies Tornparken, the Tower Park, whose dance floor was a popular meeting place in the 1940s and 50s, and in the 1970s its community sing-alongs drew big crowds. The Bristol cinema on Sturegatan opened back on New Year's Eve 1939.
Sundet Tappström är omkring en och en ha: The Tappström strait is about one and a half kilometres long and 3.2 metres deep. On the east side lies Fiskarfjärden and on the west Långtarmen.
Sundet binder ihop två fjärdar: Fiskarfj: The strait links two bays: Fiskarfjärden to the east and Långtarmen to the west. On the Ekerö side there's a guest harbour for leisure boats.
Sundet är en del av Mälaren. I sydväst a: The strait is part of Lake Mälaren. To the south-west it joins the Långtarmen bay, and to the north-east it opens out into Mörbyfjärden and Malmvikssjön.
Svandammen i Solhem är både park och bad: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, in Solhem is both a park and a swimming spot, and it's become a favourite hangout for teenagers and families alike. No wonder, really, since buses leave from there in almost every direction: to Brommaplan, Backlura, Vällingby, Hallonbergen, Solna centrum and Spånga station. A swim and a bus ride, all in one.
Svandammen är både park och badplats, oc: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, is both a park and a place to swim, and a favourite meeting spot for teenagers and families in Solhem. The name Spånga is really old: it was first written down as early as 1300, and means roughly 'spångar' – simple plank bridges over boggy ground. Spånga parish once took in both Hässelby Castle and Akalla.
Svanhuset hade en bassäng i mitten och t: The Swan House had a pool in the middle with wedge-shaped pens around it, and a hayloft under the roof. In winter it was heated by a tiled stove. That's how the park's swans lived right up until the 1960s.
Svartedalen byggdes mest under 1950- och: Svartedalen was mostly built in the 1950s and 60s, and between 1965 and 1967 the city's own housing company put up 358 flats here. A little way off is Jättesten, named after the boulders on the hill, and A C Lindblads gata, a street named after the newspaperman who became the first Gothenburger to sit in parliament for the Social Democrats.
Svea artilleriregemente låg här fram til: The Svea Artillery Regiment was based here until 1963, which is why the streets are called Lavettvägen (Gun Carriage Road), Pjäsbacken (Gun Hill) and Kavallerivägen (Cavalry Road). Other names, such as Valkyriavägen and Odalvägen, allude to the area's many ancient remains.
Svea ritades av arkitekten Lennart Cleme: Svea was designed by the architect Lennart Clemens and had three auditoriums seating 90, 61 and 60. Back in its days as Klappan, the same cinema held 238 seats – more than it ever did afterwards.
Sveabron was meant to be a simple wooden bridge. But the company Skånska Cement offered to build an eight-by-eight-metre concrete arch bridge for just 1,800 kronor and got the job. The bridge opened in time for the General Art and Industrial Exhibition of 1897.
Svedmyra låter oskyldigt, men namnet kom: Svedmyra sounds harmless enough, but the name comes from a croft called Svinmyran – ‘the pig bog’. Known since the 14th century, the croft belonged to Östberga farm. The district is ringed by woods and parkland, and the City of Stockholm classes the Svedmyra woods as a core area of high ecological value. In the metro station, the artist Torgny Larsson has created a 40-metre glass screen decorated with the leaves of broadleaf trees.
Svedmyra tunnelbanestation ligger trots: Despite its name, Svedmyra metro station isn't in Svedmyra at all, but just west of the boundary in Stureby. From around 2032 the station will belong to the blue line instead of the green.
Svedmyra tunnelbanestation ligger, trots: Svedmyra metro station, despite its name, isn't in Svedmyra but in Stureby. A stone's throw away is Svedmyrabadet from 1969, where the water is kept at a toasty 32 to 34 degrees for warm-water exercise. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, which opened in 1924 and hosted jumping competitions right up until 1990.
Sven Markelius ritade 1931 en hangar för: In 1931 Sven Markelius designed a hangar for seaplanes. In winter it became Lindarängen's ice palace, Sweden's first indoor arena for ice hockey, curling and figure skating. Today the building is a state-listed monument and still stands in the container port.
Sven Markelius skissade 1958 på en stor: In 1958 Sven Markelius sketched a great ring of slab blocks on top of the rocky hill, but the plan gave too few homes and was rejected. Instead, Åke Östin designed the large parallel buildings that form big urban blocks.
Svenska mästerskapen i friidrott har avg: The Swedish Athletics Championships have been held at Sollentunavallen five times: in 1969, 1971, 1995, 2006 and 2016. An athletics Grand Prix is also staged here every year.
Sveriges enda väg till havet: Sweden's only route to the sea
Sveriges första golfklubb bildades i Göt: Sweden's first golf club was founded in Gothenburg in 1891. Three years later, local man Viktor H. Setterberg laid out an 18-hole course of 1,692 metres on the Skalebackarna slopes in neighbouring Arendal. The course was turned into farmland during the First World War.
Sveriges första järnvägstunnel, 276 mete: Sweden’s first railway tunnel, 276 metres long, was blasted with gunpowder by prisoners from Långholmen prison. The rock was hoisted out with hand-operated cranes under the eye of armed guards. Work began on 16 July 1858.
Sveriges första klinik för cancerbehandl: Sweden's first cancer clinic, Radiumhemmet, was founded in 1910 in a flat on Kungsholmen, and since 1938 it has been part of the hospital here in Solna. A little further on stood Norrbacka inn, one of Stockholm's well-known roadside inns on the road to Uppsala, until it burned down in 1882. There were also plans for a lookout tower in Hagaparken, but work on it never even began.
Sveriges första socialdemokratiska stats: Sweden's first Social Democratic prime minister
Sveriges tidiga golfbana: One of Sweden's first golf courses
Sveriges volymmässigt största levande lö: A short walk from here grows Sweden's largest living deciduous tree by volume: the Ekebyhov Oak. It may be around 500 years old and was declared a natural monument in 1956. Beside it is Ekebyhov Palace, a Carolean-style manor house built in the late 17th century for Carl Gustav Wrangel. It may well be the largest surviving wooden palace in Sweden.
Svindersviken har fått namn efter hollän: Svindersviken is named after the Dutchman Johan van Swindern, who had a pitch works built here. It ran from 1671 to 1825.
Svingel är ett gammalt dialektord för vä: ‘Svingel’ is an old dialect word for a bend in the road. This is where the road from Stampen swung round to reach a bridge over the dug canals – spelt ‘groopar’ in those days. The word is borrowed from Dutch or from the German ‘Zwingel’ or ‘Zwengel’.
Svingeln var från början namnet på en jo: Svingeln was originally the name of a farm property at the junction of Friggagatan and Stampgatan, listed in Örgryte's parish register for 1814–1815. Today trams 1, 3, 6 and 8 meet here, and the rebuild that began in 2017 increased the number of bus stops from two to five.
Svängbron och vattenledningen: The swing bridge and the water main
Swedbank var den första av de fyra storb: Swedbank was the first of Sweden’s four big banks to move its head office out of central Stockholm, relocating here from Brunkebergstorg. The building was designed by the Danish firm 3XN, who set out to express the bank’s values of openness, simplicity and care. SEB followed suit in 2017.
Sydost om vattentornet breder den 100 he: South-east of the water tower stretches the 100-hectare Fagersjöskogen forest. It's home to Stockholm's largest spruce, with a trunk more than three metres round at chest height.
Symbolen som inte godkändes: The emblem that was turned down
Synskadades museum: Synskadades museum, the museum of visual impairment
Synskadades museum öppnade för allmänhet: The Museum of the Visually Impaired opened to the public in April 1997. It's run by the Swedish Association of the Visually Impaired, and its Open Store exhibition shares a building with the association's offices at Sandsborgsvägen 52.
Syrhåla, stadsdelen en bit härifrån, har: Syrhåla, the district just along from here, has a name that's hardly a selling point. It's recorded in 1550 as Siöralla and means a swampy spot or sour ground, after the low, damp land between the hills east and south-east of the old village. The district was created in 1957, when Arendal was split in two.
Systerkvarnen hamnade i Ursvik: The sister mill ended up in Ursvik
Systrarna Kabaca växte upp här: Where the Kabaca sisters grew up
Säby kyrka, församlingskyrkan för hela S: Säby Church, the parish church for all of Salem municipality, is just a few steps away. A couple of hundred metres from here stood Charlottenlund, also called Lottalund, a little cottage for a farm labourer and his family. In the autumn of 1853 the labourer Lars Björkman moved in with his wife Christina Charlotta, and he put in his days of labour at Fågelsta farm. The family stayed until Björkman died in 1887.
Säby köptes in vid NK:s 25-årsjubileum 1: Säby was bought to mark the NK department store’s 25th anniversary in 1927. Staff at NK and the NK school could then spend their holidays here, and the estate became a meeting place with lots of activities.
Säteri utan huvudbyggnad: A manor without a main house
Sätra gård hör till Stockholms äldsta gå: Sätra gård is one of the oldest farms in Stockholm, known since the 1300s. It gave its name to the whole district, and its two surviving buildings probably date from the 1700s. On the district's highest point, Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, stands the water tower – a landmark since 1969 that you can see all the way from Ekerö.
Sätra radiolänktorn från 1960 står på en: Sätra's radio relay tower, from 1960, stands on a hill 71 metres high. At just over 64 metres tall, it reaches 135 metres above sea level and has become a well-known landmark. Along the shore of Lake Mälaren you'll find the Sätraskogen nature reserve and the Mälarhöjden bathing spot.
Sätra radiolänktorn, även kallat Sätra t: Sätra radio link tower, also known as Sätra telelänktorn, stands on Backvindeln, close to where Mälarhöjden meets Bredäng. Painted in the pale 'Stockholm white', it has become a familiar landmark, though it isn't open to the public. A little further on is Bredängshallen, a swimming pool and sports hall from the mid-1960s that the City Museum has marked in green for its heritage value.
Sätras högsta punkt är Sätra berg, 71 me: Sätra's highest point is Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, crowned by a water tower since 1969. The district is named after Sätra gård, one of Stockholm's oldest farms, known as far back as the 1300s. A little further on you'll find the Church of Saint Maroun, formerly Sätra church, and the Smistabron bridge for pedestrians and cyclists, which has spanned the motorway since 2008.
Säve har vuxit rejält. År 1913 bodde 1 5: Säve has grown a great deal. In 1913 Säve parish had 1,598 inhabitants; by 2000 there were almost 12,000. The parish belonged to Västra Hising hundred, an old district of Bohuslän, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. The parish church, Säve Church, is a short walk away, and since 2010 it has been part of Tuve-Säve parish.
Sävedalen betyder helt enkelt Säveåns da: Sävedalen simply means the valley of the Säveån river. It's an inner suburb of Gothenburg in Partille municipality. Right here, from 1985 to 2013, was Partille Bokhandel, a bookshop that sold mostly Swedish titles but also books in French – a little corner of Paris in the middle of Sävedalen.

Sävedalen simply means 'the valley of the Säveån river', and it's an inner suburb of Gothenburg in Partille municipality. From 1990, Partille Bokhandel, a bookshop, stood here on Göteborgsvägen. Most of its titles were Swedish, but it also stocked books in French – a little piece of Paris right in the middle of Sävedalen.

Så sent som 1901 fanns bara spridda torp: As late as 1901 there were only scattered crofts where Sannaplan lies today. The square got its name in 1918. At its south-eastern corner is the entrance to Västra kyrkogården cemetery, with kiosks from the 1920s.
Så sent som på 1940-talet bestod området: As late as the 1940s, the area around Blackeberg was mostly woods and rocky hills. Then, in the early 1950s, the district was built to a town plan drawn up under Sven Markelius. Bio Kaskad, the cinema on Blackebergsplan, opened in 1957, closed in the late 1990s and was brought back to life in 2018. And Råcksta träsk, the little pond nearby, was dredged in the early 1970s when it was starting to silt up.

Sågen som drevs av en lokomobil: A sawmill driven by a steam engine
Sågen är själva mittpunkten i Vendelsö,: Sågen is the very heart of Vendelsö, a residential area made up mostly of blocks of flats from the 1950s to the 1970s, with a grocery shop and a restaurant in the centre. Vendelsö lies on both sides of the Gudöbroleden road, between Lake Drevviken and Tyresta National Park to the east. Winding through it is the Vendelsån stream, which gathers water from three lakes on its way to Drevviken.
Söder om Dalen ligger kvarteret Barnmors: South of Dalen lies the Barnmorskan block, where 22 terraced houses were built in 2008–2010. They have drawn attention for their striking black and white facades.
Söder om Elvesta gård har det lilla vatt: South of Elvesta farm a small stream has carved out a deep ravine. The farm track crosses it on a tall structure of stone arches.
Söder om Elvesta gård har ån grävt ut en: South of Elvesta farm the stream has carved out a deep ravine, which the farm track crosses on a tall stone arch. There was a mill here as early as the 1600s, and it kept working until the 1930s. The surviving mill building dates from the 1850s.
Söder om Lundby nya kyrka står Sannegård: South of Lundby nya kyrka, Lundby New Church, is Sannegårdsmonumentet, what remains of a burial ground from the transition between the Bronze and Iron Ages. Four standing stones are lined up in a row. The biggest, a triangular stone, is still in its original spot, while the other three were moved because of gravel digging. The church's own name, incidentally, has been used for two different church buildings.
Söder om Rågsved tar Rågsveds friområde: South of Rågsved begins the Rågsved open space, also called Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of wild country with some dramatic terrain – heights, cliffs and valleys in an ancient fissure-valley landscape. Part of it became a nature reserve in 2018. In the other direction is Högdalen skatepark, Stockholm's largest, built at the initiative of a local group called Stockholm Sub Surfers.
Söder om Stockholm finns Vargen i Huddin: South of Stockholm, in Huddinge, lies Vargen, an almost identical facility. The idea was that crisis management could move between the two and feel instantly at home. The main centres were given animal names, while smaller ones got plant names – like Pionen, the Peony, on Södermalm.
Söder om Stockholm, i Huddinge, finns Va: South of Stockholm, in Huddinge, is Vargen (the Wolf), an almost identical facility. The two were built to the same design so that crisis management teams could move between them and feel instantly at home. Main centres were given animal names, while smaller units were named after plants, such as Krokusen (the Crocus) and Pionen (the Peony).
Söder om gården anlade Wijnbladh en stor: South of the house, Wijnbladh laid out a large garden with more than 400 fruit trees, and on a hillock an English-style park modelled on royal examples. The tall trees he planted in the late 1700s still stand in the park today.
Söder om höghusen ligger Akalla by, med: South of the tower blocks lies Akalla village, with buildings preserved from as far back as the 17th century. The farm is kept going with help from the youth organisation 4H. Järvafältet also has Hästa farm, the last working farm in the City of Stockholm.
Söder om höghuset finns en spegeldamm me: South of the tower block lies a reflecting pool with a fountain by landscape architect Erik Glemme, and in the basin stands Folke Truedsson's sculpture Horisontal from 1973. During the renovation that began in 2013, 1950s-style neon signs were put up above the shops.
Söder om trafikplatsen står de två tulls: South of the interchange, the two toll houses from 1733 still stand. Between them there was once a wooden toll gate shaped like a triumphal arch. When they were renovated in 2013, the original colours were uncovered: pink and white. Traffic passed between the houses right up until 1940.
Söderhöjden, en bit härifrån, byggdes 19: Söderhöjden, a short way from here, was built in 1967 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, and it's where you'll find Jakobsberg's bowling alley. The square was renovated and reopened on 31 August 2013. In the middle stands a spherical artwork that glows in different colours depending on the season.
Söderläget och bergsryggen i norr ger en: The south-facing slope and the ridge to the north give a noticeably higher average temperature, with an earlier spring and a longer summer. Over 400 species grow here, including two hawkweeds found nowhere else in the world and garden plants gone wild from the old summer villas.
Södertörn är den enda högskolan i Sverig: Södertörn is the only university in Sweden where you can study philosophy in the continental tradition. It has also been tasked by the government with training teachers in the Romani Chib language and Roma culture, in close cooperation with the Roma minority.
Södertörns villastad byggde sina första: In the early 1900s the Södertörn garden suburb company built its first villas here, north of the new Nynäs railway and close to Fagersjö station house. Many of them were demolished when modern Fagersjö was built in the 1960s.
To the south, Årstaviken bay sparkles.
Södra station öppnade 1860 som Stockholm: Södra station opened in 1860 as Stockholm's first railway station, the terminus of the Western Main Line. For nine years it was the capital's most important station, until Stockholm Central opened in 1871.
Sörgården är Tenstas enda ursprungliga s: Sörgården is the only original area of small houses in Tensta. In 1974 architects Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist won the Ytong Prize for the block, sharing it with Ralph Erskine for his Nya Bruket housing estate in Sandviken.
Sörgårdens småhus uppfördes med självbyg: The small houses at Sörgården were built by the residents themselves. Each has three bedrooms, which could become five with lightweight partitions. The living room sits at an angle and, together with a storeroom and a fence, encloses a private courtyard.
Sörred har ett namn som inte smickrar. D: Sörred's name isn't exactly flattering. It's recorded in 1388 as Surfua rudi, and the first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a lazy, careless sort of man – a slacker or a good-for-nothing. The second part comes from the Old Swedish word ryd, a clearing. Still, the slacker's clearing ended up as a place of hard work: this is where construction of Volvo's Torslanda plant began in 1960–61.
T-Centralen är en av bara två stationer: T-Centralen is one of only two stations on the green line where the art was unveiled at the same time as the station opened. On the upper level you'll find Siri Derkert's Kvinnopelaren (the Women's Pillar) and the 145-metre ceramic frieze Klaravagnen, both from 1957.
TA, som gett hållplatsen namn, är kaross: TA, which gives the stop its name, is the body plant where production begins. T stands for Torslanda, and A, B and C follow the car on its way: body, paint shop and final assembly. TA delivered its first body back in 1961, for a Volvo Amazon.

Ta med kikaren! En bit bort ligger Svank: Bring your binoculars! A short way off is Svankälla wetland park, home to marsh harriers, little grebes and lesser spotted woodpeckers. A little further west is Ligårds mosse, a bog so hemmed in by marshland that it's hard to reach. Among the reeds and water lilies, crucian carp and grass carp weighing several kilos are said to lurk.
Tack vare en donation från Nordiska muse: Thanks to a donation from the Nordic Museum in 2003, the library holds around 14,000 old dissertations from the 17th, 18th and 19th centuries, from the universities of Uppsala, Lund, Turku and Greifswald, among others.
Taket målades troligen under andra halva: The ceiling was probably painted in the rococo style in the second half of the 1700s, by an unknown artist. The organ front from 1898 was designed by Ragnar Östberg. The octagonal bell tower took its present form in 1832 and holds a bell from 1770.

Tallkrogen har fått sitt namn efter ett: Tallkrogen takes its name from an inn, Stora Tallkrogen. The district counts as one of Stockholm's garden suburbs, and one of its streets, Victor Balcks väg, is named after the father of Swedish sport. In fact there were three inns – Stora, Lilla and Gamla Tallkrogen, the Big, Little and Old – along the old country road to Dalarö.

Tallkrogen takes its name from an inn, Stora Tallkrogen. It's one of Stockholm's garden suburbs, and one of its streets, Victor Balcks väg, is named after the father of Swedish sport. The area also had a croft called Svedmyra, known in earlier times as Svinmyra, Pig Bog. It was pulled down in the 1930s but lent its name to the neighbouring district.
Tallskogen på höjderna har troligen slup: The pine forest on the heights has probably escaped modern forestry, so the trees are of different ages and there's plenty of dead wood. Look out for crested tits, black woodpeckers and goshawks. By the stream there's a pond dug in 2012 for frogs, toads and newts.
Talludden kallas också Neptuns udde. I o: Talludden is also known as Neptune's Point. Here you'll find Käppalaställningen, a Second World War anti-aircraft battery with gun pits and weapon emplacements. It was restored and reopened in 1994 as a listed memorial to Stockholm's air defence, the only one of its kind in Sweden. A little further away is Käppalaverket, a sewage treatment plant from 1969 that's regarded as one of the most efficient in the world.
Tallumpaviljongen, med sina pyramidforma: The Tallum Pavilion, with its pyramid-shaped roofs, was designed by Gunnar Asplund in 1922. Its name comes from ‘Tallum’, the motto Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz used when they entered the 1915 competition to design Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. The building was probably only meant to be temporary, but it stayed and served as a utility building until 1981. Skogskyrkogården has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.
Tandklinik i skolhuset: A dental clinic in the schoolhouse
Tanken var att båda föräldrarna skulle k: The idea was that both parents should be able to go out to work. The building had a restaurant, a day nursery, a supermarket, a photo lab, a petrol station and a chapel. The chapel is now a nursery, and in 1975 the road outside was named Olle Engkvists väg.
Tappström var en egen tätort fram till 1: Tappström was a separate town until 1975 and is now part of Ekerö. Commuter boat 89 to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay, is served by M/S Lux, among others.
Tappström är ett smalt sund mellan Ekerö: Tappström is a narrow strait between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön – about 1.5 kilometres long and only just over three metres deep. On its shore, Ralph Erskine designed Ekerö centrum, completed in 1991, with a 'dot' more than twenty metres high as its landmark. Erskine lived on Lovön himself and said he enjoyed coming here to do his shopping. From here, commuter boat 89 runs all the way into Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay.
Tappsund var ett ångtegelbruk, där maski: Tappsund was a steam-powered brickworks, its machinery driven by a steam engine until it was electrified in the 1920s. At the centre of the works stood a ring kiln, with the drying sheds arranged in a square around it. The street name Tegelbruksvägen, Brickworks Road, recalls the old works.
Taverna och centraltvätt: A taverna and a central laundry
Teater Pero bildades 1983 av Peter Engkv: Teater Pero was founded in 1983 by Peter Engkvist and Roger Westberg. Its venue at Sveavägen 114 was one of Sweden's first cinema auditoriums. In 2018 the theatre received the City of Stockholm's honorary award.
Teater och mat på Stora Holm: Dinner and drama at Stora Holm
Teatern hörde tidigare till Göteborgs St: The theatre used to be part of Göteborgs Stadsteater, the City Theatre, but has been independent since 1996. Productions staged here include Momo, A Clockwork Orange, The Cherry Orchard and Himmel över Göteborg.
Teaterälskare, spetsa öronen! Angereds t: Theatre lovers, listen up! Angereds teater, in the Blå Stället arts centre, stages brand-new plays for children, teenagers and adults, and runs its own drama school too. The arts centre is on Angereds torg, the square that was called Triörtorget until 1977. Closer to the stop is Gunnared cemetery.

Teknikintresserade Ericsson experimenter: Ever the technology enthusiast, Ericsson experimented with ventilation and electric ploughs. The ploughs were no success, but they gave the neighbours plenty to talk about. He also built the "Alby Stadium", which looked like a Roman aqueduct and carried manure.
Tekniska museet: Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology
Telefonpionjären Lars Magnus Ericsson äg: The telephone pioneer Lars Magnus Ericsson owned Alby gård, the manor by Lake Albysjön a little way from here, from 1895 to 1913, and it was in his time that the house got its distinctive look. A later owner, Alfred Ekström, founded the laundry firm AB Fittja Familietvätt and pioneered new methods of industrial washing. Also in the neighbourhood is Fittja gård, where the Svartlösa district court used to sit.
Telefonplan domineras av LM Ericssons ga: Telefonplan is dominated by LM Ericsson's old factory and head office, built between 1938 and 1940 to designs by Ture Wennerholm. The architectural historian Fredric Bedoire has called it perhaps the most beautiful of all Stockholm's functionalist industrial complexes. Today it's home to, among others, Konstfack, the University of Arts, Crafts and Design, and the interactive light installation Colour by Numbers glows above Telefonplan.
Teleskopgatan 2 var kontor åt Göteborgsh: Teleskopgatan 2 housed offices for the Göteborgshem housing company from 1975 to 1978. Lars Ågren, the architect who had designed the buildings, then converted it into Stacken, a co-housing block completed in 1980. In 2016–2017 it was turned into a passive house with a new facade.
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader: The old Televerket offices, once home to Sweden's telecoms authority
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader, en ko: A short walk away are the former offices of Televerket, the old Swedish telecoms authority, which served as Telia Company's headquarters until 2016. The complex was built in stages between 1962 and 1972 to designs by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan won the prestigious Kasper Salin Prize for architecture. If you'd like to dig deeper into the area's past, Farsta hembygdsförening, the local history society, covers Farsta's story from prehistoric times to the present day.
Tellus visade film för första gången den: Tellus showed its first film on 22 November 1920, when the auditorium had 108 seats. In the 1930s two more cinemas opened in "Kransen", Saba and Svanen, but both closed in the 1960s.
Tengbom arkitekter förvandlade kontorshu: Tengbom architects converted the office building into housing and placed 18 terraced houses on the roofs. The flats range from one room and a kitchen up to eight rooms and a kitchen. The building was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2012.
Tengbom ritade villan i nedtonad nationa: Tengbom designed the villa in a toned-down National Romantic style, with a hipped, flared roof. The Brunius couple wanted a simple house that was cheap to run, with low ceilings to save on heating. Only the study at the very top was given a high ceiling.
Tengboms arkitekter använde kameran som: Tengbom architects built the Canon building around the idea of a camera. Facing busy Uppsalavägen, the facade is closed with square windows, while the side facing the square is glazed from the ground to the roofline. The brushed stainless-steel Canon signs are almost as tall as the building.
Tengdahl arbetade som murare och ritare: Tengdahl worked as a bricklayer and draughtsman before becoming a journalist at the newspaper Social-Demokraten. When Stockholm's Folkets hus, the labour movement's meeting hall, was to be built, someone with building know-how was needed, and from 1898 to 1901 he served as its agent and the main driving force behind the project.
Tengdahl satt i 13 år i arbetsutskottet: Tengdahl spent 13 years on the working committee for the building of Stockholm City Hall. It was he who took the initiative for the architect Ragnar Östberg to be granted an annual pension of 7,000 kronor in 1924.
Tennishall med kyrktorn: A tennis hall with a church tower
Tennishallen kom till på initiativ av Gu: The tennis hall was built at the initiative of Gustaf V and paid for with backing from Marcus Wallenberg and the car dealer Ernst S. Nilson, among others. It cost three million kronor and opened on 22 October 1943, in the middle of the Second World War, with the royal family and Prime Minister Per Albin Hansson in attendance.
Tennispaviljongen är en nationalromantis: The tennis pavilion is a National Romantic wooden building with two aisles and a 'church tower' on the entrance side. It looks like a big turn-of-the-century villa, in the same spirit as the Stockholm Exhibition of 1897.
Tensta Träff, gymnasiet och Tenstahallen: Tensta Träff, the upper secondary school and Tenstahallen were completed in 1984 and stand out from the rest of the district. The architect Gösta Uddén blended modernism with traditional Asian architecture, using red brick, patterned concrete and glulam timber. All three buildings carry the blue heritage rating.
Tensta byggdes mellan 1966 och 1972 som: Tensta was built between 1966 and 1972 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, but today it's the culture that draws people in. Tensta konsthall, a few minutes away, shows contemporary art, and Tenstakyrkan church has a thriving music scene rooted in gospel, where many different Christian traditions share one congregation.
Tensta gymnasium och Tekniska i Tensta: Tensta gymnasium and Tekniska i Tensta, upper secondary schools
Tensta konsthall grundades 1998, när Sto: Tensta konsthall was founded in 1998, the year Stockholm was European Capital of Culture. Internationally renowned artists such as Wolfgang Tillmans, Julian Opie and Shirin Neshat have exhibited here. Since 2014 the gallery has also awarded a writing prize to young writers from the suburbs.
Tensta vattentorn tronar på Tenstas högs: Tensta water tower stands proudly on the highest point in Tensta and can be seen from far across the open land of Järvafältet. It was built in 1969 and the Stockholm City Museum has marked it in green as particularly valuable. Underneath the tower is the Tensta tunnel, where the E18 motorway runs through two separate 300-metre concrete tubes, built between 2010 and 2014.
Tenstakyrkan, alldeles intill, är en fri: Right next door is Tenstakyrkan, a free church known for its rich musical life with strong gospel roots. Close by is Tensta konsthall, a centre for contemporary art. And down in the metro, the artist Helga Henschen decorated the station on the theme A Rose for the Immigrants, using texts and poems among other things.
Terminalen ligger intill rorohamnen och: The terminal sits next to the ro-ro port and partly came into use in December 2018. Once fully built, it will be able to handle two trains of 560–730 metres and four trains of 420 metres at the same time.
Terminalen ritades av Gustaf Rosenberg,: The terminal was designed by Gustaf Rosenberg, who won the Tengbom Prize in 1984. The track hall has four railway lines and a roof of glulam arches, with daylight pouring in through eight roof lanterns. The total floor area is about 104,000 square metres.
Textilföretaget Gamlestadens Fabriker ha: The textile company Gamlestadens Fabriker had lots of long shafts that kept bending out of true and wrecking the rigid ball bearings. The mechanical engineer Sven Wingquist solved the problem with a self-aligning ball bearing that could adjust to the angle.

Tidig vår i söderläge: An early spring on the south slope
Tidiga sommarnöjen vid Mälaren: Early summer retreats on Lake Mälaren
Tidningen Idun gjorde 1906 ett hemma hos: In 1906 the magazine Idun ran an at-home feature on Villa Bergh, with its blue walls and Blüthner grand piano. Richard Bergh said the house was so peaceful that he often sat lost in a book until half past one in the morning.
Till Elvesta gård hörde en kvarn som fin: Elvesta farm had a mill recorded as early as the 1600s. It kept working right up until the 1930s, and the mill building still standing beside the stream dates from the 1850s.
Till GP:s hundraårsjubileum 1959 fick sä: For the 100th anniversary of the newspaper GP in 1959, the typesetting room was given Gunnar Nylund's ceramic relief "Vår tid" (Our Time). The printing works later moved to Backa, and in 1988 the old presses in the GP building were dismantled by a Chinese company.
Till Gustaf V:s 70-årsdag 1928 samlades: For Gustaf V's 70th birthday in 1928, more than five million kronor was raised and presented to him in a silver casket. The King decided the money should go to the fight against cancer, and the result was the Jubilee Clinics in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Lund.
Till Hökmossen hörde förr backstugan Mic: Hökmossen once included the cottage of Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. A little further away is Hägerstensbadet, known locally as Personnebadet after Personnevägen – an outdoor pool that opened on 21 June 1961. The water is heated by solar panels, and swimming is free.
Till Nackanäs värdshus hörde en lummig t: Nackanäs inn had a leafy garden and an octagonal pavilion out in the strait, where the annual crayfish premiere – the start of the crayfish season – was held, among other events. Breakfast, dinner and late suppers were served, and guests could play on two skittle alleys.
Till Snörom hörde inga ägor, bara ett ka: Snörom came with no land of its own – just a kappland, an old measure of just over 150 square metres, where the residents grew potatoes. The 18th-century log cabin is now let out as a holiday cottage.

On your right is Kungliga slottet, Stockholm Palace.

Till höger syns Älvsborgsbron, invigd 19: On the right is Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, opened in 1966.
Till höger, på andra sidan vattnet, ligg: Across the water on the right is the island of Långholmen.
Till höger, uppe på berget, ser du Masth: On your right, up on the hill, is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget Church, from 1914.
Till höger, uppe på berget, syns Skansen: On your right, up on the hill, is Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, built in the 17th century.
Till höger, vid kanalen, ligger Feskekôr: On your right, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church – which is why Gothenburgers call it 'the fish church'.
Till orgeln som invigdes 1885 hade kunge: The King donated 4,000 kronor towards the organ consecrated in 1885, and came to the ceremony himself with Princes Karl and Eugen. Inside the church are also some thirty gravestones, most of them for people who worked at Drottningholm Palace.
Till palatset hörde en stor trädgård. På: The palace had a large garden. In the 18th century it held 81 fruit trees, 18 clipped spruces and masses of berry bushes, and an orangery followed in 1770. A small remnant survives as today's Jakob Mommas park.
Till råoljehamnen på Hjärtholmen har äve: Even ULCC-class vessels – the world's largest tankers, 333 metres long and 60 metres wide – have called at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen. The oil is then stored in huge rock caverns next to the harbour.
Till vänster ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges: On your left is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your left is the Royal Palace.
Till vänster ligger Skansen Lejonet, en: On your left is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century fortress with a gilded lion on top.
Till vänster ligger nöjesparken Liseberg: On your left is Liseberg amusement park.
Till vänster på berget ser du Masthuggsk: On the hill to your left is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church. To your right you can catch a glimpse of the harbour and the Göta älv river.

Till vänster ser du den röd-vita skyskra: On your left is the red-and-white skyscraper that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet – 'the Lipstick'.
Till vänster syns Kaknästornet, ett av S: On your left is Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of the tallest towers in Stockholm.
Till vänster syns Riddarholmskyrkan med: On the left is Riddarholmskyrkan, the Riddarholmen Church, with its slender cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till vänster syns Stadshuset med sitt to: On your left is Stockholm City Hall, its tower topped by three golden crowns.

Till vänster, uppe på berget, syns Skans: Up on the hill to your left you can see Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, a 17th-century stronghold.
Till vänster, vid kanalen, ligger Feskek: On your left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church, and Gothenburgers have called it 'the fish church' ever since.
On the left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall, built in 1874. It looks just like a church, which is why Gothenburgers call it the “fish church”.
Tillbaka in mot centrum, förbi Ullevi No: Back towards the centre, past Ullevi Norra and Drottningtorget, named after one of the old city gates.
Tillbaka in mot centrum. Rundan slutar v: Back towards the centre. The tour ends at Kopparmärra, the bronze equestrian statue on Kungsportsplatsen.
Tillbaka in mot stan. Lyssna efter Kungs: Back towards the city. Listen out for Kungssten, where Älvsborgsbron was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966.
Tillbaka mot centrum. Rundan slutar i Br: Back towards the city centre. The route ends at Brunnsparken.
Tillbaka ner till Järntorget för att byt: Back down to Järntorget to change trams.
Tillbaka till Brunnsparken, stadens hjär: Back to Brunnsparken, the hub of the city's public transport.
Tillbaka till Liljeholmen för vidare res: Back to Liljeholmen to continue towards the city centre.
Tillbaka till Ropsten. Gå ner till båtbr: Back to Ropsten. Walk down to the boat jetty.
Tillbaka uppströms ett stopp, med Lindho: Head back upstream one stop, with the old shipyard surroundings of Lindholmen in front of you.
Tillbaka via Haga södra och Odenplan til: Back via Haga södra and Odenplan to the Central Station.
Tillbaka via Haga, Odenplan och S:t Erik: Back via Haga, Odenplan and S:t Eriksplan to the Central Station.
Tillbaka via Rinkeby centrum, vars tunne: Back via Rinkeby centrum, whose metro station is decorated with Viking art, and Sundbybergs torg.
Back across the water to Hornstull.
Tillbaka över älven. Kliv av vid Lilla B: Back across the river. Hop off at Lilla Bommen for the Lipstick tower, the Gothenburg Opera House and the sailing ship Barken Viking from 1906.
Tillhåll för tjuvar och banditer: A haunt of thieves and bandits
Timmerhus med fem kakelugnar: A timber house with five tiled stoves
Ting eller kult på berget: Court or cult on the hill
Tingen stannade inte kvar på ängen. Från: The assemblies didn't stay on the meadow. From 1667 right up until 1916, the Svartlösa district court sat at Fittja farm instead.
Tingsbyn har fått namn efter Sollentuna: Tingsbyn takes its name from the old assembly and court site of Sollentuna hundred at Barkarby torg. It was here, in the early 1800s, that Lars Molin – better known as Lasse-Maja – was convicted of stealing the church silver from Järfälla church. The coaching inn next door is now called Lasse-Maja Wärdshus.

Tingsbyn is named after the old district court site of Sollentuna hundred at Barkarby torg. It was here, in the early 19th century, that Lars Molin – better known as Lasse-Maja – was convicted of stealing the church silver from Järfälla Church.
Tingshuset hade en tingssal, en bostad f: The courthouse had a courtroom, a home for the caretaker and holding cells in the basement. It stopped being a courthouse after 1982, and the Swedish Radiation Protection Institute later moved in. Since 2010 it has housed the Hagströmer Library, a research library for the history of medicine.
Tingshuset invigdes 1907 och kostade 135: The courthouse opened in 1907 and cost 135,000 kronor. It's an imposing villa in Art Nouveau Baroque style with a black metal roof, originally rendered in white. In the 1940s it was criticised as a jarring interruption in the continuous parkland.
Tingsplatsen nedanför berget: The assembly site below the hill
Tingstadsvassen bär ett riktigt gammalt: Tingstadsvassen has a truly ancient name. Tingstad is recorded as early as 1388 and comes from a village where the ting, the local assembly, used to meet. The city was tight-fisted at first: in 1874 it turned down the chance to buy the reed beds for ten öre a square foot. Two years later it changed its mind – and paid 300,000 kronor. Today most of the district is taken up by the island of Ringön.
Titta in i Childhoodhallen, känd från HC: Peek into Childhoodhallen, known from HCZ
Titta på Gröna Lund (2 min), Sveriges äl: Take a look at Gröna Lund (2 min), Sweden's oldest amusement park, dating from 1883. Then walk to the ferry pier at Allmänna gränd (2 min).
Titta på Sköndalsskolans fasad mot Perst: Take a look at Sköndal School's facade facing Perstorpsvägen. It's decorated with playful brick figures – a sailing boat, a witch, a julbock (Christmas goat) and a girl skipping – plus the short poem 'a b c - 1953'. On the main building is the relief Noah's Ark by the artist Allan Wallberg.
Titta på Trisshusen, tidiga radhus från: Look out for the Trisshusen, early terraced houses from 1909
Titta på bergväggarna vid perrongerna nä: Look at the rock walls by the platforms when it's dark. That's where the light sculpture "En hyllning till rörelse" (A Tribute to Movement) by the artist Raha Rastifard is projected. It was unveiled in 2017 and covers a full 60 by 12 metres.
Titta på gamla Lundbybadet på Herkulesga: See the old Lundbybadet baths on Herkulesgatan
Titta på perrongen. Där sitter en kvinna: Take a look at the platform. A bronze woman in a pointed hat is sitting there waiting – and she has been since 2001. The sculpture is called Väntan, 'Waiting', and it's by Britt Ignell. Perhaps she's waiting for someone to step off the tram. In the meantime, she's watched the multi-storey car park opposite get a new top floor of homes.
Titta på taket: alla små ventilskorstena: Look at the roof: all those little vent chimneys come from the chamber-pot cupboards in the cells. Each cupboard had its own vent running up through the roof. Although the prison got flushing toilets in 1927, the cupboards stayed in use right up until it closed.
Titta upp mot en fyra meter hög granitpe: Look up at the four-metre granite column outside Karolinska Institutet. Up on top, running, is a bronze sculpture by Eric Grate called The Entomological Abduction – a woman and a man carrying off a third figure who has no arms or legs. The woman being carried wears a hat or perhaps a crown, and the man carrying her has insect-like antennae sprouting from his jaw.
