Titta upp på ÅF-huset, 65 meter högt: Look up at ÅF-huset, 65 metres tall
Titteridamm, en bit härifrån, har fått s: Titteridamm, just up the road, owes its name to a legend. On Saturday evenings, so the story goes, the girls would go down to the pond to check their reflections in the shiny water and make themselves pretty for the dance. They 'tittade' – peeked – into the pond, and that's where the name comes from! Close by is Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka, the Church of St Paul of the Cross, a Catholic parish church.
Tjugo år till första graven: Twenty years to the first burial
Tofslärkan 6 såldes färdigbyggd till Hen: Tofslärkan 6 was sold, newly completed, to Henric Tamm, a bank director and Sweden's finance minister in 1920–1921. By 1926 two of his sons, both lieutenants, were living in the house too. The attic was originally a billiard room.
Tolered hette ursprungligen Toleröd och: Tolered was originally called Toleröd, and it's mostly detached and terraced houses. Not far from here is Torpet Klara, a day labourer's croft with five buildings. It was so well hidden at the end of a road through a modern villa area that for many years the post office had no address for it. It has been a listed building since 2006.
Tompa Eken, som startade konserterna på: Tompa Eken, who started the concerts at Kafé 44, baked buns for every single gig until he retired in 2018. The café is run by volunteers and even has its own bookshop.
Tomten sluttar ner mot Magelungen, med d: The garden slopes down towards Lake Magelungen, with a pond, a pergola and cast steps leading down to the water. On the street side are wrought-iron gates decorated with oak leaves. Today the villa is a private home.
Tomter för tio öre kvadratmetern: Plots at ten öre a square metre
Torben Grut ritade Piplärkan 8 samtidigt: Torben Grut designed Piplärkan 8 while he was also working on Stockholm Olympic Stadium. The villa was built of hand-moulded Helsingborg brick, the same kind used for the stadium.
Torg efter amerikansk förebild: A square on the American model
Torget Hagaplan ligger delvis ovanpå mot: Hagaplan, a square that opened in 2023, sits partly on top of the motorway tunnels of Norra länken, the Northern Link. In the middle of its southern part stands the round office building Forskaren, 'the Researcher', and some sixty trees are planned here, among them giant sequoias and tulip trees. Since September 2023 the square has also been home to Inflyttarna, 'The Newcomers', an artwork by Johanna Karlin.
Torget anlades efter Mariabranden 1759,: The square was laid out after the Maria fire of 1759, which destroyed more than 300 properties, and was sometimes used for executions. When it was named after King Adolf Fredrik in 1768, it was on condition that no more executions would take place here. Gustav III later held one of his tournaments on the square.
Torget byggdes 1953 och ritades av arkit: The square was built in 1953 to designs by the architects Sven Brolid and Jan Wallinder. When it was refurbished in 2019–2020, three new buildings went up: two taller blocks of flats and a lower two-storey building with shops on the ground floor.
Torget byggdes 1953–1955 som ett så kall: The square was built in 1953–1955 as a "C-square" – a social, cultural and commercial centre for around 9,000 residents. It takes its name from Axel Dahlström, who sat on Gothenburg's city council from 1915.
Torget byggdes 1971 och är uppkallat eft: The square was built in 1971 and named after the author and Nobel laureate Selma Lagerlöf. It's about four kilometres north of central Gothenburg and serves as the local centre for northern Backa. It's home to two schools, Svenska Balettskolan – the Swedish Ballet School – and Skälltorpsskolan, and the square also once had Bäckebol's church hall, part of Backa parish.
Torget en kort promenad härifrån hette t: The square a short walk from here used to be called Dragonplan, and its octagonal building has become Rissne's landmark. Beneath the square, in a rock cavern 25 to 40 metres down, is the metro station. Along its walls runs a lettered timeline of historical events from 3000 BC up to 1985, an artwork by Madeleine Dranger and Rolf H Reimers.
Torget fick namnet Mariaplan 1918, efter: The square was named Mariaplan in 1918 because it sits where Mariagatan ends. The first suggestion was Ladugårdstorg, after the Älvsborg royal farm. Why Mariagatan is called what it is, nobody knows.
Torget fick ny färg och form: A square with a new look
Torget fick sitt namn 1886 efter Landala: The square was named in 1886 after Landala chapel, and fish was being sold here as early as the 1880s. Landala was one of Gothenburg's first three working-class suburbs outside the Vallgraven moat. On Landala torg it's honoured by the sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife, inscribed: ‘With a firm hand, strong from work, soft with love, you held the home together.’ The school next door opened in 1892 as Landalaskolan.
Torget fick sitt namn 1924 efter den hög: The square was named in 1924 after the high ground it sits on, and the name then spread to the whole district, Höglandet – “the Highlands”. From 1926 to 1929, Höglandstorget was the end of the line for tram route 12. On the square is the Höglandsbiografen cinema, opened in 1936, and a small park a little way off is named after the artist Einar Forseth, who lived in a villa nearby from 1925 to 1981.
Torget fick sitt namn 1939, efter den le: The square was named in 1939 after the legendary sea captain Charles – or Carl – Chapman, who was active in Majorna in the 18th century.
Torget fick sitt namn 1946, troligen eft: The square was named in 1946, probably after the governor Nils Kagg. Here stands Våren, 'Spring', a bronze statue by Eric Grate of a naked woman on a granite plinth, put up in 1950 – there's an identical one in Alingsås. The old Torpavallen ground, where Qviding FIF used to play on gravel, is now a retail park.
Torget fick sitt namn i mitten av 1920-t: The square was named in the mid-1920s after the high ground it sits on, and it was the square that later gave the whole district of Höglandet its name. From 1926 to 1929 Höglandstorget was the terminus of tram line 12. On the square is the Höglandsbiografen cinema, opened in 1936, and a little way off is a small park named after the artist Einar Forseth, who lived in a villa nearby from 1925 to 1981.
Torget formgavs av arkitekterna Backströ: The square was designed by the architects Backström & Reinius. In the middle stands Per-Erik Willö's Farsta Fountain from 1960, the year the square opened. In the north-east corner there used to be a paddling pool, now covered over.
Torget har fått namn efter Drottningport: The square takes its name from Drottningporten, the Queen's Gate – one of the three gates into the fortified city. It was first built of wood in the 1640s and then in stone in 1669, with a sandstone portal from the old Älvsborg fortress. The gate was finally demolished in 1821.
Torget har fått namn efter en by i Ostpr: This square is named after a village in East Prussia, famous for a battle in the Seven Years' War. Down at Klippan you'll find old inns linked to the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg and his book Min son på galejan, 'My Son on the Galley'. And in Kustens hus next door, emigrants liked to have one last beer before the boat left for America.
Torget har haft flera biografer. Fyren l: The square has had several cinemas. Fyren occupied the building at Stigbergstorget 1 from 1943 to 1985, and since 1986 the same premises have housed Bengans record shop. The Kaparen cinema on the west side of the square is now a pizzeria.
Torget hette Torsnästorget fram till sep: Until September 2010 the square was called Torsnästorget. It was then renamed after Jan Stenbeck, in recognition of his importance to Sweden's telecoms industry. Next door is Kista Science Tower, at 123.9 metres the second-tallest office building in the Nordic countries. And the Filmstaden Kista cinema was opened on 27 November 2002 by the actors Josephine Bornebusch and Fares Fares.
Torget hette först Kortedalstorget. Göte: The square was first called Kortedalstorget. The Gothenburg tramways company pointed out that people actually said Kortedalatorget, and that the official name was a mouthful. In 1959 the city council voted 24 to 17 for the new name, Kortedala Torg.
Torget hette länge Trätorget. Här hölls: For a long time the square was called Trätorget, the Timber Square. It hosted the Larsmässa fair, two weeks of trading in timber, hay and textiles starting on 10 August. The market got in the way of traffic and came to an end around 1900.
Torget här fick sitt namn 1944. Redan fr: This square got its name in 1944. From 1915 there was already another Wieselgrensplatsen, between Härlandavägen and what was then Wieselgrensgatan in Bagaregården, but that name disappeared when the town plan was changed.
Torget i Angereds Centrum invigdes den 2: The square at Angereds Centrum was opened on 26 October 1978 by King Carl XVI Gustaf, who had first ridden the tram all the way out from central Gothenburg. Back then it had around 40 shops; today there are about 60.
Torget med den bevingade kuben: The square with the winged cube
Torget och bostadsområdet Adventsparken: The square and the neighbouring Adventsparken housing estate were built for the municipal landlord Göteborgsbostäder and designed by G Andreasson at the architects' office of HSB, the housing cooperative. A four-storey tower block, a three-storey building and low rows of shops frame the square.
Torget ritades av Helge Zimdal och stod: Designed by Helge Zimdal and completed in 1958, the square was built in an Italian style with terraces and arches. Biskopsgården Church beside it, designed by Johannes Olivegren, was finished in 1961.
Torget ritades av Johan E. Tuvert på Rag: The square was designed by Johan E. Tuvert of Ragndal and Tuvert Architects. Under its roof you’ll find a supermarket, a library, a greengrocer, bingo, restaurants, a health centre, a dentist and a hairdresser.
Torget sticker ut med ett 16 våningar hö: The square is dominated by a 16-storey tower block completed in 1956, and the community centre is decorated with a marble-inlay mural by the artist Endre Nemes. That same year, Högsboskolan opened right next door, built for about 1,000 pupils. The school is gone now, though – it was demolished in 2013.
Torget står på Ekebäcks bys gamla marker: The square stands on the old land of Ekebäck village, whose farms went by names like "Nilses", "Sme'ns" and "Kalles" – there was even a fox farm. Of fifteen houses and farms, all but one were demolished around 1970. The survivor stands just east of Frölunda Kulturhus.
Torget vid stationen är uppkallat efter: The square by the station is named after the crime writer Stieg Trenter, who was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery by the railway station, then called Södertörns villastad, and young Stieg sometimes lent a hand – his crime novel Träff i helfigur is set in these very surroundings. The planned villa town itself never took off: the plots were slow to sell, mostly because transport links were so poor.
Torget är fortfarande under uppbyggnad o: The square is still being built, and once finished it will have homes, shops and a hotel. The library replaced Gamlestaden's library in the civic centre, which closed on 28 September 2018.
Torget är uppkallat efter polarforskaren: The square is named after the polar explorer and meteorologist Finn Malmgren, and the statue here, Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice, is dedicated to him. The oaks and pines around the square were left standing when it was built in the 1930s. And here's an unexpected former neighbour: Willy Brandt, later Chancellor of West Germany, lived at Finn Malmgrens väg 23 while in exile from Nazi Germany in the 1940s. A park nearby is named after him today.
Torn, tureller och riddarsal: Towers, turrets and a knights' hall
Tornet Nya Chartago revs 1932 för en nyb: The Nya Chartago tower was demolished in 1932 to make way for a new building that never materialised. Luxparken was laid out instead. On a rocky knoll at the end of Montebellogatan now stands the green and white iron cross of the Coldinu Order.
Tornet ritades 1943 av Ivar Callmander i: The tower was designed in 1943 by Ivar Callmander in the functionalist style, with five storeys and several balconies. From the balconies, visibility was tested against measuring points around the area, including a sighting board at Ekbacken in Larsberg, about 400 metres away.
Tornet ritades av Nils Einar Eriksson. I: The tower was designed by Nils Einar Eriksson. Up at the top, the artist Tore Ahnoff's 32-metre-long mural runs around the ceiling. It shows sights from the city, each placed in the direction where you'll actually find it.
Tornet ritades av Ragnar Ossian Swensson: The tower was designed by Ragnar Ossian Swensson. It had smooth rendered walls and a copper roof, and stood on a plinth storey with a round granite terrace. Its most striking feature was the ring of 24 windows at the very top.
Tornet ritades av White arkitekter, som: The tower was designed by White arkitekter, who won a competition in 1998. The complex consists of six buildings of different heights, all triangular in plan with transparent, double-glazed façades.
Tornet som fick spetsig hatt: The tower that got a pointed hat
Tornet som tystnade 1926: The tower that fell silent in 1926
Tornet togs ur bruk i slutet av 1960-tal: The tower was taken out of use in the late 1960s and then served as a radio mast for the city's communications radio and the National Police Board. Plans to turn it into student housing date back to the late 1980s.
Tornet är 20 meter brett och har två bas: The tower is 20 metres wide and has two tanks. The lower one, holding 2,000 cubic metres, supplies Sicklaön, while the upper one, holding 1,500 cubic metres, supplies Jarlaberg. The water level in the upper tank is 103 metres above sea level.
Tornet är en blandning av klassicistisk: The tower mixes classical and Romanesque styles and is meant to make you think of the ancient Goths, not Gothic architecture. It's octagonal, with three floors and 124 steps, and at the top is a battlement partly hidden by a roof added in the late 1800s.
Tornet är en tidig betongkonstruktion, h: The tower is an early concrete structure, entirely clad in brick from Helsingborg's steam brickworks with bold patterning in the National Romantic spirit of the 1910s. It's 27 metres high with five floors, and the tank at the top held 400 cubic metres of water.
Tornets två reservoarer rymmer tillsamma: The tower's two reservoirs hold 4 million litres of water between them. To keep insects out, the tower has 20 windows of blue glass, which refracts the light in a way insects dislike.
Tornklockorna göts 1881 och storklockan: The tower bells were cast in 1881, and the great bell weighs 925 kilos. The church has had several organs; today's 40-stop instrument from 1969–1970 was rebuilt in 2008 to suit choir and hymn singing better.
Tornvillan, egentligen Sofielund efter b: Tornvillan, the Tower Villa – properly called Sofielund after the builder's wife – was designed in Art Nouveau baroque. It was the first house in the Stockholm area to stand on poured concrete foundations, and even the balusters on the tower and veranda are concrete. The builder ran a plaster and concrete casting business.
Torp där torget ligger: Crofts where the square now is
Torparen Carl Öman, född 1767, ”avsäger: According to the tax register, the crofter Carl Öman, born in 1767, 'renounces the use of tobacco' – a way of getting his tax reduced.
Torpet Bussenhus intill Spånga kyrka var: Bussenhus, the croft next to Spånga Church, was a soldier's croft with an unusual sideline: in the 1740s the cavalryman who lived here was allowed to run a tavern. It crops up now and then in the records of the Sollentuna district court, after assorted brawls. Inside the church are fragments of Viking Age runestones, and one of them is built into the church's outer wall.
Torpet Fredriksdal vid Gamla Stockholmsv: In 1801 the Fredriksdal croft on Gamla Stockholmsvägen was home to the cobbler Erik Färnström and his family. Today it's the "crown jewel" of the Gretas backe housing area, which won Huddinge's architecture prize in 2017.
Torpet Istorp har troligen fått sitt nam: The croft of Istorp probably got its name from a hill where ice tended to form, and was likely called Isbergstorp at first. Isbergavägen in Herrängen recalls the hill. The croft stood where Hasselstigen 14 is today.
Torpet Istorp hette troligen från början: The croft of Istorp was probably first called Isbergstorp, after a hill where ice readily formed. Isbergavägen in Herrängen keeps the memory of the hill alive. The last crofter left in 1781.
Torpet Masmo under Glömsta finns med red: The croft of Masmo, belonging to Glömsta, is recorded as early as 1689. The first part, ‘mas’, is thought to be a taboo word for wolf, and ‘moa’ means dense forest – so ‘the forest where the wolf was seen’. The croft has given its name to Masmoberget hill and Masmobäcken stream.
Torpet Månskär hade ett egendomligt namn: The croft of Månskär had an odd name, and despite appearances it has nothing to do with ‘månskära’, the crescent moon. The first part comes from Måns, one of its first tenants, and the second from ‘kärr’, meaning marsh. The croft grew up along the new route of Södertäljevägen road, finished in 1673. Right next door is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's largest cinema, with eighteen screens and more than four thousand seats.
Torpet Rådan nämns första gången 1599. S: The croft of Rådan is first mentioned in 1599. Since then it has been a farm steward's residence, a manor, a boarding school from 1890, military quarters in the 1940s and a police academy from 1970.
Torpet Spikborn hade ett märkligt namn,: The croft of Spikborn had an odd name, probably from spikborr, a gimlet. It was most likely built in the 1650s as part of the Vårby estate, and the last of it was demolished in February 1977. Segeltorpsskolan, the Segeltorp school, has a dramatic past too: its first building from 1917 burned down in 1971, and a brand-new main building opened in 2010.
Torpet där vägen vände: The croft where the road turned
Torpet och nykterhetsristningen: The croft and the temperance carving
Torpet som blev Röda caféet: The croft that became the Red Café
Torpet som blev Vårbys skola: The croft that became Vårby’s school
Torpet som blev egen gård: A croft that became a farm
Torpet som blev herrgård: The croft that became a manor
Torpet som blev krog: The croft that became an inn
Torpet som blev villastad: A croft that became a garden suburb
Torrekullagården, en kort promenad bort,: Torrekullagården, a short walk away, has worn many hats. The City of Mölndal has owned the farm since 1973 and has used it for a job-training scheme and as a camp centre. There have been plans for a hotel, the adult education association Studiefrämjandet wanted to take it over, and from 2015 to 2019 it was home to young refugees who had arrived without their families.
Torrläggningen från 1872 lyckades inte h: The draining of 1872 was never quite successful, and almost every spring and autumn parts of the former lake flooded again, right up to the 1950s. Between 1915 and 1920 ice-yachting races were even held here in winter.
Torrskodd tack vare jaktstövlarna: Dry feet thanks to his hunting boots
Torsby finns inte bara i Värmland. Det h: Värmland isn't the only place with a Torsby. This is Torsby parish in Bohuslän, which has been part of Kungälv municipality since 1971, and its parish church, Torsby Church, is a short walk from here. The parish reaches out to the North Sea coast just north of the mouth of the Nordre älv river, and takes in the small town of Kärna and several villages, such as Kovikshamn and Brunnefjäll.
Torslanda hörde länge till Bohuslän och: For a long time Torslanda was part of the province of Bohuslän and the Västra Hising district; it wasn't until 1967 that the parish became part of the City of Gothenburg. Today Torslanda is a large district on western Hisingen, made up of a string of smaller villages such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Lilleby, Nolered and Tumlehed. Not far from here is Torslanda Church, one of the most popular wedding churches in the diocese.

For a long time Torslanda belonged to Bohuslän and the hundred of Västra Hising. It only became part of the City of Gothenburg in the late 1960s. Today it's a large district on western Hisingen, taking in a string of smaller places such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Lilleby, Nolered and Tumlehed. A short way from here stands Torslanda Church, one of the diocese's most popular churches for weddings.
Torslanda på västra Hisingen är känt för: Torslanda, on western Hisingen, is known for its beaches and countryside – but above all for Volvo Cars' Torslanda Works. Before Landvetter Airport opened in 1977, Gothenburg's main airport was here in Torslanda too. Homes are mostly detached and terraced houses, and the shopping areas are called Torslanda Torg and Amhult.
Torslanda är en stor stadsdel på västra: Torslanda is a large district on western Hisingen, covering 4,425 hectares and taking in smaller places such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Hällsvik and Tumlehed. A short walk away is Torslanda church, one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. And before Landvetter was built in 1977, Gothenburg's main airport was right here in Torslanda.
Torslanda är kyrkbyn i den gamla Torslan: Torslanda is the church village of the old Torslanda parish, which became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. It's known for its many beaches and its countryside, but above all for Volvo's car plant, Torslandaverken. Sport runs deep here, too: Torslanda IK was founded on 18 January 1944, and it's one of the local clubs along with Torslanda HK.
Torslandaverken började byggas i Sörred: Construction of the Torslanda plant at Sörred began in 1960–1961. The district is a big one, covering a full 886 hectares.
Torslandaverken, ursprungligen Volvo Tor: Torslandaverken, originally Volvo's Torslanda plant, was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic countries when it opened. Building began in 1960–61 in the district of Sörred, whose name has an amusing origin. The first part, Sör-, is thought to come from the nickname Surv – a careless fellow, a slacker, a good-for-nothing – while the ending -red comes from the Old Swedish 'ryd', meaning cleared land.
Torsviks skola har vuxit fram i etapper,: Torsviks skola has grown bit by bit, with buildings dating from 1906 all the way to 2021, and today it has around 850 pupils from preschool to year 9. On Stockholmsvägen, look out for Lidingö Arena, an office and shopping block from 1974–1978 designed by Bo Möller, which has become a local landmark. Just west of Lidingö centrum is Ansgarskyrkan, the Ansgar Church, built in 1996 by Lidingö Missionsförsamling, a free church congregation.
Torsviks skolas äldsta hus från 1906 var: Torsvik School's oldest building, from 1906, was Lidingö's first purpose-built folkskola, or primary school, and children came here from the garden suburbs round about. It's classical in style with National Romantic details, but the architect is unknown.
Trafikapparaten från 1935 var modern när: The 1935 traffic interchange was modern in its day, but by the mid-1940s its concrete decks were already suffering from salt damage and leaks. The new Slussen is being designed by Foster+Partners together with Berg Arkitektkontor.
Trafikljus mellan kvarn och stuga: Traffic lights between mill and cottage
Trakten här var kanske Stockholms mest k: This may well have been the most windmill-packed corner of Stockholm. Two of the mills were called Lilla and Stora Tissan, and nearby were others with names like Stora Adam and Lilla Eva. One of the Tissans was moved to Rolsta gård in Märsta in 1887. Next door was the Åhlinska school, a girls' school that Karin Åhlin founded in 1847 when she was just 17 – she started with 14 pupils and her sisters as teachers.
Trakten var bebodd redan under forntiden: People lived around here as far back as prehistoric times. Sjöberg's hillfort stands on a high plateau and measures about 210 by 100 metres. The fort wall has been dated to AD 400–550, but archaeologists also found traces of even older settlements. The fort gave its name to Borgvägen.
People lived here back in prehistoric times. Sjöberg's hillfort sits on a high plateau, about 210 by 100 metres. Archaeologists dated the wall to AD 400–550 and found even older traces of settlement.
Trakten var bebodd redan under förhistor: People lived in this area as far back as prehistoric times. On Nytorpsberget, a small hill east of the old croft site, there's an Iron Age burial ground.
Tranebergs gård: Tranebergs gård, the old Traneberg farm
Tre broar passerar här: Skansbron, Johan: Three bridges pass by here: Skansbron, Johanneshovsbron and Skanstullsbron. Right next to the metro is the Ringens centrum shopping centre – and that's what most Stockholmers have in mind when they say Skanstull.
Tre broar på samma plats: Three bridges on the same spot
Tre syskon med jätteklocka: Three siblings with a giant clock
Tre villor vid Gasverksvägen, Ingenjörsv: The three villas on Gasverksvägen, known as Ingenjörsvillorna, were built as homes for the engineers at the Värtagasverket gasworks. The gasworks buildings were designed by Ferdinand Boberg, and the plant supplied Stockholm with town gas right up until January 2011. This was also meant to be the site of Gasklockan, a residential tower of around 170 metres and some 50 floors, designed by Herzog & de Meuron. In the end, though, it was never built.
Triangelhuset är en liksidig triangel me: Triangelhuset, the Triangle House, is an equilateral triangle with sides 27.5 metres long. Each floor has three flats with three rooms and a kitchen, with the living room or a bedroom at the outer end and a balcony at the point. All 26 flats are the same size.
Trisshusen består av tre sammanbyggda en: Trisshusen is made up of three linked single-family homes. Unlike the nearby Canada houses, which were built for workers, these were designed for the well-off middle class. The facade is in National Romantic style with Old Norse details.
Trisshusen heter så för att de består av: The Trisshusen get their name from being made up of three joined single-family houses. Unlike their neighbours, the Canadahusen, which were intended for workers, they were designed from the start for the well-off middle class.
Trollbäcken är ett lånat namn. Trakten h: Trollbäcken is a borrowed name. The area used to be called Kumla, after the manor on Lake Drevviken that goes back to the Middle Ages, but in 1947 the residential areas were renamed Trollbäcken to avoid confusion with Kumla in the province of Närke. A couple of hundred metres away is Trollbäcken Church, beside county road 260. The manor itself is still called Kumla herrgård, and since 2013 it has been a restaurant and conference centre.
Trollbäckens kyrka byggdes 1992 efter ri: Trollbäcken church was built in 1992 to designs by Janne Feldt, with walls of warm red brick and an octagonal worship space. The chancel wall is decorated with thick cast blue glass by Jonas Torstensson, with a golden cross at its centre.
Trolldalen dyker upp i fem av Per Anders: Trolldalen appears in five of Per Anders Fogelström’s books. In ‘Mina drömmars stad’ (‘City of My Dreams’), Emelie and some friends go on an outing here. Around the turn of the 20th century, Methodists and Good Templars also gathered here for sermons, marches and gökotta – the Swedish tradition of rising at dawn to hear the first birdsong.
Trots att Göteborg känns nära är marken: Gothenburg may feel close, but this land is actually part of Halland. Lindome parish belonged to Fjäre hundred, an old district of Halland, and only became part of Mölndal municipality in 1971. Lindome church, the parish's old church, is a short walk away, and the church village of Lindome has now merged with the Gothenburg urban area.
Trots att Rya skog omringas av avloppsve: Even though Rya skog is hemmed in by a sewage works, refineries and a combined heat and power plant, the woodland is a favourite with botanists and birdwatchers, especially in spring. A survey in 2007 found 22 threatened and rare species here.
Trots att villan byggdes för året runt b: Although the villa was built for year-round living, the Setterwall family only stayed here in summer. Nacka municipality bought it in 1950 and used it as a health insurance office, a junior school and a hostel, among other things. Today it's a listed building.
Trots det nya namnet kallades torget län: Despite its new name, the square was long known as Möbeltorget and Trätorget – the furniture and timber market. Especially between 1876 and 1902, furniture and woodwork were sold here, much of it by the famous joiners of Lindome.
Trots namnet ligger Älvsjöbadet inte all: Despite its name, Älvsjöbadet isn't in Älvsjö at all, but in Hagsätra. The outdoor pool was built in 1937–1938 to designs by the architects Helge Zimdal and Nils Ahrbom. A short way off is Teknik och Servicegymnasiet, founded in 1963 as a workshop school to train staff for Stockholm's tramway workshops.
Trots namnet är sjön snarare långsträckt: Despite its name – ‘the Triangle’ – the lake is long and narrow rather than three-sided. It’s 6.6 metres deep and drains into Liljeholmsviken bay through a culvert under Trekantsvägen.
Trots torvbrytningen växer typiska mossv: Despite the peat-cutting, typical bog plants still grow on Älta mosse – cranberry, bog myrtle, marsh Labrador tea and cloudberry. The reserve exists to protect a less common type of habitat.
Trädgården anlades under ledning av Carl: The garden was created under Carl Skottsberg, its director from 1919 to 1948. It was funded mainly by Charles Felix Lindberg's donation fund, as a memorial to the donor.
Trädgårdsarkitekterna Sven Hermelin och: The landscape architects Sven Hermelin and Inger Wedborn kept the area's archipelago character. Hundred-year-old pines and oaks were protected during construction, and a row of garages by the entrance kept cars out.
Trädgårdsstaden har 264 bostäder fördela: The garden city has 264 homes split between seven housing cooperatives, whose names echo its gardening heritage: Botanikern (the Botanist), Floristen (the Florist), Kamomillen (Chamomile), Rödlöken (Red Onion) and Taklöken (Houseleek).
Trädgårn brann ned den 11 november 1965: Trädgår'n burned down on 11 November 1965, and again on the night before 8 July 1994. The new building, designed by Studio Grön, opened on 23 May 1998 and was nominated for awards including the Mies van der Rohe Prize.
Trähuset som fick 30 rum: The wooden house that gained 30 rooms
Trähästen Havre och betong: Havre the wooden horse, and concrete
Träkvista är en idrottsglad del av Ekerö: Träkvista is the sporty corner of Ekerö, with Ekerövallen, Träkvistavallen and Vikingahallen. It's mostly villas, linked houses and terraced houses, and there are several schools. Until 1990 Träkvista was the heart of the town, but then the centre moved when Ekerö centrum, designed by Ralph Erskine, opened.
Trävillor nära gatan: Wooden villas close to the street
Tulegatan har fått sitt namn efter det m: Tulegatan is named after the mythical land of Thule, because the street once marked the northern edge of built-up Sundbyberg. Tram line 15 ran along here from 1928 to 1959, and north of the street lies Tulemarken, with its functionalist villas from the 1930s. A short way off rises the town's best-known landmark, the water tower designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912.
Tulegatan är bred och rak och leder från: Tulegatan is broad and straight, running from Råsundavägen in Solna towards Duvbo. Along it you'll find Sundbyberg church, the swimming baths and Duvbo metro station. The Tule towers are 16 storeys high, and the area north of the street is called Tulemarken.
Tullare med vita mösskapell: Customs officers in white cap covers
Tullen som flyttade söderut: The toll gate that moved south
Tullhuset byggdes 1770 vid flottbrons fä: The toll house was built in 1770 at the end of the pontoon bridge: two angled buildings joined by a city gate. This was where you paid a toll to enter the city. It was demolished in 1933, but granite walls at Bergsunds strand partly mark where it stood.
Tullhuset med egen stadsport: A toll house with its own city gate
Tullinge gymnasium startade i oktober år: Tullinge upper secondary school opened in October 2000. It's laid out like a small campus, with six buildings side by side and about 730 students. Former pupils include the athlete Michel Tornéus. And the school has an unusual tradition: every year it gets a visit from a Nobel laureate.
Tumba bruksmuseums huvudbyggnad Oxhuset: Oxhuset, the Ox House from 1825 and main building of Tumba Bruksmuseum, has an exhibition on the history of banknotes and the Riksbank, Sweden's central bank, plus a café. In Röda magasinet, the Red Storehouse, you can see how handmade paper is produced.
Tumba gymnasium: Tumba gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Tumba gymnasium ligger precis norr om Tu: Tumba gymnasium, the upper secondary school, sits just north of Tumba station. It now shares the building with Botkyrka's arts school and Xenter, which offers vocational college courses in media among other things.
Tumba gymnasium öppnade 1974, och de röd: Tumba gymnasium opened in 1974, and at the time its red sheet-metal facades were seen as daring and modern. It was Botkyrka's first upper secondary school, and one of the first in the country built for both academic and vocational courses under one roof. In 1978 it became one of the first schools in Sweden to get its own computer – with no fewer than 16 users hooked up to it.
Tumba kyrka ligger alldeles intill. Den: Tumba Church is right beside us. It was consecrated in 1973 and, after a renovation, reconsecrated on Palm Sunday 2023. A little further away is the Lill-Tumba farm, which the paper mill bought in 1900 purely to stop anyone else using the land. And the mill has a history that's rolling in money, quite literally: Tumba bruksmuseum, the mill museum, tells the story of papermaking and banknote printing, and in 2008 it was nominated for the European Museum of the Year Award.
Tumba kyrka ritades av Börje Wehlin och: Tumba Church was designed by Börje Wehlin and has no tower – just a bell frame with two bells from Sigtuna. Below the gilded cross on the chancel wall are twelve simple wooden sculptures of the apostles, and the church windows by Ingun Wistedt depict the Creation.
Tuna gård nämns 1413, då Mathias Laurens: Tuna farm is mentioned in 1413, when Mathias Laurensson and his wife pledged land "i Tunom i Bothakirkio sokn" – at Tuna in Botkyrka parish. In the 1500s it was owned by Gabriel Kristiernsson Oxenstierna and then passed down through noble families for more than a century.
Tunnelbanan hit invigdes den 18 november: The metro line out here opened on 18 November 1958. The 320 invited guests were served coffee on the way, and the train was driven by Karl Johan Gustavsson, the tramway's longest-serving driver. The guests got to ride through practically the entire metro network of the day.
Tunnelbanan som skulle till Täby: The metro that was meant to reach Täby
Tunnelbanan svävar fram här: Bredängs st: The metro takes to the air here: Bredäng station, opened in 1965, sits on a 180-metre viaduct over Bredängs allé. In the ticket hall you'll find Pusselbitar, 'Puzzle Pieces', sculptures with wooden reliefs that the artist Lena Kriström created together with Bredäng residents in 1982. The district is hilly and has a kilometre and a half of shoreline on Lake Mälaren.
Tunnelbanan är på väg: The metro is on its way
Tunnelbanans högsta station: The highest station on the metro
Tunnelbanestationen Thorildsplan öppnade: Thorildsplan metro station opened on 26 October 1952, when the Hötorget–Vällingby line was inaugurated. On the platform is Huck Hultgren's artwork, a wooden sun on a concrete wall.
Tunnelbanestationen fick 2002 konst av B: In 2002 the metro station was given artwork by Birgitta Muhr: three bronze tulips, two and a half metres tall, with green stems and red flowers. Since 2009 the library has been in the station building, one floor up from the ticket hall.
Tunnelbanestationen ligger i berget 11,5: The metro station lies inside the rock, 11.5 metres below sea level. It shares sixth place as the deepest station on the network with Fridhemsplan.
Tunnelbanestationen strax intill är smyc: The metro station right beside us is decorated with Plexiglas rods and a loop of neon – an artwork by Kazuko Tamura from 1993. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Botkyrka's oldest school building, the church school from 1849, still in use by Botkyrka friskola. And in Hallunda's Folkets hus community hall, local residents run a cultural meeting place for northern Botkyrka themselves.
Tunnelbanestationen är utsmyckad av Taka: The metro station was decorated by Takashi Naraha, whose 1985 work is called Himmelen av kub, 'Heaven of Cubes'. A black cube stands by the entrance, and blue cubes with clouds are set into the raw rock wall by the platform. The idea is that the sky has been brought down to the platform and the dark tunnel lifted up into the light.
Tunnelbanestationen öppnade 5 juni 1977: The metro station opened on 5 June 1977 and lies deep in the rock beneath Husby centrum. Its walls are yellow, painted by the artist Birgit Broms with birch trunks and the classic Vaxholm archipelago steamers.
Tunnelbanestationen öppnade den 26 oktob: The metro station opened on 26 October 1952 as the terminus of the new line to Vällingby, but back then it was called Kungsgatan. It got its present name in 1957. The market hall was rebuilt in the 1950s and now sits one floor below ground.
Tunnelbanestationen öppnade den 5 april: The metro station opened on 5 April 1964, and Berndt Helleberg's artwork was unveiled the same day. The northern part of Hornstull is called Hornsplan, a name from its days as a tram hub.
Tunnelbanestationens norra entré, sett i: The metro station's north entrance – named for the direction the trains run – is actually geographically south of the south entrance. It has confused more than one traveller.
Tunneln som flöt i leran: The tunnel that floated in clay
Tupphuset och kyrktuppen: The Rooster House and the weathercock
Turbinhallens gavel: The gable of the Turbine Hall
Tureberg är Sollentunas administrativa o: Tureberg is the administrative and commercial heart of Sollentuna, and the centre is just a short walk away. Around the square stand Turebergshuset, the town hall, the Arena Satelliten sports hall and the Sollentuna centrum shopping centre. Closer by, in Töjnan, is Töjnaskolan, a school that takes children all the way from the reception year to year nine.
Turebergskyrkan har uppmärksammats inter: Tureberg Church has drawn international attention for its sustainable interior. The altar, font and organ case are made from offcuts of timber, the candleholders from reinforcing bars and the chairs from plastic spun from PET bottles. The idea is to show that "God can use what has been rejected".
Turturduvor i vigselrummet: Turtle doves in the wedding room
Tusentals fyndjägare varje helg: Thousands of bargain hunters every weekend
Tusentals träd på kala berg: Thousands of trees on bare rock
Tuve kyrka en bit härifrån är en av Göte: Tuve church, not far from here, is one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Past it winds Tuve kyrkväg, once the official highway from Säve into central Gothenburg. The southern stretch, between Tången and the church, vanished completely in the Tuve landslide of 1977, because it ran straight through the area that slid away.
Tuve kyrka är byggd av gråsten i romansk: Tuve Church is built of grey fieldstone in the Romanesque style, and the nave and chancel are thought to date from the 1100s. The bowl of the font, carved from amphibolite, is just as old – the oldest object in the church.
Tuve ligger mitt på Hisingen, precis på: Tuve lies in the middle of Hisingen, right where the built-up city gives way to countryside. Not far from here is Gunnestorps mosse, a patchwork of lake, fen and bog where reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow alongside cranberries, sundew and cotton grass. Around the bog are wet meadows that were once used for grazing.
Tuve ligger mitt på Hisingen, på gränsen: Tuve lies in the middle of Hisingen, right where the built-up city to the south meets the countryside to the north. The district covers 1,720 hectares. Right next to it is the Tångedal housing area, with terraced houses and L-shaped houses first lived in in 1968–1969, and a little further on is Tuve torg square.
Tuve torg, alldeles intill, stod klart 1: Tuve torg, right next door, was completed in 1971 and was originally called Norums torg. It wasn't renamed Tuve torg until 1998, and in 2007 it got a proper facelift. On the square you'll find a café and pâtisserie, a library and a pharmacy, among other things, and right next to it is Glöstorp Church, now part of Tuve-Säve parish.
Tuvevägen, som passerar en bit härifrån,: Tuvevägen, which runs a little way from here, is a long through road. It starts at Björlandavägen, passes Tuve and Skändla and ends in Säve, carrying traffic from Tuve and Säve towards central Hisingen. This area was also once home to Hökälla säteri, a manor farm in the Skogome district.
Tv-serie i ett tomt hus: A TV series in an empty building
Tvärbanan kommer till torget: The Tvärbanan comes to the square
Tvärbanan korsar Sickla kanal på Allébro: The Tvärbanan light rail crosses the Sickla canal on Allébron, a bridge from 2000 that carries pedestrians, cars and trams all in one.
Tvärbanan tar sig här över en vik av Ulv: This is where the Tvärbanan light rail crosses an inlet of Lake Ulvsundasjön on the 374-metre Ulvsunda bridge, and right beside it is the Ulvsunda depot from 2014, where the trams are serviced. On the far side of the inlet is Margretelund farm, built in 1830. The city bought it in 1904, and it has served, among other things, as a YMCA summer camp. Today several boat clubs store their boats here over the winter.

Here the Tvärbanan light rail crosses an inlet of Ulvsundasjön on the 374-metre Ulvsunda Bridge, and right beside it is the Ulvsunda depot from 2014, where the trams have their workshop. Across the inlet stands Margretelund, a manor house built in 1830. The city bought it in 1918, and among other things it has been a YMCA summer camp. Today a number of boat clubs store their boats here over the winter.
Tvärbanans ändhållplats: End of the line for the Tvärbanan
Tvättarfamiljen Johansson åkte häst och: The Johanssons, a family of laundry workers, drove a horse and cart into Stockholm to collect dirty washing and bring it back clean. The drying barn has hatches in its walls to let the wind blow through. The museum still shows how washing was done on the shore, and it has a large collection of irons.
Tvättstuga i en fängelsecell: A laundry in a prison cell
Två bassänger på varandra: Two tanks stacked on top of each other
Två dopfuntar och en gåvoklocka: Two fonts and a donated bell
Två grosshandlare köpte Farsta 1897, då: Two wholesale merchants bought Farsta in 1897 – then 2,000 tunnland, about 1,000 hectares – and from 1901 began selling plots under the name Södertörns villastad. Business was poor, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought the land. The following year the area became part of the city.
Två höga hus, Loket 1 och Porslinsbruket: Two tall buildings, Loket 1 and Porslinsbruket 29, stand guard at the northern end of Sankt Erik Bridge – and the ‘porslin’, porcelain, in the second name is no accident. Next door is Rörstrand Castle, home since 2020 to Kaggeholm Folk High School. The Atlas area takes its name from the engineering firm AB Atlas, named in turn after Atlas, the giant of Greek mythology. And by the way, Rörstrandsgatan is pronounced with the stress on ‘rör’.
Två kyrkor ligger nästan vägg i vägg. Su: Two churches stand almost wall to wall here. Sundbyberg church on Rosengatan is a protected church heritage site. Centrumkyrkan was built in 1906 as a Baptist church, and in 1986 it was taken over by an independent congregation founded that same year by the former Pentecostal pastor Stanley Sjöberg. Today it has more than 700 members.
Två stadsplaneideal sida vid sida: Two planning ideals side by side
Två stationer samma dag: Two stations on the same day
Två torg, nästan samma namn: Two squares, almost the same name
Tyresö View och grannhuset byggdes ovanp: Tyresö View and its neighbour were built on top of the shopping centre in 2012–2014. The bottom two floors of the tower are shops. A high-rise was already planned in 2004, but the financial crisis put a stop to it.
Tyresö kyrka, en bit härifrån nära Tyres: Tyresö church, a short way from here near Tyresö Palace, was consecrated on 9 March 1641 – and its very first service was the funeral of the man who built it, Gabriel Oxenstierna. Beside the church stands the Tyresö stone, the only runestone known in the municipality. Its two fragments were found in 1969 and carry a Christian prayer. Down near the palace, the Follbrinkströmmen stream runs out to the water; its power drove all kinds of local enterprises from the Middle Ages right up until the 1940s.
Tyresö är sprickdalslandskap med låga ku: Tyresö is a landscape of low hills and narrow, rocky valleys. Tucked away a little way from here is Barnsjön, a small woodland lake by Farmarstigen. It's just under nine metres deep and has a swimming spot looked after by the municipality. Closer by is the Trollbäcken sports ground, with an ice rink for hockey, an athletics track and three football pitches – so here you can take your pick between skates and football boots.
Tyresö är typiskt sprickdalslandskap, me: Tyresö is classic Swedish fissure-valley landscape, with low hills and valleys but also steep rock faces and rushing rapids. In the south of the municipality, Storskogen begins, with patches of genuine old-growth forest in Tyresta National Park. Most working residents commute to other municipalities, and the council offices are in Tyresö Centre in Bollmora.
Täby Enskilda Gymnasium startade 1999 un: Täby Enskilda Gymnasium, a private upper secondary school, opened in 1999 as Täby Mediagymnasium. It's next to Galoppfältet station on the Roslagsbanan railway, which has an unusual way of getting to the platform: via pedestrian level crossings with barriers at both ends. A little further on is Täby swimming hall, opened in November 2022 – the only one in the whole of Täby.
Täby Enskilda gymnasium: Täby Enskilda gymnasium, an upper secondary school
Täby Park är en hel stadsdel under uppby: Täby Park is an entire district under construction, on the site where the Täby Galopp racecourse stood from 1960 to 2016. The name was chosen on 24 March 2015, the first residents moved in in 2020, and it's expected to take another 20 to 30 years before it's all finished. A couple of hundred metres away is Täby's swimming baths, designed by Norconsult and opened in 2022 – the only indoor pool in the municipality.
Täby centrum har 215 butiker, 34 restaur: Täby centrum has 215 shops, 34 restaurants and cafés and, since 2022, the official name Westfield Täby Centrum. The Filmstaden cinema, which opened in 2013, has five screens and 516 seats in all. And the library holds something far older: fragments of Viking Age runestones found at Lissby in 1930.
Täby kommun bildades 1971, och 2017 flyt: Täby municipality was formed in 1971, and in 2017 the local council moved from Roslags-Näsby to a new town hall by Täby Centre. A short distance away is Grindtorp, one of Tibble's housing areas from the 1950s and 60s, along the E18 between Näsbydal and Täby's former horse racing track. The name comes from a gate – 'grind' in Swedish – on the road between Näsby and Tibble that marked the boundary between the manor and the farm.
Täby var fram till 2010 namnet på en tät: Until 2010, the name Täby covered an urban area that spread across municipal borders, taking in Enebyberg in Danderyd and a small slice of Sollentuna. At the time it was Sweden's eighteenth largest urban area. Not far off is Grindtorp, a housing area along the E18 between Näsbydal, Täby's old horse-racing track and Täby centrum.
Täbysidan ligger i Sollentuna: The Täby side is in Sollentuna
Tändstickor för hela världen tillverkade: Matches for the whole world were once made in the block next door. In 1904, the Södertelje match factory started building a branch here in Elisedal, and in 1913 it was absorbed into Ivar Kreuger's vast match empire. The factory was torn down in the early 2000s. On the site – still called the Tändstickan, or “Matchstick”, block – now stands the ÅF building, 16 storeys and 65 metres tall, opened in 2014.
Tänk att gå på förskola i ett slott! Huv: Imagine going to nursery in a palace! Huvudsta Old Palace, a wooden house from 1750 on Lake Ulvsundasjön, was the main residence of Huvudsta gård until it was moved in 1834. Until the summer of 2018 it housed Förskolan Slottet, the Palace Preschool, run by the Church of Sweden. Right next door is Huvudstabadet, a heated outdoor pool on the waterfront promenade.
Tänk dig en hel församling för de boende: Imagine a parish all of its own for the residents of a single foundation. That's exactly what the Stiftelsen Konung Oscar I:s minne parish was – a parish just for the residents of the foundation here in Bagarmossen, at first part of Maria Magdalena parish. Close by are Skarpnäck school from 1952, designed by Ture Ryberg, and Gränsberget, a park on an old moraine hill.
Tätorten Ekerö består av de tidigare ort: Ekerö town is made up of the former villages of Tappström and Träkvista, which have officially counted as one since 1975. In 1960 Tappström had 343 inhabitants; today more than 10,000 people live in Ekerö.

Ekerö town is made up of the former villages of Tappström and Träkvista, which have officially counted as one since 1975. In 1960 Träkvista had 582 inhabitants and Tappström just 343. The new Ekerö centre was designed by Ralph Erskine.
Tåg som sover i berget: Trains that sleep in the rock
Tågen har stannat här sedan 1856, och fr: Trains have been stopping here since 1856, and until 1912 the station was called Partilled. The first station building was designed by Adolf W. Edelsvärd, chief architect of the Swedish State Railways, and it became the template for a number of other stations – a design known as the Partilled model. It was replaced in 1901 by a new Art Nouveau station building, and since the 1960s the commuter trains between Gothenburg and Alingsås have stopped here.
Tågen mellan Göteborg och Borås stannar: Trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop at Mölnlycke station – though it hasn't always stood here. It opened in 1894 about 350 metres further east and only moved to its current spot in 2003. The old station building was pulled down in 2013. Further on is Wallenstam Arena, where Pixbo Wallenstam IBK play their home floorball games in front of up to 1,600 fans.
Tågen stannade här från 1890 till 1976,: Trains stopped here from 1890 until 1976, when the line between Djursholms Ösby and Eddavägen closed. A couple of minutes away is the Mittag-Leffler Institute, an international research institute for mathematics. It's housed in the castle-like Villa Mittag-Leffler, which has been rebuilt several times, with Ferdinand Boberg among its architects.
Tåghall under limträbågar: A train hall beneath glulam arches
Törstig? I Fructushuset på Ulvsundavägen: Thirsty? The Fructus building on Ulvsundavägen was once where the soft drink Pommac was made. Designed by Ture Wennerholm and built in 1939–1940, the factory is seen as a fine example of functionalist industrial architecture. Close by stood Flygtekniska försöksanstalten, the Aeronautical Research Institute, a government agency that carried out research and experiments in aeronautics until around the turn of the millennium.
U 43 restes av bröderna Ofeg, Sigmar och: U 43 was raised by the brothers Ofeg, Sigmar and Fröbjörn in memory of their father Jörund, Gunna's husband. On the stone's right-hand edge the carver has signed his work: 'Ärnfast carved these runes.' Ärnfast made at least three more runic inscriptions in Uppland.
U 43 är av ljusgrå granit och 2,35 meter: U 43 is a light-grey granite stone 2.35 metres tall. The runes run inside the body of a dragon looping around the edge of the stone, with a large Christian cross at the top. Its Urnes-style ornament dates the stone to between 1025 and 1075.
U 47 satt inmurad i kyrkans grundmur. På: The runestone U 47 was set into the church's foundation wall. In the 1860s it was dug out and moved on Karl XV's orders to the palace park at Drottningholm. In 1952 it came back to the church. The inscription reads: "Torgils and Signiut raised the stone for Vig, their father."
U 48 hittades 1932 inmurad i en av kyrka: U 48 was found in 1932 built into one of the church's foundation walls during reinforcement work. At first it was placed by the roadside, but in 1951 it was moved back into the churchyard. The inscription says that Illuge had the stone raised in memory of his son Tingfast.
U 80 är inte signerad. Men runforskaren: U 80 isn't signed. But the runologist Elias Wessén believes it was probably made by the renowned rune carver Fot, as the careful workmanship, spelling and rune forms resemble his other works.
U 89 står någon meter söder om U 88, och: U 89 stands a metre or so south of U 88; together they're known as the Häradsvägen runestones. In the 17th century the stones stood inside a ring of smaller, round stones.
Udden Hustegaholm vid Kyrkvikens norra s: The Hustegaholm headland on the north shore of Kyrkviken bay has belonged to the City of Lidingö since 1964 and is open to everyone. Three of the houses can be hired for parties and meetings, and in summer the Lidingö Pensioners' Association runs a café in Sjövillan. This is where Kyrkviken, the inlet that splits Lidingö into a northern and a southern half, squeezes into a strait just 25 metres or so wide before opening out into Hustegafjärden bay.
Udden Rya Nabbe var viktig under 1600- o: The headland of Rya Nabbe was strategically important in the wars of the 17th and 18th centuries. The Danes built an earthwork fort here in the 1640s, and the Swedes fortified it in the 1680s. Around 1800 there was both an upper and a lower battery. Only remains survive today.
Udden har fått sitt namn efter ett block: The headland is named after a blockhouse of timber and stone, built in the days of Gustav Vasa to guard the approach to Stockholm. Later it became a customs post for incoming boats, and the old customs houses at Stora Sjötullen are now homes. Out here you'll also find Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, an art museum on Djurgården.
Udden som var en ö: The headland that was an island
Ullevi hade världens första 400 meter lå: Ullevi had the world’s first 400-metre artificially frozen speed skating track. Electric heating cables were laid under the turf to speed up the switch between winter and summer. In 1959 the men’s European Speed Skating Championships were held here.
Ulvesund är en liten ort med åkrar som s: Ulvesund is a small village with fields sloping down to the Nordre älv river, plus an area of summer cottages. It has had a rather fickle relationship with the statisticians. In 2000 it became an official 'småort', a small locality, with 51 inhabitants; by 2005 the population had dropped too low and it lost that status – but by 2010 there were 70 people living here, and Ulvesund was a small locality once again.
Ulvsunda slott byggdes på 1640-talet av: Ulvsunda Castle was built in the 1640s by Field Marshal Lennart Torstenson, and several streets in the area have names linked to him. The castle got its present look in the 1830s, and today it's a hotel and conference centre. Beside it lies the almost perfectly round Lillsjön lake, with allotments that have been there since 1917. And on Ulvsundavägen you'll find one of the few surviving emergency housing blocks from 1917–1918.
Ulvsunda trädgårdsstad började planeras: Planning for Ulvsunda garden city began as early as 1912, when it went by the name Kungsholms villastad. Two unusual buildings survive from that era. Lillsjöstationen, designed by Gustaf de Frumerie, is a 1913 substation for Stockholm's electricity works. And on Ulvsundavägen stands a large block built as emergency housing in 1917–18 – one of the few of its kind still standing in Stockholm.

Planning for the Ulvsunda garden suburb began as early as 1912, and it was originally called Kungsholms villastad. The area also has two unusual reminders of the same period. Lillsjöstationen is a substation for the Stockholm electricity works from 1913, designed by Gustaf de Frumerie, and on Ulvsundavägen is a large building put up as emergency housing during the First World War, one of the few of its kind still standing in Stockholm.
Under 1800-talet växte tegelbruken på Mä: In the 1800s brickworks sprang up across the Mälaren islands to supply Stockholm with building materials. In 1863 the Mälaren region delivered 19 million bricks to the city; just over 20 years later it was 60 million. They were carried on barges towed back and forth.
Under 1800-talets senare hälft fanns en: In the second half of the 1800s there was a harbour basin with warehouses just south of Mölndalsbro. This is where the steam launches on the Mölndalsån river tied up, carrying passengers out from Gothenburg to Mölndal.
Under 1870-talets högkonjunktur hade var: During the boom of the 1870s the shipyard employed nearly 800 workers, and that's when most of the workers' housing on Slottsberget went up. The little wooden houses were built with no town plan at all – and it was they that swept away the last remains of the castle walls.
Under 1900-talet hittades fyra allegoris: In the 20th century, four allegorical paintings from the old church turned up in a barn in Askim. Today they adorn the gallery, depicting Chastity, Gentleness, Religion and Truth.
Under 1930-talet lades grunden till dage: The 1930s laid the foundations of modern harness racing. In 1930 Solvalla held 36 race days with 225 races, and turnover topped five million kronor. The first Elitloppet race was run in 1952.
Under 1980-talet startade skolan ett ege: In the 1980s the school set up its own youth centre to tackle rising youth unemployment. Its aim was to help young people into work or education.
Under 2023 byggdes torget om till ett gr: In 2023 the square was transformed into a leafy garden square, with repainted facades, furniture made specially for the site and new lighting. It reopened on 23 April 2024. The first major makeover had come back in the late 1980s.
Under 2023 gjordes torget om till ett gr: In 2023 the square was transformed into a leafy garden square, inspired by Gothenburg's vision of a modern garden city. With freshly painted façades and furniture designed especially for the spot, it reopened on 23 April 2024.
Under FN:s miljökonferens 1972 blev fält: During the UN environment conference in 1972, the field became a festival ground for the world's youth, with a tent camp and gigs by bands such as Träd, Gräs och Stenar, Blå Tåget and Kebnekajse. Some called it a hippie camp; others claimed the CIA was behind it.
Under Farsta lydde många torp och gårdar: Many crofts and farms came under Farsta, among them Burmanstorp, Forsens gård, Starrmyran, Bergholm and Lugnet. Of these, only Hökarängen farm and Larsbodatorpet survive today.
Under Göta älv i närheten löper Tingstad: Beneath the Göta älv river nearby runs the Tingstad tunnel, an immersed-tube tunnel that carries the E6 between Hisingen and the rest of Gothenburg. It's actually two tubes with three lanes each, 455 metres long. It's also a link in the key motorway between Oslo and Copenhagen – so down under the riverbed here, traffic is speeding between two capital cities.
Under Hagalund går tåget i berget. Hagal: Beneath Hagalund, the trains run through solid rock. The Hagalund tunnels are four railway tunnels about 500 metres long. The first was built in 1911, when Solna station moved to its present site at the northern entrance, and more followed later in the 20th century. The tram stop sits below the residential area known as Blåkulla.
Under Hagsätra torg finns ett stort park: Beneath Hagsätra torg is a large car park. Until the early 1990s it also housed a petrol station with a repair workshop.
Under Hammarkullen ligger en hemlis: Sve: Hammarkullen hides a secret underground: Sweden's only fully underground tram stop, 25 metres below the surface. The platforms were built to take 120-metre trams, but because of ramps and unfinished sections of tunnel, only 70 metres are in use. Up above is Hammarkulletorget, the square built in 1971 and remodelled in 1997 with new colours and a new shape.
Under Hjulstaskolan sprängdes ett bergru: A rock cavern was blasted out for the metro beneath Hjulsta School, and on 31 August 1975 the blue line's trains began running here, about 14 kilometres from Kungsträdgården. Close by are the green Hjulsta allotments. Their association was founded in 1973, and today it's held up as a model of multicultural gardening.
Under Huvudsta centrum gömmer sig en trä: Beneath Huvudsta centrum lies a hidden garden – carved into the rock. The metro station sits in a cavern 25 metres underground and is decorated with Hanging Gardens, an artwork by Per Holmberg from 1985, the year the station opened. The entrance was designed by the architect Yorgo Turac.
Under Sickla Köpkvarter finns Atlas Copc: Beneath Sickla Köpkvarter lies Atlas Copco's old test mine, still in use today. It has three kilometres of tunnels on two levels, 20 and 40 metres underground. You can visit parts of it on a guided tour.
Under Vita bergen finns Pionen, ett skyd: Beneath Vita bergen lies Pionen, a 1943 shelter for a command centre. The nuclear-proof bunker has been used for parties, among other things, and since 2007 it has been a data centre housing the largest server farm in central Stockholm.
Under andra halvan av 1800-talet tvättad: In the second half of the 19th century, crofting families on Södertörn washed Stockholmers’ dirty laundry to earn a bit of extra money. By the early 1900s there were hundreds of little laundries here, and the laundry era peaked during the Second World War.
Under andra världskriget blev fältet kri: During the Second World War the field became a military airfield. In 1943 it came out that the guards had let German military planes take off again after emergency landings, even though neutrality rules said they should have been detained. The affair made headlines in the press.
Under berget mellan Främlingsvägen och B: Under the hill between Främlingsvägen and Bäckvägen, Nässlan was built in 1943 – one of Stockholm's secret civil command centres, attached to Hägersten fire station. It closed in the 1990s. The southernmost of the new buildings stands directly above it.
Under bygget hette arenan först Änglagår: While it was being built, the arena was called first Änglagården and then Göteborgs Nya Arena. Its current name, after the sponsors, was only revealed on opening day, 10 July 2015. Construction cost 800 million kronor.
Under de första fyra dagarna kom 50 000: In its first four days the new shopping centre drew 50,000 visitors. From the very start it had nearly 3,000 parking spaces, its own tram stop and two department stores, Domus and Tempo.
Under den gustavianska tiden var Carl Mi: In the Gustavian era, Carl Michael Bellman, Sweden’s great 18th-century songwriter, was among the guests, and he sang the praises of Clas på Hörnet in his Epistles: ‘Come open our temple! Raise the Wreath as our sign!’
Under den svåra bostadsbristen efter för: During the severe housing shortage after the First World War, the whole of the Exercishuset drill hall was turned into emergency housing. Simple wooden partitions divided the floor into dozens of one-room flats, with no ceilings at all. Today the building is used for table tennis, dance and historical fencing, among other things.
Under en arkeologikurs vid Stockholms un: During an archaeology course at Stockholm University in spring 2020, two students spotted stone frames that once marked the walls of houses. The largest is about 25 metres long and is thought to be a longhouse. A nearby burial ground yielded finely made bronze objects, including a brooch from AD 475–550.
Under en period på 2000-talet var Prinsv: For a time in the 2000s, the Prince’s Villa was the residence of South Africa’s ambassador. In autumn 2004 it welcomed Nobel laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu, who was visiting to mark ten years since the end of apartheid.
Under forntiden var berget en ö. På plat: In prehistoric times this hill was an island. On the plateau are the remains of a hillfort measuring about 800 by 350 metres, probably from the Migration Period, though only around 70 metres of its wall survive. In 1735 a Viking hoard, buried in the mid-1000s, was found at Finnboda.
Under fötterna här i trakten går Gnistän: Running beneath us here is the Gnistäng tunnel, built in 1978 as part of the Västerleden road. At 712 metres, it's one of the longer road tunnels in Sweden. To begin with, traffic in both directions shared a single tube, but as the queues grew the air became stale and exhaust fumes built up, despite an extensive system of fans. So in the summer of 1996, a concrete wall was put in to separate the two directions.
Under fötterna ligger Husby tunnelbanest: Beneath your feet is Husby metro station, blasted out of the bedrock and opened in 1977. The artist Birgit Broms painted its yellow walls with birch trunks and Vaxholm archipelago steamers, bringing a surprising touch of the archipelago to the middle of Järva. Above ground stands Husby Church from 1976, given a green listing by the City Museum for its high cultural and historical value.
Under gatorna klättrar blå rankor och bl: Down below the streets, blue vines and leaves creep across the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and if you look closely among the tendrils you'll see silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was best known for his mechanical sculptures, and in 1966 he helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, ‘She – a Cathedral’.
Under jord pågår ett stort bygge: Södra: Deep below us, a major construction project is under way: Södra Hagalund will be a new station on the green line's branch to Arenastaden, no less than 45 metres underground. It's expected to open in 2029. Up above, in Eric Grate's park, you can see the sculptor's bronzes, including Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God.
Under korsningen Sveavägen–Odengatan lig: There's a bridge buried beneath the junction of Sveavägen and Odengatan. Sveabron was built in 1897, but when Sveavägen was raised in the 1910s, the bridge was simply left where it was and covered over. These blocks were once a cinema strip, too. Rialto opened on the corner of Odengatan in 1921, and since 1993 Teater Pero has staged children's theatre in its old premises. Röda Lyktan, the Red Lantern, showed films from 1917 to 1982.
Under köpcentrets passage över E20 ligge: Beneath the shopping centre's walkway over the E20 is a bus station, and the commuter train station is 200 metres to the north. In 2012 there were plans to develop the area around Kyrktorget, north of the E20, but they were dropped.
Under marken här i närheten gömmer sig E: Somewhere underground near here lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a 3,300-square-metre command centre built to withstand a nuclear bomb, blasted into the rock in the 1970s. It stood empty for 19 years until the Swedish Armed Forces bought it in 2017 and put it back into service. Far older is the Edsängen burial ground, a short walk away, with about 125 Viking Age graves – one of the largest in Sollentuna.
Under medeltiden var Frösunda by, med fe: In the Middle Ages the five-farm village of Frösunda was the largest in Solna parish. In the 1640s the privy councillor Mattias Soop bought two of the farms. Later the commerce councillor Joachim Brandenburg gave the place the feel of a charming Gustavian manor.
Under många år blinkade en rörlig ljusre: For many years an animated neon sign flashed here, showing coins tumbling into Sparbanken's piggy bank. It was a much-loved feature of the Stockholm cityscape until it came down in the late 1980s, when the bank changed its name.
Under namnet Ribo fick biografen teknik: As Ribo, the cinema was fitted out for 70 mm film and showed Around the World in 80 Days on Christmas Day 1959. After it closed, the space became a theatre, a TV studio and, from 1997 to 2015, home to the percussion ensemble Kroumata.
Under reklamtavlorna i Alby station finn: Beneath the advertising boards at Alby station are little figures sticking out their tongues and poking fun at the ads. They weren't in the sketches – Olle Ängkvist painted them while he waited during the work.
Under shoppingstråken i Sickla Köpkvarte: Hidden beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter is something you wouldn't expect: a test mine where rock drills and mining machinery are put through their paces. It's owned today by Epiroc, which was spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018. The name Sickla means roughly 'a low spot where water seeps up' – a little marsh – and comes from the old Stora Sickla estate. The area was also home to Nobelberget, an old warehouse that became a venue for concerts and events.
Under sin exil från Nazityskland på 1940: In the 1940s, while in exile from Nazi Germany, Willy Brandt – later Chancellor of West Germany – lived at Finn Malmgrens väg 23. Since 1997 the park by the metro's eastern entrance has carried his name. The street itself honours the polar explorer Finn Malmgren, and on Finn Malmgrens plan stands the statue Avskedet på polarisen, 'Farewell on the Polar Ice'. Keep your eyes peeled at the station, too: it has the smallest artwork on the whole metro, a decoration set into the brickwork.
Under skolans första femtio år var svens: For the school's first fifty years, Swedish Sign Language was used as a matter of course, both in and out of the classroom. In 1862 the oral method was introduced: sign language was banned and deaf teachers were dismissed. Today Manillaskolan is bilingual, and since 2013 it has been on Kungsholmen.
Under spårvagnshållplatsen byggs Korsväg: Beneath the tram stop, Korsvägen station is being built as part of Västlänken, the new rail tunnel under the city. From here you can also catch buses to Borås, Kungälv and Landvetter Airport, among other places.
Under stadshuset finns Dalénsalen, uppka: Beneath the town hall are the Dalén Hall, named after the inventor Gustaf Dalén, and the Raoul Wallenberg Room. The diplomat Raoul Wallenberg was born in the summer villa Kappsta on Lidingö.
Under torget byggs tunnelbanestationen B: Beneath the square, the Barkarbystaden metro station is under construction, and all around it a whole new district is springing up on the grounds of the old Svea air wing and its closed-down airfield. A little further away is Kyrkbyn, the church village, once called Järfälla gård, which played a central part in Järfälla's early history.
Under vikingatiden och tidig medeltid lå: In the Viking Age and early Middle Ages a large and influential village called Väsby stood here. When Kungsgatan was blasted through the Brunkeberg ridge, workers found skeletons, armour and coins belonging to buried villagers.
Under vikingatiden var Edsviken och Norr: In the Viking Age, Edsviken and Norrviken formed one continuous waterway with a connection to the Baltic. Just west of the burial ground was an ancient hillfort, but it was removed in the early 1970s when the Tunberget water tower was built.
Under Älvsborgsbron, en bit härifrån, li: Just along from here, under Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, is one of the city's least glamorous but most essential facilities: Ryaverket. This plant treats the wastewater of nearly 800,000 people in the Gothenburg region, and it has been extended time and again since work began in 1968. Further off rises the Rya accumulator tank, a cylinder about 60 metres tall that smooths out peaks in demand for district heating. You can see it from the harbour entrance.
Under älven en bit härifrån ligger Marie: Under the river, not far from here, runs the Marieholm tunnel, which opened to traffic on 16 December 2020. It was built from prefabricated sections sunk into place, and like the Tingstad tunnel it isn't fixed to the bedrock – instead it floats in the clay. It was expected to cost 3.5 billion kronor. The Säveån river also flows through this area; counting its headwaters, it's 130 kilometres long.
Under åren 1762–1770 arrenderades värdsh: From 1762 to 1770 the inn was leased by James Carnegie. He then moved into Gothenburg and ran a coffee house on Köpmansgatan, next to the German Church. Jacob Wallenberg stayed here in 1769 while waiting to sail on the ship Finland.
Ungdomscenter mot arbetslösheten: A youth centre to fight unemployment
Ungefär där Karl IX:s staty står byggdes: Roughly where the statue of Karl IX stands, a reservoir holding 700 barrels of water was built and opened in 1797 to the sound of kettledrums and trumpets. Inside was a poem by the mayor, Daniel Pettersson. It later became an outpatient clinic and was demolished in 1899.
Ungefär där Karolinska sjukhuset ligger: Until the 1600s there was a farming village called Bolstomta roughly where Karolinska University Hospital now stands. Tomteboda came about through a deliberate twisting of that name.
Upp mot Majorna. Titta efter Masthuggsky: Up towards Majorna. Look out for Masthuggskyrkan, the 1914 church high on the hill.
Uppdraget att rita kyrkan gick först til: The commission to design the church first went to Backström and Reinius, but they turned it down and it passed to Peter Celsing. Planning took more than six years, and building didn't start until 1958. The church is blue-listed by the City Museum, its highest category.
Uppe i biljetthallens lanternin hänger s: Up in the ticket hall's lantern roof hangs the sculpture Min vän (My Friend) by the artist couple Eva and Peter Moritz. It's made of aluminium rods bolted and welded together, and was unveiled in 2006.
Uppe på Albyberget börjar en lång rulltr: At the top of Albyberget hill, a long escalator takes you down to Alby metro station, about 24 metres underground. Down there, the artist Olle Ängkvist has painted flowers in vivid colours on moss-green concrete walls. Alby is also home to Cirkus Cirkör, the circus company, based at the Subtopia cultural centre a little way from here.
Uppe på Almhöjden finns en kvadratisk pl: On top of Almhöjden, the Elm Hill, is a square enclosure, 20 by 20 metres, surrounded by a wall of dressed granite just over a metre high. The top of the wall is a planting trough, and the space is framed by twelve high-pruned umbrella elms.
Uppe på Hökeberget står Guldhedens norra: Up on Hökeberget stands Guldheden's northern water tower, which was converted in 2008 into 74 student flats. The roof is about 140 metres above sea level, and on the eleventh floor there's a shared roof terrace. On every floor, the flats are laid out like a fan. The KV art school, founded in 1969, was also based round here until it moved to Lindholmen in 2023.
Uppe på Kvarnberget finns fortfarande en: Up on Kvarnberget hill there's still a church ruin from Karl IX's Gothenburg. Nearby is Kaféhusets trädgård, where you can still make out the foundations and steps of Villa Dalhem, a three-storey house built by the merchant Svante Gustafsson in 1896.
Uppe på Kvarnberget snurrade en gång Stu: Up on Kvarnberget, the Mill Hill, the windmill of Stuvsta gård once turned – and that's how the whole Kvarnbergsplan area got its name. Several of the millstones survive, and the municipality has put one on display on Gymnasievägen. That's also where you'll find Huddingegymnasiet, an upper secondary school whose building is rated among the most valuable in the municipality.
Uppe på Kyrkåsberget, i villastaden Para: Up on Kyrkåsberget, in the villa suburb of Paradiset, stands Villa Porthälla – known to locals, as long as anyone can remember, as Borgen, the Castle. The company director Ernst Harbeck built it between 1914 and 1918 to look like a medieval German castle in stone and brick: five floors and 17 rooms. In autumn 1972 the police carried out a major raid on the villa. Today it's divided into flats.
Uppe på Störtfjällsberget invigdes Kvarn: Up on Störtfjällsberget hill, Kvarnbyvallen opened on a Sunday in midsummer 1934. It was Mölndal's first proper sports ground and home to FK Herkules, Sweden's oldest 'frisksport' club – part of a healthy-living sports movement. The ground closed in 2007 and is now housing. Not far from here, Biografen Möllan has been showing films since 1959, with 289 seats in the Folkets hus community hall.
Uppe på Vattentornsberget reser sig Jarl: Up on Vattentornsberget – Water Tower Hill – stands the Jarlaberg water tower. It's 47.5 metres tall, and its two tanks supply the whole of Sicklaön with water. The Nacka Forum shopping centre opened in 1989, replacing a set of temporary huts that had stood there for years. A little further on, in Storängen, is Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg – the architect of Stockholm City Hall – and built in 1907 for Yngve Larsson, later a city commissioner, and his wife Elin, née Bonnier.
Uppe på berget i närheten ligger Skansen: Up on the hill nearby is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century fortress with a gilded lion on top. It was built to defend the city against attack from the east.
Uppe på berget står Larsbergs hus med te: Up on the hill are the Larsberg buildings, with their brick-red façades, green metal roofs and white balconies – classic 1960s. Just over 1,200 flats were completed here in 1969, all designed by the architect Bengt Gate. Down below is Malmstens, where students learn furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery. And the old hospital building in Högsätra was due to come down during 2025, to make way for the new Kärnan district.
Uppe på berget står ett långt hus som lä: Up on the hill is a long building that for many years stood all on its own. It was built in 1914 as housing for workers at AGA, and today it's a state-listed building. In 2001 it was renovated and the flats were sold off as owner-occupied apartments. Just along from it stands AGA's yellow optics tower.
Up on the hill you can see Sofia Church.
Uppe på ett hustak i Råcksta lyser en bi: Up on a rooftop in Råcksta, a bit of the 1950s still glows. The neon sign – RÅCKSTA in green with a swooping 'Centrum' in yellow – went up in that decade, when suburban shops lured customers with little neon signs reading BLOMMOR, FRISÖR and KONDITORI: flowers, hairdresser, pâtisserie. Most of that glowing heritage has gone, but this sign was restored in 2011 and shines as brightly as ever.
Uppe på höjden i området ligger Furulund: Up on the heights here is Furulund, where snow shovels get a lot more use than down in the valley. Furulund sits more than 100 metres higher than Gothenburg, and since the temperature hovers around freezing on many days, it gets more snow, and the snow sticks around longer. Below lies Kåhög, a small villa community on the Säveån river.
