Next to the station is Nymble, the engineering students' union building from 1930, designed by Sven Markelius and Uno Åhrén. Ever since, the students have held their gasques – formal student dinners – in Gasqueparken, the park with the fountain. On the other side of Valhallavägen is Lärkstaden, where around 1910 the architects Per Olof Hallman and Erik Josephson designed villas for themselves.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 29 mot Stoc: Welcome aboard tram 29 towards Stockholms östra! The journey takes about 35 minutes. The Roslagsbanan railway arrived here in 1937, when Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar extended the line from Lahäll, and this is the end of that branch. Näsbypark is one of Täby's more exclusive neighbourhoods, with villas and terraced houses close to the water at Stora Värtan bay. Right by the station is Näsbypark Church, part of Täby parish.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 3 mot Markl: Welcome aboard tram 3 towards Marklandsgatan! The journey takes about 41 minutes. We start in Kålltorp, a quiet residential area in eastern Gothenburg. From here it's only a short way to the Delsjön area, a large nature reserve of lakes and forest.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 3 mot Virgi: Welcome aboard tram 3 towards Virginsgatan! The journey takes about 41 minutes. This street is named after the markland, an old unit used to value land. Right next door is the Frölundaborg ice rink, which opened in 1967 with a friendly in which Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. And winding past Slottsskogsvallen, the athletics stadium where high jumpers like Patrik Sjöberg and Stefan Holm trained, is Friidrottens väg – the Athletics Way.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 30 mot Sick: Welcome aboard tram 30 towards Sickla! The journey takes about 59 minutes. Råsundavägen 45 was once home to a cinema called the Savoy. In 1974 its auditorium became the Marcus Music recording studio – according to Studio Sound magazine, the first in Sweden with a 24-track tape machine. Abba recorded most of The Album here in 1977. Today it's called Soundtrade Studios, and over the years artists such as Robyn and Joey Tempest have recorded here.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 30 mot Soln: Welcome aboard tram 30 towards Solna station! The journey takes about 58 minutes. Sit back and enjoy the view from the window.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 31 mot Alvi: Welcome aboard tram 31 towards Alviks strand! The journey takes about 13 minutes. The building on Ulvsundavägen went up in 1946 as the head office of the airline ABA and was later used by SAS. It was designed by Paul Hedqvist, the architect behind several of the airport's hangars, too – in their day the biggest in northern Europe. These days the hangars house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 31 mot Brom: Welcome aboard tram 31 towards Bromma flygplats! The journey takes about 12 minutes. Alvik's old industrial area by Lake Mälaren is now mostly offices and a handful of restaurants. Nearby is Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, an events venue where the TV dance contest Floor Filler was recorded. Watch the Tvärbanan light rail as it vanishes into the roughly 250-metre Alvik tunnel and then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the Alvik bridge – 400 metres long and finished in 2000.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 4 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 4 towards Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 57 minutes. Welcome to Mölndal. Along the rapids in Mölndals kvarnby, the mill village, water power has driven mills and factories for several hundred years. Today the mill village is a heritage area with a museum and cafés.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 4 mot Mölnd: Welcome aboard tram 4 towards Mölndals Innerstad! The journey takes about 57 minutes. Angered was built in the 1970s and is now one of Gothenburg's most international districts. It's home to the Blå Stället cultural centre, and all around are wide stretches of countryside with lakes and forest.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 5 mot Varmf: Welcome aboard tram 5 towards Varmfrontsgatan! The journey takes about 54 minutes. We're starting out at Östra sjukhuset, the East Hospital. From here it's only a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes, woods and places to swim.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 5 mot Östra: Welcome aboard tram 5 towards Östra Sjukhuset! The journey takes about 53 minutes. Sit back and enjoy the view.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 6 mot April: Welcome aboard tram 6 towards Aprilgatan! The journey takes about 78 minutes. Sit back and enjoy the view.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 6 mot Varmf: Welcome aboard tram 6 towards Varmfrontsgatan! The journey takes about 78 minutes. Årstidstorget – 'Seasons Square' – is known to most locals simply as Norra, or Norra centrum, and it's the little meeting place of northern Kortedala. You'll find a health centre, a pizzeria, a couple of tobacconists and a pâtisserie for anyone in need of a fika, the Swedish coffee break, with a restaurant close by too. Local clubs and associations have their premises around the square, which sits on tram line six, near the end of the line.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Komet: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Komettorget! The journey takes about 66 minutes. We're in Tynnered, where the streets are named after gemstones: Opaltorget, Smaragdgatan and Briljantgatan – Opal Square, Emerald Street and Diamond Street. Nature reserves and seaside swimming in Västra Frölunda are just a short trip away.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Opalt: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Opaltorget! The journey takes about 66 minutes. Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan and Meteorgatan – Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön, the street names are out of this world. Nearby is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, home to Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the local culture house. It has a library, a café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, with everything from music and art to children's events.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot T-Cen: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards T-Centralen! The journey takes about 13 minutes. Waldemarsudde was the home of the artist Prince Eugen, son of King Oscar II and one of the leading landscape painters of his day. Today his waterside villa and garden are an art museum.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Walde: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Waldemarsudde! The journey takes about 12 minutes. Down below the streets, blue vines and leaves climb across the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and if you look closely among the tendrils you'll spot silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was best known for his mechanical sculptures, and in 1966 he helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, 'She – a Cathedral'.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 8 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 8 towards Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 64 minutes. Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 as one of Sweden's first big suburban shopping centres. All around it is Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 8 mot Frölu: Welcome aboard tram 8 towards Frölunda Torg! The journey takes about 63 minutes. Angered was built in the 1970s and is now one of Gothenburg's most international districts. It's home to the Blå Stället arts centre, and all around are large stretches of countryside with lakes and forest.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 9 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 9 towards Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 57 minutes. Kungssten sits close to the mouth of the Göta älv river. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966. Out in the estuary lies the 17th-century fortress of Nya Älvsborg, built to protect the city from the Danes. And down by the water is Klippan, with its old seamen's houses and the remains of the earlier Älvsborg fortress.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 9 mot Kungs: Welcome aboard tram 9 towards Kungssten! The journey takes about 56 minutes. Angered was built in the 1970s and is now one of Gothenburg's most international districts. It's home to the Blå Stället culture centre, and all around are large stretches of nature with lakes and forest.
Välkommen ombord! Du kliver på vid Drott: Welcome aboard! You're boarding at Drottningtorget, right in front of the Central Station, on a tram that belongs to the largest tram network in the Nordic countries. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and while many other Swedish cities got rid of their trams, Gothenburg held on to its own. The Central Station opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. So sit back and relax – we're heading along the river, through the old working-class neighbourhoods and out to the sea.
Välkommen till Majorna. Titta på husen:: Welcome to Majorna. Take a look at the houses: a stone ground floor with two wooden storeys on top. That's a landshövdingehus, a type of building found almost nowhere but Gothenburg. It was a clever way round an old rule that wooden houses could be no more than two storeys high – the stone floor simply didn't count.
Välkommen till Mölndal. Längs forsen i M: Welcome to Mölndal. Along the rapids in Kvarnbyn, Mölndal's old mill village, water power has driven mills and factories for several hundred years. Today Kvarnbyn is a heritage area with a museum and cafés.
Vällingby Centrum blev en internationell: When Vällingby Centrum was completed in 1954, it became an international model for the modern town centre. The metro depot next door was originally called Spångahallen – a slightly odd name that dates from the time when Vällingby belonged to Spånga municipality, before it merged with the City of Stockholm. Right next door, too, is Jan-Pers stuga, Jan-Per's cottage.
Vällingby planerades som ABC-staden, med: Vällingby was planned as an 'ABC town' – A for work, B for housing and C for a town centre, all in one place – and it even had its own cinema. Fontänen opened in 1956, named after the fountains on the square. That same year, the Trappan community centre opened, built in terraces stepping down between an upper and a lower square. Both were designed by the architects Backström & Reinius.
Vällsjön ligger några hundra meter bort,: A few hundred metres away is Lake Vällsjön, a small lake only four and a half metres deep. It marks Pixbo's south-eastern edge, and the Vällbäcken stream links it with Lake Rådasjön. Pixbo itself is built on and around the height of Björnåsen – so expect hills.
Väntan sitter på en sockel av granit och: Väntan (Waiting), roughly life-size, sits on a granite plinth. The sculpture was placed here by Charles Felix Lindberg's donation fund.
Värden som öppnade kaffehus: The innkeeper who opened a coffee house
Värdshuset byggdes i furu- och grantimme: The old inn was built of pine and spruce logs, clad in red-painted boards and fitted with wooden gutters. Inside, the rooms had paper wallpaper and five kakelugnar, the tall tiled stoves typical of Swedish homes. Today four families live here.
Värdshuset Övre Haga fick två uthuslängo: The Övre Haga inn had two rows of outbuildings. The innkeeper lived in the western one, while the eastern one held a henhouse, a cowshed, a carriage shed and stabling for 22 horses. The western row burned down in 1956, and only the foundations remain.
Världens dans på liten scen: World dance on a tiny stage
Världens första konstfrusna skrinnarbana: The world’s first artificial-ice speed skating track
Världens första kurdiska bibliotek finns: The world's first Kurdish library is just a stone's throw from here. Kurdiska biblioteket opened in 1997 and spent its first ten years on Skeppsholmen, then, after a brief stop in Duvbo, moved into the Alvik community centre in 2011. Its shelves hold around 13,000 books in almost 30 languages, most of them in Kurdish. Next door is St Ansgar's Church.
Världens största tankers lägger till: Where the world's biggest tankers dock
Världscuphoppning varje år: World Cup show jumping every year
Världskulturmuseet: Världskulturmuseet, the Museum of World Culture
Världslitteraturhuset: Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature
Världspremiär för röntgenbehandling: A world first in X-ray treatment
Världsstjärnor i konsthallen: World stars at the art gallery
Värme, kyla och el ur avlopp: Heat, cooling and power from sewage
Värmeverket har en tydlig industrikarakt: The heating plant has a strongly industrial look, with façades of corrugated sheet metal in bold colours meant to break up the large volumes. Its tall concrete chimney, painted yellow and blue, has become a familiar landmark in Akalla.
Värtahamnen anlades 1879 till 1886 som h: Värtahamnen harbour was built between 1879 and 1886 for coal and other bulk goods. Today it's where ferries leave for Finland, Åland, Estonia and Latvia. The old Kommunalhuset building was home to Värtan fire station from 1905 to 1934. A little further on, outside the entrance to the Värtaverket power plant, stands Kungseken, the King's Oak, around 600 years old. It was probably named after Oscar II, who used to make springtime outings to the tree.
Väsjön intill skidbacken är bara 2,35 me: Lake Väsjön, next to the ski slope, is only 2.35 metres deep. Test fishing has turned up perch, pike, roach, rudd and tench. There are two swimming spots, and the water eventually drains into Lake Mälaren.
Västberga begravningsplats, mellan Solbe: Västberga cemetery, between Solberga, Västberga and Liseberg, carries the City Museum's blue rating for exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Its neighbour, Liseberg, is at 38 hectares the smallest district in all of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. A little further on is Årsta partihallar, a wholesale market where around 200 companies trade in fruit, vegetables, fish and flowers.
Västberga gård, med anor från 1300-talet: Västberga gård goes back to the 14th century, became a noble estate in the 17th century and has given its name to the whole district. The City of Stockholm has owned the manor since 1935. Not far from here runs Älvsjöbågen, the Älvsjö Arch, a 1,396-metre railway bridge that's part of the Citybanan rail link. It's Sweden's fourth-longest railway bridge and was built using a technique rarely seen in Sweden.
Väster om hamnen reser sig det cirka 35: West of the harbour rises Sörhallsberget, about 35 metres high. It's named after the 18th-century Sörhallen estate, with its herring warehouses, salting houses, train-oil boilery and loading jetties. A huge fire reduced it all to ashes on 15 June 1897.
Väster om slussen har kanalens norra sid: West of the lock, the canal’s north bank has a reed-fringed waterside walk with wooden decking and plenty of seating, while the south bank has a crisp urban quay with most of the canal’s 124 moorings. East of the lock there are natural shores.
Västerortskyrkan i Vällingby centrum rit: Västerortskyrkan in Vällingby centre was designed by Carl Nyrén and Bertil Engstrand and built in 1956. From the outside it looks closed and plain, with rendered walls, but step inside and you're in the world of New Brutalism: dramatically leaning walls of raw concrete, with light filtering down from the roof. The church is also built together with an eleven-storey block of flats.
Västertorps tunnelbanestation är den näs: Västertorp is the second-highest station on the whole metro network, at 42.8 metres above sea level. The district is also home to Stockholm's largest sculpture park, with 21 outdoor works. And on Västertorpsplan was the neighbourhood cinema Västan, which showed films from 1954 to 1971.
Västorgeln från 1861 har flera ovanligt: The west organ, from 1861, has several unusually well-preserved stops. Since 1992 the north gallery has also had an organ in the North German baroque style, built by John Brombaugh in the USA.
Västra Balltorp ligger alldeles intill e: Västra Balltorp sits right next to a golf course – and the golf club even had a hand in developing the area. Its neighbour, Östra Balltorp, has had trouble making up its mind: sometimes it's counted as a town of its own, sometimes as part of Gothenburg, depending on the year Statistics Sweden did its count.
Västra Hisingen är industrins och hamnar: Western Hisingen is the land of heavy industry and docks. Not far from here is the Preemraff oil refinery, which gets most of its crude oil from the North Sea. In neighbouring Arendal, the Arendal shipyard was in business from 1963 to 1989; today the site is home to Volvo Buses' headquarters, among others. Arendal is so thoroughly industrial that in 2012 only 90 people actually lived there.
Väveriet Krokslätts fabriker anlades på: The Krokslätt weaving mills were founded in the 1870s. By 1915 the spinning mill was the largest in Sweden, with around 1,000 workers. After merging with Mölnlycke, the company was Sweden's biggest textile firm in 1949, employing 4,600 people. Production closed down in 1973–1974.
Vågmästaren och brukspatronen Johan Oliv: Johan Oliveholm, weighmaster and ironworks owner, bought the estate in 1759 and turned it into a well-run property. In 1774 he also bought part of Skälltorps Östergård, where the private Friedländer cemetery was later laid out.
Vålberga har fått namn efter en gård som: Vålberga is named after a farm mentioned as early as the 15th century. Its 19th-century main house stood roughly where the playground is today and was demolished around 1965–66.
Vålberga är uppkallat efter en gård vars: Vålberga is named after a farm mentioned as far back as the 1400s. The main house stood roughly where the playground is today and was demolished around 1965–66.
Vålberga, en bit härifrån, är ett bostad: Vålberga, not far from here, is a housing area built around 1963, made up mostly of rows of terraced houses. It's in Barkarby-Skälby, Järfälla's southernmost district. Nearby is the manor of Skälby gård, surrounded by four ancient burial grounds. And the old parish of Barkarby was merged into a newly formed Järfälla parish in 2010.
Vårberg centrum invigdes i september 196: Vårberg centre opened in September 1968, just under a year after the metro station in the same complex, and it has been praised for its international modernist architecture. The City Museum calls it an early and well-preserved example of an indoor square. Nearby is the Kummelholmen art gallery, whose name simply comes from the building's land registry designation.
Vårberg sträcker sig hela vägen ner till: Vårberg stretches all the way down to Lake Mälaren in the north-west, and 65 hectares of the district are actually water. The homes in the Bergholmen block on Rönnholmsgränd date from the late 1960s and have a green listing from the City Museum. So does Vårbergsskolan, built between 1968 and 1972 as a lower secondary school, which today houses an adult education college and an independent school.

Vårberg stretches all the way down to Lake Mälaren in the north-west, and 65 hectares of the district is water. The flats in the Bergholmen block on Rönnholmsgränd were built in the late 1960s and have been given the City Museum's green listing for buildings of special value. So has Vårberg School, built between 1968 and 1972 as a secondary school; since 2005 it has housed adult education, and since 2020 part of Slättgård School too.
Vårbergs tunnelbanestation invigdes den: Vårberg metro station opened on 2 December 1967, and just under a year later Vårberg Centre opened in the same complex. The centre has been praised for its international modernist design and is an early example of an indoor square. Nearby are the Vårberg nursing home from the late 1960s – for many years the only major employer in Vårberg – and the Kummelholmen art gallery.
Vårbergs tunnelbanestation öppnade den 2: Vårberg metro station opened on 2 December 1967, with an open-air platform 12.6 kilometres from Slussen. Less than a year later, in September 1968, Vårberg centrum opened in the same complex. It's an indoor square that the City Museum has given a green listing for its importance in the history of town planning and its international modernist architecture.
Vårby är belagt redan 1381 som \"Warby\": Vårby is recorded as early as 1381 as ‘Warby’. The site is thought to have been strategically important for protecting trade at Helgö and Birka, and the name is interpreted as ‘Vardh by’ – the watchmen’s village.
Vårbyfjärden ligger i Östra Mälaren mell: Vårbyfjärden is a bay of eastern Lake Mälaren between Södertörn and Ekerön. At its southern end it connects with Lake Albysjön via Hagaviken and Fittjaviken. The Jungfruholmarna islets lie some six nautical miles into Mälaren from Stockholm.
Vårbyskatten hittades i april 1871 av 14: The Vårby hoard was found in April 1871 by 14-year-old Otto Ludvig Jonsson, who was out gathering brushwood in Wårby forest. He was given a reward of 250 kronor. The jewellery dates from the 10th century and is now on display at the Swedish History Museum.
Vårfrukyrkan: Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady
Vårfrukyrkan i Fruängen fick vänta länge: Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady in Fruängen, had a long wait for its church. The red-brick church centre opened in 1963, but without the sanctuary shown on the plans. Building didn't start until 2004, in cast concrete, and on the first Sunday of Advent 2005 the church was finally consecrated and given the name Vårfrukyrkan.
Vårväderstorget har blivit Sveriges förs: Vårväderstorget has become the first square in a disadvantaged area of Sweden to be certified under the BoTryggt2030 safety standard. This means it meets demanding requirements for safety and security.
Vårväderstorget ritades av arkitekten He: Vårväderstorget was designed by the architect Helge Zimdal and completed in 1958, in an Italian style with terraces and arches. The name means Spring Weather Square, one of many names in Biskopsgården on the theme of weather. The square has its own tram stop, and it's home to Göteborgs folkhögskola, a folk high school, and Biskopsgården library, one of the busiest in the city.
Waldemarsudde var konstnären prins Eugen: Waldemarsudde was the home of Prince Eugen, the artist prince. A son of King Oscar II, he was one of the leading landscape painters of his day. Today his villa and garden by the water are an art museum.
Wallander fick idén till sopnedkast på e: Wallander got the idea for rubbish chutes on a trip to the USA in 1920. The health board said no. He replied that the board could ban people from using rubbish chutes, but not from building them. So they were built – and later approved.
Wallenberg-mausoleet är byggt som ett li: The Wallenberg mausoleum, from 1912, takes the form of a small, circular Classical temple with a dome. An avenue of thujas leads up to the top of the hill, which is itself a glacial meltwater deposit from the Ice Age.
Wallenbergkullen är en isälvsavlagring f: Wallenbergkullen hill is a glacial meltwater deposit from the Ice Age, and the trees planted on it make it look even taller. On eastern Lindö there are ancient remains such as stone settings and burial sites.
Wendelsbergs folkhögskola: Wendelsbergs folkhögskola, the Wendelsberg folk high school
Wendelsbergs kamratförbund startade 1913: Wendelsberg's alumni association was founded in 1913 by former pupils and staff. Every spring it publishes a yearbook about life at the school past and present, and each year it holds a reunion where all former pupils are welcome.
Westra Piren rankades länge som en av de: For years Westra Piren ranked among the best restaurants in Sweden's food guides. But competition for business dinners grew ever fiercer, and in the winter of 2000 the starred restaurant went bankrupt.
Wisingska villan var 300 kvadratmeter i: The Wising villa was a two-storey, 300-square-metre house in the Swiss chalet style with lavish fretwork. It stood at the edge of a fault scarp, and a fieldstone retaining wall about five metres high created a level area around it. The root cellar survives.
World Trade Center byggdes 1986–89 och ä: The World Trade Center was built in 1986–89 and is joined to the Cityterminalen bus terminal, with an entrance from Kungsbron too. It contains around 45,000 square metres of office space.
Ytterby har gamla anor, bygden har varit: Ytterby has a long history: people have lived here since the Iron Age, and the area is full of ancient remains. A short way from here are the ruins of Ytterby's old church, built in the Romanesque style in the 1100s on what was then Norwegian soil. Legend credits Saint Olaf with building it, and the stone church may have been preceded by an even older wooden one from the 1000s.
Yttringe betyder den yttre ängen. Namnet: Yttringe means "the outer meadow". The name appears as Ytra ængia in a deed of sale from 1381. Västra Yttringe farm by Gråviken is now used by the Iranian embassy.
Ägaren som namngav kvarteret: The owner who named the block
Äggelundastenen, en runsten som ursprung: The Äggelunda Stone, a runestone that once stood at Äggelunda gård in Veddesta, was moved to the Fruns backe burial ground in 2014, when building work began around Barkarby commuter station. Another Veddesta runestone has had less luck: Olof Celsius the Elder mentioned it in 1728, and it has been missing ever since.
Äggelundastenen, runstenen U 84, stod ur: The Äggelunda stone, runestone U 84, originally stood at Äggelunda farm in Veddesta. In 2014, when the area around Barkarby commuter station was about to be developed, the stone was moved to Fruns backe, a burial ground south-west of Veddesta gård. Not far from there are two more Viking Age runestones, known as the runestones on Häradsvägen.
Äldreboendet Danvikshem har en historia: The Danvikshem care home traces its history back to Danvik's Hospital, which was founded in 1551 and didn't close until 1915. Close by stood the Danvik asylum, a mental hospital from 1788 to 1861, and along Kvarnholmsvägen lies an abandoned cemetery, Danvikens begravningsplats. Happier memories belong to Gomanhuset, the Goman Building, where Kooperativa Förbundet, the Swedish Cooperative Union, had its laboratory for cooked meats and sausages.
Älta kyrka från 1994 är byggd som en utb: Älta Church, from 1994, is built as an extension at the back of a five-storey apartment block. The walls of the church interior are a rusty brownish orange, and behind the altar a stained-glass window shows leafy branches with a red apple.
Älta kyrka invigdes 1994 och är byggd so: Älta church was consecrated in 1994 and is built as an extension at the back of a five-storey block of flats. You can spot the church interior from outside because it rises a little higher than the rest of the building. The walls are rendered white, and one façade bears a cross with a wreath of flowers.
Älta köpcentrum i Stensö invigdes 1968 o: Älta shopping centre in Stensö opened in 1968 and was one of the first indoor malls in the Stockholm area. Its eleven-storey centre building became sheltered housing for pensioners, and in eastern Stensö small houses of just 55 square metres were built for pensioners and single people.
Opened in 1968, Älta's shopping centre in Stensö was one of the first indoor malls in the Stockholm area. Its eleven-storey centre building was turned into sheltered housing for pensioners.

Älta's shopping centre in Stensö opened in 1968 and was one of the first indoor malls in the Stockholm area. The eleven-storey centre building became sheltered housing for pensioners. In eastern Stensö, small houses of just 55 square metres were built with pensioners and single people in mind.
Älta mosse är ungefär en kilometer lång: Älta mosse is about a kilometre long and 700 metres wide, making it the largest raised bog in Nacka. Typical bog plants grow here among sparse birch woodland: cranberry, bog myrtle, marsh Labrador tea and cloudberry.
Älta är en av Nackas fyra kommundelar, o: Älta is one of Nacka's four districts, and nearby is Stensö, home to around 2,600 people. It's named after the peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip you'll find the Stensö swimming spot. A couple of minutes away, beside Ältavägen, is Älta Church.
Ältavägen är 8,1 kilometer lång och fick: Ältavägen is 8.1 kilometres long, and its route was set in 1934. It runs mainly through open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. In the Flaten nature reserve there's an unexpected attraction: a racetrack for radio-controlled model cars, at Ältavägen 301 in the Flaten district.
Älvestaån rinner från sjön Aspen till Tu: The Älvestaån stream flows from Lake Aspen to Lake Tullingesjön, dropping 17 metres in only about 2.5 kilometres. Part of it runs through a culvert beneath Hågelby manor and the Hågelbyleden road. In Hågelby's park the stream has been reshaped into a canal, becoming part of the park's design. The name comes from Elvesta farm by Lake Tullingesjön, also spelled Älvesta.
Älvestaån var en gång en slingrande bäck: Älvestaån was once a meandering stream. In the 19th century the fields were drained and the stream became a wide, straight ditch. But about 300 metres east of Hågelbyleden it still follows its original winding course.
Älvestaån var från början en meandrande: Älvestaån started out as a meandering stream. In the 19th century the fields at Hågelby were drained and the stream was straightened into the wide, straight ditch you see today. Even so, about 300 metres east of Hågelbyleden its original winding course survives.
Älvsborgs kyrka hette tidigare Hagens ka: Älvsborg church was once known as Hagen's chapel, and it has belonged to Älvsborg parish since 1967. A little further on rises Stora Billingen, a 40-metre hill by Nya Varvet. Military facilities were blasted into the rock beneath it, but in the 2000s, once every appeal had been turned down, the housing cooperative HSB was given the go-ahead to build 50 small houses on the site.
Älvsjö gård har mycket gamla anor, med k: Älvsjö gård has deep roots, with owners known by name from the mid-15th century. One family held the farm for almost two hundred years, right up until 1968. For a long time hardly anyone lived in the area: around 1900 the population was mainly people working on the farm or at the station.
Älvsjö skrevs 1461 Elffuesio. Förleden k: In 1461 Älvsjö was written Elffuesio. The first part may be the man's name Ælve, though that's uncertain. The second part refers to Brännkyrkasjön, a lake that lay east of Älvsjö farm and has since disappeared.
Älvsjöbadet ritades av Helge Zimdal och: Älvsjöbadet was designed by Helge Zimdal and Nils Ahrbom in austere functionalist style and opened on 22 June 1938. The entrance building survives and shows off their light touch. For the youngest, there's a small nine-sided paddling pool with a slide.
Älvsjövägen har en imponerande trafikmän: Älvsjövägen carries a remarkable amount of traffic. At 22,000 vehicles a day, that's as much as all the daily cross-border traffic between Norway and Sweden on the E6 and E18 put together. For something calmer, head to Solbergaskogen, a short way off – a wood classed as a key habitat in 2009, with ancient remains such as the Solberga burial ground.
Ända fram till sommaren 1968, då Redberg: Right up until summer 1968, when Redbergsplatsen was rebuilt, there was a turning loop for the trams here. The pavilion in Redbergslid’s People’s Park had already been pulled down in 1936.
Ända in på 1950-talet talade man om Fröl: Right up to the 1950s people spoke of Frölanns parish, and its residents were called frölänningar. Well into the 19th century they also went by the nickname “koljenackar”.
Well into the 1950s people still spoke of Frölanns parish, and its residents were known as ‘frölänningar’. Until late in the 19th century they also had another nickname: ‘koljenackar’.
Ändelsen -sta i Kälvesta betyder plats,: The ending ‘-sta’ in Kälvesta means place, and the first part of the name was originally a man’s name. The old village of Kälvesta dates back to the Middle Ages.
Ändhållplatsen ligger vid Östra sjukhuse: The last stop is at Östra sjukhuset hospital. From here it's only a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve of lakes, forest and swimming spots, where plenty of Gothenburgers spend their weekends.

The last stop is at Östra sjukhuset, the hospital. From here it's only a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes, forest and places to swim, where lots of Gothenburgers spend their weekends. Thank you for riding with us!
Ängarna en kort promenad härifrån är sed: Since 2026, the meadows a short walk from here have been protected as the Rissne ängar nature reserve – about 21 hectares where Rissne, Hallonbergen and Duvbo meet. Open meadows are ringed by wooded slopes of pine, and several red-listed beetles thrive here. A little further on is Duvbo Church, perched on a steep rocky slope among the villas.
Ängen Svartlöten, alldeles i närheten, ä: The meadow right next to us, Svartlöten, is a protected ancient site. It gave its name to Svarta Löt, a medieval assembly place mentioned in several documents from the 1400s. The meeting place itself is thought to have been at the Eriksberg croft near Kumla gård – partly where the E4/E20 motorway runs today. The Botkyrka suburb around us grew up in the late 1960s and early 1970s as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive. Alby centrum opened in 1972, and on the square just outside you can buy fresh fruit and vegetables.
Änkans hämnd i Erikskrönikan: The widow's revenge in Erik's Chronicle
Ärvinge byggdes i början av 1990-talet m: Ärvinge was built in the early 1990s with low, narrow blocks and dual-aspect flats, modelled on the suburbs of the 1940s and 50s. The office buildings sit closest to the main roads, shielding the homes from traffic noise.
Ärvinge är ett informellt område i södra: Ärvinge is an unofficial neighbourhood in southern Kista, and it's not far from here to Kista Galleria. As well as 180 shops and restaurants, the mall has a bowling alley, a multiplex cinema and a go-kart track covering a full 4,000 square metres. Students live in its two towers too – so for some, the shopping is right under their beds.
Ät eller handla i Kville saluhall: Eat or shop at Kville saluhall food hall
Ät eller handla i Kville saluhall (1 min: Eat or shop at Kville market hall (1 min) and see Carl Milles' statue Susanna on Kvilletorget (4 min).
Även Tygförvaltningen för Östra Militäro: The ordnance administration for the Eastern Military District was also based in Ursvik. It had its own railway, nicknamed Krutbanan – the Gunpowder Line.
Även fartyg av ULCC-klass, världens stör: Even ULCC-class ships – the world's biggest tankers, measuring 333 by 60 metres – have docked at Hjärtholmen. The refinery can process about 6 million tonnes of crude oil a year.
Åbyvägen har fått sitt namn efter byn Åb: Åbyvägen takes its name from the village of Åby, which lay between Brunnby and Ersta gård and is thought to have existed from as early as the Viking Age until the early 1500s. The road has also gone by the name Fabian Wredes väg. Ersta, too, is a farm that has long since vanished; it stood on the south-western edge of Årstafältet. On the same open field you'll find the Årstafältet allotments, which in 2018 counted as Stockholm's newest allotment garden.
Ågesta gårds stora stenbyggnad från 1600: Right next to us is the big 17th-century stone house of Ågesta farm, which got its present look around 1800. The City of Stockholm has owned the farm since 1945. Below it lies Lake Ågestasjön, and its name is a bit of a puzzle. 'Åg' is an old word for bulrushes and reeds, but the local heritage society believes the name actually comes from 'Åkes sta', Åke's place. The lake is part of the Orlången nature reserve.
Ågestaverket: Ågestaverket, the old nuclear power plant
Åkarlarnas by: The village of the river men
Åkermyntans centrum nämns i en av Killin: Åkermyntan's centre gets a mention in one of the comedy group Killinggänget's sketches: it's where the character Fred Asp, famous for partying with his ferret Göran, lives nearby.
Åkermyntans centrum är ett litet köpcent: Åkermyntans centrum is a small shopping centre that opened in November 1977 – and it has earned itself a place in Swedish comedy history. In one of the sketches by the comedy group Killinggänget, the character Fred Asp, famous for partying with his ferret Göran, lives near Åkermyntan. A short way off is the Hässelby garden and local history museum, and outside it stands a grey granite runestone that was found at Riddersvik in the early 1800s.
Åkeshovs reningsverk togs i bruk 1934 oc: Åkeshov sewage works opened in 1934 and is Stockholm's oldest treatment plant still in operation. But it's due to close, with the sewage diverted through a new tunnel to Henriksdal.
Åkeshovs slott var en gång centrum för e: Åkeshov Castle was once the heart of a large estate, on which districts such as Nockeby, Nockebyhov and Åkeslund were later built. Baroness Agneta Wrede lived here for more than fifty years, from 1747 to 1800, and a room in the castle is named after her. In the castle park is an elegant Rococo orangery designed by Carl Hårleman in 1749, and beside it an arboretum planted in 1998, when Stockholm was European Capital of Culture.
Åkeshovshallen invigdes 1959 och öppnade: Åkeshovshallen swimming baths opened in 1959 and reopened in 2018 after more than two years of renovation. The water in the big pools is kept at 27 degrees, and in the children's area at a cosy 29. Not far from here are the Linnéa allotments, also called Kortenslund after the old boatswain's croft that once stood on the site. And a little further on you can catch a glimpse of Åkeshov's orangery, built in 1749.
Ålkistan kallas trakten där Brunnsviken: Ålkistan is the name of the area where Brunnsviken bay meets Saltsjön, the arm of the Baltic, and the canal here was blasted out of the rock in 1863–64. On Roslagsvägen, on the north side, there used to be an inn, Ålkistans värdshus, which opened in the early 1700s and was pulled down in the 1880s. The housing estate of Sfären, also known as Himlabacken – “Heaven Hill” – was built between 1989 and 1991.
Ån slutar i Mälaren: The stream that ends in Lake Mälaren
Ån som blev en väg: The stream that became a road
Ån som nästan fylldes igen: The stream that was almost filled in
Ångloksnördar, se hit! En kort promenad: Calling all steam train fans! A short walk away is Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap, a volunteer society set up in 1972 to look after locomotives, mainly from the old Bergslagen Railways. They have around a hundred vehicles, including restored steam, electric and diesel locomotives that still run. The Rex cinema was nearby too, showing films from 1959 to 1973.
